title: 가락몰
google_addr: 932 Yangjae-daero, Songpa District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Lots of meat and seafood produce here at wholesale price. You can buy your produce and have it cooked at the restaurant upstairs. You can even have sashimi at its freshest. The mall was quiet when we arrived at noon.

Seoul evidently has some famous beef/meat markets - and this is one of them.   My family and I came here as part of a tour we booked on AirBNB to purchase our own meat and go to a local place to cook it up (which was a great experience).

I'm not sure I'd recommend coming here on your own as a tourist as there are over 100 small butcher and fish stalls with a huge variety of options.   Our guide walked us through the history of Korean BBQ (started in the 50's), the types of cuts and quality of the beef (lots), and what's considered the best.

He then took us to a certified butcher that caries the best graded beef from female cows and helped us select our cuts.   There's a restaurant at the top of the mall that allows you to cook your own cuts (as long as they're from the market below) and we had a great time eating them all.   My wife and our new friend felt like they came away a bit hungry still so don't be shy about ordering a lot of beef if you go this route.  Our guide recommended 250-350g for average and 400+ for heavy appetites.

All-in-all it was a great experience and delicious meal.  But I wouldn't make this a destination stop.

reviews.text: Worthy of one Michelin star. The food was fantastic and a very creative take on traditional Korean food. Dessert was the best. The service was excellent and the views of the city from our table were spectacular. We wer celebrating my brother's birthday and they treated him with a seaweed birthday soup.

I have had the pleasure of dining at Bicena several times, and each visit has been memorable. My first was in early 2024 for my birthday lunch; the kitchen surprised me with a bowl of seaweed soup, a thoughtful nod to Korean tradition that made the occasion feel extra special. The food was refined, beautifully presented, and the service was warm and attentive.

I returned later that year for Thanksgiving, and again, everything from the cuisine to the service lived up to the same high standard. My most recent visit was for another birthday celebration, and once again, Bicena delivered an outstanding experience. The ambiance is always wonderful, with spectacular views from the 81st floor that make dining here unforgettable.

Bicena has become a place I look forward to returning to, where refined modern Korean cuisine, thoughtful touches, and an elegant atmosphere come together seamlessly.

Michelin star restaurant worth it’s value.  Every dish taste exquisite and the lunch set meal took 2 hours for you to savor and enjoy the flavour.  Probably had their set menu refreshed for autumn and the overall menu is delicious.

Very personalized service.
Very hospitality trained.

The food was intimate for my palate as there were many different textures and the different fermented side dishes that were carefully curated which as a non-local would seldom come across. I was 60% only 1/3 into the entire course but he was assuring that I don’t need to finish but just try the dishes.

Elevated Korean Flavors with a Panoramic Vista: A Review of Bicena (Seoul)
Perched on the 81st floor of the iconic Lotte World Tower, Bicena offers a truly breathtaking dining experience, elevating Korean cuisine to new heights both literally and figuratively. From the moment you step into the sophisticated space, you are enveloped in an atmosphere of modern elegance. The dramatic double-height ceilings and expansive panoramic windows immediately draw your eye to the sweeping views of the Seoul skyline, creating an unparalleled backdrop that is as much a part of the experience as the food itself. The interior design thoughtfully blends contemporary aesthetics with subtle Korean sensibilities, fostering a luxurious yet comfortable environment perfect for a memorable occasion.

Bicena's culinary philosophy is centered on presenting contemporary Korean cuisine with an unwavering commitment to authenticity and the integrity of ingredients. Under the guidance of Chef Kwangsik Jun, the kitchen masterfully reinterprets traditional Korean flavors and dishes, infusing them with a refined touch and modern techniques. The restaurant's name, meaning "empty, fill, and share," hints at a philosophy of balance and thoughtful consumption, reflecting a deep respect for both nature's bounty and the communal spirit of Korean dining. This commitment extends to their affiliation with Kwangjuyo, a renowned Korean ceramics company that also produces traditional liquors, emphasizing a holistic appreciation for Korean craftsmanship.

The tasting menu is a curated journey through seasonal delights, showcasing a profound understanding of flavor profiles and textures. Each dish is a testament to meticulous preparation and artistic presentation. You might begin with a delicate welcome drink infused with the refreshing essence of pine needles, setting a serene tone. Highlights often include expertly aged meats, such as pork loin dry-aged with fermented rice salt, cooked to tender perfection and paired with vibrant homemade pickles. Another exquisite example could be crispy barley shrimp, offering a delightful play of textures and a harmonious blend of sweet and savory notes. The use of premium, often locally sourced, ingredients is paramount, ensuring that every bite sings with natural purity. Even traditional elements like rice, soup, and banchan (side dishes) are elevated, appearing as refined components of a cohesive culinary narrative.

The dining experience at Bicena is further enhanced by its impeccable service. The staff are highly attentive, knowledgeable, and move with a quiet efficiency that complements the serene atmosphere. They are adept at guiding guests through the multi-course menu, providing clear and insightful explanations of each dish's inspirations and preparation. This polished hospitality ensures a seamless and enjoyable journey from start to finish. Securing a window table, if possible, adds another layer of magic to the experience, allowing you to dine with Seoul's sprawling panorama as your companion.

In essence, Bicena offers an extraordinary opportunity to experience refined Korean gastronomy. It's a destination where breathtaking views meet exquisite flavors, and where traditional culinary wisdom is gracefully reimagined for the contemporary palate, leaving a lasting impression of sophisticated taste and unforgettable moments.

reviews.text:
I visited the Gahoe MinWha Museum of Korean Folk Painting and saw a special exhibition of Magpie and Tiger paintings.
The museum usually keeps original traditional folk paintings, but this time, artists from the association reinterpreted the Magpie and Tiger in creative and fun ways. It was a really great experience.

Visitors can also try painting folk art themselves. The modern folk paintings are available for purchase at a very reasonable price of about 400,000 won, which makes them valuable collectibles. The artworks are also made into postcards, keyrings, scarves, and shirts, so they make perfect souvenirs.
And You can also meet Derpy from K-pop Demon Hunters.^^

Gahoe Minhwa Museum
Welcome to the leading museum of Minhwa (Korean folk paintings).

The museum was founded in honor of Dr. Cho Ja-yong, a Harvard graduate who dedicated his life to promoting Korean culture. Today, Director Yoon Yeol-soo continues this mission by preserving traditional Minhwa and nurturing new artists through the Gahoe Academy and the Contemporary Minhwa Competition.

Here, we believe:
“What is most Korean is truly global.”

Currently, the Gahoe Minhwa Association is presenting a special exhibition:
“Welcome, We Are the Real Ones.”

Come and enjoy the world of tigers, magpies, and many other symbols that carry Korea’s unique spirit and wisdom.

reviews.text:
I love this place :)

This underground mall is one of those places where you just walk in… and suddenly lose all sense of direction !
And that’s totally normal. It’s huge. So many small shops, mostly focused on women’s fashion. Clothes, underwear, jackets, jewelry, boots, shoes, honestly everything is there.

There are benches and little places to sit, which I really appreciated after walking around for a while. My tip is to ask for prices and compare. Sometimes the same item appears again just a few meters away, but cheaper. It’s part of the experience to look around and take your time.

There’s so much cute stuff everywhere. It feels like a place you could visit every single day and still find something new. I really enjoyed just browsing without a plan and letting myself get lost a bit.

For me, it was a really nice experience. Lively, fun, and full of small discoveries. One of those places where you don’t rush, you just enjoy being there

The females will love this place! 95% for women and 5% for men. But the prices are better than most of Seoul. I was in Busan and then Gyeongju and if you take a bus from Gyeongju to Seoul the express bus station you arrive at in Seoul is the same metro station in which line 3, 7 and 9 is at and this GOTO-MALL is located. So it's a pretty decent place to shop and check stuff out if you are a lady in need of shopping. EXPRESS BUS TERMINAL is the Metro stop.
There are a lot of stalls offering the same product, so browse around first. Some stalls only accept cash but other stores accept credit cards as well. Just ask first.

title: 강동아트센터

reviews.text:
Hey, let me share something with you for a moment.

Gangdong Arts Center opened back in 2011 and their biggest hall, Hangang, seats about 850 people. It is not a huge place, but maybe that is what gives it its charm. For me, it is close to home, which means I can walk there without stress. Sometimes that little convenience makes all the difference.

I have seen a few performances there. Puccini’s Tosca in October 2023 and Mozart’s The Marriage of Figaro in November 2025. Both nights stayed with me, but one of them for an unexpected reason. Right before the opera began, the fire alarm suddenly went off. People were confused, some were frightened, and the staff did not give clear instructions. They later said it was a malfunction, but the moment itself felt unsettling. It is hard to focus on beautiful music right after something like that.

In terms of accessibility, it is much easier than the Seoul Arts Center. Godeok Station on subway line 5 is about a fifteen minute walk away. The box office is on the first floor, and there is a cloak room run by staff. Personally, I like the box seats. They let me concentrate, help me settle into the performance. The seat itself was comfortable, though the earlier chaos stayed with me longer than I expected.

Inside the center, there is a small coffee shop with reasonable prices. Coffee, bread, simple things that make your wait easier. What you will not find is a restaurant, so it is better to eat before you arrive.

Small hall, easy access, a few rough edges, but still a place where art lives.
Enjoy your visit.

Visited for the Anthony Browne exhibition and was impressed. Well layed out and lots of interactive points. The exhibition was interesting and covered 3 floors, but wasn't draining or repetitive. Would recommend.
A very nice new building, very professionally done.
I was a good showing of the Nutcracker. Impressive discipline by the young ballerinas. The design of the theater is a fancy old fashion setting. Complete with the upper deck and sides.
This is a very nice arts and performing arts center for Gangdong district. They have art galleries and stage theaters, the only problem is a smallish parking garage

title: 강변스파랜드
google_addr: 45 Guuigangbyeon-ro, Gwangjin District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Came here for the first time 5 years ago and happy to report it's stil going strong. There are many different hot rooms in the jjimjilbang area and the relaxing zone is very spacious. Plus these little nooks that I haven't seen anywhere else.

A bit outside of the city centre - it's a bus ride and then a 5-10 minutes walk - but it is one of the best jjimjilbang (relaxation centres) and Korean spas in Seoul in terms of the different facilities, and it is open 24/7.

Be aware that the majority of people who go there are local Koreans, not tourists, so very little (if any) English is spoken. However, the staff were super helpful and welcoming to me when I went (mid-week in the middle of the day, when it wasn't too busy compared to evenings and weekends).

At street level, look for the green and white sign with the red spa logo, then head down 2 flights of steps. Pay at the machine at the entrance: either the day price (spa only or spa + jjimjilbang) or night price; male or female; adult or child. Take the ticket, which indicates your locker number.

You have to be barefoot in the spa, so take your shoes off at the entrance, and place these in the relevant numbered (male/female) shoe locker. Place the key band on your wrist. This is also the key for your changing room locker and the dongle to scan for any extras (food; massages; facials; massage chairs, etc), which you pay for at the end of your stay.

Take the ticket to the reception desk. If you have paid for the jjimjilbang as well as the spa, then you will be given some lounging pyjamas in addition to towels. The spas are segregated (male/female); the jjimjilbang areas are not.

Go first to the male or female changing room for the spa. Strip naked and place all your belongings in your locker (NOTE: these are big enough to fit a slim cabin-sized trolley bag, but not larger suitcases or backpacks).

Go first to the stand-up showers in the spa area, and thoroughly wash and scrub yourself from top to toe. Riverside does not provide any toiletries, but does have items for sale at a stall in the changing rooms if you have not brought your own. Once you are thoroughly clean, you can use the spa facilities, which include various different bathing pools at different temperatures and wet saunas. Additional spa treatments (skin scrubbing, massages, facials, etc) are available at an additional cost. Before leaving the spa area, shower and scrub yourself thoroughly again, but at the sit-down showers.

Once you have dried off, put on the lounging pyjamas, and head upstairs to the jjimjilbang area. In addition to the main common area and sleeping spaces, the lounging areas include various different dry sauna spaces (yellow clay kiln; salt rock kiln; silver room; hot kiln; charcoal room; pine wood room, etc); igloo room; more massage treatment rooms; study area; play area for kids; games room; exercise room; massage chairs and foot massage machines.

There is a cafe that serves typical jjimjilbang snacks and refreshments (ramyeon noodles; hard boiled eggs; icecreams; a sweet rice drink called sikhye...), and a second cafe that does typical Korean meals.

A very relaxing experience!

It is close to Dong Seoul Terminal.
You can use Korean saunas and jjimjilbangs.
Parking is free for 3 hours.

A great place to take a bath and have a nice experience at a jjimjilbang (Korean Sauna). There are 8-9 types of Jjimjilbang, such as igloo experience, clay room, pinewood room…, in the resting area. The place is clean and there are a lot of couples resting there, which I think is a nice place for date ? I don’t know :)))
Though we didn't know how to speak English, we used Google Translate to communicate. The counter lady is so nice to us, even though we had a lot of questions... She was willing to help us and gave us a wonderful experience.

Further details:
To enter the spa land, take the lift to B2
Take off your shoes before entering the shop.
This place doesn’t have an age limit; teenagers like 17 years old are allowed.
Remember to take shampoo and soap for cleaning, or you will have to use public soap...
Tickets are around 14000 won, and you can stay up to 15 hours.
After you pay, get a suit for the Jjimjilbang and take the shoe locker key for the changing room lockers and snack shop payment.
Once you enter the bathing room, take a bath first before getting in the hot spring
An extra fee is needed for a massage

This is the best zzimzilbangs I have ever been. There are different kind of sauna room and you can sleep in the independent small cave(togool) or sleeping room.(for women or men). There are arcade game machines, singing rooms, billiards, etc... You can eat food or drinks. There is exclusive meeting room. So you can meet your business partner here. title: 갤러리아백화점 명품관
google_name: Galleria Department Store Luxury Hall WEST
google_addr: 343 Apgujeong-ro, Gangnam District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: There is a fine supermarket with many food stalls downstairs. I've tried strawberries around Seoul, but the ones they sold were the best!

This department store truly stands out for offering some of the best services compared to others.

First, their valet service sets the tone. Unlike many places where you need to be a VIP customer to enjoy that convenience, here it’s available to everyone. It makes the whole experience of visiting the store feel effortless from the very start.

Second, the food court is on another level. Instead of the usual chains or generic options, the restaurants are often popular, trendy spots that, in their original locations, are known for long wait times. Dining here gives you the same experience without the hassle of waiting in line. I also appreciate their system: you order, place your pager on the table, and the staff deliver the food directly to you. When you’re finished, they clear everything away. One of the biggest reasons I disliked eating at department stores before was the contradiction of paying high prices only to serve myself and return the tray—like at a fast-food place. Thankfully, Galleria does things differently, making the whole experience feel worthy of the price.

Third, the staff expertise is remarkable. They actually know what they’re selling. I once had a frustrating experience at another department store where a staff member recommended what I thought was French cheese, but it turned out to be butter. She didn’t understand the product herself, and worse, recommended something completely wrong. That kind of mistake would never happen here—the staff at Galleria are knowledgeable and professional, and it makes a big difference in the shopping experience.

Lastly, their grocery section feels curated rather than overwhelming. Instead of a massive selection, the products are carefully edited, almost as if they only stock what they consider the best produce, fruits, and specialty goods. The downside is that the prices are steep—sometimes even ridiculously so. But still, there are a few items I can only find here, which keeps me coming back despite the premium.

reviews.text:
Mario Outlet in Gasan-dong, Seoul, is Asia's largest downtown fashion outlet, featuring over 600 brands across three connected buildings with discounts often ranging from 40-50%. Located near Gasan Digital Complex Station (Line 7), it offers extensive shopping for apparel, luxury goods, and, specifically, Korean fashion brands.
Key Details
Location: 23 Digital-ro 9-gil, Geumcheon-gu, Seoul.
Hours: Monday-Thursday 10:30-21:00, Friday-Sunday 10:30-21:30.
Structure: Three halls (Mario Fashion Town) specializing in fashion, outdoor gear, and accessories.
Brands: Over 600 local and international brands, featuring a "No Brand Shop" and Daiso.
Amenities: Food courts (mainly in Hall 3), tax refund services, and lockers on the first floor.
Transportation: A short walk from Exit 4 of Gasan Digital Complex Station (Subway Lines 1 & 7).
Shopping Tips
Best Time: Friday to Sunday for the best selection, though it can be crowded.
Activities: Plan to spend at least 3 hours exploring the three buildings.
Deals: Look for additional discounts on top of marked prices, especially for winter clothing in October or summer clothes in April.
Nearby: Lotte Factory Outlet and W-Mall are located nearby for more options.

title: 경복궁
google_addr: 161 Sajik-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Visited the palace as part of the tour. The whole palace complex is free to enter if you are wearing the traditional hanbok. The whole place is massive and you can spend half a day just looking around. The buildings don't look old or aged at all because most of original structures were destroyed by the japanese during the war but they still look cool.
If you want to look at the places where nobility used to live in this is the place to be.

A nice palace but not as spectacular as the Chinese ones. Smaller scale than the Chinese. However, it is still nice to come here dressed in traditional costumes to soak in the atmosphere. If you are lucky, you can get to witness the change of guard ceremonies. Just check the schedule before coming so you can watch it.

Need lots of walking. Place is huge, can easily spend 1/2 day.

If you wear a hanbok no need to pay entrance fee, other wise you will need to pay.

Went during mid Jan. Was cold, lake os frozen. There are lots of places to take pretty photos. Beautiful place.

Great place to learn about the heritage.

The palace was built in the 15th century during the Joseon Dynasty., but then burned down during the Japanese invasion in the 16th century, and reconstructed soon afterwards to serve as the main residence of the kings for the next 250 years. The layout of the palace and the surroundings follows the Confucian principles with gates, courts, and residential areas, as exemplified by the similar but much larger Forbidden City in Beijing. The palace had an important influence on Korean architecture and garden design, as can be seen when visiting Seoul's many other places.

A lovely palace, my mother in law recanted when she was a little girl she would skate on the water in front of the palace. I guess times change, and places change, despite the palace remaining, what you can do here also changes. It was a great cultural experience and majestic glimpse of a different world. It was captivating to just stop and reflect on these aspects.

reviews.text:
Beautiful place to walk around and experience traditional Seoul. The hanok houses, narrow alleys, and city views make it feel like stepping back in time, especially early in the morning when it’s quiet.
It can get crowded later in the day, but if you go on a weekday or before noon, it’s very peaceful and great for photos. There are small cafes, galleries, and hidden viewpoints along the way, so it’s fun to explore slowly.
Just remember people actually live here, so be respectful and keep noise down. Overall, a must-visit spot if you want history, culture, and great views all in one walk.

Bukchon Hanok Village is easy to combine with Gyeongbokgung Palace in a day trip. The bus drops you right at Bukchon-ro, where maps help you plan your walk. The village sits on a hillside, so expect some gentle climbs, but the backstreets reveal clusters of traditional hanok homes, rooftop views, and even glimpses of Gyeongbokgung Palace. There are cozy cafes with terraces for a break. Best to allow at least 2 hours to explore and find photo spots. Keep in mind it’s a residential area with access limited to 10 am–5 pm, so be respectful when taking photos. We visited around noon in early January and found it pleasantly uncrowded, though we only managed to see a few hanok houses compared to online photos. Still, it’s worth a visit for the atmosphere and views.

A nice place to visit to see traditional architecture jn a residential estate. It is interesting to see some of these houses being converted into commercial shops, and good blend between tradition and modern contemporary. Just remember to keep your voice down to avoid causing disturbance to the residents.

There’s a tourist time window to visit certain areas: 10am to 5pm. Make sure to come within this time range.
Absolutely worth the visit!!

reviews.text:
Went here for another DAY6 concert!

Considering its size and capacity, this is the best venue to hold large number of audience indoor in Winter. Location also close to a lot bars and restaurants so you don’t have to be worried about being starved.

Good news, it’s also only walk away from the nearest Subway station Guro and Bus Stop. Again, you don’t have to worry about the public transport. They also have outdoor restroom.

The only thing cannot happen here is the 360 stage and steep higher floor. 4F seating is pretty high and steep, so you can’t stand up during the concert. Plus, in winter still so cold inside the venue.

Hey there, let me share a little baseball story with you.

Gocheok Sky Dome is the home of the Kiwoom Heroes. Sounds exciting, right? The catch is that getting there is not so simple. It sits far from the center of Seoul, and if you are like me, not familiar with this corner of the city, it feels like a bit of a journey.

The real challenge comes with Line 1 of the subway. That line is always crowded, always confusing. I have been to this stadium five times, and still I get lost. One wrong move on the train and you could find yourself in Incheon or Seodongtan. I know, because it happened to me.

As for the Dome itself, it is not huge. Sixteen thousand seats in total, which is less than half the size of Kyocera Dome in Osaka that holds more than thirty-six thousand. Still, what it lacks in scale, it makes up for in condition. The place is clean, modern, and well kept.

Before you go inside, take a moment at the entrance. You will see the large Sky Dome sign, and right nearby, a small official shop where you can pick up Kiwoom Heroes merchandise. A nice stop for souvenirs. Security will check your bag and scan your ticket, nothing out of the ordinary.

Inside, the food is straightforward. Think fast food and drinks, the kind that keep you going through nine innings. It is not fine dining, but it does the job.

So, is it worth the trip? Maybe yes, maybe no. But if you love baseball, or if you simply want to add another stadium to your list, then yes, it is worth the effort. Just double-check that you are on the right train.

title: 고척동 고인돌

reviews.text:
서울특별시 구로구 고척동에 있는 청동기시대 무덤.
고척동 고인돌은 서울특별시 구로구 고척동 산12-1번지 고척고등학교 뒷산, 삼국시대의 토성인 신정리 토성 경내에 위치한다.
고척동 고인돌은 1998년 서울대학교 조사단이 처음 발견하였으나, 정식 학술조사는 이루어진 바 없다. 그 후 관련 학자들의 조사에서 “덮개돌의 주변에 덮개돌과 동일한 형태의 돌들이 존재하지 않는 것으로 보아 원래의 위치에서 벗어난 것으로 보인다.”는 의견이 제시되었다. 또한 규모는 크지 않지만 돌방이 확인되었으며, 굄돌 등의 배치 상황으로 미루어 고인돌로 추정케 한다.
기반식 지석묘로 추정되며 덮개돌의 크기는 가로 190㎝, 세로 105㎝, 높이 28㎝이고, 굄돌은 길이 50㎝, 폭 12㎝로 크지 않은 규모이다.
고인돌 주변에서 직접적으로 출토된 유물은 없다.
현재 지석묘를 보호하기 위해 안내판과 보호 펜스를 설치하는 등 관리 상태는 양호한 편이다.
고척동 고인돌은 구로구에서 유일한 고인돌로서 주변의 고척동 유물산포지 등과 더불어 청동기시대 주변 지역 일대의 문화상 이해에 좋은 자료가 된다.

title: 고하송진우선생동상
google_addr: South Korea, 서울특별시 광진구 능동

reviews.text:
這裡是 **고하 송진우 선생 동상**（高荷 宋鎭禹 先生 銅像）附近，周圍環境非常開闊，有一片空曠的草地，非常適合野餐或放鬆。草地面積很大，視野也很寬廣，讓人感覺心情舒暢。特別是陽光好的時候，溫暖的陽光灑在身上，微風輕輕吹過，真的特別舒服！這裡不僅適合家庭聚會，也很適合和朋友一起來享受悠閒的時光。

草地周圍還有一些樹木，提供了自然的遮蔭，即使天氣稍微熱一點，也不會覺得太曬。你可以帶上一張野餐墊，準備一些簡單的食物和飲料，坐在草地上享受大自然的美好。這裡的環境非常安靜，遠離城市的喧囂，是一個放鬆身心的好地方。

此外，고하 송진우 선생 동상本身也是一個值得一看的景點，銅像莊嚴肅穆，周圍的環境也很有歷史感。如果你對歷史感興趣，可以在野餐之餘，順便參觀一下銅像，了解更多關於宋鎭禹先生的故事。

總之，這裡是一個結合自然與歷史的好地方，無論是野餐、散步，還是單純地享受陽光，都非常適合。推薦大家有空的時候來這裡走走，感受一下這片草地帶來的寧靜與舒適！
Song Jin-woo (宋鎭禹, May 8, 1890 – December 30, 1945)

어린이대공원 내 동상
송진우(宋鎭禹, 1890년 5월 8일 ~ 1945년 12월 30일)는 한국의 독립운동가, 정치인이며 일제 강점기와 해방 직후에 언론인, 교육자, 사상가, 정치인으로 활동하였다
한국민주당(韓國民主黨)의 초대 당수였으며, 1919년 3·1 만세 운동 당시 민족대표 48인의 한사람이기도 하다.
일본 유학 후 귀국, 김성수와 함께 중앙학교를 인수하여 교감에 취임했다가 1919년 2월 교장이 됐다. 정의론과 이상주의에 입각하여, 우드로 윌슨의 민족자결주의에 고무되어 1919년 3.1만세 운동을 주동한 민족대표 48인의 하나로 체포되었다가 복심에서 무죄 판결을 받아 1년 반 동안의 미결수 구류를 치르고 풀려났고, 이후 현실주의자로 변신한다. 1920년에는 학교설립 모금운동을 하다가 감시하던 경찰에게 붙잡히기도 했다. 그 뒤 김성수 등과 동아일보를 창립, 동아일보 사장, 주필, 고문 등을 역임하며 언론활동에 종사하였고, 실력 양성이 민족의 독립을 가져온다는 신념하에 물산장려운동, 민립대학기성회 운동 등에 참여, 브나로드 운동 등을 지원하였으며, 태평양 전쟁 전후에는 병을 핑계로 창씨개명과 임전 협력을 거부하다가 1945년 8월 광복을 맞았다

reviews.text:
₩32,5000 Han River Cruise 60mins.
I joined a group yacht cruise (Klook) one afternoon up to sunset, including the rainbow bridge light show. Captain and crew were both friendly, playing chill music all throughout the ride, blowing bubbles, taking photos of passengers. We were less than 10 people in total.
First, exchange your voucher to the ticket booth. Come to the gate about 10minutes before. Everyone will receive basic safety instructions and required to wear the vest before boarding. There were beverages available for everyone (inclusive), and you can also bring your own.

Golden Blue Marina was one of the most unexpected highlights of my recent visit to Seoul. Nestled along the Han River near the iconic Banpo Bridge, this yacht club offers a rare blend of luxury, tranquility, and unforgettable river views—right in the middle of one of Asia’s busiest cities.

I had the chance to enjoy an evening cruise, and it was truly magical. As the city lights slowly came on and the Banpo Rainbow Fountain show lit up the evening sky, the calm of the water and the cool breeze created a surreal contrast to the hustle and bustle of urban life just a few blocks away. The skyline looked even more beautiful from the deck.

The staff were professional yet warm, and everything from boarding to the safety instructions and cruise duration was well organized. I appreciated how clean and well-maintained the yacht was—modern, spacious, and picture-perfect. Whether you're planning a romantic date, a small celebration, or want to see Seoul from a different perspective, this place is a fantastic choice.

Golden Blue Marina also offers private rentals, speedboats, and even water sports for those looking for a more thrilling experience. And if you're lucky, you might spot fireworks or live music from nearby events at Banpo Hangang Park.

I’ve visited Seoul several times and also experienced this cruise with Golden Blue Marina and other cruising companies. Still, Golden Blue Marina is the best, and I can’t recommend it enough. Golden Blue Marina is more than a yacht club; it’s a peaceful retreat, a photography paradise, and a place to create beautiful memories.
It was a wonderful experience. It costed us 35000 Won , our ride lasted for 50 mins, the captain of the yacht also helped us to take photos, and we were served with complimentary coke and drinks.

Rivers flow through the world's major cities. The Thames River in London and the Seine River in Paris are examples. However, the Han River is on a different level from those rivers. Banpo Hangang Park is a great place to visit, but there is something special about enjoying the Han River on a yacht. The 40-minute sailing will give you the best opportunity to feel and enjoy the Han River. In particular, Captain Baby Dad (ae gi abba in korean)has many special ceremonies, which makes it even more enjoyable. If you want to enjoy the Han River and Seoul, I highly recommend it. If you make a reservation in advance through Naver, you can get a discount (as of 24.08.01)
We had a great time with the sail this afternoon to evening. Truly a one of a kind experience. Must try. Remarkably relaxing. Thank you Captain Kim.

title: 공덕동 족발골목
google_addr: 19 Mallijae-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: I like this little place. The Jokbal is very juicy and tenderly. We pick half and half which served spicy and non-spicy. Pick with vegetables to eat together👍

One of the famous places in Mapo-Dongjak area for steamed pig foot called Jokbal. This place was so crowded even though it was 5 pm. I didn't try for spicy jokbal. When you order a main jokbal, it comes with soondae and soup but it get cold quick.  Not going back, but once is enough.

This restaurant was more packed than others despite being farther in the alley and it’s a Thursday night. Look for the pig logo. We had a really great experience. While struggling to communicate with one of the owners, another customer who spoke both Korean and English was sitting at the table next to ours and helped us translate. Everyone was so nice. We ordered the half and half, which was half original flavour and half spicy flavour, for 42,000 won. With this pig feet order, they gave us a stew (which contained a lot of meat) and a plate of sundae for free. All the dishes were incredibly delicious and the portion was huge. There is a simple English menu and they accept credit cards.

Tried their most popular dish Korean pork feet 한돈족발.  We ordered a small portion of port feet to share between two people and we could not finish.  Side dishes such as kimchi and radish were very tasty.  They accept credit card payment.

This is a place where their goal is to feed people and not only making money. Big shoutout to them. The pork feet was excellent. Not too fatty and the meat was well-done but tender. The portions were very generous. We also got a Sundae guk soup (ksausage soup). They refilled several times, because they saw we enjoyed it. Also the banchan (ktapas) were refilled without delation. The steam sausage and organs were also delicious. Water and banchan are on the house. People goes to eat and drink well, don't expect a quiet place.  Very good price.

title: 과거와 현재의 시간이 겹쳐진 부암동길
google_addr: 4-1 Changuimun-ro 11-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
서울시 종로구 부암동 인왕산 자락에 위치한 옛 안평대군 거처에 마련한 한국전통 문화공간입니다. 본체와 별체를 포함한 4개동에서 체험, 전시,공연,대관 등 다양한 문화예술프로그램이 운영되는 곳입니다. 특히 눈여겨 볼만한 것은 조선시대 안견이 그린 "몽유도원도"입니다. 몽유도원도는 세종대왕의 3째 아들인 안평대군이 꿈속에서 본 무릉도원을 화가인 안견에게 이야기한 것을 안견이 3일만에 완성한 대작입니다.
This traditional Korean cultural space, located at the foot of Inwangsan Mountain in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul, is housed in the former residence of Prince Anpyeong. A variety of cultural and artistic programs, including hands-on experiences, exhibitions, performances, and rentals, are offered across four buildings, including the main building and annexes. A particular highlight is the Joseon Dynasty-era painting "Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land." This masterpiece, completed in just three days, reflects a dream Prince Anpyeong, the third son of King Sejong, had dreamed of, and told the artist about it.
안평대군의 이상향이 안견의 몽유도원도로 탄생한 장소.  종로에 있던 오진암을 그대로 옮겨와 아름다운 한옥의 모습을 재현했다고 한다.  주차장도 편리하고 고즈넉한 한옥에서 여유있게 둘러보기 좋은 곳.

종로구 부암동에 위치한 전통문화공간 입니다. 원래는 익선동에 있던 한옥 건물인데, 조선말 서화가 이병직의 집이기도 했고, 7.4남북공동성명을 도출해낸 장소였다고 합니다. 이곳은 음식점인 오진암으로 운영되다가 이 건물자재를 이용하여 현재의 위치에 한옥문화공간으로 지었다고 합니다. 현재 위치는 안견이 몽유도원도를 그리게한 장소로 유명하며 조그만 방한켠에서 몽유도원도의 복사본을 전시하여 자세하게 설명을 하는 코너가 있읍니다. 전시가 아니더라도 한옥의 아름다움을 느낄수 있는 특별한 공간인거 같습니다.
오진암이라는 조선시대 요정집(고오급 술집)을 개조하여 문화재로 만든 곳으로, 현재는 원래 목적과 상관없는 한옥전시, 전통문화 전시, 에티켓교육 등을 하는 곳으로 거듭나 사용되고 있습니다. 한옥문화 체험으로 방문하시면 좋을 것 같습니다. 입장료 따로 없고 주차장 있습니다.

Having long anticipated seeing 'Jesus Christ Superstar,' the production delivered a compelling theatrical experience, though with notable areas for improvement. The performers demonstrated exceptional talent, successfully conveying both the narrative and emotional depth of this iconic musical.
However, the technical aspects of the venue warrant attention. The sound system's performance fell considerably short of expectations for a production of this caliber, potentially impacting the overall audience experience. The VIP seating arrangements were particularly disappointing, ranking among the less comfortable premium seating experiences in recent memory.
The venue's infrastructure presents a significant opportunity for enhancement. A temporary closure for comprehensive improvements to both the sound system and seating arrangements could substantially elevate the theatrical experience. Such renovations would align the facility's technical capabilities with the high caliber of performances it hosts.
A noteworthy positive aspect is the venue's parking facilities. The spacious underground parking garage, combined with the remarkably reasonable rate of 5,000 won for five hours (applicable exclusively to ticket holders), provides exceptional value and convenience for attendees.
Despite the technical limitations, the cast's powerful performances successfully conveyed the musical's essence, demonstrating their professional commitment to theatrical excellence. The production ultimately succeeds on the strength of its performers, though the venue itself presents clear opportunities for enhancement.

reviews.text:
Visiting Gwanghwamun Square in mid-December is an absolute treat! The entire area is beautifully decorated with festive lights and ornaments, creating a warm and cheerful atmosphere despite the winter chill.

The lighting displays are stunning—perfect for evening strolls and photos. It’s a great spot to soak in the holiday spirit, enjoy the vibrant city energy, and take in the iconic views of Gwanghwamun Gate surrounded by sparkling decorations.

If you’re in Seoul during December, this is definitely a must-visit for the festive vibes and Instagram-worthy shots!

Gwanghamun Square is a very popular tourist destination in Seoul. It's a large public area where name activities are held. There are 2 statues here as well. There's the statue of King Sejong and the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. There are plenty of cafes and restaurants nearby.

Although on first sight Gwanghwamun Square might not look spectacular and any different to other city and town squares, I liked visiting it and walking around.

I started walking from one end of the square and took my time exploring the historical figures and monuments along the way. At the opposite end, the square leads to the grand Gyeongbukgung Palace.

I found the square to be quite large and appreciated the amount of space there. It was popular for tourists as well as locals having lunch and passing through yet I didn't think the area was crowded and congested. The square was very clean and well looked after.

Came across Admiral Yi, looking fierce as ever, almost like he was scolding the broken sign in front of him. The whole square has this mix of history and modern city energy that makes it really unique.  Even with a few things needing repair, the area still feels alive and inspiring.

Many people think this is just a square but behind the General's statue there is an entrance to a huge underground museum. It is so sad many people skip this place before entering the palace.

That reminds me the word: There is an unseen thing behind every visible one.

So if you go down the stairs or elevator you will at least witness the replica of this famous turtle ship here. Plus you can wear one of the traditional clothes here, get inside the replika ship and take photos.

Please visit this place before you visit the palace and you can also chill at the square there are many shadowy areas and street music is on.

title: 광복 80주년 기념 '강제동원 희생자의 길을 걷다'
google_name: National Museum of Forced Mobilization under Japanese Occupation
google_addr: Daeyeon-dong, Nam-gu, Busan, South Korea

reviews.text:
It's basically the holocaust museum for the Japanese occupation of Korea. For those who don't know, Japan took over large parts of Asia and forced (or enslaved) millions of people to work for the purpose of building its empire. This museum seeks to document the history and individual stories of survivors of the Japanese rule. If you loved Schindler's List, then you might find yourself interested in what happened here.

It's free and well worth it if you have the time and are interested. However, it's kind of hard to bring young children here even though they have a room for children on the 7th floor.

A very good museum on an important subject that shows how the ghosts of history haunt the present. Admission is free.

I expected more of the permanent exhibition would be dedicated to telling the history of the so-called ‘comfort women’, not least their struggle to reintegrate into society after the war. I thought that this particular aspect of forced mobilization wasn’t explored deeply enough.

The permanent exhibition museum can be repetitive in sections, and there are some seemingly serious factual discrepancies: see my photos of two nearby panels that variously claim 209,000 and 400,000 Koreans were mobilized as soldiers until liberation. In general, the English language descriptions would benefit from an English proofreader.

But overall, it’s a must-see when you’re in South Korea if you want to understand the country’s history and relationship with Japan. I also commend the museum for recognizing the many efforts of Japanese citizens and historians to uncover the truth and hold their conservative governments to account.
Very sad, it's a must vist. It helped my understanding of the Koreans suffering, at the hands of the Japanese.
Really interesting museum, I didn’t know much about the forced work, the “comfort women” and the atrocities that Japanese did in Korea in the years prior and during the II World War

title: 광장시장

reviews.text:
I absolutely loved visiting Gwangjang Markets! It was busy and touristy but I felt that this really added to the atmosphere and excitement. Some people might say that prices here are more expensive than else where in Seoul however I found them to be reasonable.

The market sells lots of street food and souvenirs. There is one long, main and wide corridor type strip down the centre with a number of narrower lanes branching off the sides, also selling food, souvenirs and trinkets. All stall holders we interacted with were super friendly, warm and helpful. They all appeared happy to be interacting with customers and feeding the crowds. Each food store specialises in a different type of food. Everything we ate was delicious! I liked that you were able to buy food from lots of different stores and then come together and share so you could taste a bit of everything.

I would highly recommend visiting here!

This is a very popular market to sample lots of food options and price is affordable too. You can shop for bed covers, pillows, clothing, kitchen accessories, grab coffee at coffee shops near by or just enjoy a sunny day inside and around this market. Bring your appetite and your walled for a fun time

reviews.text:
Visiting Gwanghwamun Square in mid-December is an absolute treat! The entire area is beautifully decorated with festive lights and ornaments, creating a warm and cheerful atmosphere despite the winter chill.

The lighting displays are stunning—perfect for evening strolls and photos. It’s a great spot to soak in the holiday spirit, enjoy the vibrant city energy, and take in the iconic views of Gwanghwamun Gate surrounded by sparkling decorations.

If you’re in Seoul during December, this is definitely a must-visit for the festive vibes and Instagram-worthy shots!

Gwanghamun Square is a very popular tourist destination in Seoul. It's a large public area where name activities are held. There are 2 statues here as well. There's the statue of King Sejong and the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. There are plenty of cafes and restaurants nearby.

Although on first sight Gwanghwamun Square might not look spectacular and any different to other city and town squares, I liked visiting it and walking around.

I started walking from one end of the square and took my time exploring the historical figures and monuments along the way. At the opposite end, the square leads to the grand Gyeongbukgung Palace.

I found the square to be quite large and appreciated the amount of space there. It was popular for tourists as well as locals having lunch and passing through yet I didn't think the area was crowded and congested. The square was very clean and well looked after.

Came across Admiral Yi, looking fierce as ever, almost like he was scolding the broken sign in front of him. The whole square has this mix of history and modern city energy that makes it really unique.  Even with a few things needing repair, the area still feels alive and inspiring.

Many people think this is just a square but behind the General's statue there is an entrance to a huge underground museum. It is so sad many people skip this place before entering the palace.

That reminds me the word: There is an unseen thing behind every visible one.

So if you go down the stairs or elevator you will at least witness the replica of this famous turtle ship here. Plus you can wear one of the traditional clothes here, get inside the replika ship and take photos.

Please visit this place before you visit the palace and you can also chill at the square there are many shadowy areas and street music is on.

title: 구로미래도서관
google_addr: Saemal-ro, Guro District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
25/12/20
아이랑 왔는데, 개관(25.8월)한지 오래 안되서 그런지 깨끗해요. 1층에 커피숍(브리오슈미엘) 있고, 2층엔 열람실겸 도서실이 자그맣게 있고, 3층엔 유아도서실 있어요. 주차는 유료이니 참고하세요.

개관한날이 얼마않돼서 사람들은 많지않았으나 정리되가는 환경을보고 신도림역에서의 쉼터로서 정서공간으로   있는것같다. 깨끗하고 조용한 환경이  사람들로 하여금 발길을찾게 할것같다.
교통편도 지하철1,2호선 신도림역3번 출구로나와보면 보이는건물이라 방문도쉽다.
버스편도 환승하는곳이라 좋은장소인것은틀림없다.

구로미래도서관은 2024년 8월 23일에 개관한 구로구립 도서관입니다. 위치부터가 신도림역 바로 옆에 있어서 인근 주민들뿐만 아니라 외지에서 찾아오기 좋은 위치에 있습니다.

총 3층으로 구성되어 1층 음료를 파는 북카페, 2층 종합 및 디지털 자료실, 3층 강당 및 유아자료실로 간단하게 구성되어 있습니다.

시설 자체는 쾌적하고 신선하지만 역세권에 만들어진 최신식 도서관임에도 불구하고 다만 외관과는 다르게 내부시설의 규모는 생각보다 크지 않은 수준입니다. 칸막이형 열람실도 없습니다. 자리수도 많지 않아 100여 명을 수용하기에도 어려운 크기입니다.
새로 지은 도서관이라 공이 깨끗하고 다양한 좌석이 이채롭다. 장서는 많지 않지만 최신 서적 위주라 트렌드 따라잡기에 적지다.
새로 생겨서 정말 깨끗하고, 좌석도 편안하고 쾌적해요. 특히 2층에 창가 소파 너무 좋아요.

Visited the National Theater of Korea and was thoroughly impressed! The place is huge, offering multiple performance halls that host a variety of traditional and contemporary shows. The facilities, including bathrooms, are well-maintained, and the lawns are spotlessly cared for, creating a welcoming environment. We enjoyed some beverages from the nearby cafe, which were delightful. Additionally, the accessibility is top-notch with a bus stop right in front that makes it super convenient for visitors. Highly recommend for anyone looking to experience Korea's rich performing arts culture!
It's a nice building. I see many runners in front of this building.

I’ve been to the National Theater of Korea a few times now. I watched La Traviata last September, Joyous Resonance in January, and L’italiana in Algeri in February. Each show was different, but they all had that moment when the lights dim, the orchestra begins, and the whole room breathes together. That’s the part I love most.

The theater is one of the biggest in Korea. It went through a renovation in 2021, and it looks great. The halls are clean, the seats are comfortable, and everything feels new. Still, I think a great theater needs more than just a nice building. It needs warmth. It needs to feel like a place made for people, not just for performances.

If you are planning to visit with kids, there is something you should know. Getting there is not easy. The theater sits halfway up Namsan Mountain, right in the middle of Seoul but far from the subway. The nearest station, Dongguk University on Line 3, is not within walking distance. You have to take a bus, usually number 420. Now, imagine yourself holding your child and a bag while standing on a crowded bus on your way to an opera. You will probably be tired before you even get there.

That is why I think accessibility matters. A public theater should welcome people from the moment they decide to come, not make them wonder how to reach it.

Once you are inside, things get better. The space feels open and organized. There are four floors, labeled L, 1, 2, and 3. Each one has vending machines for water and soft drinks. On the L floor, there is a restaurant called Central Yunit. It looks comfortable and has many seats, although it seems a bit expensive. There is also a KB Bank ATM nearby, which is convenient.

The box office is on the 1st floor, which feels like the 2nd floor if you are used to the American floor system. There is a small café that sells sandwiches and coffee, and the box office opens one hour before the show. The staff are calm and polite. You can leave your coat in the cloakroom across from the counter. They put a numbered sticker on the back of your ticket so you can pick it up easily after the show.

There are plenty of seats for intermission, and the atmosphere stays quiet and comfortable. After the performance, shuttle buses take people back to Dongguk University Station and Dongdaemun History and Culture Park Station. If you miss one, another comes in about twenty minutes.

Yes, getting there takes effort, but once you sit down and the music starts, you forget about all of that. The voices rise, the stage glows, and for a while, everything else fades away. That is the beauty of live performance, and it is why I keep coming back.

reviews.text: Day 2 at the museum and I have barely scratched the surface. I am still in awe of what is available to see in the permanent collection. Cost is free for the permanent collection. Access is quick for those without a bag, a little slower for those with a bag. There is a cafe inside the museum outside of security and 2 other places outside of museum building itself.

I traveled from NYC specifically to see the Impressionism exhibition at the National Museum of Korea in collaboration with the Metropolitan Museum of Art, and it absolutely lived up to the journey. Seeing works connected to the Met presented in Seoul felt incredibly special and thoughtfully curated.

What moved me just as much, though, were the Korean history galleries. Each exhibit is presented with such detail and reverence that I found myself stopping often to reflect. The exhibition on Yi Sun-sin was especially powerful. I appreciated how it explored not only his achievements as a respected admiral, but also his humanity. It felt balanced, reflective, and deeply meaningful.

I also loved spending time in the typography and print sections. As someone who appreciates visual storytelling and design, seeing the evolution of written form and print culture was inspiring.

The museum itself is clean, beautifully laid out, and very foreigner friendly. The overall energy feels calm, intentional, and elevated. And the museum shop is honestly one of the best I have ever experienced anywhere in the world. The curation, design objects, and gifts are exceptional.

If you are visiting Seoul, this museum is an absolute must. It is world class in every sense.

National Museum of Korea is an absolute gem. I honestly can’t believe the admission is free for such a high-quality experience; the maintenance and presentation are incredible. There are so many things to see, from ancient artifacts to beautiful Buddhist art. The museum is massive, so I highly recommend sparing a day or two to really take it all in. Whether you are a history buff or just appreciate beautiful design, this is a must visit in Seoul!

I really enjoyed the National Museum of Korea and it was excellent plus the admission was free.

When we went there they had special exhibition of 이순신 which was free for the day and pretty well curated (i got pretty emotional with seeing his journey again). Lastly they have an amazing museum shop with a lot of pretty and high quality items. The museum has subway entrance tunnel carved out all the way and some nearby bus stops as well. You also get a great view of 남산 and slick architecture of the museum building outside. Come ready to spend hours and walk 15k steps easy.

I believe that is what makes it so cool!

Not many foreigners know about this place, but Seoul does have an aviation museum that showcases the invention and development of aviation.

The museum spans three floors, each featuring detailed exhibition halls. You’ll find rare South Korean military aircraft on display, including the country’s first seaplane, the SX-1, and the famous Black Eagle. Retired engines such as the Merlin 61 and the R-1820 are also part of the collection.

I even had the chance to try out a check-in kiosk and go through a mock airport security experience. There's also a library filled with aviation-related books for visitors to explore.

It’s a fantastic destination for aviation enthusiasts, especially those looking to enjoy something unique before catching a flight at nearby Gimpo Airport. For those carrying suitcases or large backpacks, free lockers are available on every level, making your visit more convenient.

walking distance from the Gimpo Airport. you can easily spend a few hours here learning not only about Korean aviation but the history of aviation in general. some actual aircrafts are on display including a cut section of a B747. you can also try a flight  simulator on the 3rd floor for only 5000 won.

The museum is only 5 minutes on foot from Gimpo Airport's Domestic Terminal. The best thing is its generous free admission for everyone! Yes! Totally free! The museum was huge, informative and well organized. Each floor has a different thematic exhibition with clear English translation, making our visit so much comfortable. The future aviaton technology on 3rd floor is the best to us!

Check out Korea's national Aviation Museum!
For more information check out their homepage ~~~ Enjoy ~~ 😁

This place is a must see for aviation buffs. It’s kind of stuck in another era, perhaps the’80’s?
I believe that is what makes it so cool!
Lots of aircraft, mostly antique, very few modern day. They also have an eclectic gift shop with scale models and many other items.

Not many foreigners know about this place, but Seoul does have an aviation museum that showcases the invention and development of aviation.

The museum spans three floors, each featuring detailed exhibition halls. You’ll find rare South Korean military aircraft on display, including the country’s first seaplane, the SX-1, and the famous Black Eagle. Retired engines such as the Merlin 61 and the R-1820 are also part of the collection.

I even had the chance to try out a check-in kiosk and go through a mock airport security experience. There's also a library filled with aviation-related books for visitors to explore.

It’s a fantastic destination for aviation enthusiasts, especially those looking to enjoy something unique before catching a flight at nearby Gimpo Airport. For those carrying suitcases or large backpacks, free lockers are available on every level, making your visit more convenient.

walking distance from the Gimpo Airport. you can easily spend a few hours here learning not only about Korean aviation but the history of aviation in general. some actual aircrafts are on display including a cut section of a B747. you can also try a flight  simulator on the 3rd floor for only 5000 won.

The museum is only 5 minutes on foot from Gimpo Airport's Domestic Terminal. The best thing is its generous free admission for everyone! Yes! Totally free! The museum was huge, informative and well organized. Each floor has a different thematic exhibition with clear English translation, making our visit so much comfortable. The future aviaton technology on 3rd floor is the best to us!

title: 국립현대미술관 덕수궁
google_name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Deoksugung
google_addr: 99 Sejong-daero, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: The museum is currently hosting an exhibition on nostalgia, and some of the paintings left a profound impression on me. After all, everyone carries a place in their heart they can never return to—perhaps a childhood home, a distant town, or simply a moment in time that’s gone. The exhibition beautifully captures that bittersweet feeling, inviting us to reflect on the places we’ve left behind but never truly forget.

We didn’t expected to visit this museum during our trip, but we did get to see it! Completely worth the visit. It has a lot of beautiful of modern and contemporary art, sculptures and paintings. Restrooms are clean, many spaces to seat, souvenirs store and more. Despite it was a weekend, and many people were around, you have enough space to see everything.
Beautiful place, private tours for tourist are free and by schedule time. Great place and the guide super nice friendly and very knowledgeable. Worth visiting, very peaceful.  You will love it.

We didn’t plan on visiting this museum during our trip, but we stumbled upon it during our visit to the Deoksugung Palace. It has a lot of interesting art and gorgeous embroidery pieces in the museum and I definitely think it is worth visiting. You also learn a lot about the history of traditional art in South Korea. I think this museum is definitely worth visiting, since you can visit the palace at the same time.

The museum and palace was busy because it was free for Lunar New Year and it was very cold out.  The exhibit had some Chinese artwork as well. The layout of the museum was well organized. I recommend stopping by the museum while you are visiting Deoksugung. It is right by the City Hall station, so it's easy to find.

title: 국립현대미술관 서울
google_name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
google_addr: 30 Samcheong-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
A little over a month ago, I finally crossed the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul off my must-visit list. As a venue dedicated to showcasing both established masters and the vibrant contemporary scene, the MMCA is a truly world-class institution.
The most satisfying aspect of the visit was finally standing before works that feel legendary. Nam June Paik's Junk TV (잡동사니 벽) is an anarchic, mesmerizing wall of visual noise that beautifully captures the artist's genius and prescience regarding media overload. It remains a chaotic, vital masterpiece that anchors the modern collection.
Equally compelling, though in a profoundly quieter way, was Do Ho Suh's Floor. The simple act of walking across the glass surface, supported by hundreds of tiny, straining figures, transforms the space into an interactive, existential metaphor. It's a testament to Suh's ability to imbue architectural space with deep, personal meaning.
However, the highlight of the visit, and a thrilling discovery for me, was Jung Yeondoo's Cinemagician. Experiencing this piece for the first time was genuinely captivating. Jung has a powerful way of blending the real and the imagined, and Cinemagician offered a fresh perspective on narrative and memory. It was the perfect example of the MMCA's strength: honoring foundational artists while actively championing the next generation of visionary creators.
The collection is diverse, the curation is thoughtful, and the combination of monumental installations and unexpected delights makes it an absolutely essential stop for anyone interested in contemporary art.

We visited last year and were a bit disappointed in the exhibits. Our friend convinced us to attend this year as Kim Tschang-yeul was showing and we are so glad we did. What an incredible show and artist. Another National Icon and his art is highly sought after, so to be able to see so many of his original pieces in one spot was incredible. You can also see some of his work in the main lobby to the Lotte Hotel Seoul after the show finishes. The Gallery itself is extremely large and they've done a great job renovating the old building and creating a large gallery behind it. There is a large cafe in the lobby with limited food options  and lots of large spaces so it never feels too busy. It's free to walk around the main building but depending on the exhibits you will need to purchase tickets, which can be done easily at the museum in person or at a both. I think you can book online too. The price was really low for an exhibit this size and quality.

I loved this visit and the art work on display this time. The grounds and buildings of the museum are really quite interesting in themselves. Busy coffee shop on site as well as a matcha tea shop.
Don't miss the two art gallery shops and the bookstore. The surrounding neighborhood is also good to explore.

I went on a weekend, there were no queues for the tickets even though there’s quite a lot of people, ticket is also very affordable to see all the exhibitions. The place is huge, with the exhibitions, cafes, and souvenir area. Overall a very interesting place, well-organized for each sections too.
When I visited there were not many exhibitions going on. One day I just want to try their cultural shuttle buss going to other national morden museums in other cities on a day.

title: 국제갤러리
google_addr: 54 Samcheong-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
This place is free to enter, but when I went in, they were closed while preparing for the next exhibition.

So please check their schedule online before visiting (I just checked, but there was nothing :)))

Update: Finally, I was able to go inside when there was an exhibition. I came here around noon, but the exhibition at that time wasn’t very interesting—there were just a few pictures on the first and second floors. There was only one staff member at the reception desk, and she didn’t greet the guests who came in (including me and another person I saw), which made the atmosphere feel a bit unwelcoming. I wouldn’t recommend this place after my second visit.

Undoubtedly one of the best art spots to visit in Seoul, the curation is impressive and it highlights the clever design of the buildings the gallery is composed of. I had the fortune of seeing Bill Viola’s work, it was a breathtaking exhibition. If you are an art person and are visiting Korea, don’t walk, run!

A phenomenal gallery experience that is really a mini art town. Made up of atleast 5’/7 buildings and many galleries the spaces are architecturally beautiful and very practical for showing art. The buildings range from old Korean architecture from the ancient times to a few regular galleries to one created by architect Florian Isenberg, a renowned architect. The visit is worth it for the architecture but there is so so much more. The shows are always amazing and right now there is a South Korean woman who works with North Korean artisans to complete works through middlemen and the whole show brings back memories of the war and what it could have been like for all those forgotten people in North Korea. We ended the tour with lunch at their restaurant which was superb. The experience is a must do in Seoul.

If you have to visit only one private sector gallery in Korea, this may be the one. Check the website so you know the exhibition schedule.  The restaurant and the cafe is also very good.
You can reserve a seat beforehand.

It is a gem of center of Seoul with nice selections all time.
You should visit here whenever they update the artist masterpieces.

title: 국토발전전시관
google_addr: 18 Jeongdong-gil, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: A well-designed theme museum. A perfect place for students majoring in planning, civic engineering, or geography. Although there are some factors for fun, it may not be sufficient to bring kids from a far distance. But, if you are interested in planning or Korea's development, it is one of the must go places in my opinion.

This is a good place to know about the efforts Korean people made to be a developed nation. Here 1st floor is for the reception and convenience. 2nd floor is for Future Homeland - Future Technology and Overseas Construction - Overseas Cooperation, this floor has a display of the world-famous constructions by Korean throw out the world. It has also the facility to take a photo with world-famous backgrounds, they call it Chroma-key Photo zone. 3rd floor is for the chronological display of transportation development, it has a chance to experience HEMU430X and V-World Map simulation. The 4th floor is for an exhibit of the national development plan.
It will be good to start from the 4th floor.

Very enjoyable museum with tons of interactive displays showing the incredible growth of Korea since independence. You can experience driving a plane or KTX train at the times shown in the picture. Surprisingly, an amazing place for kids/families to have fun and relax together. Added bonus- Dutch coffee from the cafe on the first floor is fantastic.
Cool museum that gives a sense of Korea’s develop narrative in recent decades. Close to the Seoul Museum of Art as well as many nice cafes and dining spots.

The museum is a very good starting point and is pivotal in understanding the systematic and planned development milestones Korea has gone through over the past decades. I recommend it for everyone to visit.

reviews.text:

title: 국회박물관
google_addr: 1 Uisadang-daero, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I came here on Sunday, but it was closed, so I’ll definitely come back next time.

Updated: I came here on Saturday and joined their free experience program inside for about 40 minutes, and I really enjoyed it.

I learned how elections in South Korea work with the help of a friendly tour guide, which I had booked online a few days before. This place is great for both children and adults to experience. They also have an exhibition hall where you can learn more about the history of the National Assembly.

I highly recommend this place to everyone. Just make sure to check the schedule before you come—it’s open from 10:00 to 1:00 on Saturdays, closed on Sundays, and mainly open on weekdays.

Tour is only in Korean so you'll need to understand Korean or have someone who can translate.
You need to go early to register but then you have to wait for the exact time for your tour to start.

A place with rows of Cherry blossoms trees lined up both sides of streets and many different kinds of flowers. It was a beautiful scenery at this place. There was a bike path and a safe place for you to enjoy the scenery and taking a walks along.

The building of the National Assembly Museum is just like any other government buildings. Here you can learn about Democratic history of Republic of South Korea. Staffs hardly speak english but there are Robots as tour guides and you can learn everything in detail. We did not book in advance to come here. We use the brochure that were given to us, and the 'Robots' to guide us around. It was fun and very educational.

It was established in 1998 as a commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the opening of the National Assembly of the Republic of Korea. It is a place where you can learn about the democratic history of the Republic of Korea.

title: 국회의사당
google_addr: 1 Uisadang-daero, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I didn’t know that this place was open to the public from the outside, because every time I passed by I always saw police officers.

This time I just walked in, and inside there is a small park and some statues that made the visit worthwhile. I’ll definitely come back here in the future.

Updated: This time, I had the chance to go inside for a guided tour program that lasted about 30 minutes in the main hall.

I booked it online a few days before my visit. There were many other people joining as well. I’m not sure if it was on a Saturday or not, but it was a bit noisy.

Still, learning about South Korea’s political system was very interesting, and I highly recommend this tour to everyone. I think it’s better to book on a weekend, because my weekday reservation was once canceled due to an unplanned meeting.

If you're interested in exploring some of the important political landmarks in Korea, I highly recommend visiting the National Assembly Building.

It's like the Korean version of Capitol Hill, where our lawmakers work.

The architecture is pretty cool, with a big blue dome that symbolizes the unity of the Korean people.

You can also book a guided tour to learn about Korean politics and even watch a session in progress if you're lucky.

It's a great way to get a deeper understanding of how Korea's democracy works, and the area around the building is really nice for a walk along the Han River.

Let me know if you want any help with planning your visit!

The National Assembly building is where members of the National Assembly discuss state affairs. It includes various buildings of the National Assembly, including the main conference hall, committee conference rooms, the Speaker's residence, the Members' Hall, the security building, and the vehicle maintenance depot. It is a stone building with 1 underground floor and 7 above-ground floors, and is the largest single parliamentary building in the East. It was completed in August 1975 after 6 years of construction, and is a modern building style with traditional Korean beauty. The 24 pillars surrounding the National Assembly building represent the diverse opinions of the people, and the dome roof symbolizes the essence of parliamentary democracy, where the people's opinions are discussed for and against and then come to a conclusion.

This is a beautiful building with lovely grounds! Sadly we we unable to tour inside due to time constraints, however it was still nice to walk the grounds. We even got to see a camera crew filming a scene from a K Drama!
Nice tour!  Didn't get much time to explore whole building. It's free tour. Just have to registered yourself or group in advance.

title: 궁산 땅굴 역사전시관
google_addr: 106 Yangcheon-ro 49-gil, Gangseo-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: 강서구 가양동의 작은 산인 궁산에 위치한 인공땅굴. 2008년에 우연히 발견되었고, 조사결과 일제강점기인 1940년대에 군사용 목적으로 일제가 주변의 주민들을 강제로 동원해서 굴착한 것이라고 밝혀졌다. 혹시라도 북한에서 뚫고 내려온 것이 아닐까하고 한 때는 걱정했다고 하니 이해도 된다. 근처의 김포공항까지 지하로 연결할 목적이었으나 일제가 패망하면서 미완성으로 남았다고 한다. 총 길이가 68미터에 이르고 높이가 2.7미터, 폭이 2.2미터로 갱차가 충분히 이동할수 있는 크기라고 한다. 2010년 중반부터 일반에 무료로 개방되었다고 한다. 나선형 계단을 따라 조금 내려가면 아주 작은 전시실이 있고 근무자가 간단한 설명을 해 준다. 땅굴은 실제로 들어갈 수는 없고 입구쪽에서 눈으로만 구경해야 한다. 땅굴과 굴착 당시의 상황, 그리고 당시의 역사에 대한 짧은 동영상도 시청할수 있다. 실제 수준에 비해서 장소의 이름이 좀 거창하게 지어진듯 하다.

비교적 최근인 2008년에 발견된 유적이에요. 태평양전쟁이 한창이던 1940년대, 일본이 굴착한 군용땅굴입니다. 주민들을 보국대로 삼아 강제 노역해 만들었다고 해요. 패망 후 잊혀졌고 한동안 무당이 거처했었다는 해설을 들을 수 있었습니다.

둘러보는데 5분이면 충분했어요. 길이는 68m의 땅굴이지만 낙석으로 인한 사고예방 차원에서 땅굴 안으로 들어갈 수는 없었습니다. 양천향교나 겸재정선미술관 들를 때 한번 들러보세요~

- 구암공원 광주바위 및 허가바위

발견된것은 비교적 최근이었고 그동안 무속인이 살았다고 한다.
내부 붕괴 위험이 있어서 안으로 들어가는 것은 하지 못한다.

지하로 내려가서 한번 보면 나올 수 있다.

title: 궁중문화축전

reviews.text:
Visited the palace as part of the tour. The whole palace complex is free to enter if you are wearing the traditional hanbok. The whole place is massive and you can spend half a day just looking around. The buildings don't look old or aged at all because most of original structures were destroyed by the japanese during the war but they still look cool.
If you want to look at the places where nobility used to live in this is the place to be.

A nice palace but not as spectacular as the Chinese ones. Smaller scale than the Chinese. However, it is still nice to come here dressed in traditional costumes to soak in the atmosphere. If you are lucky, you can get to witness the change of guard ceremonies. Just check the schedule before coming so you can watch it.

Need lots of walking. Place is huge, can easily spend 1/2 day.

If you wear a hanbok no need to pay entrance fee, other wise you will need to pay.

Went during mid Jan. Was cold, lake os frozen. There are lots of places to take pretty photos. Beautiful place.

Great place to learn about the heritage.

The palace was built in the 15th century during the Joseon Dynasty., but then burned down during the Japanese invasion in the 16th century, and reconstructed soon afterwards to serve as the main residence of the kings for the next 250 years. The layout of the palace and the surroundings follows the Confucian principles with gates, courts, and residential areas, as exemplified by the similar but much larger Forbidden City in Beijing. The palace had an important influence on Korean architecture and garden design, as can be seen when visiting Seoul's many other places.

A lovely palace, my mother in law recanted when she was a little girl she would skate on the water in front of the palace. I guess times change, and places change, despite the palace remaining, what you can do here also changes. It was a great cultural experience and majestic glimpse of a different world. It was captivating to just stop and reflect on these aspects.

title: 귀어귀촌 어촌관광 한마당
google_name: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
google_addr: 175 Sejong-daero, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: My trip started on a high at Sejong Theatre, where I watched the musical Phantom. The performance was absolutely stunning—the set, the music, the voices. For a couple of hours, I was so absorbed I didn’t even check my phone (which, let’s be honest, says a lot for a Gen Z like me). It felt like stepping into a different world, and I left with goosebumps.

My time exploring Sejong Plaza was spent enjoying the beautiful statue of Sejong the Great. There's many animations on the buildings, hidden alley restaurants that are ALL 10/10, and subway/public transportation hub.

The Sejong Center for the Performing Arts is an iconic performance venue located in Gwanghwamun, Seoul. For Korean artists, performing here is considered the ultimate honor, and it wouldn't be an exaggeration to call it the Carnegie Hall of Korea. While the facilities are somewhat dated and inconvenient, they are receiving positive feedback. It is conveniently located right next to Gwanghwamun Square, and it is also great for a walk after the performance. Making its own original performances like Ilmu(One Dance) is also a promising idea.

Exhibition
Masterpieces from the San Diego Museum of Art: "From the Renaissance to Impressionism"

Hey, let me share a quick thought with you.

If you ever find yourself near Gwanghwamun, take a moment to walk by the Sejong Center. And if you already have a ticket in hand, even better. You are about to step into one of Korea’s most meaningful performance halls.

Sejong Center has long been considered a symbol of Korean performing arts. When it opened in 1978, its pipe organ was the largest in Asia. Back in Europe, pipe organs were a way for cities to show their pride and prosperity, and Sejong Center carried that same spirit here in Seoul.

Sure, some people might say it is not the most modern venue anymore. And they would not be completely wrong. But this place holds memories. It has watched generations grow up, quietly standing its ground while the city changed around it. That kind of history matters.

Personally, I have spent some memorable nights here. I watched THE GREATEST: Thrill with Jeong Dong-ha and Sohyang in September 2023, Universal Ballet’s The Nutcracker in December 2023, and Chung Myung-Whun conducting Beethoven’s Ninth with the KBS Symphony at the end of 2025. Since it is a multipurpose hall, you might not always get the same powerful acoustics as a dedicated concert hall, especially for classical music. Still, the experience feels special every time.

Getting there is easy. Just hop on Seoul Subway Line 5 and get off at Gwanghwamun Station. One small thing to note, though. There is no traditional cloakroom. Instead, you will find unmanned lockers on the second floor. They work, but the touch screen can be a little tricky. Maybe it is just me getting older.

The box office is on the first floor, and there are kiosks if you already bought your ticket. You will also spot vending machines for water on each floor, which always comes in handy.

One last tip. The Grand Theater usually opens about two hours before the performance for security reasons, and audiences are allowed into the hall about thirty minutes before the show starts.

Take your time, soak it in, and enjoy the moment.

A very beautiful space.
Even though all the books are in Korean and foreigners can’t really read them, it’s still a perfect place to completely switch off and spend a relaxing, mind-empty afternoon ʕ•̫͡• ʔ•̫͡•ཻʕ•̫͡•ʔ•͓͡•ʔ

Really cool place in Seoul, located in a beautiful unmarked building on the edge of a residential neighborhood. We thought we might be lost when the taxi dropped us off because it looks like a fancy house— but after going up a little walkway and through the door, we discovered a wonder within!! Multi-story library reading room and bar with some of the finest graphic novels and books about illustration. For the entry fee we were given the option to purchase drinks or pay a flat fee. We ordered a few Mai Tais and some jelly beans which were delivered to a cute little comfy lounging spot we found upstairs. The whole place had the gentle murmur of a library but with a very relaxed vibe. Everyone was quietly enjoy books alone or in various small groups or couples and I really think you need at least 2-3 hours (if not longer) to make the most of this space. Once you get set up at a spot, you can wander around the place and select books to bring back to your table to read. The staff was just as unique and charming (and intriguing) as the books and architecture and they had a cool vinyl collection upstairs near the bar area. An app downloaded to your phone allows for ordering of drinks and inquiries into books. They did not have stock on hand of the books I read there that I would have liked to purchase, but I’m sure they could have ordered them for me had I been local. Don’t come here looking to party— it’s more of a temple dedicated to books and their inquisitive admirers. Highly recommend.

title: 기린성형외과
