reviews.text:
I decided to do double eyelid surgery at Girin because I wanted a more defined and refreshed eye appearance while still looking natural. It was something I had considered for a long time, and I felt this procedure would suit my facial features and boost my confidence.

I found Girin Clinic through online research and reviews while looking for a reliable clinic for double eyelid surgery. What stood out to me was the doctor’s experience and specialization, along with the clear and detailed consultation provided. The before-and-after photos gave me confidence, and communication with the staff was smooth and professional. The team was friendly, patient, and reassuring, which made me feel safe and comfortable. I also felt that the pricing was reasonable compared to other clinics offering similar procedures.
After the consultation with the doctor I felt confident to proceed immediately. The doctor explained the procedure clearly, addressed my concerns patiently, and made professional recommendations based on my eye condition. This gave me peace of mind and trust in the decision.
The recovery process went smoothly. In the first few days, there was some swelling and mild discomfort, which was expected. By day 3–4, the swelling gradually reduced, and by the 7th day, my eyes already looked much more natural. The clinic provided clear aftercare instructions, which helped the healing process.
I did not experience any major complications. Whenever I had questions during recovery, the staff responded promptly and professionally, which made me feel well supported throughout the healing period.

I got my Gyareum fat-dissolving injections and Onda lifting treatment on my stomach at Girin Plastic Surgery, a KIMA-affiliated clinic officially recognized by Korea’s Ministry of Health and Welfare.
Located in Gangnam, it’s super clean, easy to reach, and the staff made the whole process feel safe and professional. Both treatments were quick and almost painless, with only mild swelling after.
Highly recommend if you’re looking for a trustworthy clinic in Seoul!

It has now been about three months since my under-eye fat repositioning surgery at GIRIN, and I’m very happy with the final results. My eyes have fully healed, and the area looks smooth, refreshed, and natural. The dark circles that used to make me look tired are now barely noticeable, and the overall effect makes me look younger and more awake without changing my natural appearance.

The recovery process went exactly as the doctor explained, and I’m glad I followed their recommendations closely. GIRIN’s English support team has continued to be attentive, checking in through WhatsApp and making sure everything is going well even after I returned home. Their consistent communication and care really stand out and made the entire experience worry-free.

Overall, I’m extremely satisfied with the results and the professionalism of the GIRIN team. My eyes look great, I feel more confident, and I would definitely return to GIRIN again in the future for any other procedures.

I found Girin while researching arm liposuction in Seoul and comparing multiple clinics. I read a lot of reviews and carefully checked before-and-after photos. What stood out to me was their focus on natural-looking body contouring results and the detailed consultations mentioned by other patients.

During my consultation, everything was explained clearly including realistic expectations, swelling, downtime, and recovery discomfort. I appreciated that Dr. Lee Jong Ho was straightforward and did not overpromise results. The staff were professional, and communication was smooth, which made the process less stressful as a foreign patient. The pricing was also in line with other reputable clinics I researched.

My upper arms have always been an area that didn’t slim down proportionally, even when I lost weight. I wanted a more refined and balanced silhouette, especially in sleeveless clothing. After thinking about it for a long time, I decided liposuction was the right solution rather than continuing to try to spot-reduce through diet or exercise.

After the consultation with Dr. Lee Jong Ho, I felt confident moving forward. I didn’t feel pressured, just informed. On surgery day, the team was organized and reassuring. I was nervous, but the staff made the process feel structured and professional from start to finish.

For the Healing Process, the first 1–2 days were the most uncomfortable. I experienced significant soreness (similar to intense muscle soreness), swelling, tightness, and limited arm mobility. It was difficult to lift my arms high enough to wash my face or brush my hair at first.

By around day 3–4, the pain became more manageable, although swelling and itching increased as healing progressed. I wore my compression garment consistently and followed post-op instructions carefully.

By day 7, mobility improved gradually, but there was still visible swelling which I understand is completely normal at this stage. Recovery requires patience.

For Complications & Support, I did not experience any major complications. I did have concerns about swelling and itching in the first few days, but the clinic responded quickly and reassured me that my symptoms were part of normal healing. Their responsiveness helped reduce anxiety during recovery.

My Double jaw surgery experience at Girin:
I had a case of bimaxillary protrusion and invisalign treatments at dentist just made my gummy smile worst(really affected my confidence)
It was my dentist who suggested for such cases jaw surgery is final solution and i began researching a lot on this and finally came up with Girin based on reviews and video of such cases in youtube and insta(my Korean friend also did some review checks on Girin and said it looked trustworthy).
It wasn’t an easy decision to make as its a major surgery and its VERY important to choose a doctor you have confidence on. I went ahead with consultation.

The surgery went well but the first week is the worst after such a major operation. Its more about discomfort and difficulty eating etc but not pain as you are given pain killers. For 3 months you are on soft food diet but i got the result i wanted❤️my main source of insecurity got fixed and i couldn’t be happier about this decision. My smile looks normal and good now not the heavy gummy smile with protruding front face. Also all sensations on lips and face have fully returned ❤️After 3 months now i can eat normally and i like to thank Girin for all the support during my 3 weeks stay and specially to Dr. Yoon 🙏🏻

finally 6 months!

reviews.text: Visiting the 통감관저터, 기억의 터 was a profound experience. The memorial features an upside-down statue of Hayashi Gonsuke, commemorating his role in the Eulsa Treaty and the annexation of Korea. The statue was originally erected by the Japanese emperor and later inverted to mark the 70th anniversary of Korean independence. The site offers a powerful reflection on this dark chapter of history, though it does not focus much on the comfort women. It provides a solemn space for remembrance and is good to visit for those seeking to learn more about Korea's history.

reviews.text:
Gingorangro Valley (긴고랑 계곡) وادي جينجورانجرو

- "Gingorang-ro Valley" (긴고랑로 계곡) is a valley located in South Korea. The name "긴고랑로" translates to "Long Ditch Road" in English. This valley is known for its scenic beauty and natural landscapes, often featuring hiking trails, streams, and lush greenery. It is a popular destination for outdoor activities such as hiking, picnicking, and nature walks. The specific details and features of the valley can vary, so it would be useful to refer to local guides or tourist information for more precise descriptions.

- It's located between  용마산 (Youngma mountain) and 야차산 (Yacha mountain).

- It's following 광진고시gwangjingu city and very close to Sejong university.

- It has very beautiful view from the top and you can see a good part of Seoul.

- There is a free badminton  🏸 courts with 8 slots: 6 for double teams memand 2 for single teams.

- You can enjoy the badminton 🏸, play with valley  water, do hiking 🚶‍♀️

وادي جينجورانجرو (긴고랑 계곡)

- وادي "جينجورانج-رو" (긴고랑로 계곡) هو وادٍ يقع في كوريا الجنوبية. يُترجم الاسم "긴고랑로" إلى "طريق الخندق الطويل" باللغة الإنجليزية. يُعرف هذا الوادي بجماله الطبيعي ومناظره الخلابة، وغالبًا ما يحتوي على مسارات للمشي، وجداول مائية، وخضرة وافرة. إنه وجهة شهيرة للأنشطة الخارجية مثل المشي لمسافات طويلة، والتنزه، والتجوال في الطبيعة. يمكن أن تختلف التفاصيل والميزات المحددة للوادي، لذا سيكون من المفيد الرجوع إلى الأدلة المحلية أو معلومات السياح للحصول على أوصاف أكثر دقة.

- يقع الوادي بين جبل يونغما (용마산) وجبل ياكا (야차산).

- يتبع مدينة غوانجينجو (광진고시) وهو قريب جدًا من جامعة سيجونج.

- يتمتع بإطلالة جميلة جدًا من الأعلى، حيث يمكنك رؤية جزء كبير من سيول.

- يوجد به ملاعب تنس الريشة المجانية 🏸 مع 8 مسارات: 6 للفرق المزدوجة و 2 للفرق الفردية.

- يمكنك الاستمتاع بتنس الريشة 🏸، واللعب بالمياه في الوادي، وممارسة رياضة المشي لمسافات طويلة 🚶‍♀️.

reviews.text:
The Kim Dae-Jung Library is more than just a library – it’s a historical memorial and museum that honors the life and legacy of former President Kim Dae-Jung. Rather than shelves of books, you’ll find powerful exhibitions showcasing his journey through democracy, imprisonment, the Nobel Peace Prize, and his tireless efforts for peace and human rights.

The space is well-organized and quiet, ideal for reflection. While it’s part of Yonsei University, the atmosphere feels more like a presidential memorial hall or a modern history museum. Admission is free of charge, but note that group visits (10 or more people) require a reservation in advance via email or their website.

The museum is open on weekdays only (10:00 AM to 5:00 PM) and is closed on weekends and public holidays, so plan accordingly. It’s easily accessible on foot from Hongik University Station (Exit 6 or 7) or Sinchon Station (Exit 8).

Highly recommended for anyone interested in Korea’s modern history, democracy, or global peace movements.

title: 남산 팔각정

reviews.text: Namsan Palgakjeong is a peaceful retreat with stunning views of Seoul’s skyline. The octagonal pavilion’s intricate design adds a touch of tradition amidst the city buzz. While it can get busy, it’s a great spot to catch your breath after a hike or cable car ride. Stay for sunset if you can—the blend of colors over the city is truly unforgettable and worth the visit.

Its another 🆓 spot in same vicinity as namsan tower.

We came here during late afternoon early evening on a pretty sunny day. It was a nice spot to sit down and cool off and take in the views and people watch.

Its visually pleasing and wasnt crowded either given that it was pretty busy otherwise at the base of namsan.

Hope to see it during night time views whenever i visit next. (Hopefully soon)

It is so beautiful. I never expected there was a traditional resting zone over here. That was cool. This traditional zone is called the Octagonal Pavilion. The name sounds so cool too. There are many people sitting over there at that time. I guarantee I will come here again in the future.

Originally known as Unamjeong Pavilion, the pavilion was built in 1959 to commemorate Rhee Syngman. It was demolished by the 4.19 movement in 1960 and was rebuilt on November 11, 1968.

A great place to take in the culture and history of Namsan mountain.
Great spot to take pictures of the city without spending the hefty amounts of money to get to the top of the Tower. The view is pretty unobstructed here already.

reviews.text: This beautiful, quiet park is the perfect place to escape the noisy city. There’s so many different paths and places to sit and relax. It’s also never very busy!

Quiet and beautiful place with plenty of greenery. The traditional Korean atmosphere feels very authentic and calming. The fact that entry is completely free makes it even more impressive. It is perfect for a short visit, and a simple thirty minute walk through the park already feels rewarding. I highly recommend stopping by if you are in the area.

Namsagol Park is a hidden gem for those who want to escape the hustle and bustle of the city. With its serene atmosphere and picturesque scenery, it's the perfect place to take a leisurely stroll. Although it's not a well-known tourist spot, it's a popular destination for locals who want to unwind and relax. On a sunny day, the park comes alive with vibrant colors and the sound of nature. I highly recommend visiting Namsagol Park if you're looking for a peaceful retreat in the middle of the city.
This is a nice place to end your tour after Hanok Village. Lots of instagrammable corners left and right. You can completely relax after walking down the historical Hanok village.
Great place to see cherry blossoms in the spring! A nice park with a fairly unique layout and a hanok village inside.

title: 남산골한옥마을
google_addr: 28 Toegye-ro 34-gil, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
A truly peaceful and beautiful place where time feels slower. From here, you can even see the Seoul Tower, which makes the view even more special.

I visited early in the morning, and it was the best decision — there were hardly five people around. The ambiance was extremely calm and quiet. After 9 AM, the crowd slowly starts coming in, so going early is highly recommended to experience the serenity.

Walking inside and around every corner of the village feels refreshing and soothing. Each side has its own charm, with traditional houses, open spaces, and nature coming together so beautifully.

The staff members were very kind and welcoming, adding warmth to the overall experience. This is a perfect place to walk slowly, explore every part of the village, and truly enjoy a peaceful moment in the city.

~throw back to mid of November 2025~

If you love Korean culture and tradition, this is a great place to visit.
The entire area isn’t very large, and I spent about 1.5 hours leisurely walking around, exploring, and taking photos.

We stumbled upon this curious place almost by accident.

In fact, the village is only relatively historical. On the one hand, houses from the Joseon dynasty era were brought here from all over the city. On the other hand, there was no such village here before, it was created artificially.

So, it is a collection of many old buildings gathered in one place, allowing visitors to explore a concentrated snapshot of architecture from a bygone era.

I am no expert in architecture, so I simply enjoyed wandering around the village, looking at the houses, and trying to imagine what life was like in a traditional Korean village.

The place is beautiful and not overly crowded with tourists.

Surrounding the village, just like near many other attractions, are only modern buildings, which somewhat detracts from the historical ambiance -)

It is an interesting place where you can enjoy a leisurely walk and admire the old houses.

This sight is so pretty, never crowded in any of the times I have visited it, with gorgeous views of Namsan tower. I don't get the hullabaloo in the residential Bukchon Hanok Village where tourists get on the nerves of the locals, when this one fullfils the purpose better.

Beautiful scenery for a nice walk, to read a book, or to take amazing photos. Entry was free. Traditional Hanok houses, mini forest trails, water features, monuments, views of Namsan and the Seoul Tower all in one spot.

title: 남산공원(서울)
google_addr: 231 Samil-daero, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
N Seoul Tower is one of the best places to enjoy a full panoramic view of Seoul. From the observation deck, you can see the Han River, modern skyscrapers, and the entire city spread out below, especially beautiful at sunset and at night when the city lights come on.

The area around the tower is clean and well organized, with many photo spots, the famous love locks area, and cafés to relax. The cable car is convenient, but walking up the mountain is also a great option if you enjoy nature and fresh air.

The staff are friendly and the signs are clear, making it easy for visitors to get around. This is a must-visit place in Seoul, perfect for couples, families, and anyone who wants to experience the romantic atmosphere of the city.

We came in winter and it was a cold cloudy dark windy day. It was depressingly brown so this affected my review

This is the lower area of Namsam Tower and it didn't feel like a park

The cable car to the top was not operating due to high winds and it was a bit to slippery to hike up
So we did not get to see the tower part which is supposed to be spectacular.
Very nice park in the 명동 area of Seoul. I enjoyed another hike after eating lunch close by. Very scenic with nice fall breeze on a Monday afternoon. Pretty views everywhere and it wasn’t too crowded.

I was fortunate to make the long walk (around 5km), easy to west, twice in the last week. Up from the east part, starting at Dongguk University Station and Jangchungdan Park up through Seoul Namsan Park to the tower and then down to Myeong-dong on the west site. It's strikingly beautiful a great climb, some steps are numbered, between those and the ones you don't count I imagine it's the equivalent to about 1,000 steps up the mountain and there are also a few steeper inclines. The steps, paths and roads are in excellent condition, everything is so clean and well signposted in many languages. You can also use N aver Maps to get you there.

The walk from Dongguk University Station to the base of Namsan Seoul Tower covers approximately 2.2 miles (3.6 km) with an elevation gain of about 797 feet (243 meters).

This route is one of the most rewarding ways to reach Namsan Tower, especially if you're seeking a blend of urban forest, cultural landmarks, and a bit of cardio. If you're up for it, you can extend your walk along the Namsan Trail network, which spans nearly 8 km across the mountain.

Outstanding urban park perfect for walking, running, and cycling! Features multiple trails and beautiful paved, hilly roads with stunning viewpoints. Well-maintained with convenient public facilities. The place comes alive at 5am with enthusiastic athletes - such great energy! Plenty of shaded areas to rest. A true urban gem!

title: 남산국치길
google_addr: 5-22 Juja-dong, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Cool park. Much colonial history. Smallish and easy to walk around. Credit to the city because there was nothing here for years.

Nice place for a leisure walk, and we were able to take our father in law who was in a wheelchair.  They have tracks in the middle of the road for those with impaired vision which I thought was very thoughtful
중앙정보부라는 아픈 현대사와 일제 시대의 흔적까지 있는 장소가 공원으로 정비되어 있었습니다. 기억6이라는 전시장소가 있었는데, 아쉽게도 2024년 9월부터 현재(2025년 3월)까지 남산 곤도라 설치 관계로 휴관중이었습니다. 언제 다시 개장할지는 안적혀있네요.

충무로 세종호텔 정면 남산에 위치한 작은 공원입니다.
규모는 그리 크지는 않지만 점심 때 힐링 코스로 좋습니다.
저는 가끔 가는 편입니다.

위치상 찾기가 쉽진 않지만 사람 없어서 더 좋습니다 .
역사적 의미를 알기 쉽게 설명해 놓은 점이 좋았습니다. 산책하기에도 좋은 도심 속 공원입니다.

title: 남산서울타워
google_addr: 105 Namsangongwon-gil, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Lots of people haha. Exit queue line very very long. However I enjoy the experience on the top observation viewing. The sunset view is stunning. The climbing is really a hell . As we didn’t board any bus up . But five star for the facilities:)

Hiking up Namsan can be a bit challenging because the path is quite steep. Even though I’m in my 30s, I still found myself catching my breath while walking up. My friend suggested a funny trick,walking up while facing slightly backward,which actually made the climb feel a little easier.

Despite the steep hike, the experience is worth it. The view from Namsan is beautiful, the air is cool, and the atmosphere feels very romantic. It’s a great place to enjoy the scenery, take photos, and spend time with someone special.

Overall, Namsan is a lovely spot to visit, especially for couples and lovers who want a romantic walk with a wonderful view.

The iconic N Seoul Tower and definitely a must visit when you are in Seoul. It is one of those places you really have to see at least once. The view from the top is amazing and gives you a great look over the city, especially at night when everything is lit up. There are lots of activities around the area, places to walk, take photos, and just enjoy the atmosphere. It is a good spot to spend a few hours and really take in the experience. A very memorable and iconic part of Seoul.

I hiked up to Seoul North Tower and walked all 1,000 stairs to the top. The trail is beautiful with all the fall colors and the air feels so fresh. Someone even marked the stair count along the way, which kept me going. I went up for the 5:15 sunset and I was definitely ambitious because I barely made it on time. The view over Seoul is absolutely breathtaking.

The stairs are very well maintained and there are little resting spots every few minutes. At the top there is a plaza, a 7-Eleven, and a restaurant. After watching the sunset it got dark really fast, and that’s when I realized I couldn’t get an Uber to come up. I panicked a bit because the only way down was by bus and I had no money on my T-money card. I managed to reload it at the 7-Eleven and just hopped on the first bus going down the mountain. When it gets dark there, it is really dark.

What an adventure. It was an amazing hike and I highly recommend it. Just make sure your T-money card has enough balance if you stay late! 😅

Sooo beautiful 😍 ! I recommand.
Nevertheless, take a great shoes and little water because the clim it's something. You can do it 💪🏾, I promise !  Take deep breath and it's perfect. You don't regret 😊

reviews.text: Tickets were given to us from the Lotte Hotel we were staying.  I don't think we would have gone  hadn't provided free tickets.  However,  the experience was good as you do get nice 360 degree panoramic views of the city made famous in many K-dramas. Terrific - this is a great way to reach Namsan Tower. Whilst the ticket price is about 12,000 won (single) or 15,000 (return) it is absolutely worth it. The view up and back is great. It can get quite busy so be prepared for a little bit of a wait - but still, this is highly recommended.

I took 30 minutes on Sunday 11am. to wait for the cablw car. However, It took only 3-5 minutes to go up. A little too pricey. We can see the view of seoul city. The ambience somehow impressive. It's worth going up for the 1st timer that visit seoul

title: 낮이 좋아? 밤이 좋아? 서울의 주경, 야경 여행코스
google_addr: 68-1 Yeouigongwon-ro, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Very interesting concept which allows customers to take hot air balloon in the city, even though the hot air balloon rises and falls without "flying" around.
It is located in the park near IFC mall and a 15min ride for us to take.
It is a pity when we took the ride, the visibility was very poor on that day.
Safety briefing was conducted before the ride and it is recommended to purchase the tickets in advance.

Loved this! I had tried to do this last year but there wasn't availability as it was fairly new so the fact that you can now book online makes things so much easier! I thoroughly enjoyed my visit at sunset and the view is amazing. Went again a few nights later as only 1 space on my previous ride and I wanted to go with my daughter - this time we went at 8pm. The view is spectacular at night 😍 the set up is really well organised and the staff are friendly and helpful. Looking forward to doing this again next time I visit Seoul.

This was the first time we took a tethered helium balloon. We chose to come in the evening at 5pm. The ground staff were helpful; making sure that we filled up the necessary documents correctly. The "pilots" were cheerful and made sure that we were evenly spread before taking off. The evening sky was  colorful and lovely. The "ride" was smooth. When the balloon slowly escalated, we were treated to breath-taking views. The balloon was so stable that taking photos was not difficult at all. Strongly recommend this fun memorable activity.

This is such a fun way to see Seoul from a completely different perspective than you’d get at Seoul N Tower or Lotte World Tower. We reserved our tickets online in advance (recommended, since space is limited), but you can also buy them on site.

After a short safety video and signing the consent form, you’re lifted 426 feet into the air, and it really does feel high up! The views were spectacular, and it gave me a new appreciation for just how beautiful Seoul is. The ride itself is for 15 minutes but you will want to budget about an hour end to end. Yeouido, where this is located, is also a lovely area to explore.

Afterwards, you can stop by The Hyundai Seoul nearby to stroll around or grab a bite to eat. If you want to experience Seoul from a true bird’s-eye view, I definitely recommend trying this.
Loved the experience! With a very reasonable price, you get to rise up to as high as skyscrapers. The whole trip is about 15 minutes. Totally worth it.

title: 내를건너서숲으로도서관

reviews.text:
내를 건너서 숲으로 도서관은 2018년 6월 21일에 개관한 은평구립의 도서관입니다. 일제강점기의 저항 시인이자 독립운동가인 윤동주의 탄생 100주년을 기념하기위해 만들어진 도서관입니다. '내를 건너서 숲으로' 라는 명칭은 시인 윤동주의 '새로운 길'에 나오는 시어를 인용한 것입니다. 참고로 도서관 건물 인근에는 윤동주 시인의 모교인 숭실고등학교가 위치해 있습니다.

만들어진 지 얼마 되지 않은 도서관인 만큼 전반적인 시설들은 굉장히 신선하고 깔끔합니다. 외관이나 내부 시설이나 일반적인 도서관들과는 다른 독특한 디자인이 색다릅니다. 아기자기한 소품들로 꾸며진 공간도 많이 있고 2층에는 윤동주 시인의 일대기를 알 수 있는 전시홀도 설치되어 있었습니다.

칸막이가 있는 독서용 열람실은 없었지만 학습을 위한 목적으로 와도 부족함이 없는 시설입니다. 대부분 흰색을 위주로 만든 테마 덕에 신선하고 아득한 분위기를 느끼며 머물기에 좋습니다. 어린이/유아자료실은 좀 협소한 편이였지만 그만큼 아득해서 좋습니다.

윤동주 시인을 기리기 위해 만들어지고 그에 맞춰 만들어진 도서관 의 디자인 또한 상당히 개성적이고 남달랐습니다. 은평구 지역으로 여행을 온다면 한 번쯤은 방문해볼만한 가치가 충분한 도서관입니다.
조용하고 깨끗한 도서관입니다. 2층에는 윤봉주 시인 전시장도 있습니다. 주차장은 협소한 편이라서 차는 안 가지고 가는 것을 추천합니다.

reviews.text:
I had the best and freshest seafood here at a remarkably reasonable price. A tip: know what you want and order it directly, otherwise the friendly ahjumma and ahjussi might enthusiastically try to offer you everything they have!

The sashimi and crab were absolutely to die for—incredibly fresh, with a natural sweetness that really shone through. An outstanding meal.

I have mixed feelings about this place. On one hand the seafood is top notch but just the idea that you know prices will be hiked up makes one think if we are getting fleeced.

That said it is competitive so I woke recommend walking around to get a feel of the prices before deciding. Once you’ve settled the purchase of the items, they’ll bring you up to the affiliated restaurant so they can cook it.

The meal after is pretty good, as usual! Fresh king crab and good sashimi. Always order the  ramyeon and fried rice. Overall, it was v delish. But you just gotta go through the buying process first!

Noryangjin Fish Market is a place I occasionally visit for sashimi. It's been a while since I last visited, and it's much cleaner than before, with parking much easier. And there's almost no solicitation like there used to be, so I can walk around comfortably, browse, and get my sashimi. It's not close, but there are few places in Seoul where you can get sashimi at such a good price. I'll have to come back often whenever I crave sashimi.

I had a positive experience here as a tourist. Lots of the stalls were trying to get us to buy their stuff which is expected. Hard to walk around without someone trying to get you to buy their stuff. Most stalls seemed to sell the same stuff. The people selling just fish in the back weren’t as pushy and helped us find someone selling eel which was all the way in the back. The stall we went to the lady was nice and picked out a crab for me. I believe it was 100000 won. She also gave me clams for service as well. Then a man took us to the second floor restaurant which steamed the crab and bbq our eel. We even got the crab head fried rice. I don’t remember the price for cooking but I don’t think it was a lot like some people said they charge tourists. Overall a great experience for a seafood lover.

Noryangjin Fish Market is huge! You could easily spend hours walking from stall to stall comparing prices! Instead, we decided to go with one stall we felt comfortable with (and with no language barrier). To our surprise, many of the sellers could speak Chinese quite well, which made communication much easier!

There are so many seafood choices that you’ll be spoiled for options but since we had only 3 pax, we kept it simple and got king crab, abalone, prawns, and the friendly stall lady even added some shellfish for free ☺️☺️☺️
We spent around SGD $300+ for all our seafood (the crab was slightly over 2kg).

After payment, we were led to the 2nd floor restaurants where they cook your seafood the way you like it. We also ordered a few extra dishes there, which came up to about SGD $200 including cooking fees.

Everything was fresh, delicious, and the whole experience was so enjoyable!

Definitely a must-visit spot ☺️

reviews.text: Decent range of craft beer brewed in house. Upstairs, downstairs, and outside seating. Take away beers also available.

This place has high aspirations.  A brewpub in North Seoul?? Yes please!  But it falls so short.

If you're coming for the food, you've made a big mistake.  Basic but expensive. Your best bet is the French fries, but for prices North of 13,000, just go to your local 봉구비어.

You've probably come here for the beer. And you're excited. You've got the right to be!  Unfortunately the beer, though it seems like it's made on site, is very underwhelming.  The hazy ipa was without haze (lacking dry hops?) and tasted something like ARKs 광화문 Ale.  The signature beer, the cherry blossom lager, amazingly, was about as bland as a can of Fitz: lacking any mouthfeel, and not a hint of hops.

I really wanted to like this place. I did!  As a local of North Seoul, I was so excited for a craft beer joint that I could rely on.  Instead I'll stick to a 4 for 10.
Very nice typical craft brewery atmosphere. Friendly but slow service. Inconsistent pours, but a nice red ale available. Food looked very 'ajosshi beer pub' style, although we didnt sample any.

reviews.text:
I am a foreign patient from Australia, and I came to Seoul in February 2026 for breast augmentation. I interviewed three different clinics, and Note PS was my top choice—and the best choice I’ve ever made. This is also the clinic that my travel agent highly recommended. The clinic setting is very laid-back, calming, and professionally set up. The consultants, management team, and in-house translator went above and beyond. Dr Kwon was my surgeon, and he is very skilful at what he does. The fact that he is highly experienced with revision surgery is a bonus, so I can rely on just one surgeon.

Despite this being my first cosmetic surgery, the process was seamless. Recovery for me was much easier than what I had heard others experience. The results looked amazing from day one. I am now almost a month post-op and can do most things easily without any restrictions, and the implants have become much softer. Highly recommend!!!

I chose Note Plastic Surgery through a recommendation from Soomin at Freqty Agency, and I’m very happy with my experience. The entire process was smooth and well-organized, and the staff at the clinic were kind, professional, and attentive.

It has been one month since my procedure, and I’m already pleased with the results. The doctors addressed all my concerns, and I felt supported and well-informed from consultation to aftercare.

I’m grateful to both Note Plastic Surgery and Soomin for guiding me through this journey, and I would confidently recommend them to others.

This was my first plastic surgery and also my first solo trip to South Korea, so choosing the right clinic was really important to me. I’m really glad I chose Note Plastic Surgery.

Dr. Yoo (facial contouring) and Dr. Lee (rhinoplasty + platysmaplasty) were amazing — incredibly skilled, patient, and reassuring throughout the whole process. They really listened to my goals, and gave honest advice

I am now one month post op and very happy with the results so far! The neck/jaw area hasn’t changed much yet, but I know it takes time. The whole team was professional, organised and attentive. I’d definitely recommend Note Plastic Surgery to anyone thinking about facial surgery in Korea.

I was referred to Note Plastic Surgery by a friend, and I’m so glad I chose them for my surgeries. I’ve always been self-conscious about my jawline and nose and wanted a slimmer, more balanced look.

Traveling alone to Korea made me a bit nervous, especially about communicating in a language I’m not fluent in. But the staff and translator were amazing. They made everything easy and stress-free.

Dr. Yoo (Facial Contouring + Zygoma Reduction) and Dr. Lee (Rhinoplasty) really listened to my concerns and gave honest, thoughtful advice about what would suit my face best. They were patient, kind, and explained every step clearly. Even on surgery day, they took time to reassure me and made me feel completely safe.

It’s now been four months since my surgery, and while I’m still healing, I’m happy with how everything is turning out.

Following a friend's recommendation, I chose Note Plastic Surgery for my under-eye fat repositioning (눈밑지방) with fat grafting, and my experience was exceptional.

From the welcoming consultation where the doctor, interpreter, and consultant ensured my goals were met, to the streamlined surgery day, everything was handled with detail and care. Dr. Lee was reassuring and clearly explained the procedure (which involved fat transfer from my side under anesthesia).

The post-surgery care was top-notch. Minseon and Annette were wonderful, thoroughly explaining medications. The team even arranged for pumpkin juice (호박주스) and porridge (죽) to be delivered to my accommodation, and provided transportation to and from the clinic, which was a huge help.

Recovery was just as Dr. Lee predicted: slight puffiness at week one, and by week two or three, my under-eye darkness was gone! I look and feel incredibly refreshed.

I highly recommend Note Plastic Surgery for their professionalism, outstanding care, and amazing results.

google_addr: 173 Dongho-ro 17-gil, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: One of my favorite libraries in Seoul
멋진공간이라 또 오고 싶은곳이였어요. 아이들 공간은 좋은데 오픈되어있어 유아들이 있기에는 좀 불편해 아쉬웠어요. 도서관에 아이들 유아들 공간이 많이 생기면 좋겠어요~

다산성곽도서관은 2021년 5월에 개관한 중구 구립 도서관입니다. 이름대로 서울성곽길 외곽쪽에 위치해 있고, 주변보다 지대가 높은 곳에 있어서 야외좌석에서 서울시의 전경을 내다볼 수 있을 정도로 전망이 좋습니다. 건물 외관상으로도 성곽길과 어울리게 한옥스타일로 만든 점도 좋습니다.

규모는 총 3층으로, 3층 문학자료실, 2층 일반자료실, 1층 유아어린이자료실과 야외테리스로 구성되어 있습니다. 도서관 시설 자체는 굉장히 작은 편이지만 좁은 공간속에 만들어진 이색적인 인테리어 덕분에 아득하고 쾌적하게 머물다 갈 수 있습니다. 게다가 '더마실카페' 라는 이름의 카페도 운영하고 있습니다.

이 도서관의 유일한 단점은 접근성입니다. 제일 가까운 버티고개역부터 도보로 600m정도 떨어져 있는데, 상당한 오르내리막 경사가 있어서 근방 주민들이 아니고선 외지에서 이용하러 오기에는 어려운 접근성을 가지고 있습니다. 그래도 나름 개성있는 도서관이라서 한번쯤은 구경해 볼 만한 도서관입니다.

운영시간은 매일 오전 9시부터 밤 10시까지 꽤 길게 운영하는 편이며, 매주 월요일은 휴무일입니다.

아기자기하고 운치있는 도서관을 찾는다면 방문을 권하고싶다.

한 줄로 표현한 것과 같이 도서관에서 수용할 수 있는 인원이 많은 것은 아니다. 그럼에도 꽤나 매력적인 장소라는 것은 부인하기 힘들다.

reviews.text: I travelled from the US to go to Dasipium specifically. I had researched so many other clinics in Gangnam and I knew that Dr Kwak was the surgeon I wanted to get a facelift with. His before and afters and documentation of the healing process on his patients was so impressive I contacted them and sent photos and videos on my face and I received some recommendations on what I would need to achieve the results I was looking for. The pricing was much more affordable than anything in the United States too. It was an adventure! Plastic surgery is so common there that I didn’t feel embarrassed walking around with bandages and swelling. I’m still in the healing process but so far I’m happy with my results! I highly recommend this clinic and Dr Kwak. Dr Kwak and his entire staff were awesome. Very kind and helpful I can’t say enough good things about my experience. The aftercare was top notch and I saw the doctor almost every single day after my surgery until I left. I was there about 2 weeks total.

I just came back from Korea where I had my facelift at Dasipium in Gangnam, and honestly, I’m so glad I did it. I’m 50 and wasn’t looking for anything drastic, just wanted to look a little more refreshed, and Dr. Kwak completely nailed it.

The clinic is spotless, super welcoming, and having their own translator made things stress free. Surgery and recovery were way easier than I expected, and I even got to use their oxygen chamber which I think sped everything up.

I’m only three weeks out and already love how natural everything looks. Couldn’t recommend them enough!

PLEASE , PLEASE PLEASE 🙏 do your research thoroughly!
And be aware of this Clinic!!!!
I failed to do mine and I had a massive disappointment.
I have contacted Dasipium online at the end of February and have enquired about virtual consultation, however that didn't happen. A message was sent with number of suggested procedures and the price.
The protocol was established and now I was waiting for either video call, ZOOM, TEAMS or face to face appointment.
Nither of this happened ,unfortunately and 2 days prior the surgery,the doctor has added one more procedure,which will change the shape of my eyes ..irreversibley. I was put into an impossible situation just 48 hours prior to the date of the surgery to pick and choose like I'm in Starbucks ( decaf or normal ,late or cappuccino, suger or no sugar)
But this time only was my face and I was Infront of impossible task to choose either to do the extended lower blepperoplatry but with canthopexy ( change the shape due to secure of the muscles to avoid ectropium) or not to get it at all and don't get the best result only 30% improvement.

Bare in mind that there are options. ( I have learned that through research and asking other sergeants) Don't forget that there over 7850 clinic in Seoul.
But I wasn't given any other options!

My heart was jumping and racing like a loudspeaker on New year's Eve on Times square in NYC .

The clinic already had my deposit and they were rushing me to make up my mind.
Noone can make such a decision!
From the star I felt truly pushed , sending a deposit in a rush securing a date ,lack of any effort to see me face to face and avoid this utter shock of a change in the protocol,lack of understanding and professional consideration for the patient. How can you not invite the patient who has already paid upfront 1.650 000 ml and is traveling nearby 15 hours. For 8 days prior they didn't find time to accommodate me ,so the doctor to avoid this massive change and change of heart due to poor organisation,lack of smooth communication, apsolutly no skills of comfort and courage to the patient. I felt like part of a industry and Money making machine. There is no sign of understanding of the emotional stress and state of the patient, their vulnerability. The emotional intelligence of the team of Dasipium with the leading role of the Doctor Kwak is non existent.
Further more I understood that I will not be staying even one night,and I would not be given any meals ( after fasting 8 hours at least) ,I'll be sent home after a 6/7 hours of operation with the tubes in a taxi and no nurse around and find my way back the next day for post op service either by taxi or public transport.
I have realised that there is no anastesiologost on side and Dr.Kwak is taking this responsibility,there is no emergency car in case something unexpected happens with me.
So at the end I cancelled the operation and despite the fact that it was entirely the clinic mistake of 1. Not organising face to face appointment as soon I have told them I'm available (8days prior)
2.Chaning the protocol last minute and left me discombobulated. 3 Kept my money unscrupulously and did not offer any other procedure for the massive mess they have created.
Disappointed is a understatement.!
It was totally and utterly unprofessional,greedy and unhumain what Dasipium did!

Not only I would not recommend it but if I have to put a banner in the air I would have written:
Stay away from Dasipium!

I have never felt so rushed ,pushed and ask to compromise with my face !
That experience of humiliation will stay with me forever!
Avoid them at all cost !

52 year old Caucasian male. Did lots of research online before choosing Dasipium. No doubts beforehand, and no regrets after. Dr. Kwak and his team of nurses, helpers, and translator Jude were extremely helpful, efficient, and attentive from the time I booked 6 months ago until my surgery a couple of days ago. Dr. Kwak didn't push anything on me, and explained the pros and cons of every option before letting me think and choose. I am absolutely satisfied with my early results and look forward to seeing improvements as the days go by.

As an international traveler that took lots of time and effort to find the right clinic, Dasipium was the right choice for me.  I am extremely happy with my surgery outcome. Post-op care is fantastic. A great overall experience for me.

reviews.text:
Mixture of good to desirable items on wnd floors in half of the proud vendors/ collectors themselves. Then, there are souless seller who put in mass produced knock-off antique repros from China and copycat paintings from South Asia. The latter are the one who will discourage people to come and cobfidently buy authentic Korean heritage pieces.

I don't think I will dig this place much as they are retailers with overpriced retail prices for not superior quality pieces but they have put the popular items in good conditions. Not so much of unique sides. But you will still meet a few genuine collector/ vendors on 2nd floor who you will befriend with during your visit. They share their passion for the antiquity and history of Korea and the neighboring countries that will humble you.

Just stay away from  tourist stores. I just can't believe some crass Korean visitors fall for these tasteless water color or oil paintings from South Asia with fancy modern frames, or, massive granite carvings from China with Korean subjects, that was never authentically Korean scale at any rate. Shame on them both.

title: 대림중앙시장
google_addr: 21 Digital-ro 37na-gil, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Pretty interesting Chinatown in Seoul. A lot of Korean Chinese influence including banchan stores, lots of lamb skewers, and north east Chinese food options. It had its unique demographic and Korean-Chinese influence that is different from Japan/Singapore/US Chinatowns. Some people who work here do not even try to talk in Korean, but in Chinese. The main languages are Chinese and Korean and I don’t imagine English would work here.

Good place to get authentic Chinese seasonings and banchan. I’d get produce and seafood from other places.

I had heard a lot about this traditional market, and I finally visited on the first day of the Lunar New Year. I was surprised to see that it was still very crowded, as I had expected most stores in South Korea to be closed for the holiday.

Walking around, I almost felt like I was in China because there were so many shops selling Chinese products and a wide variety of Asian groceries, including durian. The atmosphere was lively and interesting. If you have some time while you’re in Seoul, I definitely recommend checking this market out. I really enjoyed my visit.

A small Chinatown near Daerim station. You can find some Chinese produce and a variety of Chinese food such as Xiao long Bao and La Mian. Overall it is a small place but a pretty great find not far from Seoul.

The biggest Chinese market in Korea.
You can enjoy verious street foods and fresh vegetables.

Do you want to eat Chinese food and speak Mandarin? This is your chance.  This is a major Chinese enclave and this market is liable to make you forget the you're actually in Korea.  This is the first place I've been to where the merchants assume that you're Chinese and start the conversion in Chinese.  Some of them don't even speak Korean.

You know this is real Chinese food because you will be one of the only non Chinese people here.  Almost any ingredient or Chinese staple dish can be found here.

I personally don't speak Chinese but my friend who used to live in China was having a ball.  "I really feel like I'm back in China on this street!" Definitely an interesting twist to the normal  시장 (traditional market).

I'm not so into it,  honestly, but my friend who speaks the language and loves Chinese food said she'd be going back ASAP.

Free museum. Several floors, with exhibits on 5th and 3rd. Interactive kids on 4th. Interior room with a view, and on the 8th floor roof outdoor viewing of the palace and Blue House.  couple cafes and areas to sit and rest. The exhibitions were nice, with some English translations.

After Korea’s liberation in 1945, this building served as the headquarters for the Ministry of Education and later the Ministry of Culture and Information, becoming the administrative center for national education and cultural policy in the early Republic of Korea.
When those offices moved to Sejong City, the site was reborn in 2012 as the National Museum of Korean Contemporary History.
This makes the museum’s location itself historically meaningful — it’s a place where the modern nation’s governance and cultural identity first took shape.

Inside, the exhibitions are well organized by period, from liberation to the present, making it an excellent introduction to modern Korean history — even for first-time visitors or foreigners.
Its surroundings also add to its significance: right across from Sejong Center and the Government Complex, and just behind it lies Gyeongbokgung Palace and Mt. Bukak. Together they form the symbolic axis of Korea’s politics and history.

One place you absolutely shouldn’t miss is the rooftop observatory on the 8th floor.
From there, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the entire Gyeongbokgung Palace, beautifully framed by the surrounding mountains.
It offers a perfect vantage point to appreciate the geomantic (Pungsu-jiri) harmony of the palace’s location — encircled by mountains that were believed to protect the king and ensure the dynasty’s stability.
It’s not just a museum; it’s a window into Korea’s landscape of power and tradition.

Highly recommended — especially the rooftop view that reveals the deeper meaning of Gyeongbokgung’s setting.

google_addr: 59 Jangchungdan-ro, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: The building is quite huge with few performance halls at different blocks. Tickets always sold out especially on weekend. Many kiosks were set outside the building (weekend only or for some special occasions) Tickets sold out fast especially on weekend so get your tickets early. I recommend buying online for cheaper price and no hasle queing for tickets.

Visited the National Theater of Korea and was thoroughly impressed! The place is huge, offering multiple performance halls that host a variety of traditional and contemporary shows. The facilities, including bathrooms, are well-maintained, and the lawns are spotlessly cared for, creating a welcoming environment. We enjoyed some beverages from the nearby cafe, which were delightful. Additionally, the accessibility is top-notch with a bus stop right in front that makes it super convenient for visitors. Highly recommend for anyone looking to experience Korea's rich performing arts culture!
It's a nice building. I see many runners in front of this building.

I’ve been to the National Theater of Korea a few times now. I watched La Traviata last September, Joyous Resonance in January, and L’italiana in Algeri in February. Each show was different, but they all had that moment when the lights dim, the orchestra begins, and the whole room breathes together. That’s the part I love most.

The theater is one of the biggest in Korea. It went through a renovation in 2021, and it looks great. The halls are clean, the seats are comfortable, and everything feels new. Still, I think a great theater needs more than just a nice building. It needs warmth. It needs to feel like a place made for people, not just for performances.

If you are planning to visit with kids, there is something you should know. Getting there is not easy. The theater sits halfway up Namsan Mountain, right in the middle of Seoul but far from the subway. The nearest station, Dongguk University on Line 3, is not within walking distance. You have to take a bus, usually number 420. Now, imagine yourself holding your child and a bag while standing on a crowded bus on your way to an opera. You will probably be tired before you even get there.

That is why I think accessibility matters. A public theater should welcome people from the moment they decide to come, not make them wonder how to reach it.

Once you are inside, things get better. The space feels open and organized. There are four floors, labeled L, 1, 2, and 3. Each one has vending machines for water and soft drinks. On the L floor, there is a restaurant called Central Yunit. It looks comfortable and has many seats, although it seems a bit expensive. There is also a KB Bank ATM nearby, which is convenient.

The box office is on the 1st floor, which feels like the 2nd floor if you are used to the American floor system. There is a small café that sells sandwiches and coffee, and the box office opens one hour before the show. The staff are calm and polite. You can leave your coat in the cloakroom across from the counter. They put a numbered sticker on the back of your ticket so you can pick it up easily after the show.

There are plenty of seats for intermission, and the atmosphere stays quiet and comfortable. After the performance, shuttle buses take people back to Dongguk University Station and Dongdaemun History and Culture Park Station. If you miss one, another comes in about twenty minutes.

Yes, getting there takes effort, but once you sit down and the music starts, you forget about all of that. The voices rise, the stage glows, and for a while, everything else fades away. That is the beauty of live performance, and it is why I keep coming back.

Many performance showing at this national theatre of Korea. Get your tickets early on line to avoid queing up for tickets that selling fast. This place is huge with many performance Halls. If you love Arts nd Shows this is a must place to watch outstanding Korean performances.

reviews.text: I loved everything about this clinic: the doctor, the staff, my results, and the aftercare. Dr Lee is really professional, skilled, ethical, and safe. I am grateful for his work and for his unwavering patience and do not think I could have found a better doctor for my case. Moreover, the staff here made me feel more comfortable than the staff at many other clinics in Seoul, for they are consistently friendly, laidback, and not ingratiating.

Very Experienced, Knowledgeable, Professional, Friendly, Approachable Oral Surgeon. I came from Singapore and it was my first time visiting Korea, I have malocclusion and bad underbite since i was a teenager. I had Double Jaw Surgery and it was to correct my bitting and bone structure while taking aesthetic into consideration. Before i even went to Korea, i have been talking to Dr Lee for the past couple of months to clarify doubts and questions. He always manage to reply me even though i know he must be very busy. I booked surgery date before i finally visit Korea and on consultation day, Dr Lee greeted me warmly and he was so patient in answering all my enquiries and all of his explanation was splendid. Although i have been asking questions to him for months through online portal, i still had a lot of questions in mind and he always answer them thoughtfully. In addition, His english was very good so I did not had problem with communicating with him. He explained thoroughly on the surgery procedure, what to expect, the after-care and always emphasise safety first. He even showed me amazing transformations profile of his other patients. I was very terrified of the surgery but he always reassured me that everything will be fine. Dr Lee is very caring towards his patients even in his midst of hustle schedule. He visited me a couple of times during my stay in hospital making sure Im on the right track of recovery. To me, that is something I really appreciate. The surgery went very well as per discussed and right now Im at 2 weeks post operation recovery. Although the post-surgery was very painful especially the first day, the nurses there were very prompt and helpful in taking care of me. Very grateful for them for making my surgery journey a more bearable one. Overall, I would like to thank Dr Lee, all the beautiful nurses who took care of me during my 2 night stay in hospital, the anaesthesia team who calmed me down before the actual surgery as well as the manager lady who always try her best to clear my doubt even though there was language barrier. Her initiatives was very commendable in trying to bridge that gap of language barrier. I cant wait to recover and might even consider dental implant with Dr Lee after my post braces treatment in my hometown. For those who are considering Facial Bone Surgery or encounter complications with their teeth, should really consider The Face Dental Clinic as one of the top choices.

I did jaw surgery before the pandemic. Toilets are unisex single person only, very respectful of people. Dr Lee understood english perfectly and most importantly, knows what i want.  Like i did not want my wisdom tooth removed, and Dr Lee kept them which was very important.

The nurses are great especially the one who attended to me on the first day. There were some other minor issues like i have to pay a deposit upfront but the korea bank refused to let me withdraw more then 1000 usd  as the atm limit, i forgot the exact amount but yes, i think i fall short of the amount deposited since i thought i can paid everything via wire transfer but luckily they were understanding. The price is also very good compared to some other clinic that charges a lot more.

Very knowledable surgeon and i think  the patient can feel comfortable with the surgeon. all my questions clarified comprehensively.
Skilled doctor as I have seen many patients who went there with amazing results. I can also say that Dr is focused on safety first! I ended up not going to Korea but my online consultation was pleasent and good experience.

One of my friend recommended this clinic and I got the V-line surgery here. And the result was more than I expected! I was satisfied with the result of my surgery. The clinic was very clean and everything was systematic. The doctor and the staff were very nice and explained every step so I wasn't nervous at all. I'm sure everyone will love this place!

title: 더현대 서울
google_addr: 108 1F Yeoui-daero, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I came to this mall as part of the Incheon transit tour where I had some time to wander this mall and attend a Paldo cooking class.

I really enjoyed relaxing in the terrace on the upper floor and walking through the Dyson demo area.

While I didn’t get a chance to take many photos of the food hall in the basement floors, it was quite massive with lots of food options.

There’s B1 food court that has a great concept here, easy ordering by kiosk and convenient collection of food via SMS once ready. Their fish set is quite impressive, and the bibimbap beef is a must-try—it’s delicious! They also have spicy beef rice that’s equally tasty. There’s a wide variety of food choices in basement 1, so come hungry!

The Hyundai Seoul is a modern and stylish shopping mall that offers a great overall experience. The food court is impressive, with a wide range of delicious options, and there are many popular cafés gathered in one convenient location, which makes café hopping very easy. The spacious and clean layout makes it comfortable to walk around and shop. If you are a fan of luxury brands, this place would easily be a five-star destination thanks to the number of high-end stores available.

Super clean, modern, and nice. Even the bathrooms were impressive. It's designed nicely and they have cool resting area with a lot of plants on the fifth floor. But that's about it, i don't think it's worth the trip to 여의도 for just this place. We intentionally avoided weekend to come on a Monday afternoon but there were still a lot of people! We were like man where are all these people from?  Do they not work? They can't all be on a PTO. Anyways, it's  a nice spot and maybe worth a visit just once so you can say you've been there. Honestly my wife and I prefer shopping at Lotte Mall and dept store in Jamsil where we are staying.

We love the Hyundai Department Store and made sure to visit again this time. It’s super spacious, with plenty of shops and brands. Everything is spread out in a way that creates a relaxed and enjoyable shopping environment.

The garden area on the upper floor is especially impressive. The entire floor is dedicated to relaxation and recharging. It is huge! They could have easily filled this space with more shops and restaurants to generate revenue, but instead they chose to create such a delightful area for visitors. I really admire that decision and philosophy.

The top floor features a range of restaurants. Some are just okay, but most are excellent. Down in the basement, the food corners are amazing, with endless things to see and eat. You could easily spend an entire afternoon here.

Highly recommend a visit when you’re in Seoul!

title: 덕수궁

reviews.text: Incredible view. Well preserved historical structure. Definitely a must-see when visiting Seoul. Make sure to rent out a hanbok, to get fully immersed, and also admission is free if you are wearing one.

Deoksugung stands out among Seoul’s royal palaces for its unique, captivating blend of traditional Joseon architecture and 19th-century Western-style stone buildings. Located at the city’s busiest intersection, it offers a serene escape where history feels layered and alive. Don't miss the Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony at the main gate for a vibrant display of traditional costumes and music.

Deoksugung Palace is absolutely beautiful and full of history, with such a peaceful atmosphere right in the middle of the city.

Walking through the grounds felt calm and immersive and the contrast between traditional architecture and the surrounding modern buildings was stunning.

Unfortunately, I missed the guard changing ceremony, which I’ve heard is amazing, but the visit was still completely worth it for such a bargain price of 1000 won.

It’s a lovely place to explore, take photos, and learn more about Korea’s history.

It's a small palace at the city center. Easy access, cheap entrance fee of 1000KRW. The Palace grounds is quite nice, with trees in multi fall colors. The main palace hall needs some restoration to bring out the lovely details which are now old and dusty. The grounds also has a museum or gallery. So it is quite a pleasant location to spend an hour

Beautiful palace and gardens in central Seoul. It was my first time to visit, and it was awesome. They have free tours in various languages (although I just walked around myself), and Monday has free admission (the day that I went). Amazing place, and a definite must-see in Seoul!

reviews.text: The main gate of Deoksugung Palace at Deoksugung-gil & Sejong-daero. Beautiful traditional architecture with a historic feel, right in the heart of Seoul. A nice spot for photos & to start a peaceful stroll along the palace grounds.

Daehanmun is the main gate of Deoksugung Palace. Originally built as the east gate of Gyeongungung Palace, it was demolished for road construction in front of Inhwamun, the main gate and south gate of Deoksugung Palace. Following a fire in 1904, Daeanmun on the east side was renamed Daehanmun and designated as the main gate.

Daehanmun is the main gate of Deoksugung Palace.
'Daehan' means "Hanyang will prosper."
Hanyang refers to the sunny region north of the Han River and was the old name for Seoul, the capital of the Joseon Dynasty.
'Han' means 'Han River', and 'yang' means 'north of the water' or 'sunny place, reflecting Hanyang's geographical characteristics.
Originally built as the east gate of Gyeongungung Palace, it was demolished for road construction in front of Inhwamun, the main gate and south gate of Deoksugung Palace.

title: 덕수궁 돌담길

reviews.text: The most beautiful ginkgo biloba walking trail in Seoul in autumn last year appeared like this. It was in full bloom. From Deoksugung Stone Wall Road to Jeongdong Street, the streets are full of golden ginkgo biloba. On one side is the stone wall of an ancient palace. Looking up, you can see the yellow and green leaves. You can encounter various art galleries along the way. Feels surreal.

Finally I got to walk this street by the stone wall of Duksoo Oalace. I was here late on a week night. The street was empty. No padestrians. If you enter from the City Hall side and keep following the wall and, you would come out close to GwangHwaMoon square. Unless you are seeking a quiet walk at night, visit during the day when the palace is open so you get to see both.

These are lovely grounds and buildings, some with markers in English to describe the history. However an audio guide would have been appreciated.

The site is listed as accessible but much of it is not. There are ramps in places, but getting to them is frequently impossible in a wheel chair. The pond near the exit, the most serene spot on the property at totally inaccessible.
Strolled along Deoksugung Doldamgil near Sejong-daero 19-Gil in the evening. The stone-wall path is peaceful & calming, perfect for a relaxing walk while enjoying the historic surroundings

Deoksugung Doldamgil (Stone-wall Road) is a walking path lined with the quaint stone walls surrounding Deoksugung Palace in Jung-gu, Seoul.
The tranquil atmosphere offers a glimpse into the fusion of Joseon palaces and modern Seoul. Its beauty is particularly evident in spring and fall, attracting many tourists.
Nearby cafés and galleries make it a great place to spend some time after exploring Deoksugung Palace.
It‘s also connected to Jeongdong-gil and the Seoul Museum of Art, making it a great place to visit together.

title: 도곡시장
google_addr: Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Lively, clean, with a wide variety of prepared goods, fruit, vegetables, and seafood. If you can't find something you want here, you're just not trying.

LNestled in the heart of the city lies a small traditional market that packs a flavorful punch. With approximately 20 shops clustered together, this market offers a vibrant snapshot of Korean culinary traditions.

As you navigate the narrow alleyways, you're immediately enveloped by a tapestry of aromas and sights. The market boasts an impressive array of Korean staples: from the pungent notes of gochujang (red pepper paste) and doenjang (soybean paste) to the briny scents of saeujeot (fermented shrimp) and galchijeot (fermented hairtail fish). The golden hues of chamgireum (sesame oil) and deulgireum (perilla oil) glisten in bottles, promising to add depth to any dish.

Beyond the fermented goods and oils, the market is a treasure trove of fresh produce. An assortment of seafood glistens on ice, while vibrant vegetables add splashes of color to the bustling scene. It's a one-stop-shop for those looking to stock their pantries with authentic Korean ingredients.

However, the market's popularity comes with its challenges. The high foot traffic can make navigation somewhat difficult, especially during peak hours. Shoppers should be prepared for close quarters and the occasional brush with fellow market-goers.

A word of caution: the narrow pathways are sometimes shared with small motorcycles making deliveries. While this adds to the market's lively atmosphere, visitors should remain alert to ensure their safety.

Despite these minor inconveniences, the market remains a must-visit for food enthusiasts and those seeking an authentic Korean shopping experience. The density of shops means you can compare prices and quality easily, ensuring you get the best products for your won.

In conclusion, this compact traditional market offers a concentrated dose of Korean food culture. It's a place where centuries-old culinary traditions meet the hustle and bustle of modern city life. Just remember to watch your step, and you're in for a treat for all your senses.

title: 도시의 고풍스러운 정취를 즐기다
google_addr: 10 Oyanam-ro 38beon-gil, Sujeong-gu, Seongnam-si, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea

reviews.text:
A traditional Hanok tea house located outside of Seoul with peaceful surroundings.

I visited from when they opened at 11 am, and luckily there wasn't many people. So I do recommend to visit as early as possible, before the big masses of people pays a visit.

The garden:

As you walk in you walk, you'll find yourself infront of a beautiful open outdoor space.
With several seatings and a small pawn.
To be honest, the pawn would have looked much better with "cleaner" water, but with that being said, it is also part of the charm of this place.

The surroundings and outdoor area is peaceful and quiet. I aim to visit later in the afternoon or evening next time.

In the main house:

The main building is also where you place your order in addition to having more seating options.
Old dark wood carry a different feel to the experience when you have the greenery outside mingling in with the building in a calm and balanced nuance.

On the walls are pictures displaying the heritage of this Hanok cafe.

Food :

It was more like tea time snack. Even so, the different bites gave a crash course of traditional Korean flavor. Sweet, savory, bitter in a well balanced harmony.
Jujubee tea alongside the Omija tea held a great powering flavor without being overwhelming.

A sensation of flavours when you combine the tea and the small nibbles.

Price :

The price is very high compared to others. Arguably so, keep in mind you pay extra for the experience of visiting this local Hanok tea house.
With that in mind, all beverages are priced above  10 000 won per tea. For the "mini" tray of traditional snack is 18 000 won 💸💸💸💸

Overall verdict:

To me, this traditional tea spot is a great little get away for tasteful tea in old school Korean surroundings.
I personally like this location much better than the overcrowded touristy streets of Ikseondong.

Having only tried two teas and tasted a mere handful of bites the food and beverages needs to be explored more. This explains why I can't give a full 5 stars. But from what I've tasted it didn't dissapoint.

Service wise was as expected, maybe a little bit under for my for preference. Staff was polite and all but I didn't feel that genuine feeling.
When you have a concept of heritage and culture, making it more memorable will only gain more fame. While the location and the architecture is great, small details from the server or like a small note, explaining the tea you drink etc would make it even better. That's just me though. Until next time service is a 3 star for me.

Atmosphere is great. This thanks to the garden and the building creating a cozy and beautiful balance of history. The pawn is a nice little touch as well as the enclosure surrounding the cafe.

It definitely is a cafe worth visiting as it brings a different vibe with its garden.

Can't wait to make a visit again!
Hopefully I can update the score as well ~

A traditional Korean house that dons itself as a cafe. It is far into the mountains so you might have a hard time finding it. However, overall vibe is very unique. They have tea which tastes like medicine and some rice cakes. They also have simple bingsu (shaved ice)
Beautiful HanOk cafe in the forest. Enjoy Korean traditional tea.

The place is beautifully restored with respect for the old traditional elements of the design and architecture. On the same note, the new modern elements are used in a discrete way to give this place a new life and new function. I look forward to come back here to enjoy this place when it's all green and warmer. The coffee was also good, but I hope they introduce some traditional alcohol on the menu. It would make it much easier for a foreigner to sit on the floor
Beautiful Hanok cafe in the suburbs of Seoul. The red bean dessert menus were great and the omija tea was so tasty!

title: 도심속 바다축제
google_addr: 674 Nodeul-ro, Dongjak District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I had the best and freshest seafood here at a remarkably reasonable price. A tip: know what you want and order it directly, otherwise the friendly ahjumma and ahjussi might enthusiastically try to offer you everything they have!

The sashimi and crab were absolutely to die for—incredibly fresh, with a natural sweetness that really shone through. An outstanding meal.

I have mixed feelings about this place. On one hand the seafood is top notch but just the idea that you know prices will be hiked up makes one think if we are getting fleeced.

That said it is competitive so I woke recommend walking around to get a feel of the prices before deciding. Once you’ve settled the purchase of the items, they’ll bring you up to the affiliated restaurant so they can cook it.

The meal after is pretty good, as usual! Fresh king crab and good sashimi. Always order the  ramyeon and fried rice. Overall, it was v delish. But you just gotta go through the buying process first!

Noryangjin Fish Market is a place I occasionally visit for sashimi. It's been a while since I last visited, and it's much cleaner than before, with parking much easier. And there's almost no solicitation like there used to be, so I can walk around comfortably, browse, and get my sashimi. It's not close, but there are few places in Seoul where you can get sashimi at such a good price. I'll have to come back often whenever I crave sashimi.

I had a positive experience here as a tourist. Lots of the stalls were trying to get us to buy their stuff which is expected. Hard to walk around without someone trying to get you to buy their stuff. Most stalls seemed to sell the same stuff. The people selling just fish in the back weren’t as pushy and helped us find someone selling eel which was all the way in the back. The stall we went to the lady was nice and picked out a crab for me. I believe it was 100000 won. She also gave me clams for service as well. Then a man took us to the second floor restaurant which steamed the crab and bbq our eel. We even got the crab head fried rice. I don’t remember the price for cooking but I don’t think it was a lot like some people said they charge tourists. Overall a great experience for a seafood lover.

Noryangjin Fish Market is huge! You could easily spend hours walking from stall to stall comparing prices! Instead, we decided to go with one stall we felt comfortable with (and with no language barrier). To our surprise, many of the sellers could speak Chinese quite well, which made communication much easier!

There are so many seafood choices that you’ll be spoiled for options but since we had only 3 pax, we kept it simple and got king crab, abalone, prawns, and the friendly stall lady even added some shellfish for free ☺️☺️☺️
We spent around SGD $300+ for all our seafood (the crab was slightly over 2kg).

After payment, we were led to the 2nd floor restaurants where they cook your seafood the way you like it. We also ordered a few extra dishes there, which came up to about SGD $200 including cooking fees.

Everything was fresh, delicious, and the whole experience was so enjoyable!

Definitely a must-visit spot ☺️

This greenhouse features an elegant combination of glass and steel. The greenhouse houses a wide variety of plants, including rare tropical species and traditional Korean flora.

Honestly, Changgyeonggung is so underrated and out of all the palaces in Seoul, this is my favorite. It’s so serene.

At night there are food trucks and little markets with local artist. Also, there are relaxing areas where you can lay down and pianos where people like to play music!

This should be one of your stops when visiting Seoul as you'll be able to absorb both modern and cultural experiences within walking distance of each other. It's easy to get here by subway. Once you exit, you'll be greeted with an amazing building that looks like a spaceship has landed in the middle of Seoul. Tons of activities to do here from shopping to local night markets.
We were there in the evening and it was unforgettable experience. The lighted silent temples and palaces in the middle of mordern city - it is a kind of surrealism.

Came on a Monday afternoon and was not busy at all - I might go back again while here because it was a trip highlight!

Dongdaemun Plaza looks really impressive from the outside, the architecture and lights make it feel fun, futuristic, and almost magical, especially at night. It's definitely a great spot for photos and just walking around to enjoy the atmosphere. Inside, though, it's quite minimal and feels a bit bare, so there isn't too much to see compared to how exciting it looks from the outside. Still, it's worth visiting for the unique design and experience outside.

If you love architecture and art, you will definitely enjoy Dongdaemun Design Plaza. Designed by renowned architect Zaha Hadid, DDP is an iconic landmark known for its futuristic curves and seamless, flowing form that blends architecture, design, and urban space.

I visited early in the day when there were only a few visitors, and the experience was amazing. The atmosphere felt calm and peaceful, allowing me to fully appreciate every corner of the space, both indoors and outdoors.

While DDP hosts many art and design exhibitions, the building itself is truly a work of art.

This should be one of your stops when visiting Seoul as you'll be able to absorb both modern and cultural experiences within walking distance of each other. It's easy to get here by subway. google_addr: 266 Jong-ro, Jongno 6(yuk)-ga, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
예전에 동대문상가 가끔 방문한 적이 있었는데, 오랜만에 큰애 패션쇼 출품으로 원단이나 소품 구매하러 방문했네요.
도매점이라서 낱개 등 소매 구입은 어려운 점이 있으나 큰애 소품으로 벨트 보려했는데 점포 대부분이 손을 흔들며 안판다는 제스쳐나 없어요 라고 단호하고 냉정하게 대하는 점이 있네요.

물론 하루에 얼마만한 사람들이 왕래할지 분주하겠지만 학생의 간절한 물건 구매에 계속 여쭤보는데 엄두가 안나네요.
다행히 D동 BOB 점포에서 학생의 구매하려는 의상 벨트를 구경시켜주고 판매해 주시네요.
용도도 물어봐주시고 의상 공부하는 하는 학생인지도 관심 보여주심에 감사드리네요.
언제라도 방문하라는 배려에 큰애가 용기를 내니 저도 마음이 훈훈합니다.

(동대문종합시장)
1995년 현재 대지면적 9,920㎡, 건물연면적 2만 3471㎡의 규모에 종사자수는 2,880명이다.
상점은 대부분 도매상이며, 상권은 서울시내의 각 시장은 물론, 수원·대전·대구·부산 그리고 강원도지방까지 포함된다.

한편, 동대문종합시장은 구동대문시장(광장시장)에 비하면 그 역사가 짧지만, 전국 최대의 원단 전문상가로 2,453개의 점포가 있다.
또한 동대문쇼핑센터에는 345개의 점포가 있는데, 원단과 혼수용품이 주로 거래되고 있다.

이처럼 혼수품을 취급하는 전문점들이 다양하게 있기 때문에, 한 곳에서 신혼생활에 필요한 물건을 거의 다 골라 갖출 수 있다는 점이 이 시장의 특징이다.
(한국민족문화대백과, 한국학중앙연구원)
동대문종합시장에 이런 시장 탑 있는거 오늘 방문으로 처음 알았네요
다양한 제품이 있어 쇼핑하기 좋고 가격 또한 저렴 합니다. 옥상 주차장 전경 좋습니다.
요즘 사람별로없어서 다니기좋아요~시원한음료도 넘맛나네요!
다른동에 비해서 가격이 싸지만 동대문시장은 무조건발품입니다.돌아서면 가격이 달라요.직원이 달라도 가격을 다르게불러서 놀라고 같은사장인데도 저번이랑 다른가격을 불러서 놀라구~ 조금사니까 다행이지 많은양이라면 제가격을 제시할까요? 정말의문입니다

title: 동십자각
google_addr: 1 Samcheong-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: A lone watch tower which was part of the palace in the past. Now it is at a road intersection.

Dongsipjagak (동십자각) is a small guard pavilion located at the eastern corner of Gyeongbokgung Palace in Seoul. Built during the Joseon Dynasty, it served as a watchtower and a key point in the palace's defense system. Its unique architecture reflects traditional Korean design and historical significance.

Known as the lonely pavilion, the Dongsipjagak was once part of the palace watch tower is now standing as the center of what seems like a roundabout. There appeared no door to this pavilion but was told of its history dated back to be part of Gyeongbokgung Palace.  I guess must be the new city layout that now stands its current position. So, next time when you pass by this lonely pavilion, give a second look and appreciate its history and its once critical role as a watch tower protecting the Palace.
