reviews.text:
Despite not being listed as a major tourist attraction nor being located near the most touristic parts of Seoul, I visited this museum and rather enjoyed it. It's actually smaller than I imagined it to be, so don't expect to spend any more than 30 min to one hour to have a look at everything there.
Free entrance, and exhibition guides and videos were translated into English.

This one is way out there in the northern reaches of the city.  But worth the trip, I suppose.  Like all of the SEMA facilities the art tends towards the avant-garde.

It is a pretty big spot, so you might be able to spend a few hours.  Also check out the library on the top floor.  It has a ton of books (non-circulating) about art in both English and Korean.

Well the facilities are great. Each floor has space for individual artist to showcase their art. The roof has a nice garden. The field surrounding the museum is good for kids. The art inside... well it's contemporary.

Not bad place and it's free. The free lockers are nice and bathrooms are sparkly clean. Staff are friendly. I took a star away because the art was eehh. I feel like some exhibits portrayed nothing of the artist and the process, rather random stuff they created that was trying too hard. Sorry, I know it's art, but come on.

I was for appreciation art that was painted in early 19th century in Korea. Most of them were introduced in my school book when I was a high school student. Prior to this exhibition, I never saw paints that my teacher in high school teach taught me during the school class. All paints and portraits are genuine.

The place is nice.
Their exhibitions are really good.
Once, a docent explained me the exhibition in English !
A place to go !

title: 디뮤지엄
google_addr: South Korea, Seoul, Seongdong-gu, Wangsimni-ro, 83-21 디뮤지엄

reviews.text: The D Museum invites the visitor inside -- not just to view some art, but to imagine it in one's own life. The current exhibition sets up scenarios of family members' households at different stages of their lives -- complete with exquisitely designed furniture and modern artwork. It features lesser- and well-known artists, such as Picasso and Frank Lloyd Wright. You might find yourself wanting to sit in that beautiful chair in that beautiful living room to admire the art (or in my case, the curtained dining area on a raised platform surrounded by stones), but please don't as you will be immediately escorted out.

We visited D Museum for the Art is Life, Life is Art exhibition and had a wonderful experience. The curated “houses” were beautifully designed—modern yet deeply rooted in Korean culture. It was inspiring to see such a thoughtful mix of works by Korean, Japanese, Spanish, and Italian artists, alongside big names like Picasso, Frank Lloyd Wright, and Patricia Urquiola.

It’s a fantastic and well-rounded exhibition that we’d definitely recommend to art and design lovers. A helpful side note—there are lockers available and they’re free for the first hour, which made it convenient to explore comfortably. 🖼️🏠🎨✨

We saw the Romantic Days gallery and it was fantastic. It's 3 floors worth of display so admission is definitely worth it. The also have courteous ushers so that visitors are assisted every step of the way. I'd say this place is perfect for dates. They even have photobooths at the lobby so that you can take home a memory of the day.

I visited the D Museum during the Romantic Days exhibition. I recommend this museum as it often changes up their theme and the tickets are afforable if you  book online. The area is also very nice and near Seoul Forest, so perfect for a day out.

I thought D Museum would be slashed off my itinerary, but I'm glad it didn't. I arrived an hour before it closes in the evening, and it was packed with young visitors (which I wasn't surprised about). The "Weather" exhibition is so amusing that it takes you to the sensations of each season, transitioning from one room to another. My favorite must be the collection for winter. This is definitely one of my favorite destinations in my recent Seoul trip, and this particular gallery is one of the most unique I've been to.

title: 디키디키
google_addr: 1-2 Euljiro 7(chil)-ga, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Multiple play areas. Lots of space for them to explore. However, the play ticket is very expensive but restricted for only 2 hours. I also think it is tricky to make parents pay extra to come in keeping an eye on their kids 😐 Like, I won’t leave my kid alone there and I won’t play with your toys 🤷‍♀️
Anw, there’s a coffee shop and toilet inside. We parents will happily sit down and have a drink if you aren’t (almost feel like) enforcing the extra fee like that.

Great way to spend 2 hours with a toddler. The time goes by fast and they're so enthralled by the different play areas that you can take a break too. Plenty of seating for adults to watch / play with their kids on a comfortable surface.

Only downside is how strictly they try to enforce their way of "playing", which means always following the arrows on direction to walk, not climbing while holding any toys, etc. Bro, they're kids. You can get past this by just paying lip service but not relenting to their demands. That's pretty much what I did until they stopped bothering us.

This was the largest kids cafe we visited while in Seoul (we went to several) and my son LOVED it. He ran around everywhere and we also played with him on this digital running game that’s beneath the jungle gym. They have several play stations and my son even loved the lady at one of the stations. However! Something to note! I was in desperate need of a coffee and the cafe was on a break at the exact time we arrived (they take an hour break from 2-3 or 3-4. I like that they have some areas where the parents can sit on the floor as well. We were very comfortable.

This experience honestly still makes me angry and upset.

Last summer, when I was nine years old, my mom and I traveled over an hour by train from my grandma’s house just to come here. I was extremely excited. I had been to the Diki Diki playground before when I was younger, and it was one of my happiest memories. I was waiting for the elevator, full of excitement, thinking I was finally going to play there again.

Then everything fell apart.

I was denied entry because of the age limit, even though I was only ONE year over. One year. For a huge playground where many other places allow kids my age without a problem. That alone was heartbreaking.

But what truly made this experience unbearable was the staff’s behavior.

The employee who stopped us was rude, rolled his eyes, ignored my mom, and treated her with complete disrespect. Watching my mother be treated like that was devastating. She is older than him, a paying visitor, and a parent who spent time, money, and effort just to bring her child somewhere special.

What made it even worse was that the other employees did absolutely nothing. They didn’t step in. They didn’t call a manager. They didn’t try to calm the situation. They just ignored us and continued serving other customers as if nothing was happening, while a child was crying nearby. I felt invisible. Like we didn’t matter at all.

The situation escalated, voices were raised, and I was completely overwhelmed. I was hiding in corners, crying, sitting on the floor, wishing I could disappear. I didn’t even want to be there anymore. My excitement turned into humiliation, fear, and heartbreak within minutes.

That night at dinner, I couldn’t even speak. I shut down completely.

Rules are rules, but there is absolutely no excuse for staff acting this way and for others standing by and ignoring a clearly distressing situation involving a child. This wasn’t just a bad visit. It was an experience that stayed with me and still hurts to think about.

I hope management seriously reflects on how staff behavior and inaction can deeply affect families and children.

A place that is suitable for kids around age 4-5. A lot of slides for kids who like to play slide. Have one person looking around for the kids playing and one auntie non stop cleaning. Hygiene is at tip top condition for kids

title: 딜쿠샤

reviews.text:
Free museum dedicated to the American columnist Albert Taylor. a figure who played a decisive role to promote the fierce independence movement of Korea and the brutality of Japan on March 1, 1919. It is Albert Wilder Taylor, a temporary correspondent of the Associated Press and the first person to disseminate overseas the Declaration of Independence of the March 1st Movement.
The house is beautifully restored with furniture and memorabilia from Albert and his wife. There are some English translation from the exhibits.
Very interesting place bares history of modern Seoul. Worth visiting hidden  gem north of the river. 470yo ginko tree is still going strong.

Dilkusha means 'Heart's Delight' in Persian. This house was built by Albert W. Taylor and Mary L. Taylor in 1923. Mary was a stage actress, but she also drew very well. I was impressed by her drawings and paintings. This place is free of charge, so I highly recommend it to everyone.

Not easy to find but an unexpected local treasure. It was abandon and rundown for many years and now restored to its original glory. A wonderful tale of the house history along with an excellent restoration. Worth the trek if in the area.

Just visited it today. A great discovery and a beautiful restoration of this house. Great to learn that it was with the help of a journalist that the existence of the Korean resistance and the  Independence Movement was made known to the world.
The visit is free.

title: 떡박물관

reviews.text: Great little museum about the history of rice cakes.

This is the place to learn about the traditions and history of rice cake in Korea! If you're staying in/near Insadong, it's also close by and you can look at everything in less than 30 minutes. Considering how this is a smaller museum, there's so much excellent information on how rice cakes were traditionally made, the tools and cookware that were used, and the Korean celebrations where different rice cakes and food were served.
It looks like some people were expecting ricecake to be sold here but this isn't a huge museum. :) Hopefully, as they get more interest, they can expand to sell ricecake and also have a gift shop. But I felt that it was a wonderful museum.
The only thing to note is that while the 2nd floor has everything in English, the 3rd floor exhibition doesn't have English translations yet. For now, if you can, use the Google Lens translate feature.
Enter through the Institute of Traditional Korean Food and the entrance is on the 1st floor. The exhibition is on the 2nd and 3rd floors. I went on a Sat, early afternoon, and it wasn't crowded at all. Tickets are very affordable and no need for reservations.

Quiet place and not much to see
But it’s cheap only 3000won for one adult

Rice cake has a long history in Korea. This is a private run museum which provides a details introduction of rice cake and its history. You can also have the chance to join a cooking class to bake your own rice cake. A cafe is also located on the ground floor and you can enjoy rice cake and coffee.

This is a privately run ttoek museum, the building also sell classes if you want to do extra activities. The museum runs on two levels and showcase various sort of tteok depending on seasons and life events. Give some good overview around this rice cake tradition. reviews.text: A nice lovely park which is within a short walking distance from the train station. Very windy if you’re coming around January and best to eat ramen since it’s nearby too. Ownself cook ramen which will turn out nice to eat in this cold weather with lovely view. There’s a handful where you can eat or drink. Starbucks is there too. Also go play the snow slide and other activities which you have to pay for. The snow slide which you have to sit on a float and slide down on the icy. For all ages and have fun.

A small but very neatly designed Park on the Seoul northern riverside.
We went here to watch the famous drone show and it was really cool!

The park is not designed to host THAT many people though. It's really crowded fir the show and there only are 3 narrow passageways under a highway to enter or exit the park.
Good place to visit in the evening time. Lots of option to do. boating, surfing, picnic, cycling & many more. Or you can just relax watching the beautiful river & city together.

We knew the drone show was going to be going on while we were there and we're so happy we were able to catch it. It seemed a lot of the crowd didn't know, so hearing their gasps of surprise was fun. If you're ever able to catch it, definitely do so. The bridge lit up at night was beautiful. And it's definitely fun to have snacks there while sitting by the water at night.

We went here to watch the drone show, and it was a blast! The park is also well-maintained, and a bunch of places that rent picnic mats and the like. It's a great place to visit, especially when most places in Seoul are all urbanized.

reviews.text:
The Raum Social Venue

I recently attended the Seoul ADR Festival at the Raum Social Venue, which is conveniently located within walking distance from my hotel.

Space and Facilities:
The conference room was huge, providing ample space for attendees to move around and engage comfortably.

Comfort:
However, I found the chairs provided to be totally unsuitable for all-day conferences. They lacked the necessary comfort for extended periods of sitting, which negatively impacted the overall experience. I hope they consider changing the chairs to accommodate long events better.

Overall, while the venue was spacious and well-situated, improvements in seating would significantly enhance the experience for future conferences.

reviews.text: I can wholeheartedly recommend this clinic. Even the communication in advance via WhatsApp was smooth and very friendly - I felt I was in good hands right from the start. I had contacted several clinics in Seoul, but I definitely had the best gut feeling here. This trust was absolutely confirmed: The translator was incredibly warm, the whole team took a lot of time for me and all my questions. I am also completely satisfied with the result to this day. I would go there again and again and recommend it to anyone looking for a competent clinic. Thank you!

I'd love to share my incredibly positive experience at Rovl Avenue for liposuction surgery. From the moment I first contacted them for my consultation, I felt an immediate sense of welcome and ease, which continued throughout my entire journey with them.

The clinic itself is beautifully maintained and exceptionally clean, creating a very reassuring environment. Every single member of the staff I encountered was genuinely kind and pleasant, contributing significantly to a comfortable experience.

A special shout-out goes to Toni, my translator. She was an absolute gem – so kind, patient, and pleasant to interact with. She meticulously answered all of my questions, no matter how many I had, and ensured I understood every detail, which was incredibly helpful.

The doctor, Jung Rae Jun, was equally impressive. He was incredibly thorough in his explanations, detailing every aspect of the procedure and what to expect. What truly set Rovl Avenue apart from other consultations I had was their unwavering focus on safety; I felt that this was a top priority for them, unlike elsewhere. I particularly appreciated their use of an ultrasound to accurately assess the amount of fat, which demonstrated a precise and personalized approach. Dr. Jung Rae Jun also set realistic expectations regarding my results, which I found very reassuring. Throughout the entire process, I felt completely safe and well-cared for.

Beyond the procedure, Rovl Avenue also provided excellent recovery services, ensuring I was comfortable and healing well. They even went the extra mile to make sure I was well enough and prepared for my travel home, which was a huge relief.

Overall, if you're looking into liposuction and want a clinic that emphasizes professionalism, safety, and thorough care, Rovl Avenue is worth considering. I'm very satisfied with my experience and the care I received.

Recently I had thigh lipo in Rovl. From my first online consultation and my first visit everyone in the clinic is very sweet, they explained everything very thoroughly and reassured me. It made me feel very comfortable and at ease from the consultant, front desk personnel to the nurses.

Dr. Kim acknowledged  all my concerns and goal.  Answered every question I had and also I could tell he put patient safety a top priority. Never once did I feel rushed as I did with the other surgeons I had previously visited.

On the day of my surgery, I was very nervous but I knew I was in good hands he explained everything in details told me what I should expect before and after the surgery. He wasn’t over promise and went through all the consequences.

Although I am only 7 days post-op, its still swollen,  and numb in some area. But all the pain is gone and I don’t have much bruises in the back thigh area. I could sleep, walk, squat, sit comfortably. It indicate thats the Doctor was very gentle during the suction procedure.

Thank you so much Rovl Avenue, I appreciate your time and attention in smoothing out my lipo journey.

I recently had arm liposuction at Rovl and I'm really happy with both the results and the overall experience. The staff were kind and made sure I felt comfortable throughout the whole process. They were great about answering all my questions, which really helped ease my nerves.

Doctor was professional and was not pushy (mainly me being the pushy one), which made a big difference. The follow-up care was great too—they checked in to make sure everything was going smoothly during my recovery.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to get a liposuction done!

reviews.text: If you are a fan of E-Sports it is a lot of fun, even if you do not play League of Legends. You need to book tickets at least 1 day in advance (we bought ours using the NOL world website). Beer and snacks available for purchase at the venue. Such a great atmosphere. You will have more fun if you choose a team and sit with the supporters instead of in the "neutral" seats. NOTE: You can make placards on site but the only country name you can display is "Korea," city names are fine. There is a 17:00 session and a 19:00 session which require different tickets. The 2nd session will be delayed about half an hour if the first session stretches to 3 games.

We visited LOL Park without any plans and were lucky to get tickets for a match on the same day — it was an amazing experience! The atmosphere was incredible, the staff was very friendly, and the whole place is a must-visit for any League of Legends fan. Totally worth it!

Getting tickets is kinda hard. But you can still visit LoL Park (3rd floor) and watch the games on the screens in the lobby.

The PC Café offered us to test the new fighting game 2XKO made by Riot Games. For submitting feedback they offered us a drink and 30 minutes of free PC Café time

LoL Park is a must-visit place for League of Legends fans.
The atmosphere is amazing, especially during LCK match days. The screen, sound system, and stage setup make the experience feel immersive and exciting. Even if you’re not watching a live match, the place itself is iconic and worth visiting. Highly recommended for esports fans visiting Seoul.
Plethora of activities to do from store, games, food court, and the arena to view games. All reasonable priced items. Must visit for any LOL fans!

reviews.text:
We landed flew from Jeju to Gimpo and had a few hours to kill before catching out flight from Incheon to Vancouver. We followed the advice from reddit and visited the Lotte Mall Gimpo. It us a pretty easy underground walk even with my carry-on backpack.

It is a nice mall with a coffee shop "And Terrace" and an observation deck on the top floor. You have a view of the Gimpo terminal.

It's not a bad stop if you want to do some last minute shopping before flying home. Lots of major brands and good selection of food service.

***Arrive early for your flight and have a meal here***
I personally hate feeling rushed for a flight so I arrived early and took a ten minute walk through the underground passage way which is well marked.

A large variety of restaurants. The Shake Shack took close to 30minutes so to get the food around lunch time.

Knotted which I bought to eat on the plane was very good.

Massive mall, with plenty of eateries, convenience stores, supermarkets etc. can be accessed from the domestic airport prior check in. Just use the subway station and follow it till you reach the mall.

It’s the usual Lotte Mall experience, nothing very special. The basement looks more interesting than the main bulk of the building. When I went there was an interesting new space exhibit going on. There is an observation deck on the roof which gives you a decent view of the whole Gimpo airport. Probably worth a visit if you’re headed to the airport anyway.

Korea's first malling park LOTTE DEPARTMENT STORE Gimpo Airport is a complex shopping culture space where you can enjoy shopping, entertainment, leisure, and relaxation at the same time. Furthermore, an environmentally-friendly park has been established nearby the store, offering comfortable relaxation space. Great accessibility of this store helps attract not only domestic consumers but foreigners.

reviews.text:
1/2026

1979년 12월 17일 서울 중구 소공동 1번지 소재 지하 1층 지상 7층 규모의 롯데쇼핑센터로 개점했다.

1983년 한국산업은행으로부터 부지를 사들인 뒤 롯데호텔 신관 겸 백화점 본점 확장 증축 공사를 진행해 1988년 1월 28일 증축 공간을 개점했고, 1988년 11월 1일에 가서야 현재의 롯데백화점으로 이름을 바꿨다.
한동안 '롯데쇼핑센터'라는 이름을 쓴 것은 당시 서울특별시청에서 백화점의 도심지역 추가 출점을 규제했기 때문이며, 이름이 롯데백화점으로 돌아온 이유 역시 해당 규제가 이 무렵 해제되었기 때문이었다.

앞서 언급한 옛 산업은행 본점 부지와 옛 한일은행 본점 건물(현 에비뉴엘관), 옛 미도파백화점 본점 건물(현 영플라자) 등 주변의 건물들과 땅을 인수하여 리모델링한 뒤 건물과 건물을 통로로 연결했기 때문에 전체적으로는 가로로 길다.
그래서 구도상 사진 1장에 다 담기가 어려워, 보통 언론에서는 백화점 본관과 롯데호텔 서울 정도만 싣는다.

에비뉴엘, 영플라자는 별도의 건물이며, 서로 통로로 연결되어 있다. 때문에 내부 동선이 다소 부자연스럽고 일부 층수는 층고도 낮은 편이다.
예전에는 서울 최대 규모의 백화점이었으나 더현대 서울, 신세계백화점 강남점, 에비뉴엘과 합쳐진 롯데백화점 잠실점에 밀려 현재는 4위 규모로 밀려났다. 그래도 서울시내 최대 규모 백화점은 자사의 잠실점이 타이틀을 유지하는게 그나마 위안이다.

2025년 기준 매출은 전국 4위 백화점으로, 전성기 대비 지금은 꽤나 침체된 상황이지만, 약 37년 동안 전국 백화점 매출 1위를 기록하고 처음으로 연 매출 1조 원을 돌파하는 등 여러 기록을 갖고 있기 때문에, 롯데백화점에서는 여전히 핵심 점포로 대우받고 있다.  (나무위키)

From the moment we entered Lotte World, the grand size of this amusement park amazed us. The sheer scale is impressive, with four spacious indoor floors and an expansive outdoor area that offered a vibrant mix of attractions. The colourful decorations, themed zones, and lively atmosphere made it feel like stepping into a whimsical wonderland.

However, our excitement was tempered by some frustrations. Many of the popular rides such as the Atlantis were closed without prior notice, which was quite disappointing as we had been looking forward to experiencing them. The rides that were open were heavily crowded, and without purchasing the Magic Pass tickets, we found ourselves queuing for long stretches of time, often longer than the rides themselves. It quickly became clear that Magic Passes are almost essential if you want to make the most of your visit.

On the brighter side, we were able to enjoy some of the shows and smaller attractions, and the staff were very friendly and helpful throughout the day. The food stalls offered a variety of local snacks and treats, which gave us a chance to rest and take in the vibrant surroundings.

Overall, while Lotte World left a memorable impression with its scale and charm, the experience would have been far more enjoyable had more of the signature attractions been operational and the queues been less daunting. Planning ahead and investing in Magic Pass tickets is highly recommended for a smoother, more thrilling day at the park.

reviews.text:
Easily my favorite concert hall in Seoul. Modern and has good views from nearly all seats.

The staff at the ticket counter are always great at resolving issues and usually can speak English, if needed.

I wish there was a water fountain though. It’s strange that every floor of the mall has free drinking water available near the restrooms, but once you reach the concert hall, the only option is to buy refreshments from the cafe.

I really enjoyed music.

Hey buddy, got a sec? I gotta tell you about this amazing concert hall experience I had in Seoul. Over the past few months, I’ve been lucky enough to catch some seriously unforgettable performances at Lotte Concert Hall—and man, what a ride.

I was there for the GPO Rachmaninoff Symphony No.2 on October 22, 2023, and that was just the beginning. Nikolai Lugansky blew my mind with his full Rachmaninoff concertos on December 15. Then came Jaap van Zweden’s “Ode to Joy” on December 22—goosebumps, seriously. Krystian Zimerman’s piano recital on January 3, 2024 was pure magic, and the Prague Symphony Orchestra just a couple weeks later on January 18? Stunning. Oh, and let’s not forget the legendary Jonas Kaufmann on March 4, 2025. That voice? Unreal.

Now, about the hall itself—it’s inside Lotte World Mall in Jamsil, which is kinda wild, right? A huge concert hall in the middle of a shopping center. But hey, it works. It’s Seoul’s second-largest classical venue, opened back in 2016, and super easy to get to with Subway Lines 2 and 8 right nearby.

When you get there, head to the 8th floor where the box office opens an hour before the concert. They’ve got a cloak room, and if you’re feeling a little fancy (or just need a caffeine fix), there are bars on the 8th and 9th floors where you can grab coffee, water, even wine. Oh, and the vending machine on the 10th floor? Total lifesaver.

title: 루트의원

reviews.text:
In December, I underwent an FUE hair transplant at Root Hair Clinic, which surpassed all expectations. The procedure was painless, thanks to their skilled team and advanced technology. The doctor was experienced and reassuring, guiding me through each step with ease. The staff, including the English team led by Zahid, was warm, attentive, and dedicated, ensuring a comfortable experience from start to finish. Zahid, in particular, was very friendly and put a lot of effort into ensuring everything went well. The most discomfort I can think of was the injection to numb the scalp, which lasted maybe 20 seconds. It was very mild. Aftercare was pretty simple. Although it was only a few months ago, I don't remember much besides being gentle when cleaning the graft and donor area.

In South Korea, language barriers aren't a big deal. Many speak English, and there are translation apps and helpful locals if you need to communicate in Korean. Getting around and interacting is usually easy, even if you're not fluent! As someone from North America, friends and family might express worry due to their exposure to news, which tends to sensationalize the political situation with North Korea. However, it is like background noise. South Koreans are used to occasional tensions, and with their focus on daily life and development, it's more of a nuisance than a real concern. Just thought I might mention this because it was a worry before leaving home, but was quashed a few days upon arrival.

Overall, Root Hair Clinic provided exceptional care, making the hair transplant process smooth and efficient. I highly recommend them to anyone considering such a procedure.

Thanks again so much, guys. I'm really happy with the results.

I found out about Root Hair Transplant Clinic through google searching, and I thought I would reach out to them from their reviews and their website. I got a hairline  transplant using FUE5000. The whole process was very smooth and fairly easy. I messaged them through their website and was able to get a quick reply back. They provided me with the needed guidelines and informations. In total, I visited the clinic three times. First, to get an initial consultation done where I meet with the doctor to discuss what kind of hairline I would like and what they would recommened. Then the next day was the surgery day. For me, it took my about 5h to finish everything. Just make sure you have someone with you so they can come pick you up after your surgery day as you might be a little loopy from the anesthesia. Then I visited the clinic again the day after the surgery for the doctor to check the hair, and for the bandages to be taken off the hair donor area, and teaching to be done on washing and maintaining cleanliness on both the donor and grafted area. It's now been a little more than 2 weeks since my surgery, the back of my head where the hair was donated is feeling fine now, and the front grafted area is spiky and has a lot of dandruff but I guess that's just a part if the process since you can't touch them yet. Overall I am happy with the result so far and look forward to seeing how my hairline looks in 6 months to a year. I havent done too much research on hair transplant clinics, but this one was nice and the process went smoothly so I would recommend this to anyone else who is thinking of getting a hairline transplant done in Korea. Also if you worried about communication difficulties, there is a translator that you talk to throughout the whole process as well as at the clinic when you are with the staff. Good luck to everyone!

Travelled from abroad for my hair transplant (4000 hairs FUT) with all initial contact through Seoul Guide Medical.

I chose to have my consultation and surgery on the same day at my request (do not recommend, allow yourself some time to think and process consultation information!). Doctor suggested I was a better candidate for FUT rather than FUE, of which I was set on, due to my naturally thin and very blonde hair (likely more follicles to be damaged in extraction process meaning more follicle extraction required). This took me by surprise but the doctor and everyone else were extremely supportive and provided plenty of information on this procedure and still the option to proceed with FUE. I had no pressure placed on me, allowing me time to think and make a decision (I did proceed with FUT and so glad I did!).

I was accommodated well during the entire procedure ensuring I was comfortable and free from pain, with Zahid translating and checking on how I was regularly. The doctor and nurses were very comforting and professional, during all steps of the procedure.

After care was fantastic. Pharmacy is next door for convenience and instructions are given both verbally and written (there's a lot to take in so very grateful for that!). I had regular check ins via Whatsapp up to 2 weeks after the procedure with any questions I asked answered quickly and with plenty of information.

Extremely happy with the overall procedure from start to finish. From initial communication, consultation, procedure to after care, Root Hair Clinic exceeded my expectations. My husband will be using this clinic for his hair transplant in the near future and I'll be sure to recommend to anyone else looking for a hair transplant!

Thank you all, 2 weeks since surgery date and can't wait to see the results in time to come.

I set a goal for myself a few years ago to start doing things to improve myself inside and out. One of the things wanted to do in my journey of self-improvement was to restore my hair. Seoul Medical Guide and Root Hair Clinic helped me achieve this goal with confidence, ease, and medically positive results.

I began my journey online through Seoul Medical Guide, which connected me with Sam. Sam was my go-to person for all information regarding Root Hair Clinic. They provided me with all the necessary details before I made my journey from the US to South Korea for the procedure. Upon arriving in South Korea, I had a final consultation with Zahid, the clinic manager, who translated everything between me and Dr. Lee Yun Joo. The doctor took the time to answer all my questions and did not make me feel rushed, which was very reassuring. Zahid, from the surgery going forward, was my point of contact for any questions. He was very kind and patient and always got back to me in a timely manner with any inquiries.

On the day of the surgery, the only painful part was the anesthesia shot. I had prepared for it by reading other people's reviews, and I would compare the pain to going to the dentist and getting a shot of Novocaine in the gums before a procedure. It was a slight pinch and uncomfortable, but tolerable. After a minute or two, it was completely numb, and I felt nothing.

I’m currently two weeks post-op and just got my stitches taken out. The surgery I had was a FUT/FUE combo to get the maximum amount of hair possible. I was so nervous about having this procedure, but I’m so thankful to Seoul Medical Guide, Root Hair Clinic, Sam, Zahid, Dr. Lee Yun Joo, and their whole team for taking such good care of me and putting all my nerves at ease. I don’t regret my decision to go on this journey one bit. I have other things lined up for myself through Seoul Medical Guide for this winter, so I look forward to while I’m back in South Korea to stop back and see Zahid and give an in-person update on my hair growth.

Update: It has now been over 6 months since my surgery and I decided to add a before and after photo to show my results

Latest update as of 07-18-2025: It’s been 1 year since I’ve had my surgery. I’ve added two more photos to show my results after 1 year that I just took as of this date. My life has been forever changed and so thankful for Root Hair Clinic for giving my confidence back! If you’re thinking about doing it…don’t wait book your appointment now! It will forever change your life ❤️

My hair transplant experience was pleasant, and the procedure went smoothly. Although the process took several hours, the staff was kind and professional throughout. The doctor was friendly and knowledgeable. It has been two months since my surgery, and while I am still in the awkward phase, I am excited about the new growth.

As the first stop on my Seoul art adventure, the Leeum Museum of Art set an unforgettable tone—especially on a drizzly early fall afternoon when the city's rolling hills felt even more dramatic under gray skies. Tucked away in the posh Hannam-dong neighborhood, I couldn't help but smile at the parade of sleek Mercedes and BMWs gliding by; it was a subtle reminder that I'd stumbled into one of Seoul's most refined corners. The museum's modern architecture, with its clean lines and reflective glass, seemed to embrace the rain, heightening the suspense.
I arrived buzzing with anticipation, having read online that Leeum might showcase Damien Hirst's provocative pieces. Unfortunately, no spotty cows or diamond-encrusted skulls graced the walls that day—but honestly, that minor letdown only amplified my delight in what was on display. The collection leaned heavily into conceptual art, which has always held a magnetic pull for me, inviting that delicious mental unraveling where ideas linger long after the visuals fade.
Jenny Holzer's stark, LED-like truisms hit like a quiet thunderbolt, their glowing phrases probing the soul amid the patter of rain outside. I saw one of On Kawara's date paintings, a meditative masterpiece rendered with such precision that it made time feel both infinite and achingly personal. There were also plenty of works by Lee Ufan. I saw his works on Naoshima Island, too. His minimalist strokes and subtle interactions with space were pure poetry, echoing the Zen-like calm of a rainy Seoul day. Each work sparked that "aha" spark, turning a solo visit into a profound, introspective journey.
Even with the weather urging cozy cafes, I lingered for hours, emerging refreshed and eager for more. If you're in Seoul and crave art that challenges and soothes in equal measure, Leeum is a must—rain or shine.

What a wonderful museum! We truly enjoyed our visit to Leeum. The traditional exhibit is free to enter, while the special exhibits require a ticket, but they’re absolutely worth it.

We especially loved the headset system, which uses indoor GPS to provide commentary in multiple languages whenever you approach an artwork. Just note that they’ll hold onto your ID while you borrow the device, so be sure to bring one if you want the audio guide.

The highlight for us was the Lee Bul exhibit. Spanning multiple floors, it was truly epic. The scale, creativity, and boldness of her contemporary art were remarkable. I loved how they let you experience the art fixtures, not just seeing them.

Don't forget to take pictures at their iconic spiral stairs.

The gift shop is also fantastic, filled with unique items. Some of the ceramics and artifacts were pricey, but I would have happily bought them if budget wasn’t a concern.

Highly recommend!

reviews.text:
3.5 months post op - DES & ptosis correction with under eye fat repositioning

I went for surgery mid November and it’s been 14 weeks since my eyelid surgery. My main concern was my right eye’s fold getting droopier than before, causing my eyes to look uneven. I also wanted to try under eye fat repositioning because I also wanted to address the dark circles, hollowness, and a wrinkle line.

The consultation started on WhatsApp with a consultant who was fluent in English. She was very friendly and provided quick responses to all of my questions, despite the time difference (I’m from Canada). My questions were all addressed the day of or the following day during their business hours. I went with Marble PS because their other reviews online were good overall and they had some good before and after photos. They also gave me the best quote and I liked their consultation the most.

After finally making it to Korea and having the in person consultation with Dr. Suh, I felt reassured and confident in moving forward with the procedure the next day. Dr. Suh was really attentive and patient throughout the entire process. He made sure to address all of my concerns and answered any questions I had. I found that Dr. Suh focuses more on natural-looking outcomes rather than dramatic changes and if he believes a requested procedure is unnecessary or a bad idea, he will let you know. I find this important when choosing the right surgeon because this shows that they actually care. He used a toothpick to show me a few options for the creases and I went with the highest he could go without giving me “sausage eyes”.

Surgery day: Even though I had an idea of what to expect based on my friends’ experiences and what the consultant explained to me, it was still reallyyy intense lol. I remember getting put under and then all of a sudden I felt like I was going through a vortex and these colourful walls were closing in. Then after that part was over, all I could see was black and I could hear Dr. Suh speaking to the nurse and the tools they were using. I felt the tugging but it wasn’t painful, not until near the end, that was when it started to feel a little bit uncomfortable. During the surgery, Dr. Suh asked me to open and blink my eyes numerous times. I could tell he was very attentive to details because he went back and forth on both eyes many times and did not stop until he was finally satisfied. He explained later that he spent more time for my procedure because it was really asymmetrical due to one of the muscles being a lot stronger and he wanted to make it as symmetrical as possible.

After I was done, I was brought into the resting area and the consultant allowed me to stay for however long I needed. She checked in and made sure I was okay before I left. All of the staff at Marble PS were very friendly, especially the team that dealt with the foreign clients. Many thanks to my consultant, who was absolutely delightful and made me felt comfortable throughout the entire process.

Overall, I am pleased with my DES results so far. My left eye is healing a little bit slower than my right, but apparently that is normal. Most say the final results aren’t settled until at least 6 months and for some even up to a year. As for the under eye fat repositioning, they did mention that the procedure won’t correct the colour pigmentation, so I was aware of that. The procedure did not fix my dark circles, but I did notice more volume at the 2 months mark. They said it can also take a few months for it to settle so I will see in a couple of more months if that procedure was actually worth it. Overall, it was a good experience and I am glad I chose Marble PS for my procedures!

Hi fam. I got a non-incisional double eyelid surgery at Marble in Seoul mid April 2025. I am now one month post-op and wanted to share my experience.

In early April, I scheduled a consultation at Marble. I first connected with the team via KaKao Talk about 2 weeks prior to going to Seoul. The person I spoke to via KaKao was also the translator I met at the clinic, so this continuity was really great to have. During the consultation, the surgeon reviewed my eyes. The Marble surgeon, Dr. Kim Jun Hyung gave the option to do an incisional surgery, which would last forever, but as I was going to Japan after I wouldn't have an easy way to get the stitches removed. The surgeon used little toothpicks to show me different options for eyelid shapes, which was something I didn’t have the luxury to pick the first time around. He also told me that they would try to take out the old line during my new surgery. I had a few other consultations planned, but because I vibed quite well with the Marble team I decided to cancel the consultation and go with Marble.

On the day of the surgery, you are asked not to eat/drink for at least 4 hours prior to surgery, which was totally fine for me. They take you into a little changing room where you’ll get changed into surgical robes with lockers for your stuff. I also met with the surgeon one more time to decide on the final shape, which they drew out with a pen on my eyelid. Soon I was taken to the surgery room. It was a little scary at first as there are restraints to make sure you don’t move excessively during the surgery, but once the anesthesia hit, time went by really fast. The whole process took about 45 min but as the person in the chair it doesn’t feel that long. Afterwards you are taken into a dark room with comfortable chairs. I also got an ice pack to put on my eyes to reduce swelling.

Once the surgery ended, I was pretty much immediately able to move around and get back to exploring Seoul. Of course my eyes were puffy and red but in Gangnam it really isn’t uncommon at all for people who just got plastic surgery to be walking around. If you can bring a friend for emotional support that would be best, but even alone it shouldn’t be a big deal! I rested a little bit earlier than the rest of my travel days but other than that the surgery did not hinder any of my travel plans.

During the first few days, I was asked to use the ice pack to reduce swelling. During this time as the swelling gradually decreased I did form bruising in my eyelids, which went through the usual colors of purple -> red -> yellow. These went away around the 1 week mark. I’ve posted some photos below with key time points up till today.

Finally as a wrap up, I will say that for the first week or so post-op, sometimes in the morning, the shape of one eyelid was higher than the other. I think this was just morning puffiness because they looked more even by the afternoon. Also there is one needle point that is slightly visible when I close my eyes. Maybe it will go away over time? None of these are deal-breakers for me. I’m so happy to have even and pretty (to me) eyes again.

I did Sub-brow lift and Undereye Fat Repositioning with Dr. Suh, he was very patient, very professional, he took his time listening my questions/needs carefully, that made me feel safe to do surgery with him. They have in-house translator and my one was Ms. Heekyung, she was very nice and good at her job until i didn’t need to bring my own. The doctor didn’t force me to do or suggest any unnecessary surgery without me asking, his suggestions were more to natural-looks which I was seeking for. If you want dramatic changes, I believe they can do it as well. I had the same day surgery, it took around 2 hrs for both surgery, I had local anaesthesia and sedation, sub-brow lift was already done when I woke up, under-eye surgery got a lot of pullings and some pain but bearable, recovery time was smooth and easy. Didn’t have any pain from 2nd day onwards, I could start to walk around for sight-seeing and shopping. My surgery was done on 3rd Jun and stitches were removed on 9th Jun, and had red light treatment for swelling for 15 mins. The clinic provided one microwavable ice pack, bought medicines at pharmacy downstairs of the clinic. You can see attached photos for the result. I definitely look fresher and slightly younger. But I wish I requested to cut a bit more skin for Sub-brow lift, feel still a bit sagging. Or maybe this is the best for me.

Sub-brow lift - 1.65 mil won
Under-eye fat repositioning - 1.65 mil won

I had incisional double eyelid surgery, ptosis correction, blepharoplasty, and epicanthoplasty with Dr. Suh at Marble. He was the only doctor who recommended epicanthoplasty, and although I hadn’t considered it, I’m so glad I trusted his advice. He was honest about my eye asymmetry and explained he would do his best to make them as even as possible.

I’m about 1.5 months post-op and already very happy with the results! Dr. Suh was very attentive, and Heekyung, the in-house translator, was amazing; she thoroughly explained the process and aftercare and answered every single question from the beginning to very end. She even gave me extra gauze and supplies to help with my bruising and swelling.

Recovery was quicker than I expected with most of the bruising was gone by day four. There’s still some swelling left, and my left eye remains a bit more swollen than my right but I'm soo happy with my results

UPDATE* - I'm now two months post-surgery at Marble. Most of the swelling has gone down, and my eyes are looking more defined yet natural. While one eye is still slightly puffier but I can already see how much more balanced my overall appearance is.

Dr Suh from Marble Plastic Surgery was very detailed, considered and professional throughout the entire consultation and surgery itself. I had an incisional double eyelid surgery with ptosis correction and epicanthoplasty, which was recommended by Dr Suh.
It’s currently 2 weeks after the operation, and I’m very pleased with the result. The initial swelling and bruising has settled with some mild redness remaining at the epicanthoplasty site. I'm excited to see the progress in the coming months. My before and after are attached below.

21/11/24 Update:
- It is now 4 weeks post the operation and I am still happy with the progress. The swelling has reduced further, and opening my eyes feels effortless. I'm still waiting for the epicanthoplasty site to completely heal over with no residual redness - there's still some mild redness/lumps/bumps, but this seems to be easing with time too.

10/01/25 Update:
- My final update on the double eyelid surgery - I'm extremely happy with the result, and am now able to add cosmetic lash extensions as well (as pictured).
The incisional scar is visible when I close my eyes, however it is faint and causes no harm to day to day functioning.

title: 매헌 윤봉길의사 기념관
google_addr: 99 Maeheon-ro, Seocho District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: A small scale museum of a Korean independence activist during Japanese occupation in Korea. Admission is free and audio guide in English is available. Estimated tour time 30 mins.

A memorial park for the famous freedom fighter Yun Bonggil, located in Seoul's Kang Nam region.
Yun was born in 1908, 2 years before Korea became Japan's colony.
Yun's father was a poor farmer, but his family was the extremely honorable Yun clan of Papyoung,  and even as a child,  he was proud and patriotic.
Yun wanted to do anything for liberation of Korea, so he left behind his parents, beloved wife and children and went to China, to become a freedom fighter.

On 29 April, 1932, during the birthday celebration ceremony of Hirohito, the then emperor, in Shanghai, China, on the last note of Kimikayo, Japanese national anthem, Yun succeeded in a solo operation of throwing a bomb and killing highest Japanese generals in China, including Sirakawa Yosinori, the head of Japanese army in control of China.  This operation was ordered by the Korean government in exile.

(Yun was driven to the venue by George Ashmore Fitch, the famous US missionary who was later known as one of the brave persons in the  Nanjing Massacre.)

Yun's operation was desicive for the Korean government in exile getting much needed Chinese support, and any proud Chinese could not openly abandon it after this operation, so Japan could not destroy it.

Yun was tried by Japanese army, as an enemy soldier, not as a terrorist, unlike other Korean freedom fighters, because Japanese Army wanted to honor their dead generals as being killed in a military battle, not being harmed by a civilian.

Yun was executed and buried secretly beneath a public road in Noda hill, Kanajawa, Japan in 1932.  He was only 24.  His children had to endure everyday harassment in school by Japanese teachers.

Later, in 1946, his bone was brought home with the help of Koreans and Japanese citizens.

Yun was buried in Hyo Chang park, Seoul, and we Koreans could build  this memorial museum for him, because Japan, one of Korea's  amicable partners now, already tried him as a soldier on duty, not a terrorist, in 1932.

reviews.text: Nanta in Myeongdong, Seoul is an absolute gem, and after my fourth viewing, I’m still hooked. Each performance brings a fresh energy, wit, and precision that never fails to impress. The show’s creative fusion of culinary rhythm, comedy, and high-energy percussion keeps me on the edge of my seat every time I visit Seoul, and I always find myself eagerly anticipating the next watch. The pacing is tight, the performers are incredibly skilled, and the interactive moments add a playful, memorable touch that makes the experience feel personal rather than just a spectacle. If you’re in Seoul and want a uniquely entertaining, high-spirited show that’s worth returning to again and again, Nanta in Myeongdong is a must-see. I can’t wait for my next visit.

We had such an enjoyable time at the Nanta Musical Show with the Green Team.

It’s a truly entertaining theatrical experience and easy to follow along. The show is almost narrativeless, yet the storyline flows seamlessly from one scene to the next; bit romance, bit comedy, bit tension. No abrupt shifts, just a smooth, rhythmic pace that keeps you fully engaged from start to finish.

It was also the perfect spot to rest and unwind after all the shopping and snacking along Myeongdong Street. The audience engagement made everything even funnier, and the cast really knows how to pull everyone in. Beyond the comedy, the show also showcases elements of Korean culture, traditional drums, kitchen rhythm, food culture, and a bit of artistry woven throughout.

Nanta Show Review (Black Team)
Absolutely hilarious and entertaining — perfect for families, especially those with teens! The musical performers were incredibly skilled, blending rhythm, humour, bit of romance and theatre seamlessly. It’s an absolute must-watch show when you’re in South Korea. Lockers are avail free of charge to store shopping bags. Strictly no photo/video when it starts.  Some lucky audiences may get to be on stage.

Our performance was by the Black Team, and they were fantastic! After the show, you can queue to take photos with the cast. The staff are super efficient — they’ll help use your phone or camera and snap multiple shots within seconds. A truly fun and memorable experience!

The Nanta show is excellent, hilarious, and incredibly easy to follow even if you don't speak Korean. The actors are very funny and expressive. They are very energetic. My only note is that the venue got quite hot and stuffy once the theater filled up.

Ok, I wasn't sure what to expect, wow, wow, wow!!! This show was so much fun. The sounds, the visuals, and the actors were all brilliant. I mean laugh out loud hilarious. Great show for all ages. U do not have to speak Korean to enjoy it either. U get the full jist of the shown from the beginning. The theater is very cozy with make the show even better. Im not too sure how it would be for those who may be wheelchair bound. There is an elevator, but i didn't see any area, in the actual theater, to accommodate the chairs.

reviews.text:
~throw back to mid of November 2025~

This area is such a great place to explore!
There are so many shops, offering a wide range of food, clothing, beauty products, and more.
Each store is spacious and fun to shop and explore!!

Around the area, you’ll also find many street vendors selling local food and delicacies.
The prices are reasonable — not too high or too cheap — and definitely worth trying.

My favourite time to visit is during the Christmas season, when the decorations are everywhere and the atmosphere is absolutely festive and lively.

A Korean experience that all visitors should not miss. Atmospheric shopping, a wonderful and vast selection of shops. Good for people watching and also offers a huge selection of food to choose from.

The vibes during the day and evening are very different. Do go at different times to savour the sights.

This place comes alive at night, especially on weekends. There is a lot of police presence, so there is a sense of safety.

Recommended, a must-go.

It is incredibly fun with lots of things to see and eat, especially the legendary street food stalls. While the prices can be a bit expensive and it is clearly targeting tourists, the energy is infectious. It’s the perfect place to get lost in the crowds, shop for K-beauty, and try every snack imaginable!

Myeongdong Street Food is a nice place to try a lot of different Korean snacks in one area. There are plenty of choices, savory and sweet, and most of the flavors are easy to enjoy for international tourists (not too strong or unusual).

Many stalls cook the food fresh, so it’s warm and better compared to pre-made snacks. Portions are good for sharing or trying a few items while walking around. The area is also convenient and lively, so it’s a simple stop if you’re already shopping in Myeongdong.

Overall, it’s a solid street food spot with good variety and generally tasty, tourist-friendly flavors.

I tried Lafullen, performed by Dr. Kwon, who was very detailed and attentive in ensuring my face looked its best. The whole treatment process was smooth and felt safe. I’m really happy with the results and will definitely come back again!

This was my first time getting facial treatment ever! And I had a great experience with a reasonable price here at Mods clinic!!

I had a consultation appointment with Dr. Kim in the morning and got Ulthera Prime treatment done in the evening of that same day. Dr. Kim was professional and knowledgeable yet friendly. For a first timer I had a lot of questions. The dr. was able to answer all my questions and concerns. More importantly he didn’t try to upsell or pushy at all!

Even though Ulthera Prime maybe less painful than the previous version, I could feel the pain (I’m not going to lie) but it was bearable! Again the dr. tried to talk to me as a distraction and comfort me, so I didn’t feel like I suffered much.

It was my first time in Korea for skin treatment. I had Potenza and PRP done. The price was much more affordable compared to what I paid in Los Angeles. I don’t speak Korean, but there was a translator with me the entire time. I’ll definitely come back again! :)

You are forced to rent helmits and purchase gloves. Cloth gloves are for safety reasons apparently? Been to ice rinks around the world, and this rink has the strictest skating rules I have ever seen. Such a shame. Even more of a shame when there are six year olds in the same rink at a lesser skill level allowed to break all those rules because they are paying for a lesson. Weird double standards, I again do not recommend to anyone who is moderately serious about skating and trying to skate during holiday.

title: 목멱산 봉수대 터
google_addr: 8-1 Yejang-dong, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Its an early warning system to transmit news about enemy invasion from great distances. Literally the "beacon hill in the capital" which is final relay site of all the long distance communication of this type in the city. Fire (by night) and smoke (during the day) signals where used to relay important emergency news from the borders to the capital. The beacon hill is one of the 5 stations that originally stood in the area.

Namsan Beacon Station, nestled near N Seoul Tower, is a charming historical site that once served as a crucial communication hub during the Joseon Dynasty. Today, it offers visitors a peaceful retreat with scenic views of Seoul, blending history with natural beauty. The restored beacon mound and informative plaques provide a glimpse into Korea’s past, while the surrounding walking paths and lush greenery make it a perfect spot for a leisurely stroll. Less crowded than the nearby tower, it’s a hidden gem for history buffs and those seeking a quieter moment with a view. A small but worthwhile stop to appreciate Seoul’s layered heritage.

This was in the same vicinity as namsan tower.

I did not see the morning ceremony wuth the guards as we came by in the afternoon early evening.

Nice spot for photos and viewpoint.

Tickets are not required for this attraction

This is probably the most historical part of Namsan, as it was used for fire/smoke signals throughout the Joseon dynasty. The beacon mound in place currently is new construction (built in 1993), although supposedly they were exhaustive in their research and construction, trying to make this as close as possible to the original. Not a must-see attraction by any meanas, but it is at the summit of Namsan with the observation tower and all that, so you might as well visit if you come to Namsan
Not much to see except for its historic past. At 11am, you see the guards in their beautiful uniforms.

title: 몽촌토성
google_addr: 424 Olympic-ro, Songpa District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: 백제시대 판촉식 성벽 올림픽공원속에 있는데 둘레를 걸으면 하루 10,000보가 됩니다

1988년 서울 올림픽을 위해 한강 변에 경기장과 선수촌을 지었다. 올림픽이 끝난 뒤 이 구역에 88 올림픽을 기념하여 몽촌토성을 중심으로 공원을 조성했다. 몽촌토성은 백제 초기의 토성으로 전체 둘레는 약 2.7㎞에 달한다. 성벽 높이는 현재 6~40m로 지점에 따라 차이가 있다. 성벽 바깥쪽에 목책(나무로 만든 울타리)이 있으며, 토성을 감싸는 해자(적의 침입을 막기 위해 성 주위를 둘러서 판 못)가 있다. 토성 내부에는 백제 초기의 움집터와 함께 토성 발굴 당시 발견된 유물이 전시된 몽촌역사관이 있다. 약 2.4㎞의 몽촌토성 산책로가 함께 조성돼 있다. 백제 역사의 숨결과 88서울 올림픽의 감동을 따라 몽촌토성 산책로를 걸어보았다.
몽촌토성 둘레길입니다.
걷기 좋아요.

title: 무계원
google_addr: 4-1 Changuimun-ro 11-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
서울시 종로구 부암동 인왕산 자락에 위치한 옛 안평대군 거처에 마련한 한국전통 문화공간입니다. 본체와 별체를 포함한 4개동에서 체험, 전시,공연,대관 등 다양한 문화예술프로그램이 운영되는 곳입니다. 특히 눈여겨 볼만한 것은 조선시대 안견이 그린 "몽유도원도"입니다. 몽유도원도는 세종대왕의 3째 아들인 안평대군이 꿈속에서 본 무릉도원을 화가인 안견에게 이야기한 것을 안견이 3일만에 완성한 대작입니다.
This traditional Korean cultural space, located at the foot of Inwangsan Mountain in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul, is housed in the former residence of Prince Anpyeong. A variety of cultural and artistic programs, including hands-on experiences, exhibitions, performances, and rentals, are offered across four buildings, including the main building and annexes. A particular highlight is the Joseon Dynasty-era painting "Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land." This masterpiece, completed in just three days, reflects a dream Prince Anpyeong, the third son of King Sejong, had dreamed of, and told the artist about it.
안평대군의 이상향이 안견의 몽유도원도로 탄생한 장소.  종로에 있던 오진암을 그대로 옮겨와 아름다운 한옥의 모습을 재현했다고 한다.  주차장도 편리하고 고즈넉한 한옥에서 여유있게 둘러보기 좋은 곳.

종로구 부암동에 위치한 전통문화공간 입니다. 원래는 익선동에 있던 한옥 건물인데, 조선말 서화가 이병직의 집이기도 했고, 7.4남북공동성명을 도출해낸 장소였다고 합니다. 이곳은 음식점인 오진암으로 운영되다가 이 건물자재를 이용하여 현재의 위치에 한옥문화공간으로 지었다고 합니다. 현재 위치는 안견이 몽유도원도를 그리게한 장소로 유명하며 조그만 방한켠에서 몽유도원도의 복사본을 전시하여 자세하게 설명을 하는 코너가 있읍니다. 전시가 아니더라도 한옥의 아름다움을 느낄수 있는 특별한 공간인거 같습니다.
오진암이라는 조선시대 요정집(고오급 술집)을 개조하여 문화재로 만든 곳으로, 현재는 원래 목적과 상관없는 한옥전시, 전통문화 전시, 에티켓교육 등을 하는 곳으로 거듭나 사용되고 있습니다. 한옥문화 체험으로 방문하시면 좋을 것 같습니다. 입장료 따로 없고 주차장 있습니다.

If you're into clean, simple, and effortlessly cool fashion, Musinsa Standard is a must-visit. Located inside Lotte World Tower, this store showcases the best of modern Korean minimalism at very reasonable prices.

Clothing Selection:
Musinsa Standard carries both men's and women's fashion, from casual basics like t-shirts and jeans to more tailored pieces like trousers and structured jackets. Most items come in neutral or muted tones—think beige, white, black, grey, and soft pastels. Perfect for mixing and matching.

Quality & Style:
For the price, the quality is impressive. The fabrics feel nice, cuts are clean, and the designs are timeless. It’s the kind of clothing you can wear daily and still look put together.

Pros:

Affordable yet high-quality

Stylish in a minimal, Korean way

Easy to find pieces that go with everything

Wide range of sizes

Great customer service

reviews.text:
A beautiful, very historical looking building right outside of the modern Seoul Station. The architecture really stands out, classic red brick, grand windows, and elegant interior details that make it feel like you’ve stepped back in time. It’s a nice contrast to the busy, modern station.

There are exhibitions and cultural displays inside, though it depends on what’s on when you visit. I wasn’t entirely sure why it’s called “284,” but overall it’s worth a quick stop if you appreciate historic buildings and architecture.

After shopping for snacks and fruits and korean items to bring back home, decided too heavy our shopping bags and went to look for taxi stand to call local kakaoT cab. Found this beautiful building beside our Lotte mall. Found out it's 100 years old building, former Seoul train station. As its was drizzling and quite cold, we took photos from where we were waiting for our cab to arrive.

This building was the vintage Seoul station built 100years ago and now located next to Seoul station. Though it was not functioning as train platform but it has been restructured and used as a various cultural exhibition. You can normally get inside freely but currently they have paid exhibition for periods.
Love the exhibition and the atmosphere of the space. It will feel like a little exploration of a historical building.

From April 25 to May 18, 2025, in celebration of the 100th anniversary of the opening of the former Seoul Station, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Craft & Design Foundation held the ’Seoul Department Store - Local to Seoul 100 Diaries‘ exhibition at Culture Station Seoul 284, introducing famous places from all over the country and allowing visitors to see over 100 local lifestyle and cultural brands in one place.
Seoul Department Store introduced local cultural resources through images and spaces by organizing the unique tastes, styles, and games of each region in the form of experiences and sales. The first floor exhibition space introduces local brands and cultures of each of the seven train lines, and the second floor has a space where you can purchase related products.

As the first stop on my Seoul art adventure, the Leeum Museum of Art set an unforgettable tone—especially on a drizzly early fall afternoon when the city's rolling hills felt even more dramatic under gray skies. Tucked away in the posh Hannam-dong neighborhood, I couldn't help but smile at the parade of sleek Mercedes and BMWs gliding by; it was a subtle reminder that I'd stumbled into one of Seoul's most refined corners. The museum's modern architecture, with its clean lines and reflective glass, seemed to embrace the rain, heightening the suspense.
I arrived buzzing with anticipation, having read online that Leeum might showcase Damien Hirst's provocative pieces. Unfortunately, no spotty cows or diamond-encrusted skulls graced the walls that day—but honestly, that minor letdown only amplified my delight in what was on display. The collection leaned heavily into conceptual art, which has always held a magnetic pull for me, inviting that delicious mental unraveling where ideas linger long after the visuals fade.
Jenny Holzer's stark, LED-like truisms hit like a quiet thunderbolt, their glowing phrases probing the soul amid the patter of rain outside. I saw one of On Kawara's date paintings, a meditative masterpiece rendered with such precision that it made time feel both infinite and achingly personal. There were also plenty of works by Lee Ufan. I saw his works on Naoshima Island, too. His minimalist strokes and subtle interactions with space were pure poetry, echoing the Zen-like calm of a rainy Seoul day. Each work sparked that "aha" spark, turning a solo visit into a profound, introspective journey.
Even with the weather urging cozy cafes, I lingered for hours, emerging refreshed and eager for more. If you're in Seoul and crave art that challenges and soothes in equal measure, Leeum is a must—rain or shine.

What a wonderful museum! We truly enjoyed our visit to Leeum. The traditional exhibit is free to enter, while the special exhibits require a ticket, but they’re absolutely worth it.

We especially loved the headset system, which uses indoor GPS to provide commentary in multiple languages whenever you approach an artwork. Just note that they’ll hold onto your ID while you borrow the device, so be sure to bring one if you want the audio guide.

The highlight for us was the Lee Bul exhibit. Spanning multiple floors, it was truly epic. The scale, creativity, and boldness of her contemporary art were remarkable. I loved how they let you experience the art fixtures, not just seeing them.

Don't forget to take pictures at their iconic spiral stairs.

The gift shop is also fantastic, filled with unique items. Some of the ceramics and artifacts were pricey, but I would have happily bought them if budget wasn’t a concern.

Highly recommend!

reviews.text:
たまたまソウルから乗った電車、車窓から見つけた「何か博物館みたいな新しい建物」。全部聞き取れなかったが「・・democracy･･ museum･･･」と車内放送。
ソウルから一駅、南営駅から徒歩3分。もともとあった旧南営洞対共分室(M2)の敷地に新たに常設・特別展の展示棟(M1)、教育棟(E)を併設してオープンしたのが2025年6月10日。
M1
韓国の民主化運動の歴史の展示と、民主主義を改めて考えさせられる空間。それぞれ壁面一杯の 「LED ○ タッチスクリーン」は日本語でも表され、とても分かりやすい。2001年から民主化運動に関する史料を寄贈してくれた日本人を含む個人・団体も記録されている。後半には民主主義を小学校低学年でも理解が進められるような内容もあり、来館者のキャッチメントエリアを拡大している。
M2
1987年「6・10民主化抗争」の発端となった民主化運動リーダーの朴鐘哲が拷問致死に至った建物、定礎には1976年と刻まれている。悲劇の場所、取調室が生々しくも丁寧に保存されている。胸がつぶれる思いだが、民主化を悲願として命がけで勝ち取ったシンボルとして保存しているのだから、韓国国民に敬意を払う思いで見学。
通常は施錠されており、来館の際は先ず「M1 受付で時間予約」、「M2観覧時間になったら再度受付集合」、「M2へ移動」。
定期解説は毎日M1、2共に各2回とのことですが時間は不明。わたくしたちは他の観覧者2名と一緒に M2の建物入口を開鍵して貰い、自由観覧でした。
【感想】
改めて日本人の「無知の知」を思い知らされるとともに、韓国の「黒歴史でもしっかりと記録し伝承する」強烈な意思を実感する。
建国を1948年とすれば1988年ソウルオリンピックまでの間、軍事・独裁政権下で庶民はずっと民主化を目指してきたのか･･･。
翻って日本。憲法はGHQが1週間で作ったのでは･･･。そもそも慰安婦問題・強制労働問題、遡れば秀吉の朝鮮出兵時の敵兵耳鼻剃り落とし・関東大震災時の朝鮮人虐等々･･･学校では教えなかった。
日本は自らの黒歴史を認知しない・させない悲しい文化が歴然とある。大人になった日本人は他山の石として未だ未だ勉強していかないと。
訪問日2025/12/5

Mario Outlet in Gasan-dong, Seoul, is Asia's largest downtown fashion outlet, featuring over 600 brands across three connected buildings with discounts often ranging from 40-50%. Located near Gasan Digital Complex Station (Line 7), it offers extensive shopping for apparel, luxury goods, and, specifically, Korean fashion brands.
Key Details
Location: 23 Digital-ro 9-gil, Geumcheon-gu, Seoul.
Hours: Monday-Thursday 10:30-21:00, Friday-Sunday 10:30-21:30.
Structure: Three halls (Mario Fashion Town) specializing in fashion, outdoor gear, and accessories.
Brands: Over 600 local and international brands, featuring a "No Brand Shop" and Daiso.
Amenities: Food courts (mainly in Hall 3), tax refund services, and lockers on the first floor.
Transportation: A short walk from Exit 4 of Gasan Digital Complex Station (Subway Lines 1 & 7).
Shopping Tips
Best Time: Friday to Sunday for the best selection, though it can be crowded.
Activities: Plan to spend at least 3 hours exploring the three buildings.
Deals: Look for additional discounts on top of marked prices, especially for winter clothing in October or summer clothes in April.
Nearby: Lotte Factory Outlet and W-Mall are located nearby for more options.

reviews.text:
N Seoul Tower is one of the best places to enjoy a full panoramic view of Seoul. From the observation deck, you can see the Han River, modern skyscrapers, and the entire city spread out below, especially beautiful at sunset and at night when the city lights come on.

The area around the tower is clean and well organized, with many photo spots, the famous love locks area, and cafés to relax. The cable car is convenient, but walking up the mountain is also a great option if you enjoy nature and fresh air.

The staff are friendly and the signs are clear, making it easy for visitors to get around. This is a must-visit place in Seoul, perfect for couples, families, and anyone who wants to experience the romantic atmosphere of the city.

Very nice park in the 명동 area of Seoul. I enjoyed another hike after eating lunch close by. Very scenic with nice fall breeze on a Monday afternoon. Pretty views everywhere and it wasn’t too crowded.

I was fortunate to make the long walk (around 5km), easy to west, twice in the last week. Up from the east part, starting at Dongguk University Station and Jangchungdan Park up through Seoul Namsan Park to the tower and then down to Myeong-dong on the west site. It's strikingly beautiful a great climb, some steps are numbered, between those and the ones you don't count I imagine it's the equivalent to about 1,000 steps up the mountain and there are also a few steeper inclines. The steps, paths and roads are in excellent condition, everything is so clean and well signposted in many languages. You can also use N aver Maps to get you there.

The walk from Dongguk University Station to the base of Namsan Seoul Tower covers approximately 2.2 miles (3.6 km) with an elevation gain of about 797 feet (243 meters).

This route is one of the most rewarding ways to reach Namsan Tower, especially if you're seeking a blend of urban forest, cultural landmarks, and a bit of cardio. If you're up for it, you can extend your walk along the Namsan Trail network, which spans nearly 8 km across the mountain.

Outstanding urban park perfect for walking, running, and cycling! Features multiple trails and beautiful paved, hilly roads with stunning viewpoints. Well-maintained with convenient public facilities. The place comes alive at 5am with enthusiastic athletes - such great energy! Plenty of shaded areas to rest. A true urban gem!

reviews.text:
The Towering Tribute to Kim Gu: A Namsan Park Landmark

Erected in August 1969, this 10-meter statue commemorates the patriotic spirit of Kim Gu, a fervent voice and tireless organizer in the tumultuous years of Japanese colonial rule. He dedicated his life to the cause of Korean independence, and his leadership within the Korean Provisional Government was instrumental in shaping the nation that would eventually emerge after liberation. Standing tall, the statue captures not just Kim Gu's physical presence but also the immense respect and admiration he commanded as a symbol of resistance and unity. Facing the spacious plaza, it's as if his gaze still sweeps over the nation he fought so hard to liberate, a poignant connection between past sacrifice and present-day freedom.

Surrounded by the tranquil embrace of Baekbeom Plaza (백범광장공원) in Namsan Park, with well-maintained paths, the statue offers a moment for quiet reflection on a pivotal chapter in Korean history. Visiting this statue is not just about seeing a historical monument; it's about connecting with the enduring spirit of a nation and honoring the sacrifices made for its liberty.

GETTING HERE
* Subway: Exit 4 at Hoehyeon 회현역 station (blue line)
* Bus: 01A or 01B at Namsan Library
* Bus: 01A at Baekbeom Plaza (백범광장공원)
* Bus: 402, 405 at Hilton Hotel

수준높은 현대 한글, 한문 서예, 문인화를 만날 수 있다.
23년 02월 중순인 현재에는 동방대학원대학교 서예강사과정 교수전이 열리고 있었다.
역시 기대했던대로 전문 서예인을 교수하는 분들의 작품들이 전시되고있어 그 수준이 매우 훌륭했다.
조금 아쉬웠던 점은, 주로 한문서예작품이 많았는데 일반인들의 작품이해를 돕기위해 작품에 대한 주석을 간단하게나마 첨부해준다면 서예나 한문에 익숙하지 않은 분들의 작품 감상에 큰 도움이 되지 않을까 싶다.
우리문화의 큰 부분을 차지하고 있는 한글과 한문, 그리고 문인화의 자취를 느껴보기에 매우 훌륭한 곳이다.
입장료 무료, 전시는 보통 10여일 단위로 이루어지며 한달에 2~3회 전시작품이 바뀐다.

title: 백인제가옥
google_addr: 16 Bukchon-ro 7-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: My favorite part of the Bukchon area. The house is incredibly well-kept and rich with history, having served as a home for a pioneering surgeon. It’s a beautiful building that blends perfectly with its surroundings not too flashy but definitely not boring. It feels very authentic and provides a great look at how upper-class Seoul residents lived in the early 1900s. Best of all, it's free and very peaceful!

This house is open to the public for free, and they even offer guided tours at specific times. It was built during the Japanese colonial period, so its structure is a bit different from other houses.

After many years and different owners, it is now managed by the government, and part of the building is used as office space.

I highly recommend visiting this place when you’re in the nearby hanok village.

Other than the culture center, this was the most comprehensive and free house museum in the area. Some rooms were off-limits, but you can see the decors through the glass windows. You can expect to spend about 30 mins here.

A visit to Baek Inje's House is highly recommended if you're in Bukchon. Built during the Japanese colonial era by a pro-Japanese collaborator, the architecture is fascinating. The building is a remarkable blend of Korean, Western, and Japanese design. The size is about 3300 square meters. Both the building and the courtyard are really impressive. Best of all? Admission is free! Also, you can reserve a free 40 mins tour of the house on Naver map which work better than Google maps in Korea.

Terrific - this was such a lovely and interesting part of the Bukchon area. The house (indeed the whole surrounding area) is incredibly so well-kept and is a beautiful reflection of how the "upper-class" residents of Seoul lived in the early 1900s. Highly recommended when in the area.

reviews.text:
The Starfield Library inside COEX Mall is a truly special place. It’s huge, open, and impressive, and you can access it from different sides of the mall. The space feels iconic the moment you step in.

The library is open and in two-floor space, with elevators and escalators connecting the levels. There’s a Starbucks inside, so you can grab a coffee and enjoy the atmosphere. Normally, there are many areas to sit, read, study, or just pause for a moment. It’s also a very instagram picture friendly place, with lots of beautiful spots for making pictures.

That said, it’s unfortunately very overcrowded. If you want to enjoy it in a calmer way, you really need to come early on a weekday. On weekends and in the afternoons, it’s extremely busy, with many tourists and visitors. It can get noisy, and it’s hard to take nice pictures or find a quiet corner.

Right now, because of the crowds, most all of the seating and reading areas are closed, which honestly made me a bit sad. It takes away from the original purpose of the space as a place to read, study, and slow down.

Still, it remains an impressive and unique library, and if you catch it at the right time, it can be a beautiful experience

Absolute must-visit if you are in Seoul! It’s such a unique and pretty space. the massive bookshelves are breathtaking and make it a perfect spot to take pictures. I love that it’s located indoors within the mall, so it’s a great escape from the weather. Despite the hustle and bustle, you’ll see people reading and studying, giving it a real library feel alongside the nearby coffee shops, restaurants, and stores. A truly iconic landmark!

An iconic library and definitely a must see in Seoul. The space is beautiful and impressive, especially the tall shelves filled with books. It is a great place to take photos, grab a coffee, and just relax for a bit. The atmosphere is calm and cozy, perfect if you want a quiet break while exploring the city. A nice spot to slow down and enjoy the surroundings.

One of the rare sight to see and should be followed by everyone as it maybe their culture but i had to admire it as this is a modern type of library thing combined in a settings of being inside of a mall but it is still filled with kids and parents who are teaching and read together with a very mixh beautiful bonds. The youth also do their own stuff and readings. Well due to its magnificent architecture and layout, it cant be denied for tourists flocking to be here and take the picture of it. My advice to the tourist, be polite and don’t disturb the locals as for them itself a daily activity and for us its a trip. The overall atmosphere was chaotic as we visited during the public holidays and everyone was rushed in and packed over. The settings ans architecture was amazing to see as the stacking of racks was very much thoughtful. For some people mentioned there is nothing to see because it should be as its a library and we should consume the materials and not just trying to to get a shot. Overall a fun place and thoughtful ones to visit with your family and friends

서울특별시 성북구에 있는 고려전기 승려 담진이 창건한 사찰.

대한불교보문종의 총본산이다. 1115년(예종 10)에 담진(曇眞)이 비구니의 수련장으로 창건하였다. 창건 당시에는 조그만 암자로, 탑골에 있었으므로 탑골 승방이라 하였다. 그 뒤 1692년(숙종 18)에 대웅전을 개축하는 등 수차례 중수를 하였으며, 1945년부터 비구니 은영(恩榮)이 주지로 취임하면서 절을 크게 중창하였다.

원래는 조계종 산하의 소속 사찰이었으나 1972년 독립하여 보문종을 창종하고 보문종의 본산이 되었는데, 현재 그 규모면에서 굴지의 거찰(巨刹)이 되었다.

현존하는 당우로는 대웅전을 비롯하여 극락전 · 석굴암 · 호지문 · 선불장(選佛場) · 보광전(普光殿) · 산령각(山靈閣) · 석굴암노전(石窟庵爐殿) · 삼성각(三聖閣) · 별당 · 요사채, 한의원 및 특별양로원이 있는 시자원(施慈園) 등이 있다.

이 가운데 석굴암은 은영이 그 분야의 권위자를 모아 준공위원회를 구성하여 조각과 설계를 하였고, 공사비만 1억을 들여 1972년 부처님 오신 날에 착공하였으며 3년 6개월의 역사 끝에 점안식을 가졌다. 경주 석굴암과 똑같은 규모로 만들었으나, 구성면에서 볼 때 경주 석굴암은 정면이 1문인 데 비하여 이곳은 3문이며, 실내 벽을 이중으로 만들고 실내 천장으로 공기가 유통되게 하였다. 단지, 경주 석굴암의 전실에 있는 팔부신중상(八部神衆像)을 이곳에서는 생략하고 있다.

특기할 만한 오래된 문화유산은 없으나 석굴암 앞의 높은 단 위에 세워진 팔각구층석탑은 강원도 오대산 월정사(月精寺)의 팔각구층석탑을 그대로 재현한 것으로, 탑 안에는 인도에서 가져온 석가여래 진신사리가 봉안되어 있다. 이 절은 세계 유일의 비구니들만으로 구성된 보문종의 총본산으로서 언제나 150명이 넘는 비구니들이 수도하고 있을 뿐 아니라 수도의 분위기가 특히 엄숙한 도량이다.
