reviews.text: Incredible and beautiful place. It has several temples and the big one has 3000 golden Buddhas. Monks live there and are well preserved. Behind the temple is the trail for the mountain. Nice place to visit.

In a country proudly steeped in culture, with so many temples around, Bongwonsa must truly be one of the few unspoilt ones. This is because it is located on a hill top.

I’ve seen pictures of Bongwonsa at spring time and notices the pride of the caretakers to keep it neat and spruced at all times for all visitors.

As with any visit to a place of worship, do treat the place with utmost respect.

A small temple in a serene forested setting. The 7024 bus has a stop near the temple.  Inclined easy walk on the neighborhood street from the bus stop to the temple entrance.   After viewing the Buddhist temple, walking through the forested trail to Yonsei University is an easy walk where there’s a small temple within the University Medical Complex. Free admission for both temples
It’s far from downtown. Not easy to make the bus connections at Sinchon station and make journey to the temple but it is very nice and interesting. It’s mingled in the midst of a small community .

Quiet, cool and peaceful. This temple is bigger than I thought and I was surprised when I came here.
- Next to the temple is the mountain and wild parks for you to explore.
- If you want to visit Korean traditional temples but you don't have time to go away, come here. You will not regret coming here. Trust me.
- My only regret is that there is no lotus and beautiful sun so I can have good photos.
- Direction: easy and convenient. Take bus No.7024 (Green) from Seoul Station.

reviews.text:
A great park with a lot of open space for walking, kite flying, getting some food, looking at flowers in the spring and summer, and taking the family for outdoor activities.

If you come during the summer, there are several read to have the kids play in water features and cool off.

There are shaded areas on the sides of the park and a some areas for more rigorous hiking if you want. The southern part of the park has the visitor and recreation center and the north has more water areas, restaurants, and the observatory building.

I came on a Sunday in the afternoon and there were many families with children but it did not feel crowded as it is quite spacious.

Maps of the park are available in the visitor center in multiple language to help you navigate if you need support.
Very calm and peaceful park perfect for a picnic or a walk in the nature. Looks amazing at all seasons

Calm place with an observatory to see mountains from a far. Walking here is recommended. There is a huge plateau for dog-walking and picnic.

Recommend trying to visit in autumn when the fall leaves are red.

If you are tired of city life and looking for fresh air in Seoul this is the perfect place for you. This forest gives a window of green canvas inside the city. You can walk around enjoy the nature and sit beside the lake. The place is free. It have a parking lot which charges according to time.
Huge area, ideal for families and dog owners. Cute exhibition for kids. And as usual, sport pitches and playgrounds. My fav is the Mirorr Lake.

I have been to most of the other city gates on previous trips here.

reviews.text: I didn’t know this place existed, even though I’ve visited this hanok village more than 15 times, because it’s located in a less well-known area. There is a small free restroom inside, and they often hold exhibitions (when I visited, there was a gallery exhibition).

Bukchon Hanokcheong (聽)' is a public Hanok(traditional Korean residence) located on the hill of 11 Gahoe-dong, and it is a fairly large hanok with a size of 120 pyeong, which is rare in Bukchon, Seoul

'Bukchon Hanokcheong' is a place of Hanok cultural content that citizens create and enjoy together, and it has the concept of a shared Hanok that opens up various education  and cultural activities such as exhibition, lectures, performances.

If you step into the wooden door of the place, typical Korean garden and Hanok give you a pleasant isolation from the busy street.

And if you’re willing to take off the shoes and enter inside, there are mostly exhibitions going on like Minhwa, Korean traditional paintings. Now undergoing exhibition titled “Tuesday Afternoon” showing  about 20 pieces of authentic traditional Minhwa where I am participating.
Free entrance. Quiet with AC. Good choice to take a rest after walking in Bukchon Kanok under the sunshine.
Free Admission to view the Bukchon Hanok Hall, build with solid wood and nice view here.
Sit, relax, and enjoy the view of bukchon village through the open air windows. Also got a history lesson. Weekly exhibits from various artists add interesting twists to this historic hanok.

title: 북촌동양문화박물관
google_addr: 76 Bukchon-ro 11-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Surprisingly spacious, really just a large house with wide backyard-type garden around it, many nooks and crannies to sit in both inside and out, and some adjacent sitting traditionally-styled sitting rooms. A “museum” in the sense that the walls are lined with shelves showcasing various old ceramics and earthenware. The entrance, which is a gift shop, is free, but a small ticket of ~$6 needs to be purchased to enter the real area. It includes a simple drink or you can choose to upgrade to something better. It’s not the most amazing tea or coffee or setting, but we found it a quiet, relaxing time to rest a while, peer out over the Bukchon area, and refresh ourselves before journeying on. Not “trendy” perhaps but cozy and cute. Kids even enjoyed exploring the grounds on their own.

This was a good quality for the price of admission. It is not really a museum, more of a nice place with old art and pieces of tea ware. The 6,000 won ticket is well worth it and the tea is nice to enjoy while looking out over Bukchon. It’s not particularly fancy or cheap. Just a nice place to go that’s very relaxing.

This cultural art museum is interesting for two groups of tourists. On one side the incredible view you get over Bukchon Hanok Village including a „free“ drink that comes with the entry ticket. Even if you’re not interested in the museum, it is totally worth it and I think most visitors are there for the view.

On the other hand is the „extra“ that is the museum. There is very fine pottery, tea sets and craftmanship displayed in the different parts of the museum.

The place was not fully understandable to us. It's not a museum, it's a shop with a cafe plus garden with entrance fee. The location is nice, but terribly overrun. Event though one drink is included in the ticket price, we felt it was not worth it. You wait in the queue to get an instant tea. There are so many beautiful tea houses around where you can also get hanok experience with much better tea quality.

Red it was the best view ... Definitely not. 60,000 for a view and a tea (which we had to pay 1000 extra) and it's just not it. Serve in a dollar store cup and not a traditional tea cup, the view was non existent with the surrounding constructions on adjacent buildings ... not worth at all the 6,000 to enter. Save your money for a better cup of tea elsewhere.

The programs include tea ceremony, handicraft, and gugak as well as a Public Relations Exhibition Hall introducing Bukchon culture and hanok. reviews.text: speakue englisheu not good. redeu belbet

Maybe good place to visit for younger generation.

As a middle aged person with Korean background, mostly what I used to use/see or still can see at my parents/ grandparents' home.
There were photos interested me but they stopped us to go into the area because there was a kids' activities in the area. - so the visit was for nothing; waste of money.

I was quite upset as they failed to clearly inform us; but still happy to give 3 stars as younger people still can find some fun there.
Private museum with entrance fee.

The frontage of the location is the costume rental show window and the entrance could be easily missed. Exhibit is in the upper level from the street, in the converted home.

This is a great place to see the transition of modern time Seoul through the everyday furniture and tools and utensils average Seoulites used from 1910~1970s before the contemporary consumerism rejected and eradicated the traditional Korean life style as if shabby old timers. Most of the items are saved by the private collector, Dir. Lee, Kyung-ae, who saw the rapid changes in the area since 2000 when things were thrown out from the easement of zoning bylaws of the long time preservation area, where the high rise buildings were restricted due to the close proximity to Chongwadae, the President office. I truly enjoyed the place, and, enjoyed the long conversation with Dir. Lee, and adore her enthusiasm. There is also a young female staff who can speak English for help. But much of the insight of the history should be translated from Dir. Lee. Go talk to her.
Excellent spot. Be here or be square!

title: 북촌을 중심으로 한 조선시대 생활 이야기
google_addr: Gyedong-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Beautiful place to walk around and experience traditional Seoul. The hanok houses, narrow alleys, and city views make it feel like stepping back in time, especially early in the morning when it’s quiet.
It can get crowded later in the day, but if you go on a weekday or before noon, it’s very peaceful and great for photos. There are small cafes, galleries, and hidden viewpoints along the way, so it’s fun to explore slowly.
Just remember people actually live here, so be respectful and keep noise down. Overall, a must-visit spot if you want history, culture, and great views all in one walk.

Bukchon Hanok Village is easy to combine with Gyeongbokgung Palace in a day trip. The bus drops you right at Bukchon-ro, where maps help you plan your walk. The village sits on a hillside, so expect some gentle climbs, but the backstreets reveal clusters of traditional hanok homes, rooftop views, and even glimpses of Gyeongbokgung Palace. There are cozy cafes with terraces for a break. Best to allow at least 2 hours to explore and find photo spots. Keep in mind it’s a residential area with access limited to 10 am–5 pm, so be respectful when taking photos. We visited around noon in early January and found it pleasantly uncrowded, though we only managed to see a few hanok houses compared to online photos. Still, it’s worth a visit for the atmosphere and views.

A nice place to visit to see traditional architecture jn a residential estate. It is interesting to see some of these houses being converted into commercial shops, and good blend between tradition and modern contemporary. Just remember to keep your voice down to avoid causing disturbance to the residents.

There’s a tourist time window to visit certain areas: 10am to 5pm. Make sure to come within this time range.
Absolutely worth the visit!!
Beautiful buildings, art museums, several perfume shops and shopping in general.
Very picturesque place

This is one of the most memorable place I’ve been in Seoul. The Village is really nice and Clean. The designs are superb. I love how the government protect and preserve the historic structures in there country. I was there during summer time. Although it’s hot and humid but it was so worth it to see those beautiful things.

reviews.text: Perfect spot to escape the crowds and take a break while enjoying the view. The place charges 3,000 won and includes a drink. Worth a visit.
The best place to try to absorb the landscape of Seoul. Lovely welcome and amazing atmosphere. The views are breathtaking.

After a climb up a residential building, it is a 3000 KRW price for a balcony rooftop view of Seoul (and the N Seoul Tower in the far distance), with a choice for a paper cup of coffee, tea or orange juice. Chairs to sit, relax, or sketch

I thought this was definitely worth the cheap cost of entry.  You basically pay for your drink, which also gets you access to the house and gardens.  The drinks were totally decent, but it's the gardens and views of the surrounding area that are worthwhile.  I felt like I got a better experience/views of the Hanok village here than on the crowded main alleys with all the people posing for photos.  It was quiet and pleasant.

Showed up right as they opened on Sunday morning and had the view to ourselves. Very sweet owner gave us coffee and a few maps as well. reviews.text: We had a wonderful experience at the craft center! Our children (age 10 and 13) made two paper lanterns. It took 30-60 minutes in total. The lanterns are gorgeous and the lesson was well taught: the instructor was very kind and patient. There are also lots of other workshops, including laquerware, and woodworking. In addition to paper lanterns there are also very realistic paper dolls and cute paper animals. I believe you can make advance reservations, but we did a drop in class, and had no wait. It was not busy.

This place feels like a yard for the residents. It is super peaceful in here. I am walking around here and took some pictures of it. It is worth my everything. There are still residents walking around here when we are visiting. I feel so bad for disturbing them. I am looking at every room. Imagine you are waking up in the morning and looking out the window. It will be super energized and superb at the same time. Whoa, I love those feelings. I am in love with this yard. I can stay here for a long day if I can.

You can do some simple tie-dye handkerchiefs with your child. It cost quite cheap and so easy to follow.
Also they have this stick with Hangul on it, so you can take a picture with it. They borrow you the stick if you want to wandering around to get a better photos.
I was lucky not to wait so long but I highly recommend you to book before you get here.
If you are planning to visit 북촌 this place is definitely recommended. You get to craft Korean traditional items and they guide and teach you very well. I really enjoyed the experience

What a lovely place! It feels like a community centre where various workshops are offered every day exploring traditional crafts/crafting methods. We did 2 different ones, average time is an hour per activity and the price varies but most workshops are between 10,000 and 20,000won per person.
There is a weekly schedule so check the website for the workshops available on the particular day.
We did papier mache (decorating traditional shoes and fan), and weaving.

title: 북촌한옥마을
google_addr: Gyedong-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Beautiful place to walk around and experience traditional Seoul. The hanok houses, narrow alleys, and city views make it feel like stepping back in time, especially early in the morning when it’s quiet.
It can get crowded later in the day, but if you go on a weekday or before noon, it’s very peaceful and great for photos. There are small cafes, galleries, and hidden viewpoints along the way, so it’s fun to explore slowly.
Just remember people actually live here, so be respectful and keep noise down. Overall, a must-visit spot if you want history, culture, and great views all in one walk.

Bukchon Hanok Village is easy to combine with Gyeongbokgung Palace in a day trip. The bus drops you right at Bukchon-ro, where maps help you plan your walk. The village sits on a hillside, so expect some gentle climbs, but the backstreets reveal clusters of traditional hanok homes, rooftop views, and even glimpses of Gyeongbokgung Palace. There are cozy cafes with terraces for a break. Best to allow at least 2 hours to explore and find photo spots. Keep in mind it’s a residential area with access limited to 10 am–5 pm, so be respectful when taking photos. We visited around noon in early January and found it pleasantly uncrowded, though we only managed to see a few hanok houses compared to online photos. Still, it’s worth a visit for the atmosphere and views.

A nice place to visit to see traditional architecture jn a residential estate. It is interesting to see some of these houses being converted into commercial shops, and good blend between tradition and modern contemporary. Just remember to keep your voice down to avoid causing disturbance to the residents.

There’s a tourist time window to visit certain areas: 10am to 5pm. Make sure to come within this time range.
Absolutely worth the visit!!
Beautiful buildings, art museums, several perfume shops and shopping in general.
Very picturesque place

This is one of the most memorable place I’ve been in Seoul. The Village is really nice and Clean. The designs are superb. I love how the government protect and preserve the historic structures in there country. I was there during summer time. Although it’s hot and humid but it was so worth it to see those beautiful things.

reviews.text: Did this hike back in April & took the main “difficult” route. It wasn’t too bad and was manageable, only packed the main necessities food, water, and hiking boots. Watch clocked it at 3.6 miles, 2900 feet elevation gain, & took me about 4 hours total (with an hour break at the peak). Had limited visibility unfortunately when I got up there but views were still stunning throughout the hike. Peak wasn’t as busy as other peoples experience.

This was a fun hike that wasn't too crowded at all. I was able to take the subway to Bukhasan-UI station and then walk up to the Baegun Information Center, where the trailhead starts.

This is a great hike and easily accessible from Seoul. It was especially beautiful hiking it in the Fall.

We went on a weekday, so there were fewer people.
We took the difficult route first—lots of rocks and some steep climbs.

On the way down, we wanted to take the easy route but chose the wrong one. We ended up heading toward the East Gate and descended via the Sogicheon Park Guard Post. This route turned out to be even more difficult than the path we went up.

There were lots of loose rocks, and at certain points we had to cross the river to continue on the path. You need to be very careful. The good thing is, you’ll have the chance to wash up at the river—I even saw one experienced local doing so. If you plan to take this route, I recommend bringing a walking stick (suitable for experienced trekkers only).

The locals often use walking sticks, and they move very quickly with them. A stick provides good support and makes the hike much safer.
So easy I did it in slippers. Took me maybe 3 to 3.5 hours. Very beautiful!

It was such a fun walk. You need a certain level of fitness and i would recommend at least sneakers that you can lace up tightly. trail running shoes are perfect! Everything (stairs, paths) is very well secured. Please don't leave any trash in nature!

title: 뷰티플레이

reviews.text:
Best FREE experience ever! I came here on a weekday during lunch so there was nobody here. It was a little hard to find. I made an appointment as I arrived and had someone help me right away!

You get to choose between a few things for your first free service and I chose the skin-analysis. It was extremely informative. I learned that I had dry skin this whole time, though I believed I’ve always had oily skin. The reason my skin was oily is because it’s dehydrated and it’s overcompensating by producing oil!

Sun was so helpful, friendly, informative, and caring. He made me feel important and took his time explaining to me what my needs are and also helped me picked out the perfect red lipstick for my skin tone.

The products that are displayed are small, new, local businesses I believe. It is a great way to learn about Korean beauty and what is upcoming and trending.

There are also beauty products to sample as well. This place was so much fun and interacting.

Highly recommend giving them a visit! You can find free goodies/samples (often in the form of following accounts on Instagram or posting something) inside the store when you see the events wall and speak with an associate. I also highly recommend registering for a free skin analysis! We had our appointments with Hyeonha and she was very polite and informative. She used a translator and I used the translate app on my phone so we had no issues with language barrier. The store/showcase is quite big and they also have a little colour analysis you can check out. It can get busy because of the free skin analysis takes around 10-15 minutes per person but it is still a great thing to take advantage of and learn how dermatologists grade different parts of your skin for moisture, elasticity and colour.

Great free service to use! They now have an ai scanner to do a colour analysis on you for 7,000krw! They print it out and you can scan the QR code at the end to save it on your phone :) i also got free goodies by following certain brands on Instagram.

I don't know why there are a lot of 1 star review. But for me more than 5⭐ for this place.

Just so everyone know Beauty Play is like a program by the government. They support small-medium businesses such as the products that are available.

ALL PRODUCTS/EXPERIENCE ARE FREE. We tried a lot of good products. We got a lot of FREEBIES such as masks, sunscreen and facial. It may be a bit intimidating but nonetheless we really enjoyed this place.

Btw, this is a much better branch because of the elevator and much wider option of products.

Lastly, it would have been better if they have a section wherein we can buy some products. Especially for foreigners who cannot order online and have limited time.

Today I went to Beauty Play Myeongdong. I noticed a sign for a lactation/prayer room and was very happy, as it would have allowed me to pray without having to search elsewhere.

I went inside, but to my surprise there were staff members inside and I was told that it was actually a staff room and that I had to leave. If the facility is not available, the sign should be removed to avoid confusion. This was the only disappointing part of my visit.

Aside from that, I had a skin analysis done and I am very satisfied. The staff member who assisted me was very friendly.

Overall, a good experience, but the signage regarding the room should be clarified.

title: 비체현대무역점
google_name: Hyundai Department Store Trade Center Branch
google_addr: 517 Teheran-ro, Gangnam District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Big, stylish department store with 11 levels of fashion, lifestyle brands & luxurious boutiques. Well laid out & easy to browse.

There’s a pleasant sky garden on the 11th floor for a short break, while the food plaza at B1 offers plenty of dining options. Duty-free shopping is conveniently located on the 8th & 9th floors.

A great upscale stop in the COEX area  ✨

The Hyundai Department Store is one huge building with several floors, and every visit feels like an experience. I mainly explored the ground floor and the food sections.

On the ground floor, there are many jewelry and luxury beauty brands like Clinique, Estée Lauder, and Chanel, for makeup and perfumes. It feels elegant and well curated.

If you go downstairs, it opens into a wonderful world of food. There are snack and pastry corners, boulangeries, sweets, and cakes, and the smell is simply amazing. You can even watch how some of the pastries are being prepared. There’s also a food corner, which I didn’t try this time, but everything looked and smelled so tempting.

The grocery and cookery section is beautiful. Fresh vegetables and fruits of very high quality, fresh meat and fish, frozen items, and a great selection of international foods. There’s even a special corner for items from around the world, like pasta and imported products, plus a section with fresh kimchi and pickled specialties. Prices are slightly higher than in other places, but the quality really shows.

What I truly appreciate is the staff. Everyone is helpful, friendly, and very polite. If you have a question or need help finding something, they really take care of you.

It has its price, of course, but it always feels like a small adventure and a pleasure to walk through. And whenever I’m looking for something specific and can’t find it elsewhere, I know this place will have it.

Hyundai is a large conglomerate in South Korea and one of the many businesses they operate is a high end department store. This store has 10 floors and has 2 floors of duty free shops. The very top floor has a nice open garden area. There's also a floor full of nice restaurants are the top. The basement has a supermarket and many gourmet food stalls. Designer labels are spread all throughout the store.

A very good mall for shopping. Clean and neatly arranged.

The star highlight was the basement food court - it serves excellent food that is reasonably priced. Portions are substantial and there are lots of tables around for customers.

I will definitely return to the food court - high quality food, clean environment and an overall pleasant dining experience.

Highly recommended. Thumbs up!

The Hyundai Department Store food court is an absolute 10/10. I seriously wish we had something like this in the States. The food is incredibly good, with so many high-quality options that it feels more like a collection of restaurants than a typical food court. Every stall offers something different, and everything I tried was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. I came here so often that it basically became part of my daily routine—and somehow, I never got bored. There’s always something new to try, which makes it dangerously easy to keep coming back (like I did lol). If you’re a food lover, this place is a must-visit and easily one of the best food court experiences I’ve ever had.

reviews.text:
Hanok, Living with nature:
Time & Space led by Architect Yoo Byung An for/with Jaewon Tony Jo

In conformity with nature:
Hanok is designed according to the terrain and climate without damaging the surrounding environment, and it emphasizes nature-friendliness and environmental sustainability.

Solid & Void Open & Close:
The interaction between empty space and filled space forms an aesthetic harmony through the sing-interaction.

 : Archigroup MA Archive

Sup Sogui Hosu' in Minnesota,is the name of a Korean village among 14 foreign language village programs run by Concordia Language Vilage,
a non-profit organization. Designed by Archigroup MA architect Yoo Byung An,the Korean language vilage consists of a dormitory with a "ㄷ"  shape, a device to feel the borrowing landscape, and an American-style heavy-wood structure with elements to feel the spatial beauty of Hanok.
Architect Yoo Byung An designed the ratio, aesthetics, and philosophy of Hanok based on Byeongsan Seowon Mandaeru and Jongmyo Shrine.
4 out of a total of 10 units have been built, and six more are being funded.
Mr. Yoo would like to show these design processes and examples of the completed 'Sup Sogui Hosu' through archives and present a future that we can easily access In various ways that contain the space and philosophy of Hanok beyond realizing Hanok as a one dimensional traditional structure.

I think what we should learn from Hanok is not simply the reproduction or details of traditional Hanok, but rather the reinterpretation of the Spirit and Philosophy that Hanok tries to convey to us with the spirit of our times.
- Architect Yoo Byung An

Amidst Seoul's vibrant cityscape, Sayuksin Park provides a serene oasis steeped in historical significance. This park honors the six martyred ministers of the Joseon Dynasty, creating a space where history and natural beauty converge. Visitors can wander through tranquil paths lined with lush greenery and discover statues and monuments that tell the story of these revered figures. Offering stunning views of the Han River, Sayuksin Park stands as a peaceful retreat from urban life. It’s a place where one can reflect on Korea's rich cultural past while enjoying a moment of quiet amidst nature's embrace.

Whether you're looking for the latest fashion trends, classic styles, or unique pieces to add to your wardrobe, Samik Fashion Town has something to suit every taste.

Samik Fashion Town often hosts boutiques and stores specializing in various fashion categories, ensuring that shoppers have access to a diverse range of styles and brands. The mall is known for its vibrant atmosphere, making it a popular destination for those seeking to update their wardrobes or explore the latest fashion trends in Korea.

Whether you're a fashion-forward shopper or simply looking to indulge in some retail therapy, Samik Fashion Town offers an exciting and diverse shopping experience with a focus on clothing and accessories to help you express your unique style.

잠수함 조종 시뮬레이션, 터치 패널 등 다양한 액티비티가 있으나 어른 입장에서는 재미를 보지 못했다.

하지만 아이들이 있는 가정이라면 교육적으로는 배울 것이 많다고 생각한다.
중간중간 배치되어 있는 도우미들이 아이들 눈높이에 맞추어 잘 설명을 해주기에 좋은 교육 기회가 있으리라 예상한다.

reviews.text: Bought admission tickets from the self-service kiosk. Learned about the sacrifices made by the Koreans in their fight for independence. Also got to see the prison cells, execution building and exercise building.

Amazon well preserved location with a ton of history and you can feel the feelings of human suffering over the years that occurred. Most of the written descriptions also had English translations which was much appreciated. Some of the videos in the historical prison cells however were Korean audio only with no English subtitles which was a missed opportunity. Easy to buy tickets outside using the automated machines that accept foreign credit cards.

This place used to be an actual prison until more recent times. You don't really need a tour guide, most of the places inside have information written on them usually available in Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese and German. Some of the scenes are depicted by life size dummies and can be graphical. Not very suitable for younger children.
Very interesting and poignant place to visit.  This was built in 1907 to incarcerate Korean Patriots during Japanese Colonial rule.  It housed both men and women.  It shut down in November 1987.

Excellent museum with many displays and plenty of material to read. I had no problem spending the whole morning here. It is a grim period of history, and this museum details not only the barbaric treatment of Korean prisoners but their struggle for freedom and independence from Japanese imperialism. Many "political" prisoners were tortured and  executed here. But many also died from the unsanitary and harsh living conditions.
When I visited, over 90% of the visitors were children,  school groups who treated this place as entertainment and didn't even read any of the many information boards. Sadly, the significance of this place in modern Korean history is lost on them. I hope they will return one day as adults and give this place the respect and reverence it deserves.
Free to visit if you are 65+

title: 서울 삼전도비
google_addr: Seokchonhosu-ro, Songpa District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
It is fascinating that this Mongolian script monument and the city of Ulaanbaatar are essentially the same age.
The Samjeondo Monument in Seoul, built in 1639, contains inscriptions in traditional Mongolian script and stands as an important historical monument reflecting the complex relationships between the Qing Empire, Korea, and the Mongols.

Interestingly, that same year—1639—was also a significant moment in Mongolian history. Öndör Gegeen Zanabazar, a descendant of the Golden Lineage of Genghis Khan, was recognized as the spiritual leader of Buddhism in Khalkha Mongolia at just four years old. Around that time, the “Urga Mobile Monastery” was established. This monastery moved from place to place across the steppe and eventually became the foundation of modern-day Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia.
This is a rock that commemorates the surrender of king kejong somewhere near namhansanseong to the Qing dynasty.… mongols maybe? Anyways rocks for nerds

조선에게 주어지는 항복마저 황제의 덕이어서, 청은 그 자리에 대청황제공덕비를 세웠는데 그것이 '삼전도비'로 불리면서 여태 전해지고 있는 이 비석이다.
그 사이에 이 비는 시류에 따라 무너지고 다시 세워지길 반복했다. 청일전쟁 이후에 고종이 뽑아서 엎어버렸고, 일제 때 총독부에 의해 다시 세워졌다. 그러나 해방 이후에 도로 땅 속에 묻혔다가 후에 다시 세상으로 나왔다.
그 뒤로는 또 누군가에 의해 칠이 되었다가 복구되기도 하였는데 아마도 칠로 치욕을 칠할 수 있다고 생각한 모양인 듯하나, 칠로 치욕을 칠해서 욕됨을 없앨 수 있었다면 세상에 치욕이란 이미 없을 것이었다.
지금은 단 위에 앉아서 항복을 받았던 청도, 아래에서 머리를 찧었던 조선도 다 망하고 없어서 아무도 삼전도비를 보러오지 않는다.
한적한 나루였던 곳도 천지가 개벽해서 이제는 넓은 도로에 차들이 쌩쌩 내달리고 주변에는 비석보다 수십 배는 높아 보이는 건물들이 즐비하다.
그 앞에 서서 세상의 번화를 내다보고 있자면, 이 비석은 역사의 치욕은 칠로 칠할 수 있는 것이 아니고 그 욕됨을 현실로 메운 뒤에야 겨우 치유할 수 있는 것이라고 말하는 듯하다.
우리의 굴욕적인 장소, 남한산성에서 나온 인조가 이곳에서 청 황제 홍타이지에게 삼궤구고두례를 한곳... 근처엔 석촌호수와 롯데타워, 롯데월드가 있다. 놀이공원에서 놀기만 하고 오지말고 역사의 중요한곳인 이곳도 한번은 보고오면 좋을것 같다

Visited Seolleung and Jeongneung Royal Tombs (선릉과 정릉) and really enjoyed the experience. The site is open during the day (hours vary depending on the season but we went at 7.30am) and free to enter, which makes it a great spot for a calm city break. There’s a helpful information booth near the entrance and clean bathrooms available.

The tombs of King Seongjong, Queen Jeonghyeon, and King Jungjong are beautifully maintained, set within peaceful forest surroundings. I spent about 1.5 hours walking around, enjoying the shaded paths, gentle slopes, and benches where you can sit and relax. There’s no café inside, so it’s best to bring your own drink or snack.

A quiet, historical, and refreshing green space right in the middle of Seoul — perfect for a relaxing stroll or some quiet reflection

title: 서울 양천고성지
google_addr: Gayang-dong, Gangseo-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
궁산 정상에 자리잡은 옛 삼국시대의 산성. 조선시대 때도 이미 ‘고성(古城)‘이었습니다. 한강 하류에 접해 조수간만에 따른 흐름을 주시하고 김포 평야·마포·안양천 일대를 내려다볼 수 있어 옛 서울 일대 방어의 주요 거점이었을듯 싶습니다.

성벽은 궁산 정상면을 감싼 울타리 바로 밑에 잠들어 있습니다. 사진속 돌들이 일렬로 나열된 모습이 양천고성 석축 유구에요. 볼거리가 그닥 없어 딱히 올만한 곳은 아닌 것 같습니다.

근래 양천고성 발굴조사 보고서에 따르면 신라가 한강을 점유하던 대략 6~7세기에 축조되었다고 합니다. 20세기까지 군부대가 있었기에 유적지가 훼손된 상태고, 정밀 조사가 이뤄진 건 아니라서 확실치는 않다고.

일단 신라가 쌓은 게 유력하다고 해요. 그전에 이미 한성 백제가 쌓았을 가능성도 있고, 성벽을 보수한 일부 구간에선 또 고구려 계통 축성술을 띈다는 내용이었습니다. 고려시대 언젠가부터 버려졌고 임진왜란 때 권율 장군이 행주대첩 전 머물렀다는 기록이 있습니다.

근처 갈만한 곳
- 양천향교, 궁산땅굴 및 겸재정선미술관
- 서울식물원, LG아트센터, 스페이스K
- 허준박물관과 허가바위, 구암공원 광주바위
- 하늘공원, 난지도 한강공원, 월드컵 공원
- 국립항공박물관 또는 기생충박물관

삼국시대에 부터 아니 그전 부터 높은 곳에는 군사시설이 있어왔다. 멀리서 오는 적들이 오는 것을 감시할 수 있어서 당연한 것이다.
맞은편에 행주산성이 있는 것도 미루어 짐작할 수 있다.
삼국시대의 성은 토성이었으며 고려 조선으로 넘어가면서 돌을 이용한 성으로 바뀐다.

1992년 3월 10일 사적으로 지정되었다. 지정면적 2만 9370㎡, 석축둘레 762척(약 218m)이다.
궁산 정상부 근처에 옛성터 형성되어 있으며 소악루. 성황사등 있고
바로 위에 정상 넓은 광장이 있음

종각역 근처에 한국의 유명한 사찰인 조계사 바로 옆에 위치한 우정총국. 우정총국은 조선시대 후기 개화파관료인 홍영식에의해서 1884년 근대 통신. 우편을 도입하고자 설립한 대한민국의 최초의 근대식 우체국이다. 옛 우정총국 터에 지금의 우정총국 건물 일부를 만들었다고 한다. 우정총국 박물관에는 조선시대후기에 한국의 최초 근대식 우체국이 어떻게 설립되었고 발전했는지 설명이 되어있고 개화파 관료인 홍영식에 대한 내용과 다양한 우표가 전시되어있다. 우표는 기념우표와 일반 우표가 있는데 88올림픽과 같이 국가행사를 기념할 때 기념우표를 발행한다고 한다. 우표는 우편에 대한 요금을 먼저 지불한 것에 대한 표시를 작은 종이 형식으로 우편에 붙이고 우편에 대한 요금을 미리 냈다는 의미로 쓰인다고 한다. 지금은  보내는 사람이 우편요금을 냈지만 여러가지 우편 요금의  비합리적인 부분때문에 우편을 보내는 사람이 우편에 대한 요금을 미리 내는 방식으로 바뀌었다고 한다. 옛 우정총국을 보며 근처 한국의 유명 사찰인 조계사와 한국 전통을 느낄 수 있는 인사동을 방문하면 좋을 것 같다.

우정총국은 조선 최초의 근대적 우편 기관으로, 단순한 건축물이 아니라 근대 통신의 시작을 알린 상징적 공간이다. 또한 개국 축하연이 열리던 자리에서 갑신정변이 발발하면서, 근대적 개혁을 꿈꾸던 당시 개화파의 열망과 좌절을 동시에 담은 역사적 현장이 되었다. 본래 기능인 우편 행정은 짧은 기간에 그쳤지만, 우리 근대사의 전환점을 각인시킨 의미 있는 공간으로서 방문할 가치가 충분하다.

Unhyeongung Palace is a quiet and charming historical site in the middle of the city.

While it is smaller than the main palaces, it is beautifully well-kept and rich with history from the end of the Joseon Dynasty. I found the architectural details to be very interesting, offering a different perspective than the larger grand palaces. Best of all, it's completely free! A perfect, peaceful spot to learn about Korea's past.

It’s free to enter, and there’s also a small exhibition space inside. I really enjoyed my 30 minutes here. If you’re around Anguk Station, it’s definitely worth checking out.

의릉의 주인공과 역사
The Occupants of Uireung Royal Tomb and lts History
의릉은 조선 20대 왕 경종(재위 1720-1724)과 두 번째 왕비 선의왕후
(1705-1730)의 능입니다. 경종이 세상을 떠난 1724년 왕릉을 조성
하였고, 1730년 선의왕후가 세상을 떠나자 경종 능 아래쪽에 왕비릉을
조성하였습니다. 의릉은 하나의 능침 구역에 위.아래로 능이 있는
동원상하릉 형태입니다. 1960년대 중앙정보부가 의릉 권역 내에 설치
되면서 크게 훼손되었다가, 1995년 국가안전기획부(구 중앙정보부)를
서초동으로 옮기면서 2003년부터 본래 왕릉의 모습을 찾아가고
있습니다.
Uireung Royal Tomb houses the remains of King Gyeongjong (. 1720-1724,
the twentieth king of the Joseon Dynasty) and his second queen consort,
Seonu (1705-1730). A royal tomb was constructed when King Gyeongjong
passed away in 1724, and a second was constructed downhil from it in 1730
after Queen Seonui died. In the 1960s, the construction of the office of the
Korean Central Intelligence Agency (KC|A) Within the grounds of Uireung
Royal Tomb severely damaged its precincts. The KCIA was relocated to
Seocho-dong in Seoul in 1995, and a restoration of the royal tomb to its
original state was initlated in 2003.

google_addr: 19 Jong-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Took one of the longest queu in my life to try out this play aka the legendary octopus eatery in seoul. It paid off though. Food was pricey but the quality matches up with it, so no complaints at all. Octopus was juicy and heavenly fresh. They bacon stir-fried is well seasoned too. Kimchi and side dishes were good. Important note: the octopus is very spicy and that's default, cannot request anything more or less spicy so be extremely aware.

Perfectly cooked octopus in a garlic filled spicy sauce paired with rice, nori and lettuce. The side dishes were well seasoned and act as a perfect palate cleanser. Word of caution - the octopus is next level spicy, definitely not your standard heat!

This spicy octopus restaurant is the best of its kind in Seoul, not only because of the great spicy octopus. If you're not coming right when it opens for lunch or at, say, 5 pm for dinner, you'll stand in line and wonder why so many people are waiting at this restaurant on the 2nd floor of an office building. When you are finally seated, a hot pot of bacon with bean sprouts will be sitting at your table. Tell the server politely to take this away. If you are in a party of 2 to 4, order 1 to 2 servings of the spicy octopus (낙지볶음), 1 to 2 servings of the egg omelette (계란말이), and 1 clam soup (조개탕). It is the perfect trifecta. Order 1 or 2 servings of rice, grab some of the metal bowls next to self service kimchi station, and mix some octopus with the rice with a splash of sesame oil (also next to the kimchi station). The rice will mellow the spicy octopus *a bit* but the combo of the egg and the garlicky and simultaneously light and rich clam broth will cut the spiciness into perfect balance. I challenge you to have a more perfect meal that says, with absolutely all skill and no performativity, "we are Korea."
Good nakji place. Be warned tho they are know for their extra spicy nakji sauce. So spicy that even some Koreans struggle finishing them. Order their omelet to cool things off

Very spicy but delicious octopus! If you're not good with eating spicy food, you should pass on this. But if eating spicy food makes you sweat but you enjoy that feeling, give it a try! Comes with one bowl of rice and one bowl of broth/soup per person and pickled radish side dishes (you will need to eat them to cool down, lol) and a soup of bean sprouts, onions, green onions and hotdog sausages to mix the octopus into. The restaurant is on the second floor and you have to walk/wind around the floor before you find it.

A must if you're in the area. Very traditional market area that caters to the locals. The area around the market is becoming Seouls next up and coming foodie area as well, with more hip restaurants and cafes moving into the old kitchen appliance stores. The market has local fresh seafood, spices, clothing and even a top rated taco stand! But the highlight is the lady selling the Sweet Pancake (HOTTEOK). She makes hers with less oil and lots of filling so you can taste the pastry and filling instead of just oil. She takes great care making each one so it takes longer than other stalls and often has a long line of locals.
The market was very quiet when we arrived. There weren't many people and many shops were still closed. It wasn't attractive for tourist.
There was no ripped off, they were friendly, and the prices were reasonable (of course, this is the case with the tavern I visited).

1/2024

However, the peaceful vibe you might expect is a bit disrupted by the busy urban environment. The noise from bustling traffic and the chatter of city life can sometimes drown out the calm you'd normally look for in such historic sites. Even with the crowds that often gather here, the tombs create an interesting blend of history and modern life, making them a popular spot for those wanting to connect with the legacy of Korea’s former kings and queens amid the hustle and bustle of Seoul today.

reviews.text: 조선 3대 태종 이방원과 원경왕후가 묻혀진 장소입니다.

헌릉은 조선3대 태종과 원비 원경왕후 민씨의 쌍릉이다. 건립당시부터 오른편을 비워두어 쌍릉으로 계획되었으며 난간석으로 두 능을 하나로 연결하였다. 조선 건국이래 첫 쌍릉으로 능상위에 배치되는 문, 무인의 수가 다른 능보다 두배 더 배치되었다. 1856년 순조의 인릉이 건립되면서 헌인릉으로 불렸다.
1420년 7월 원경왕후가 승하하자 광주군 대모산 남쪽에 터를 잡았다. 9월17일 국장하여 능호를 헌릉이라 불렀다. 1422년 태종이 승하하자 9월 6일에 재궁이 석실에 안치되어 쌍릉으로 안치되었다.
- 1446년 헌릉 서쪽에 세종과 소현황후의 합장릉으로 영릉을 조성하였으나 1469년 여주로 옮겼다.
한적하게 구경하며 산책할 수 있어 좋아요

Perfect place for a stroll and relaxation

Paired with the cool breeze, it truly feels like the Seoul you see in Korean dramas. There is a free-entry zoo and botanical garden here, and I think spending an entire day in this park would be no problem at all. In a busy life, we all need time to relax!

reviews.text:
I visited during an exhibition period and really liked it, especially since admission was free. I spent around an hour and a half walking both inside and outside to see the exhibitions.

There are permanent and contemporary exhibitions located in different areas, and several buildings are connected to each other. Even though I visited on a weekday, there were still quite a lot of visitors.

Each building has clean restrooms, but they are small, so I saw long lines of people waiting outside.

I highly recommend this place to everyone, even to those who don’t usually like art—it’s still a fun place to visit. They also have souvenir shops and a café inside.

The museum was pretty nice. Some of the exhibition was closed of and renovated so I couldn't visit everything, but that's honestly fine.
It was also for free so if you have time,it's definitely worth of visit! There's also a nice cafe.

The Seoul Museum of Craft Art is located in between the Gwanghwamun area and Bukchon. Having three floors, it showcases modern art that's crafted so the art pieces are three dimensional art pieces. Some are functional while some are created for aesthetics.

Interesting to see daily objects and learn more about the background story of each one of them.
Lockers are also available for visitors. You can put your belongings there before entering, and it's for free!

Permanent collection of korean texile, ceramic and wood objects is presented and curated beautifully.
Along with contemporary exhibitions of korean designers as well as group exhibition of contemporary sustailable design projects from all over the world

reviews.text: Aw... I visited this place a long time ago but didn’t take any photos back then. This time, I came too early for the roses to bloom. On top of that, we visited on a rainy day in May, so as you can see in my photos, there was almost nothing. However, I noticed that a newly opened coffee shop is now inside the garden. I’ll definitely come back next year.

It's a huge area that you will enjoy a millions of various varieties of roses that bloom here, the rose festive until 25th May 2024. There is no entrance fee. There are the parking spots here during the festival time.

The amount and variety of roses is just magnificent. Apart of gardens of roses, there was also a tunnel of roses for you to walk through which is the distance of like three train stations and took me 40mins to stroll through. Kinda out of the way from central Seoul where the happenings are but worth visiting if you have the time.
The best time to visit is when the festival is going on in the month of May.  It looks beautiful. So, many different roses.. Also the decoration with roses looks so beautiful..

Beautiful display of roses! Easily accessible by train or bus which is the preffered method of transportation as parking is VERY limited.
This festival is a must if you find yourself close to Seoul in the month of May. There is no entrance fee as it is on a public park.
It offers a close look to roses in many colors, and sizez. In adition there is a breathtaking 5.12 km long tunel of roses next to the Jungnangcheon Stream.
There are plenty of street vendors and restaurants available to enjoy local food at very affordable prices.

Highly reccomend!

reviews.text: One of rare public libraries in downtown center of Seoul. It’s great that they’ve repurposed the old city hall to a library but the facilities and the building itself are lackluster like a typical public property. It seems to need a proper remodeling.

It's a beautiful architectural building dating back to 1926 was originally built by the Japanese and later converted into Seoul Metropolitan Library.

The space outside has a large lawn which organizes reading space events. Did not get a chance to join in as we were on our horses heading to the next tourist destination.

A lovely building located in the downtown center of Seoul. I think that they repurposed the old city hall to create the Library. Given the age of the building, the facilities are a bit dated - but overall it is a good place to visit.

We ended up in the Seoul Outdoor Library event organized by the Seoul Metropolitan Library. We were surprised by how well thought the event was. It has tents and couches so you can seat and read. Books are sorted by categories and you can pick them freely. In addition, there were musicians playing music. Definitely worth to stay around a grab a book!

Hike was extremely icey, but among the most beautiful I’ve ever done and would not have been possible without the team here. Thanks again

reviews.text: Highly recommended visit for a few hours of wandering and appreciating the architecture. If the timing works out, there's a free architecture tour that was super informative. A lot of random exhibits and photographer friendly. The whole place is lit up at night, but definitely go during the day. .

Really cool plaza and worth a visit when in Seoul. The design is awesome and the design store was a highlight! So many unique, contemporary, and elevated souvenirs from Seoul. Did the Basquiat exhibit and it was incredible. If you enjoy contemporary art and beautiful design as part of your travels highly recommend. Came on a Monday afternoon and was not busy at all - I might go back again while here because it was a trip highlight!

Dongdaemun Plaza looks really impressive from the outside, the architecture and lights make it feel fun, futuristic, and almost magical, especially at night. It's definitely a great spot for photos and just walking around to enjoy the atmosphere. Inside, though, it's quite minimal and feels a bit bare, so there isn't too much to see compared to how exciting it looks from the outside. Still, it's worth visiting for the unique design and experience outside.

If you love architecture and art, you will definitely enjoy Dongdaemun Design Plaza. Designed by renowned architect Zaha Hadid, DDP is an iconic landmark known for its futuristic curves and seamless, flowing form that blends architecture, design, and urban space.

I visited early in the day when there were only a few visitors, and the experience was amazing. The atmosphere felt calm and peaceful, allowing me to fully appreciate every corner of the space, both indoors and outdoors.

While DDP hosts many art and design exhibitions, the building itself is truly a work of art.
What an amazing place! The New Years event was incredible with light show then fireworks. Great music, unique art installations and the building was so futuristic.

Also go play the snow slide and other activities which you have to pay for. The snow slide which you have to sit on a float and slide down on the icy. For all ages and have fun.

A small but very neatly designed Park on the Seoul northern riverside.
We went here to watch the famous drone show and it was really cool!

The park is not designed to host THAT many people though. It's really crowded fir the show and there only are 3 narrow passageways under a highway to enter or exit the park.
Good place to visit in the evening time. Lots of option to do. boating, surfing, picnic, cycling & many more. Or you can just relax watching the beautiful river & city together.

We knew the drone show was going to be going on while we were there and we're so happy we were able to catch it. It seemed a lot of the crowd didn't know, so hearing their gasps of surprise was fun. If you're ever able to catch it, definitely do so. The bridge lit up at night was beautiful. And it's definitely fun to have snacks there while sitting by the water at night.

We went here to watch the drone show, and it was a blast! The park is also well-maintained, and a bunch of places that rent picnic mats and the like. It's a great place to visit, especially when most places in Seoul are all urbanized.

title: 서울로 7017
google_addr: 432 Cheongpa-ro, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Perfect place for a walk with unique city views. Modern, clean, and very pleasant. A great example of Seoul’s urban innovation.
Strolling on this walkway is the best thing to do when you come across Seoul Station! You can get a good view of the city on it.

The night view is awesome!
And it’s free.😊😊

It’s a surprise discovery that you can actually walk from Seoul station all the way to one of the most famous shopping districts with ease (I think it’s south gate market.)

It’s an abandoned road turned into a walkway park, a bit like the one in New York. The scenery was awesome! Great view from the skywalk, with Seoul station and the old South Gate in sight.

There’s little shop here and there, and connect to lots of surrounding buildings and market. Lots of “ramp” for better accessibility. Very convenient.

Do pay here a visit during night time, for the lighting and the night skyline of Seoul is awesome!

If you’re looking for a chill spot in the middle of Seoul, Seoullo 7017 is a great place to check out. It’s basically an old overpass turned into a sky garden, and it’s packed with all kinds of plants, trees, and flowers—it almost feels like a mini botanical garden in the city.

There are plenty of spots to just sit and relax, which is perfect if you need a break from walking around. I also loved the public piano—sometimes you’ll catch someone playing, and it adds a really nice vibe. There’s a cute little café too, so you can grab a drink and enjoy the view.

Speaking of views, you get a pretty awesome one of the city, and you can even see N Seoul Tower from up there. It’s all very clean and well-maintained, which makes the experience even better.

Overall, it’s a peaceful place to walk, chill, or people-watch. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area!

reviews.text: My three year old had a blast here, but I think kids up to 9-10 would have plenty to do. We tried to get tickets in advance, but the system only took Korean cards, even though they say there's an option for foreign cards. That wasn't a problem though, we were able to walk right in and get tickets. So much of their staff had great English, and the english signage was the best we saw. While that isn't necessary it was very appreciated.

Fantastic museum for kids. Have visited this with a 3 y.o. on three separate occasions and had plenty to do for several hours each time. We purchased tickets on the spot on all visits and had no issues. There are lockers to store clothes and/or other items and an area to park strollers.
The surrounding park is also great - several playgrounds, funfair, zoo. You could easily spend at least half a day here. Without a doubt my top recommendation for kids this age in Seoul.

An absolutely amazing museum for kids. There is so much to do for them and he really helps and to understand physics, animals and the environment. Different areas dedicated to different topics that helps the kids to explore and understand by play. The water room is absolutely incredible and offers so many so many options of fun. A lot a lot of the more structured activities need to be booked so I would suggest you organise your day as soon as you get in. They have cooking classes, film showing and other different workshops. Inside are many of opportunities to really interact with their exhibitions by playing with them taking photographs and showing how the kids actively participating in the museum. The park outside is absolutely incredible as it offers a variety of playgrounds and facilitiate hours of play.

Wow, although my toddler is only 2 years old, she really enjoyed herself! 4 floors of fun, mind you! I really love that it's minimal use of screens and there's different themes of elements. It's also situated in a lovely park, we took a stroll thereafter and even had bread for tea break while enjoying the scenary. Highly recommend to go there after a full meal as there's only a mart and a simple cafe. Facilities and staff are children friendly. The ajumma at level 1 introduced some sections to us and that warmed us up to the activities there. Can buy tickets directly at the counter, don't need to purchase in advance.

Very fun but maybe for elementary kids and under. 3 floors with enough activities for a good two to three hours. Some exhibits hit or miss. Water area closes for cleaning so be mindful of times and it has a capacity limit. Also space exploration area requires free reservation. Nice little cafe on site.

reviews.text: Highly recommended visit for a few hours of wandering and appreciating the architecture. If the timing works out, there's a free architecture tour that was super informative. A lot of random exhibits and photographer friendly. The whole place is lit up at night, but definitely go during the day. .

Really cool plaza and worth a visit when in Seoul. The design is awesome and the design store was a highlight! So many unique, contemporary, and elevated souvenirs from Seoul. Did the Basquiat exhibit and it was incredible. If you enjoy contemporary art and beautiful design as part of your travels highly recommend. Came on a Monday afternoon and was not busy at all - I might go back again while here because it was a trip highlight!

Dongdaemun Plaza looks really impressive from the outside, the architecture and lights make it feel fun, futuristic, and almost magical, especially at night. It's definitely a great spot for photos and just walking around to enjoy the atmosphere. Inside, though, it's quite minimal and feels a bit bare, so there isn't too much to see compared to how exciting it looks from the outside. Still, it's worth visiting for the unique design and experience outside.

If you love architecture and art, you will definitely enjoy Dongdaemun Design Plaza. Designed by renowned architect Zaha Hadid, DDP is an iconic landmark known for its futuristic curves and seamless, flowing form that blends architecture, design, and urban space.

I visited early in the day when there were only a few visitors, and the experience was amazing. The atmosphere felt calm and peaceful, allowing me to fully appreciate every corner of the space, both indoors and outdoors.

While DDP hosts many art and design exhibitions, the building itself is truly a work of art.
What an amazing place! The New Years event was incredible with light show then fireworks. Great music, unique art installations and the building was so futuristic.

title: 서울숲

reviews.text:
Seoul Forest Park - This park is nearly the new zone of Seoul city. Lots of free has yellow leaves on the end of October.

I think they're free for visitors who want to come here to take a relax, jogging or just want to find a peaceful place to reset the mind. Very clean and has a good hygiene restrooms.

Seoul Forest Park is a beautiful, expansive green space that truly shines in autumn, when the trees turn vibrant shades of red, orange, and yellow. Entry is free, making it a perfect spot for a leisurely stroll or an afternoon escape from the city’s bustle. The park features numerous art installations, sculptures, and interactive displays scattered throughout, adding a creative and modern touch to the natural setting. Wide, well-paved pathways make it ideal for walking, jogging, or cycling, and there are plenty of benches and open lawns for relaxing. It’s a popular destination, so expect to see many people—families, couples, and photographers—especially during weekends and peak foliage season.

Seoul forest is wonderful to go. Quiet and calm and relaxing even during the winter season. Not many were walking when we were there. Probably it’s cold and it’s refreshing walking around here for awhile. Also it’s near to Seongsu which is a good thing.

This is a very big, beautiful and relaxing park to stroll around. There are lots of people exercising, walking their dogs and children. It’s very clean and well kept with a large pond and a big field on which events are held. there are even sports courts where young people play pickle ball and basketball.

A worthwhile visit in the spacious lush forest in the middle of Seoul. Contains three parks featuring different things and at one end, there's a bridge connecting to an amazing cycling path surrounded by the riverside. If you want to enjoy the nature and take a break from the busy, crazy shopping scenes, come here to see a different side of Seoul.

The insect garden inside Seoul Forest is a charming little greenhouse that offers a warm and peaceful escape from the bustling park. Although it’s not very large, the space is thoughtfully arranged with a wide variety of lush plants, creating a cozy, tropical atmosphere the moment you step inside.

In addition to the greenery, there is an impressive collection of insect specimens on display. These exhibits are well-presented and educational, making it interesting for both children and adults to learn more about different insect species up close. The combination of living plants and preserved specimens gives the garden a small yet engaging natural history feel.

It’s especially pleasant to visit during colder months, as the greenhouse provides a warm and comfortable place to stroll while still enjoying nature. Overall, it’s a quiet and worthwhile stop within Seoul Forest, perfect for a short, relaxing walk.

예술전공이 아니라 얼마나 책이 다양하고, 전문적인지는 모르겠다. 하지만 역시 공간이 주는 힘이 크기에 이런 깔끔하면서도 다양한 지식을 접할 수 있는 공간이 있다는 것이 참 좋아보인다. 다만, 이런 시설들이 접근성이 좋은 곳에, 타 도시에도 이러한 시설들이 많이 생기면 좋겠다.

서울시립미술아카이브는 서울시립미술관의 분관 형태로 미술의 역사를 보존하고, 연구하는 미술관입니다. 처음으로 방문하게 되었는데, 개관한지 얼마 안되서인지 시설도 깨끗하고 공간들도 매력적이었습니다. 1층에는 라이브러리가 개방형으로 있었고, 아카이브 관련 전시실이 있었습니다. 지금은 강홍구의 전시가 열리고 있었습니다. 그외에도 세미나가 가능한 공간, 다목적홀과 교육공간들이 있었고 카페도 있습니다. 주차장은 생각보다 크지않아 방문객이 몰릴경우에는 대기나 다른곳에 주차해야 될수도 있습니다.
서울시립 미술관 분관 중 하나. 우리는 끊임없이 다른 강에 스며든다 전시를 보러 방문했다. 도슨트 설명이 좋았고 권은비 작가의 마지막 작품에선 마음이 먹먹해졌다. 지하철 접근성이 낮은 게 좀 아쉬웠다.

아담한듯아니듯  제법  규모있는 건물.아카이브관이지만  전시도 있어서  더욱 좋음.자료조사차 들렀는데  아직은  흡족할만큼의  자료가 없어서  좀  아쉬움. 건물외관은  유리창의  발을 연상케하는 디자인,언덕길에  위치한 건물이라 단층구조가  재미남.옥상정원도 있음. 길건너  미술관 카페 커피는  그냥그렇지만  평일이라 한적하고,유리창도 전시컨셉과 일치시킨 점 인상적.

reviews.text: i throughly enjoyed the exhibition of nam jun paik’s work. the work was a series of interactive synth machines. there is also a cafe there if you want to get a coffee
Must visit if you like his work. Unique Hanuk designed for this space, overview of works and sounds experiments. Texts are in Korean, but you can scan a QR code to receive English. Free entrance

This small memorial house provides thorough explanation about Baek Namjun's biography and the outlook on his art. The huge house in which his family used to live when he was young was located on the exact same spot. There are not many things to look around here, but it is an interesting and meaningful place to stop by.

One of the fluxus spots in the Asian area.

As soon as I arrived, I realized that my credit card was missing.
Such happenings are also fluxus.
Beautiful place where you can see some works of Nam June Paik

title: 서울시립 북서울미술관
google_addr: 1238 Dongil-ro, Nowon-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Despite not being listed as a major tourist attraction nor being located near the most touristic parts of Seoul, I visited this museum and rather enjoyed it. It's actually smaller than I imagined it to be, so don't expect to spend any more than 30 min to one hour to have a look at everything there.
Free entrance, and exhibition guides and videos were translated into English.

This one is way out there in the northern reaches of the city.  But worth the trip, I suppose.  Like all of the SEMA facilities the art tends towards the avant-garde.

It is a pretty big spot, so you might be able to spend a few hours.  Also check out the library on the top floor.  It has a ton of books (non-circulating) about art in both English and Korean.

Well the facilities are great. Each floor has space for individual artist to showcase their art. The roof has a nice garden. The field surrounding the museum is good for kids. The art inside... well it's contemporary.

Not bad place and it's free. The free lockers are nice and bathrooms are sparkly clean. Staff are friendly. I took a star away because the art was eehh. I feel like some exhibits portrayed nothing of the artist and the process, rather random stuff they created that was trying too hard. Sorry, I know it's art, but come on.

I was for appreciation art that was painted in early 19th century in Korea. Most of them were introduced in my school book when I was a high school student. Prior to this exhibition, I never saw paints that my teacher in high school teach taught me during the school class. All paints and portraits are genuine.

The place is nice.
Their exhibitions are really good.
Once, a docent explained me the exhibition in English !
A place to go !

reviews.text:
visited with my kids on weekday. it's at the north of Seoul but worth for visiting for kids, they can experience variety science things. it's for free since it's public museum running by Seoul city.   kids were really enjoyed here. for me it's so impressive tornado generator which is 17m , the biggest in Asia region.
some experience needs to be reserved through online and other experience can be reserved kiosk at the museum.
Good place for learning science! Would recommend it to elementary-high school students
Fantastic science center. Admission was 2000 for adults and 1000 for kids. There are lots of hands-on exhibits for kids.
The place that became the seed of future science of the Republic of Korea, which had been lagging behind. The prospects for science in Korea are bright.
A lot of interesting things in here related with science. So, kids especially elementary schools are very good to see and experience.

title: 서울시티투어 버스를 이용하면 서울여행이 쉬워진다
google_addr: 135-7 Sejong-daero, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
We started our tour on the Tiger Bus, which unfortunately had poor A/C. Luckily, our next bus had a closed top and was much more comfortable.

Our tour began at 3:20 PM, though I think doing it at night would be a better experience. My only complaint is that both drivers had a habit of tapping the gas pedal frequently, which made the ride a bit jerky.

Overall, it’s a great way to explore the city.

The tour cost ₩25,000 per person as of 2025.

If you found this helpful, please give it a like—thanks!

Lisa Choi was our tour guide and she was amazing!! So helpful and full of knowledge- knew the best spots to take pictures- even took pics for us! We did the DMZ tour and … super memorable! Words can not express what being able to see and touch a part of history and the ongoing struggle. Thank you, Lisa and Seoul City Tour. If I am ever back on this side of the world, will do again!
A must for an around one and half hour tour where you can get off and get in in all the must see places for a complete day out tour.

My husband and I plus our 23 month old daughter took the evening tour bus that leaves at 7pm and returns at 8.30pm.

It was such a fabulous experience. The views of Seoul by night are spectacular. What a vast and sprawling city that it super impressive. If you are short on time, or with young kids like us this is a great way to see it all in a short span of time.

The cut lights are stunning and make it extra special.

Great value for money - highly recommend this experience. Be sure to book the day before you plan as it does get sold out!

I recommended to use this service from City bus tour. You could go anywhere in Downtown and Uptown to see many places. They had a schedule for stopping by for each place. You could plan and select the time. In addition, you could spend time in some place and get back with other city bus. The view along the way was nice and interesting. They had a radio for explanation of each place.

title: 서울식물원
google_addr: 161 Magokdong-ro, Gangseo-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Worth checking. Well-maintained and beautiful botanical garden. It felt especially exotic and nice because it was extremely cold outside and the indoor garden was warm and tropical. If you liked Singapore’s Gardens by the Bay, you might like it here too. There is a cafe inside to chill and other shops to check out too.

Just one negative: parking. Their machine does not accept non-Korean-issued credit card and their customer service was horrible. The staff suggested giving a ‘random person’ around us cash and asking them to pay for us with their Korean credit card. I wish she was kidding.  There was no sign that only Korean credit cards were accepted.
There are a few parking lots for this garden and the one we parked in was 13 minutes away. It was challenging to walk all the way in -10 degree weather.

stroll around the outdoor garden and go to the conservatory. it is a nice greenhouse for the tropical plants and flowers. there are diferent areas like the meditteranean and tropical plants that you can explore. it is not air conditioned and will feel hot when you have a jacket/coat. there's a gift shop and plant/seed shop.
Beautiful park with nice walking paths all year round. Loved the sections where the public is invited to design small parts of the garden around different themes.

Would not recommend, especially in winter. I can imagine (although difficult to) it would look nice in bloom but when I went absolutely everything was dead. Have to pay a 5,000 won entrance fee to look at literally nothing. Why is there an entrance fee if the garden is not maintained to look nice year round?
The conservatory was nicer but was so humid inside it was suffocating so had to leave immediately.

The Beautiful botanical gardens and park are a must see if you have a little free time away from work or on the weekend or if you are traveling to Seoul South Korea and it is raining or snowing.  Warm inside like a sauna😊.  Try it out

reviews.text: Nodeul Island is a great place to take a break and enjoy a slower pace in the middle of Seoul. Highly recommend bringing your own food and drinks, finding a spot to sit, and just soaking in the city’s unique vibe. A perfect little escape that captures the soul of Seoul.

Will be missing this place so much while it closed later:(
Such a best place to enjoy sunset.

I visited this place during Summer Vibe Festival. I like the atmosphere of festival as well as plenty of space for seating or lying on your own blanket. There are some restaurants and bars, but during festival it was quite crowdy. I would appriciate some convinient store on the island.

Nice island to visit on a warm day. Different events take place there too. Gets busy on weekends, with many people having picnic. I'd recommend taking the bus there as it's very fast and you avoid walking next to the road

Good place to go on a picnic. To get a good place to sit down, you might want to go early cause this island is getting so popular. There is convenient store, library, and some restaurants within it but not various in a kind. To bring your food with you is recommended. Lots of good spots for pics.
Especially like the library in the island. With a couple of seats inside, there were quite many books to cuddle. If i had more time, would defenitely stay longer. Scenery of han river and bridges was splendid. One of the best places in seoul to see sunset.

title: 서울아트책보고
google_addr: South Korea, Seoul, Guro District, Gocheok-dong, Gyeongin-ro, 430 스카이돔 지하 1층

reviews.text: 고척돔 지하에 위치한 서울책보고. 계단을 내려가면 밖에선 보이지않던 보물창고가 있다. 다양한 전시. 다양한 웹툰.만화. 다양한 예술관련 책. 하루종일 앉아 웹툰, 만화,그림책 실컷 봐도좋은. 북까페에서 커피도 저렴하게 한잔.
매달 독서모임 진행하고 있어요. 좋은 공간이여서 나만 알고 싶은 그런 곳입니다. 편의시설 잘 되어있고, 쾌적하고요. 큰 테이블이 있어서 노트북 작업하는 분들도 계시고 경기관람 전에 들리셔서 쉬는 분들 계세요. 열람실 내부가 가장 조용합니다. 카페 메뉴가 저렴해서 좋아요.

이런 곳이 많이 생겨야 합니다.
예술관련 서적이 꽤 많이 구비돼 있습니다. 막연한 관심으로 제가 보고 이해할 수 있는 수준의 책은 못 찾았지만 쉬운 책도 꽤 눈에 보입니다.
예술가 분들에게는 부족한 도서량일 수 있지만 지속적으로 책을 추가하는 것 같네요.

열람실 또는 카페에서 볼 수 있으며 구입도 가능합니다.

아트북 체험존이라는 곳은 아이와 함께 할 수 있는 공간입니다.
의자에 앉거나 빈백(용어를 몰라서...)에 눕거나 앉아서 아이와 함께 그림책을 볼 수도 있습니다.
컬러링 이벤트가 진행 중이여서 색칠할 수 있는 테이블과 색연필도 구비돼 있네요.

23년 2월 19일까지는 팝업 북 전시도 하고 있습니다.

모두 무료로 이용할 수 있고, 카페의 음료도 저렴합니다.

고척돔 지하라 경기나 공연있는 날은 어떨지 모르지만 적당한 북적거림 속에 아이와 책 잘 보다 왔습니다.
왼쪽 아트책이 있는 공간은 한적하고 조용하구요 멋진 팝업북을 맘껏 볼 수 있어서 좋아요. 오른쪽 카페겸 유아용 그림책이 있는 공간은 좀 산만하지만 아이들공간이라 그렇게 이해하면 됩니다. 카페 음료값이 저렴해서 좋아요.^^

고척돔 지하에 있고, 행사나 경기 없으면 주차 가능합니다. 공간은 상시 전시장/라이브러리(대출 불가)/서점/ 북카페 등이 있고 커피 가격은 저렴한 편이에요. 아트북은 디자인, 건축, 사진 등 부터 외지 위주의 고급 양장본 많고요. 패션이나 뷰티 관련 명품 브랜드 컬렉션도 마련되어 있습니다. 특히 아이들 볼만한 입체 북이 있고, 엄마와 갓난쟁이들 쉴수 있는 수유실도 쾌적하고 넓습니다.

title: 서울아프리카페스티벌
google_addr: 281 Eulji-ro, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Highly recommended visit for a few hours of wandering and appreciating the architecture. If the timing works out, there's a free architecture tour that was super informative. A lot of random exhibits and photographer friendly. The whole place is lit up at night, but definitely go during the day. .

Really cool plaza and worth a visit when in Seoul. The design is awesome and the design store was a highlight! So many unique, contemporary, and elevated souvenirs from Seoul. Did the Basquiat exhibit and it was incredible. If you enjoy contemporary art and beautiful design as part of your travels highly recommend. Came on a Monday afternoon and was not busy at all - I might go back again while here because it was a trip highlight!

Dongdaemun Plaza looks really impressive from the outside, the architecture and lights make it feel fun, futuristic, and almost magical, especially at night. It's definitely a great spot for photos and just walking around to enjoy the atmosphere. Inside, though, it's quite minimal and feels a bit bare, so there isn't too much to see compared to how exciting it looks from the outside. Still, it's worth visiting for the unique design and experience outside.

If you love architecture and art, you will definitely enjoy Dongdaemun Design Plaza. Designed by renowned architect Zaha Hadid, DDP is an iconic landmark known for its futuristic curves and seamless, flowing form that blends architecture, design, and urban space.

I visited early in the day when there were only a few visitors, and the experience was amazing. The atmosphere felt calm and peaceful, allowing me to fully appreciate every corner of the space, both indoors and outdoors.

While DDP hosts many art and design exhibitions, the building itself is truly a work of art.
What an amazing place! The New Years event was incredible with light show then fireworks. Great music, unique art installations and the building was so futuristic.

title: 서울어린이대공원
google_addr: 216 Neungdong-ro, Gwangjin District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
What a wonderful place for families. There much to see and do without an entrance fee. This even includes a small zoo! I was pleasantly surprised to see the are fairly large, compared to the ridiculously small cages in Japan zoos.

There's even a theme park with rides, including a rollercoaster (small amount per ride), playgrounds and botanical gardens.

The park is well maintained and clean and easy accessible.

Sprawling public park for children. The playgrounds are dated but decent. The surprise was the free zoo with many animals on close display. These animals are not hiding inside their enclosures which makes it fun for children. Multiple convenience stores within the park. There is a paid indoor playground at the main pavilion tower. Good day trip to bring your child for fun and exploration. No admission charges to the park!
Good place to visit with family.  Free admission and above expectations.

Great place and park in this part of Seoul. Composed of different parts with various activities - from inactivity to playing sports, zoo, botanical gardens.
Perfect place for a stroll and relaxation

I visited on an autumn afternoon, and the bus takes you directly to the park entrance. The park in autumn is incredibly beautiful, with ginkgo and maple trees already changing color. Paired with the cool breeze, it truly feels like the Seoul you see in Korean dramas. There is a free-entry zoo and botanical garden here, and I think spending an entire day in this park would be no problem at all. In a busy life, we all need time to relax!

title: 서울억새축제
google_addr: 95 Haneulgongwon-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Our first stop was here - Hanuel Park. This is a beautiful park with silver grass making our photos dreamlike. We came in the morning when the sunlight was just nice, not too hot. There were quite many ready-to-snap photos spots at different part of the park. The walk was easy and comfortable.
Calling an Uber will drop you off at the front of the entrance, much better than taking the bus, which getting off at World Cup Stadium, it was a very long walk.
Very romantic place in autumn. Purple, brown, yellow, red. Many photo shots places,  ladies will like this place, beautiful 😍
What a beautiful park! We didn't find the famous pink grass, but we still had a great time there. And there weren't many people, which was also very nice :)

This park in autumn is simply breathtaking. I visited during peak foliage season and was blown away by the golden silver grass (eulalia) swaying gently in the wind. Even though it was a bit cloudy when I came, the whole hill still felt magical — peaceful, golden, and full of life. The soft light actually added a calm, dreamy atmosphere, and every corner was still incredibly photo-worthy.

Getting up to the park does require some effort (a decent walk up a long flight of stairs or a shuttle ride), but it’s absolutely worth it once you reach the top. The contrast of nature and city views is stunning, especially around sunset. It’s a perfect escape from the busy city without actually leaving Seoul. If you’re in the city during autumn, don’t miss this place — it’s one of the most beautiful seasonal spots I’ve experienced in Korea.

A really solid place to understand Seoul beyond just palaces and cafes. The museum walks you through how the city evolved—from Joseon-era streets to modern Seoul—and it’s surprisingly easy to follow, even if you don’t know much Korean history.
Most exhibits have English explanations, and the layout is spacious and well organized. I especially liked the large-scale models of old Seoul and the sections showing how daily life changed over time. It’s calm, educational, and not overwhelming.

One of the best museum I ever went to. It feels very planned out, from start to finish. You go through multiple eras of South Korean history with different exhibitions you can experience. I really enjoyed the information flyers you could take for each part, especially since most parts were only written in Korean but those flyers were available in Japanese, Chinese and English as well. Once you’re done, you’re able to stamp a little card at the end with a very friendly man that helps you out.

This free museum offers incredible value and a great learning experience. I love that it focuses on storytelling rather than just displaying artifacts. In about an hour, you can get a clear understanding of Korea’s history.

The miniatures are fantastic, showing how people lived from thousands of years ago to more recent times. The highlight, though, is the Seoul miniature room. It's a huge space with the entire city of Seoul recreated in scale beneath a glass floor you can walk across. It’s absolutely fascinating.

I highly recommend visiting this museum, especially since admission is free! :)

A French Perspective on Seorae Village: Overrated, But Not Without Charm

Having heard the hype about Seorae Village, Seoul's so-called "French Quarter," I ventured in with cautious optimism. As a French person, I was naturally curious to see a slice of home abroad. However, I must concur with the prevailing sentiment: Seorae Village is decidedly overrated and lacks the authentic French flair it purports to offer.

Let's be clear—it's not a complete disappointment. The village is undeniably a quiet, peaceful enclave, a welcome respite from the relentless energy of the city. The architecture is charming, with pretty, unique houses perched on the hillside, creating a picturesque, almost Mediterranean feel. The cafés here are a definite highlight; they are cozy and offer genuinely high-quality pastries and coffee that would not be out of place in a Parisian neighborhood. They provide a pleasant spot to relax.

The main issue lies in the surroundings and the overall atmosphere. Beyond the cafés, the area feels rather bland and sterile. There are a few token French flags and the occasional bakery, but it lacks the vibrant, bustling energy of a true French quartier. The "village" feels more like a quiet, affluent residential area that happens to have a few nice cafes than a cultural hub.

My verdict is situational. If you are on a tight schedule in Seoul, skip it entirely. There are far more compelling and authentically Korean neighborhoods to explore. However, if you're staying for a couple of weeks and find yourself with a free afternoon, it's worth a quick stroll for the cafés and the unique architecture before heading to the nearby Seorae Forest. A final word of warning: be prepared for a workout! The village is built on a significant incline, so wear comfortable shoes and carry water—the climb can be quite physical.
