Sungnyemun Gate (also known as Namdaemun Gate) is National Treasure No. 1 of South Korea.
Yes, that is literally what it is.
The gate is listed as National Treasure No. 1 - part of the nation's cultural heritage.

The gate was built back in the 14th century and marked the southern boundary of Seoul (by the way, the name itself translates as "Great South Gate").
All the key events in Korean history took place here; the gate was one of the eight entrances to the city.

Namdaemun Gate suffered serious damage during the Korean War. Of course, it was later restored but in 2008, a man who felt wronged because he hadn't received an insurance payout set the gate on fire.
And it burned down…

The restoration took five years, and now the gate is open to visitors once again.

I might be wrong but my feeling was that Seoul doesn't seem to have a single center like most European cities do (with the central square, government building, central cathedral, the oldest restaurant - all in one place). As a result, many monuments are located in places that might seem unusual to a European tourist.
Here, for instance, there are only modern buildings and new roads around the gate, and seeing the historic structure surrounded by contemporary structures can feel a bit puzzling… On the other hand, if you look at 19th‑century photos showing shacks all around it, this modern setting is definitely better...

The gate itself is stunningly beautiful.
I believe it is an absolute must to visit the Gate if you come to Seoul.
After all, it is No. 1 national treasure!

Sungnyemun Gate (officially Sungnyemun, meaning "Gate of Exalted Ceremonies") is arguably the most famous historical landmark in Seoul. It is better known to many as Namdaemun (South Great Gate).

The Beginning (1398): Construction was completed in 1398 during the reign of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty. It was the main southern entrance to the walled city of Seoul.

The Vertical Sign: You might notice that unlike other gates, the name sign on Sungnyemun is written vertically. According to feng shui principles, the nearby Gwanaksan Mountain had a strong "fire" energy that threatened the capital. The name "Sungnye" also represents fire, and by writing it vertically, it was believed to act as a "fire against fire" shield to protect the city.

The Tragedy of 2008: On February 10, 2008, a 69-year-old man set fire to the wooden pagoda atop the stone base in an act of arson. The entire nation watched in shock as the 600-year-old wooden structure collapsed.

The Restoration (2013): It took over five years and approximately 27.7 billion won ($24 million USD) to restore the gate using traditional tools and methods, including the use of rare 500-year-old pine trees. It reopened to the public in May 2013.

Passed by this historic gate while visiting Seoul, snapped a couple of shots.

A must see if you’re heading to the palace.

The gate dates back to the 14th century and you can truly feel the history it has witnessed and endured through the centuries.

Standing there really gives you a sense of how much it has withstood to remain preserved to this day.

Sungnyemun Gate (commonly known as Namdaemun) is one of the most iconic historical landmarks in Seoul, South Korea. Built in 1398 during the Joseon Dynasty, it served as the main southern gate to the walled city of Seoul. The name "Sungnyemun" means "Gate of Exalted Ceremonies." As a symbol of Seoul's heritage, Namdaemun is designated as National Treasure No. 1 of South Korea. The gate features a traditional wooden pagoda-style pavilion atop a massive stone base, showcasing classic Korean architectural style. In 2008, the gate was severely damaged by arson but was meticulously restored and reopened to the public in 2013. Today, it stands not only as a historical structure but also as a reminder of Korea’s resilience and dedication to cultural preservation.

There is one long, main and wide corridor type strip down the centre with a number of narrower lanes branching off the sides, also selling food, souvenirs and trinkets. All stall holders we interacted with were super friendly, warm and helpful. They all appeared happy to be interacting with customers and feeding the crowds. Each food store specialises in a different type of food. Everything we ate was delicious! I liked that you were able to buy food from lots of different stores and then come together and share so you could taste a bit of everything.

I would highly recommend visiting here!

This is a very popular market to sample lots of food options and price is affordable too. You can shop for bed covers, pillows, clothing, kitchen accessories, grab coffee at coffee shops near by or just enjoy a sunny day inside and around this market. Bring your appetite and your walled for a fun time

This place is old school meets new school. Food stores are a plenty, even those most stores sell the same food. Many Michelin rated food places and the famous kalguksu featured on netflix is here too. Definitely a place to come for buying souvenirs and good quality blankets back to your home country.

Easily accessible via bus or the metro (Dongdaemun station) with a 10 minute leisurely stroll

I went because it's near my hotel but don't go just for it. It's definitely not worth. Maybe at the end of it you will find some good local food at decent price but don't stay too much time. It's 80% blankets and old people cloths. Not such a good place to hangout.

This market didn’t impress us. The food selection was repetitive and nothing was really appealing to our eyes. We ended up trying a mungbean paste pancake and walnut-shaped pastries. The taste wasn’t bad but definitely not something that I would travel for.

reviews.text: COEX is one of the best places to visit in Seoul, especially if you’re interested in shopping, culture, and events all in one spot. The COEX Aquarium and the famous Starfield Library add a unique charm to the place. It’s also a major venue for exhibitions and conferences, making it a lively hub throughout the year. The location is very convenient, easily accessible by subway and bus. Overall, COEX offers a perfect balance of entertainment, business, and relaxation.
Get ready to lost in this mall. Its really huge. One of the best mall to do shopping in Seoul.
About 7 storey high, loxated in Daegu, there are integrated restaurants within the exhibition center. Opposite the COEX is the Inter Bulgo Exco hotel.

Conveniently located and there are restaurants and shopping area at the basement.

The COEX hall is big and great for holding exhibitions here.

This place is pretty cool. Large mall with the nice library you see all over FB. Didn't know about the Gangnam style Psy hands until my wife told me about it. It was cool to take pictures in front of.

title: 서울창포원
google_addr: 4 Dobong-dong, Dobong-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
The park is stunning but mainly had older people on the occasions that I went. It was still nice and when I was studying Korean on a bench a few of the older women joined me. i still need to explore more of the park which I will do on different days.

There is also a cafe with a great view. I had a cheese toastie with a scoop of chocolate powder on top with a strawberry yoghurt smoothie

Kind of community park at the edge of Seoul. One part is called bunker. One local told me it used to be chemical storage of US military before they moved to Pyeongtaek. Now there are some artist work shops plus couple tanks. I visited on spring Sunday and this park is very colorful with many happy people. It is also the startin point for around Seoul hiking trail. Many foreigners and excellent service from the staff.

This park is one of the best places located in Seoul. If you happen to visit Dobong dong area, really like to recommend you to stop by there. Dobong mountain is right in front of the park so you may enjoy this beautiful mountain from the park. And it takes 5 minutes to get from Dobongsan MTR station.

It is "Seoul Changpowon". It is a beautiful place where the beauty of iris and the background of Dobongsan and Bukhansan are harmonized throughout the four seasons. The subway station is right next to it, so accessibility is good.
For couples of hours, if you wish to be relaxed and refreshed in some lonely outskirts' of this large city, try once, and then you will not regret.

title: 서울크루즈
google_addr: South Korea, Seoul, Yeongdeungpo District, 여의도 한강공원길 231

reviews.text:
Perfect way to see another side of Korea!
I've seen it on several episodes of 2 Days and 1 Night and since then I've been wanting to see it and be on it. Upon getting inside the boat, we were greeted with arrays of Korean foods. Just thinking about it makes me really hungry. As soon as we are seated, we were greeted by the Captain. The lunch and the entertainment started at once. I really loved how the singer sang Korean songs, and English songs in Korean! Korean trot songs were also played. The combination of Korean food, Korean songs, and the beautiful view of the around Han River just made the trip perfect. You can also go up the third level or the first level. Each offering different forms of entertainment. The top level though really has the best view; with the sky, water, and the surroundings, everything was just perfect. If you are into singing, you could also ask the person in-charge to allow you to sing a song!
I think HyunDai can provide much better program and service for the price they charge. Appears to be a tourist rip-off.
Absolutely fantastic
Not recommend. Ara cannel is noting to seeing place

title: 서울특별시교육청 동대문도서관
google_addr: 22 Cheonho-daero 4-gil, Dongdaemun District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
건물이 오래된 거 같으나
시설이 넓고 크고
층별로 구성이 잘 되어 있어요
자료도 넉넉하고
자율학습실엔 콘센트 섭이
따로 있어서 좋아요
풍물시장 바로 옆에 있는 도서관으로 시립도서관이다. 건물은 낡고 노후되었지만 내부는 나름 인테리어 공사를 해서 이용하기에 불편은 없다.  나름 많은 프로그램을 하며 지역과 유기적 관계를 가지려고 노력하는 모습이 보인다. 바로 곁에 우산각공원이 있고 조금 떨어져 있지만 10분 이내거리에 청계천이 있다.
직장근처라 퇴근후 한번 가 봤는데 깨끗하고 조용히 책도 보고 공부도 할 수 있고 1층에 커피숍과 지하엔 간식도 사 먹을 수있어 좋아 보였다.

동네에 이런 도서관이 있어서 너무 좋아요.
40년 전이나 건물 외관은 크게 변함없지만 내부는 많이 변했습니다. 더 다양해진 책들과 엘리베이터가 생기고 실내에 화장실이 생겼습니다. 디테일하게 편리해진 시설이 좋습니다.
동네마다 이렇게 큰 도서관들이 있다면 너무 좋겠습니다.

동대문도서관은 1971년 3월 31일에 개관한 서울특별시교육청 소속의 도서관입니다. 삼각형 모양의 건물 구조가 독특합니다. 크기는 지하 1층부터 지상 5층까지로 되어 있습니다. 개관한 지 50년이 넘은 역사를 가지고 있지만 2013.11.03부터 보수공사를 위한 휴무를 하고 같은 해 12월 16일에 재개관을 한 덕분에 내부 시설은 그럭저럭 준수합니다. 또한 2016년에는 카페도 새로 생겨서 편의성이 증가했습니다.

도서관 지하에는 식당 및 매점, 전자레인지와 음료수 자판기가 갖춰져 있습니다. 그리고 식당에서는 지참해 온 도시락을 먹거나 음식을 주문할 수 있습니다.

도서관 주변 환경으로는 바로 옆에는 우산각 어린이공원, 3개의 역이 만나는 신설동역, 서울풍물시장, 그리고 청계천 등 다양한 시설들의 중심에 있어 바깥으로부터의 소음의 영향이 꽤 있을 것 같습니다. 거기에 더해 주차장은 없어서 반드시 도보로만 접근이 가능합니다.

매월 2/4번째 수요일과 법정공휴일은 휴무입니다.

title: 서울특별시교육청 어린이도서관
google_addr: 7 Sajik-ro 9-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: If you love children's book, this is tje right place to visit
Lots of books for kids. There is a playground, too.
1980년대 백일장때 와본 추억의 공간. 책의 양이나 수준은 다른 어린이 도서관보다 낮은편. 그리고 와일드한 종로 부모와 종로 아이들을 많이 볼 수 있는 곳. 솔직히 중국에 온듯한 느낌을 받았다.

어린이도서관은 1979년 세계 어린이의 해를 기념하여 5월 4일에 설립된 대한민국 유일의 어린이 전용 공립도서관입니다. 조금 특이하게도 도서관이 하나의 건물이 아닌 유아관,자료관,문화관 3개로 분할 운영을 하고 있습니다.

통상 도서관의 시설중 일부에 불과했던 어린이 자료실이 아닌 어린이 전용으로 만들어진 도서관이다 보니 어린이에게 맞춰진 시설 규모도 역대급이였습니다. 다만 시설이 오래되다 보니 연식이 좀 있어 보입니다.

입구에 들어가자마자 보이는 문화관은 DVD관람 및 가족과 함께 각종 체험활동을 할 수 있는 건물이며, 메인 도서 시설은 자료관입니다. 자료관은 총 3층으로 구성되어 있으며 3층 시청각실과 다문화실이,  2층과 1층이 어린이들이 주로 이용하는 도서관 시설입니다.

가족과 함께 찾아오기에 더없이 좋은 도서관이지만 매점이나 휴게실이 없는 점은 아쉬운 부분입니다. 이용시간은 평일은 09~18시, 주말은 09~17시까지이며 매달 1,3번째 월요일은 공휴일입니다.

여기를 찾아올 때는 사직파출소로 찍고 오면 편함. 내비찍으면 돌아서 와야 함ㅠ(특히 도보일 경우)
애들 수업시간 대기하는 장소는 냉방되지 않아 덥다ㅠ
옆에 사직공원이 있어 청량감을 느낄 수 있는 view가 있음

용산도서관은 1981년 4월 21일에 개관한 서울특별시교육청 소속 도서관입니다. 서울 지하철 4호선 서울역 11번 출구에서 약 1km 떨어져서 걸어서 등산해서 20분 정도 걸리는 장소에 있습니다. 또한 남산도서관과 4차선 도로 하나를 사이에 두고 마주 보고 있어서 상당히 가깝습니다.

도서관 건물은 1960년대에 지어진 것으로 당시 박정희 정권의 집권 여당이었던 민주공화당의 중앙당사 건물이였습니다. 이후 1980년 8차 개헌의 일환으로 공화당의 정식 해산이 결정되었고, 용도가 사라진 당사 건물을 서울특별시에서 인수하여 도서관으로 개조한 역사가 있습니다.

주변보다 꽤 높은 곳에 위치해 있고 건물도 높은 덕분에 접근성은 좀 떨어지지만 그만큼 서울시내 전경을 내려다볼 수 있는 뷰가 최고입니다. 그래서 그런지 2층 입구 옆에는 야외휴게소 자리가 있고, 3층에는 옥외휴게실도 있습니다.

건물의 규모는 총 5층으로 구성되어 상당히 많은 시민들을 수용할 수도 있습니다. 입구도 1층과 2층 2군데가 있습니다. 1층에는 식당 겸 매점도 있어서 간단한 간식을 사먹거나 식사도 할 수 있는 점이 주변에 편의점도 없는 도서관으로서는 상당히 편리합니다.

전반적으로 연식이 꽤 되보이는  시설이지만 2018년에는 열람실을, 2023년에는 디지털.간행물실을 리모델링한 덕분에 중간중간 최신식 시설도 눈에 띕니다. 큰 강당시설도 있는 등 서울교육청도서관들 중에서는 최상위 규모를 자랑하는 것 같습니다.

매주 2,4번째 화요일은 휴무일입니다.

title: 서울풍물시장
google_addr: 21 Cheonho-daero 4-gil, Sinseol-dong, Dongdaemun District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: This place is well worth a wander around. Antiques and collectibles as well as some vintage clothes, watches… so many things! Not far from the Dongmyo flea market too.

This place could be a museum but it’s not really good for buying any souvenirs as a tourist as most items are massive and heavy. Vendors weren’t interested much on negotiating or haggling prices. They seem to just be waiting for those high spenders who turn up and buy-buy-buy without a care in the world.

Flea Markets are my absolute love and weakness. If so for you as well, this place is a must-visit. Be prepared to see many shops with modern (probably made in China) goods as well, but pass by them, they are not worth any attention. As for the antiques, there are lots of Asian and European items, kind, mostly elderly sellers. Not so high prices, especially if you are a good haggler. Had a success buying some century old statuettes and theater masks.

If you're looking for odds and ends, 2nd hand items from hardware tools, to bikes and clothing. It's all here. There is even a section for more fun and intimate items for everyone. Not sure if they are 2nd hand or not 🫣😜

There is a food court on both the upper and ground floors with the ground floor being the larger one.

There are many stalls outside the flea market also.

For those who aren't interested in the shopping experience and have been dragged along for the experience, there are plenty of snack and drink options along the way.

There are certainly a lot of stalls here to keep you occupied for many hours.

Nice to pop by if you are in the neighborhood but I wouldn't recommand going only for the market. I felt the prices were extremely high, even for all the fake products. But that might have to do with me being a tourist.

On the top floor, they have a section that shows you what older stores used to look like in Seoul, pretty cool to check out !

The Seoul K-Medi Center is a wonderful place to experience traditional Korean medicine and culture. I recommend visiting when you need a break during your trip.

title: 서울한양도성 백악구간
google_addr: South Korea, Seoul, Jongno District, 청운효자동 산15

reviews.text: 한양도성에 대해 듣고 언젠가 한번 가봐야겠다고 생각하던 차에 다녀왔다. 시작부터 가팔라 쉽지 않았다. 그러나 성이 잘 복원되어 있어 뿌듯했다. 올라가며 서울 도심의 멋진 모습을 볼 수 있어 좋았다.

600년 고도(古都)의 상징. 1392년 조선 건국후 서울, 즉 한양이 1394년 조선의 수도로 지정된 이래(실제로 옮긴건 1396년) 내사산(內四山), 즉, 東으로 낙타, 西로 인왕, 南으로 목멱, 北으로 북악산을 따라 설치된 성곽.

성곽뿐 아니라 성곽을 둘러싸고  있는 총 8문(4大門과 4小門)도 한양도성길의 일부.
4대문은 흥인지문(동대문), 돈의문(서대문, 현재 유실), 숭례문(남대문), 숙정문(홍지문 또는 북대문, 4소문은 혜화문(동소문), 소의문(서소문), 광희문(남소문), 창의문(북소문)으로 구성.

임진왜란, 병자호란, 왜정시대, 6.25동란 등 수많은 전란과 국난을 거치며 많이 소실되었지만 1974년 본격적으로 복원직업이 시작된 이래 현재까지도 진행중인 大국책사업.

그 중에석도 가장 온전히 보전되었다고 할 수 있는 구간이 자로 이 백악구간(서울성곽길/한양도성길 1코스). 구간은(서에서 동으로 진행했을 때) 창의문-돌고래쉼터-백악쉼터-백악마루(해발342m)-1.21사태 소나무-청운대-청운대쉼터-숙정문-말바위전망대-와룡공원-성북역사문화공원-혜화문.

조선시대나 구한말에도 많은 이들이 성곽길/도성길을 도는 순성(巡城)을 즐겼다고
창의문에서 북악산으로 혜화문까지의 구간을 혜화문에서 출발해 와룡공원 지나 올라가니 시내와 주변경치가 잘 보이는 전망대를 지나 말바위안내소까지 갔다가 내려와 삼청공원을 가보았어요.

북촌에 있는 오래된 우물. 물맛이 좋아 궁궐에서도 사용하던 곳 이라고 함.
보름동안은 맑고, 보름동안은 흐려지곤 했기때문에 보름우물이라 부름.
주문모신부가 1801년 새남터에서 순교하기 전까지 계동 최인길마티아 집에 숨어지내며 선교활동을 할때, 이 우물물로 세례를 주었다고 전해짐. 1845년 김대건신부도 이 지역에서 사목할 때, 이물을 성수로 사용했다고 전해짐.

서울에 상수도 시설이 본격적으로 도입되기 시작한 20세기 초까지 우물은 주된 음수 및 생활용수 공급원이었다. 북촌 주민들의 중요한 음수원이던 석정보름우물은 15일 동안은 맑고, 15일 동안은 흐려진다고 해서 붙은 이름이다.
1794년 중국에서 압록강을 건너온 우리나라 최초의 외국인 주문모 신부가 1801년 새남터에서 순교하기 전까지 계동 최인길의 집에 숨어 지내면서 조선땅에서 첫 미사를 봉헌할 때, 이 우물물로 세례를 준 것으로 전해지고 있다. 또한 1845년 한국인 최초의 신부인 김대건 안드레아 신부도 이 지역에서의 짧은 사목기간 동안 이 물을 성수로 사용한 것으로 알려져 있다. 천주교 박해 당시 많은 순교자가 발생하자 갑자기 물맛이 써져서 한동안 사용되지 않았다는
이야기가 전해진다.

Water wels had been the main source of drinking water and water for living for citizens in Korea until the early 20th century when the mu-
nicipal water supply system began to be established. The Seokjeong Boreum Wel which was the main source of drinking water for the
residents of Bukchon area got its name because it provided clear water for fifteen days (boreum) of the month and unclear water for the
remaining fifteen days.
The well is known to have provided water for the earliest baptism ceremonies secretly held by Father Zhou Wenmo, the Chinese Catholic
priest and missionary who crossed the Amnok River in 1794 to become the first foreign Catholic priest in Korea. He hid at the home of
Choe ln-gil until he was martyred in 1801. The welwas also known to have been the source of the holy water used by Father Andrew
Kim Tae-gon, the first Korean Catholic priest, during the brief period of his missionary as a priest in the area in 1845. It is said that the
water of the wel tasted bitter during the persecution of Korean Catholics and had to be disused for an extended period of time.
주문모 신부께서 성수로 쓰던 우물이라고 하는군요. 이름과 웹사이트 수정 완료.

title: 석파정
google_addr: 4-1 Changuimun-ro 11-gil, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Seokpajeong Seoul Art Museum offers a mixed but ultimately rewarding experience for art enthusiasts and casual visitors alike. The gallery itself is decent, featuring a modest collection of contemporary and traditional Korean art. While the exhibits are thoughtfully curated, they may not be groundbreaking enough to justify the admission fee on their own. However, the real highlight of the museum is undoubtedly the breathtaking panoramic views from the fourth floor. The vantage point offers a stunning glimpse of Seoul's skyline, seamlessly blending the city's modernity with its natural beauty. This alone makes the visit worthwhile, as the serene atmosphere and picturesque scenery provide a perfect escape from the bustling city below. If you're willing to pay the price, the views alone will leave a lasting impression, making Seokpajeong a unique spot for both art and nature lovers.

Seokpajeong Seoul Art Museum is a private art museum located in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul, and manages Seokpajeong, which was the villa of Heungseon Daewongun.
This museum opened in 2012 and presents various planned exhibitions on the theme of modern art.
It introduces works by famous domestic and international artists and holds exhibitions that highlight various aspects of modern art.
It is also a special place where you can appreciate art in a space where tradition and modernity come together.
Visitors can gain artistic inspiration and spend leisurely time with beautiful nature.

It was remarkable to learn about the history of this museum, where the passion for art of a salesman blossomed into an impressive collection. Behind the museum, lies the Seokpahung area. This charming spot features traditional hanok houses surrounded by beautiful deciduous trees, evoking the classic holiday retreats once favoured by royal families during the late Joseon Dynasty.

Came just to see 'The life of Jesus' exhibition, only to find out it at already ended at 3pm despite the brochure stating the museum was open until 5pm with nary a sentence on the exhibition timings. Would have been nice if the ticket sales lady had mentioned this earlier, as 20,000won for the rest of the museum's paltry exhibitions and  small but picturesque seokpajeong does not justify the entry price.
The place is not foreigner friendly unless you understand Korean, as the commentaries are not in English.
Do wear shoes with good traction if visiting on a snowy day, many people were seen slipping when visiting seokpajeong.
Won't recommend this museum unless there is a must see exhibition for you, otherwise one is better off going to visit the secret garden at changdeokgung palace than seokpajeong itself.
Fantastic art museum with rotating exhibits and beautiful garden. A real gem that you shouldn't miss in Seoul. Lots of good restaurants around the area too.

reviews.text:
금호역 인근에 멋스럽게 지었지만, 사실상 주차공간은 장애인주차를 제외하면 일반차량 두 대만 가능하고 작은도서관 앞 도로는 주정차 불가이며 인근 공영주차장 안내조차 없다.

도로앞 불법주차된 차량들이 많아 혼잡스럽다. 기획단계부터 현재까지 무대응 무계획이란 점에서 탁상행정, 전시행정을 잘 나타낸다.

매봉산숲속도서관은 2020년 10월 7일에 개관한 성동구립의 7번째로 만들어진 도서관입니다. 숲속의 도서관이라는 테마를 바탕으로 해서 그런지, 실내 인테리어도 나무 느낌이 가득한 천장과 책상의자가 특징입니다. 또한 야외 파라솔 자리도 있습니다.

다만 구립도서관 치고는 규모가 1층 하나로 일반자료실과 어린이자료실, 사무실이 한 공간에 있어서 협소하고 접근성이 떨어져서 이 근방의 학생과 레미안 아파트 주민들 말고는 찾아올 일은 별로 없는 도서관일 것 같습니다.

이름대로 매봉산자락에 위치해 있어서 주변보다 지대가 높은 곳에 있는지라 제일 가까운 금호역 기준 900m 정도를 오르내리막으로 걸어서 가야 하는 점이 살짝 불편할 수 있습니다.

운영시간은 오전 10시부터 오후 8시까지이며 매주 월요일은 휴무일입니다.
옥수동 매봉산 아래에 숲속도서관은 힐링 그 자체예요. 클래식 음악에 조용히 책을 읽기도 좋고 유아부터 성인에 이르기까지 책을 대여하거나 독서하기 좋은 장소입니다.

숲 속에서 조용히 책읽고 자연을 느끼기 좋은 곳입니다.
주차면이 두 개 뿐인 것이 아쉽지만
아이랑 같이 가도 볼 책이 많았어요.

김승영 작가님의  전시가 궁금해서 방문해 보았습니다. 당일 예약이라 약 한시간 뒤 시간대밖에 예약 할 순 없었지만 그냥 기다리겠다는 마음으로 예약하고 보고 왔어요. 정말 잘했다 싶습니다.
한 시간당 5인으로 입장제한을 하고 있어서 평일 기준으로는 거의 혼자 본다고 생각하시면 됩니다. 정말 조용히 고요하게 관람을 할 수 있었습니다.

입구에서 네이버 예약인 확인을 하고 엘리베이터로 2층, 3층 올라가며 관람하는데 1층에서 엘리베이터를 타자 마자 고객 한분 올라가십니다. 이렇게 무전을 하시더라구요. 각 층마다 안내해 주시는 분이 작품 설명도 해 주시고 기본 동선과 주의해야 하는 점 등을 아주 상세하게 설명해 주셔서 좋았습니다. 1:1로 케어받으면서 관람한다는 기분이 들더라구요.
작품 자체가 많은게 아니라 설치 위주로 공간안에 들어가서 영상을 보고 소리를 듣고 냄새까지 맡으며 하나되는 경험을 해야 하는 전시입니다. 관람객이 통제되어서 더 좋았던 것 같습니다.

아주 좋은 기억으로 남은 전시입니다.
전시실의 향기와 빗자루 쓰는 소리는 내도록  기억에 남네요.

자치구 최초 공립미술관이며 윤중식님의 작품이  아카이브포함 500점이나  기증되어있다함. 외부 산책로에 거리갤러리 공공미술프로젝트도 함께 있어서  일상생활 속  좋은 작품감상 기회를  누구나 누릴수있어서  진심 박수침.  입구에 최만린 작가님의  조각품도 인상적임. 화가의 벗-시대공감  이중섭.윤중식. 박수근의  작품을  감상할수있는  너무 좋은 전시에  더군다나 무료관람에  다시한번 깊은 감사드림. 도슨트도  너무 좋았음^^ 작지만 알찬 구성.알찬 공간   자주  가고 싶은 곳중 한 곳임. 직원들도  모두 친절함.

성북구 성북동 안쪽에 위치한 서울 최초의 자치구 미술관입니다. 2009년에 문을 열었으며, 한국의 근현대미술을 중심으로 한 기획전시를 개최하는 미술관입니다. 서울에서 성북동이라는 장소가 저에게는 예향의 이미지로 남아있어 예전부터 간송미술관을 자주 다니던 기억부터, 최만린미술관 등 많은 기억과 추억을 간직하게 하는 장소인거 같습니다. 이번에 유근택 전시가 있다고해서 방문하게 되었습니다. 원래는 6월23일까지였는데, 7월21일까지 연장되었다고 합니다. 동양화기법을 통해 실험적인 다양한 작품을 만드시는 분이신데, 특히 목판화 작업 140여점도 전시한다고 하여 기쁜마음에 달려오게 되었습니다. 전시공간이 넓진않지만 재미있고, 충실한 전시라고 생각되네요.

어제 일요일 오후4시쯤 성북동에 살며 성북동을 그리는
《유근택: 오직 한 사람 》2024.04.25~06.23

This is such an unique place!

It really made me surprised and helped me to learn a different side of Korean history.

The place is not very crowded, the scenery is beautiful, and the entrance fee is only KRW 1,000. Definitely worth a visit!

Visited Seolleung and Jeongneung Royal Tombs (선릉과 정릉) and really enjoyed the experience. The site is open during the day (hours vary depending on the season but we went at 7.30am) and free to enter, which makes it a great spot for a calm city break. There’s a helpful information booth near the entrance and clean bathrooms available.

The tombs of King Seongjong, Queen Jeonghyeon, and King Jungjong are beautifully maintained, set within peaceful forest surroundings. I spent about 1.5 hours walking around, enjoying the shaded paths, gentle slopes, and benches where you can sit and relax. There’s no café inside, so it’s best to bring your own drink or snack.

A quiet, historical, and refreshing green space right in the middle of Seoul — perfect for a relaxing stroll or some quiet reflection

光化門廣場 近期正好配合 首爾燈節，整個廣場在夜晚氣氛和白天完全不同。燈飾沿著廣場與清溪川一帶延伸，主題多半結合韓國歷史、傳統文化與童趣元素，即使只是隨意散步，也會不自覺一直停下來拍照。

傍晚開始點燈後，人潮會慢慢聚集，但廣場空間夠大，不會覺得擁擠。燈光映著周圍的宮殿、銅像與城市街景，畫面很有層次感，很適合把光化門廣場排在晚上行程，從市政廳或德壽宮一路走過來，邊走邊看。

如果剛好是冬天來首爾，搭配燈節一起逛，會覺得這一帶比白天更有溫度，也更能感受到首爾節慶時的城市氛圍。
2025년 12월 27일에 방문했습니다. 참 좋았습니다.

title: 세종문화회관
google_name: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
google_addr: 175 Sejong-daero, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: My trip started on a high at Sejong Theatre, where I watched the musical Phantom. The performance was absolutely stunning—the set, the music, the voices. For a couple of hours, I was so absorbed I didn’t even check my phone (which, let’s be honest, says a lot for a Gen Z like me). It felt like stepping into a different world, and I left with goosebumps.

My time exploring Sejong Plaza was spent enjoying the beautiful statue of Sejong the Great. There's many animations on the buildings, hidden alley restaurants that are ALL 10/10, and subway/public transportation hub.

The Sejong Center for the Performing Arts is an iconic performance venue located in Gwanghwamun, Seoul. For Korean artists, performing here is considered the ultimate honor, and it wouldn't be an exaggeration to call it the Carnegie Hall of Korea. While the facilities are somewhat dated and inconvenient, they are receiving positive feedback. It is conveniently located right next to Gwanghwamun Square, and it is also great for a walk after the performance. Making its own original performances like Ilmu(One Dance) is also a promising idea.

Exhibition
Masterpieces from the San Diego Museum of Art: "From the Renaissance to Impressionism"

Hey, let me share a quick thought with you.

If you ever find yourself near Gwanghwamun, take a moment to walk by the Sejong Center. And if you already have a ticket in hand, even better. You are about to step into one of Korea’s most meaningful performance halls.

Sejong Center has long been considered a symbol of Korean performing arts. When it opened in 1978, its pipe organ was the largest in Asia. Back in Europe, pipe organs were a way for cities to show their pride and prosperity, and Sejong Center carried that same spirit here in Seoul.

Sure, some people might say it is not the most modern venue anymore. And they would not be completely wrong. But this place holds memories. It has watched generations grow up, quietly standing its ground while the city changed around it. That kind of history matters.

Personally, I have spent some memorable nights here. I watched THE GREATEST: Thrill with Jeong Dong-ha and Sohyang in September 2023, Universal Ballet’s The Nutcracker in December 2023, and Chung Myung-Whun conducting Beethoven’s Ninth with the KBS Symphony at the end of 2025. Since it is a multipurpose hall, you might not always get the same powerful acoustics as a dedicated concert hall, especially for classical music. Still, the experience feels special every time.

Getting there is easy. Just hop on Seoul Subway Line 5 and get off at Gwanghwamun Station. One small thing to note, though. There is no traditional cloakroom. Instead, you will find unmanned lockers on the second floor. They work, but the touch screen can be a little tricky. Maybe it is just me getting older.

The box office is on the first floor, and there are kiosks if you already bought your ticket. You will also spot vending machines for water on each floor, which always comes in handy.

One last tip. The Grand Theater usually opens about two hours before the performance for security reasons, and audiences are allowed into the hall about thirty minutes before the show starts.

Take your time, soak it in, and enjoy the moment.

The Story of King Sejong exhibition hall offers a vivid historical experience. It opened on Hangeul Day, October 9, 2009.
Operated by the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts, the exhibition hall commemorates the life and achievements of King Sejong, the fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty and one of the most revered and proud kings of Korea.
The Story of King Sejong exhibition hall consists of six exhibition spaces: Sejong, the Man, People-Oriented Ideology, The Creation of Hangeul, Science and Art, Military Policy, and Hangeul Library.
Offering a variety of hands-on and educational programs, the museum offers a vivid historical experience, attracting numerous domestic and international visitors and establishing itself as a Seoul tourist attraction.

title: 소다현대무역점
google_name: Hyundai Department Store Trade Center Branch
google_addr: 517 Teheran-ro, Gangnam District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Big, stylish department store with 11 levels of fashion, lifestyle brands & luxurious boutiques. Well laid out & easy to browse.

There’s a pleasant sky garden on the 11th floor for a short break, while the food plaza at B1 offers plenty of dining options. Duty-free shopping is conveniently located on the 8th & 9th floors.

A great upscale stop in the COEX area  ✨

The Hyundai Department Store is one huge building with several floors, and every visit feels like an experience. I mainly explored the ground floor and the food sections.

On the ground floor, there are many jewelry and luxury beauty brands like Clinique, Estée Lauder, and Chanel, for makeup and perfumes. It feels elegant and well curated.

If you go downstairs, it opens into a wonderful world of food. There are snack and pastry corners, boulangeries, sweets, and cakes, and the smell is simply amazing. You can even watch how some of the pastries are being prepared. There’s also a food corner, which I didn’t try this time, but everything looked and smelled so tempting.

The grocery and cookery section is beautiful. Fresh vegetables and fruits of very high quality, fresh meat and fish, frozen items, and a great selection of international foods. There’s even a special corner for items from around the world, like pasta and imported products, plus a section with fresh kimchi and pickled specialties. Prices are slightly higher than in other places, but the quality really shows.

What I truly appreciate is the staff. Everyone is helpful, friendly, and very polite. If you have a question or need help finding something, they really take care of you.

It has its price, of course, but it always feels like a small adventure and a pleasure to walk through. And whenever I’m looking for something specific and can’t find it elsewhere, I know this place will have it.

Hyundai is a large conglomerate in South Korea and one of the many businesses they operate is a high end department store. This store has 10 floors and has 2 floors of duty free shops. The very top floor has a nice open garden area. There's also a floor full of nice restaurants are the top. The basement has a supermarket and many gourmet food stalls. Designer labels are spread all throughout the store.

A very good mall for shopping. Clean and neatly arranged.

The star highlight was the basement food court - it serves excellent food that is reasonably priced. Portions are substantial and there are lots of tables around for customers.

I will definitely return to the food court - high quality food, clean environment and an overall pleasant dining experience.

Highly recommended. Thumbs up!

The Hyundai Department Store food court is an absolute 10/10. I seriously wish we had something like this in the States. The food is incredibly good, with so many high-quality options that it feels more like a collection of restaurants than a typical food court. Every stall offers something different, and everything I tried was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. I came here so often that it basically became part of my daily routine—and somehow, I never got bored. There’s always something new to try, which makes it dangerously easy to keep coming back (like I did lol). If you’re a food lover, this place is a must-visit and easily one of the best food court experiences I’ve ever had.

들어가면 무료입장권과 금메달 모양의 종이를 준다

title: 숭례문

reviews.text:
Sungnyemun Gate (also known as Namdaemun Gate) is National Treasure No. 1 of South Korea.
Yes, that is literally what it is.
The gate is listed as National Treasure No. 1 - part of the nation's cultural heritage.

The gate was built back in the 14th century and marked the southern boundary of Seoul (by the way, the name itself translates as "Great South Gate").
All the key events in Korean history took place here; the gate was one of the eight entrances to the city.

Namdaemun Gate suffered serious damage during the Korean War. Of course, it was later restored but in 2008, a man who felt wronged because he hadn't received an insurance payout set the gate on fire.
And it burned down…

The restoration took five years, and now the gate is open to visitors once again.

I might be wrong but my feeling was that Seoul doesn't seem to have a single center like most European cities do (with the central square, government building, central cathedral, the oldest restaurant - all in one place). As a result, many monuments are located in places that might seem unusual to a European tourist.
Here, for instance, there are only modern buildings and new roads around the gate, and seeing the historic structure surrounded by contemporary structures can feel a bit puzzling… On the other hand, if you look at 19th‑century photos showing shacks all around it, this modern setting is definitely better...

The gate itself is stunningly beautiful.
I believe it is an absolute must to visit the Gate if you come to Seoul.
After all, it is No. 1 national treasure!

Sungnyemun Gate (officially Sungnyemun, meaning "Gate of Exalted Ceremonies") is arguably the most famous historical landmark in Seoul. It is better known to many as Namdaemun (South Great Gate).

The Beginning (1398): Construction was completed in 1398 during the reign of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty. It was the main southern entrance to the walled city of Seoul.

The Vertical Sign: You might notice that unlike other gates, the name sign on Sungnyemun is written vertically. According to feng shui principles, the nearby Gwanaksan Mountain had a strong "fire" energy that threatened the capital. The name "Sungnye" also represents fire, and by writing it vertically, it was believed to act as a "fire against fire" shield to protect the city.

The Tragedy of 2008: On February 10, 2008, a 69-year-old man set fire to the wooden pagoda atop the stone base in an act of arson. The entire nation watched in shock as the 600-year-old wooden structure collapsed.

The Restoration (2013): It took over five years and approximately 27.7 billion won ($24 million USD) to restore the gate using traditional tools and methods, including the use of rare 500-year-old pine trees. It reopened to the public in May 2013.

Passed by this historic gate while visiting Seoul, snapped a couple of shots.

A must see if you’re heading to the palace.

The gate dates back to the 14th century and you can truly feel the history it has witnessed and endured through the centuries.

Standing there really gives you a sense of how much it has withstood to remain preserved to this day.

Sungnyemun Gate (commonly known as Namdaemun) is one of the most iconic historical landmarks in Seoul, South Korea. Built in 1398 during the Joseon Dynasty, it served as the main southern gate to the walled city of Seoul. The name "Sungnyemun" means "Gate of Exalted Ceremonies." As a symbol of Seoul's heritage, Namdaemun is designated as National Treasure No. 1 of South Korea. The gate features a traditional wooden pagoda-style pavilion atop a massive stone base, showcasing classic Korean architectural style. In 2008, the gate was severely damaged by arson but was meticulously restored and reopened to the public in 2013. Today, it stands not only as a historical structure but also as a reminder of Korea’s resilience and dedication to cultural preservation.
Each time I’m in Seoul, I always visit here. Today, a nice day in mid-October I visited it again. Lots of locals and tourists.

아이가 자라면서 함께 갈 수 있는 곳이 늘어난다는 건 부모에게 참 고마운 일입니다 이번에 다녀온 롯데스위트파크는 그런 의미에서 꽤나 밀도 있는 시간을 선물해 주었습니다 사실 어른들에게는 익숙한 과자들이지만 아이의 눈으로 바라보는 거대한 초콜릿 세상은 그 자체로 동화 같은 풍경이었나 봅니다

​공간이 아주 넓지는 않지만 예약제로 운영되어 쾌적하게 둘러볼 수 있다는 점이 마음에 들었습니다 아이와 함께하는 여행이나 나들이는 항상 여유가 중요한데 이곳은 그 여유를 충분히 보장해 주더군요 화려한 미사여구보다는 아이의 천진난만한 표정 하나로 모든 설명이 끝나는 그런 곳이었습니다 김포 근처에서 아이와 함께 의미 있는 오후를 보내고 싶은 분들이라면 한 번쯤 걸음 해보시길 권하고 싶습니다

reviews.text:
Big, stylish department store with 11 levels of fashion, lifestyle brands & luxurious boutiques. Well laid out & easy to browse.

There’s a pleasant sky garden on the 11th floor for a short break, while the food plaza at B1 offers plenty of dining options. Duty-free shopping is conveniently located on the 8th & 9th floors.

A great upscale stop in the COEX area  ✨

The Hyundai Department Store is one huge building with several floors, and every visit feels like an experience. I mainly explored the ground floor and the food sections.

On the ground floor, there are many jewelry and luxury beauty brands like Clinique, Estée Lauder, and Chanel, for makeup and perfumes. It feels elegant and well curated.

If you go downstairs, it opens into a wonderful world of food. There are snack and pastry corners, boulangeries, sweets, and cakes, and the smell is simply amazing. You can even watch how some of the pastries are being prepared. There’s also a food corner, which I didn’t try this time, but everything looked and smelled so tempting.

The grocery and cookery section is beautiful. Fresh vegetables and fruits of very high quality, fresh meat and fish, frozen items, and a great selection of international foods. There’s even a special corner for items from around the world, like pasta and imported products, plus a section with fresh kimchi and pickled specialties. Prices are slightly higher than in other places, but the quality really shows.

What I truly appreciate is the staff. Everyone is helpful, friendly, and very polite. If you have a question or need help finding something, they really take care of you.

It has its price, of course, but it always feels like a small adventure and a pleasure to walk through. And whenever I’m looking for something specific and can’t find it elsewhere, I know this place will have it.

Hyundai is a large conglomerate in South Korea and one of the many businesses they operate is a high end department store. This store has 10 floors and has 2 floors of duty free shops. The very top floor has a nice open garden area. There's also a floor full of nice restaurants are the top. The basement has a supermarket and many gourmet food stalls. Designer labels are spread all throughout the store.

A very good mall for shopping. Clean and neatly arranged.

The star highlight was the basement food court - it serves excellent food that is reasonably priced. Portions are substantial and there are lots of tables around for customers.

I will definitely return to the food court - high quality food, clean environment and an overall pleasant dining experience.

Highly recommended. Thumbs up!

The Hyundai Department Store food court is an absolute 10/10. I seriously wish we had something like this in the States. The food is incredibly good, with so many high-quality options that it feels more like a collection of restaurants than a typical food court. Every stall offers something different, and everything I tried was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. I came here so often that it basically became part of my daily routine—and somehow, I never got bored. There’s always something new to try, which makes it dangerously easy to keep coming back (like I did lol). If you’re a food lover, this place is a must-visit and easily one of the best food court experiences I’ve ever had.

reviews.text:
This was one of the better, cleaner jjimjilbangs I've been to in Seoul. We paid 22,000won for a 8-hour use, and was given a gown and two towels. Even though it was a weekday night (10pm) the baths were somewhat crowded and there was a queue for the scrub. Scrub was 40,000won and super thorough, would recommend.

Good for people who have not experienced jjimjilbangs before as this facility is quite well-equipped, providing shampoo and soap, as well as basic skincare.

Cleanliness was honestly not the best but manageable and far better than many neighbourhood saunas. Have a sikhye and some eggs for the full experience.

I had a nice cultural experience at the spa. The entry fee was 22k kwn, they give you a key for your shoe locker, and then you go to the official spa area. There were many plunge pools to choose from and I quite enjoyed my Korean Scrub, which was 40k kwn (paid in cash). I slept in their sleeping area, which was fine as I always bring noise-cancelling headphones due to my overall noise sensitivity. I have many tattoos, and I'm not white; I'm Puerto Rican. At no time was there any bad treatment from anyone there (customers or staff). I would 100% recommend this place and will be visiting again in the near future.

I loved my experience in this jjimjilbang so much that I easily spent the whole weekend here. I guarantee you’ll feel the same way that you’ll immediately want to go back the next day.

They have good facilities, cozy and relaxing space, a restaurant that serves traditional Korean food and drinks. But the main thing I loved about it is it’s a female-only jjimjilbang (unlike other bathhouses in Seoul) which made me feel very comfortable, as a foreigner trying it for the first time.

After a weekend here, I’ve never felt so refreshed, light, and relaxed in my life. 10/10 would highly recommend!

I had a wonderful experience at Spa Rai! The atmosphere is relaxing from the moment you walk in — clean, calm, and beautifully designed. The staff are very professional and friendly, making me feel completely comfortable throughout my visit. The massage was one of the best I’ve ever had — you can really feel their skill and attention to detail. The prices  are reasonable for the quality of service you get. I left feeling refreshed, relaxed, and will definitely come back again. Highly recommend Spa Rai to anyone looking for a quality spa experience!

The perfect place to go after a long flight or during your stay in Seoul. I went here twice and the front desk woman and the scrub lady were both very nice. The other women that were guests were very kind and I never felt uncomfortable as a foreigner. The Ramen is very good here too.

reviews.text: As far as malls go, this one serves its purpose well. There are plenty of selections and it's not very crowded and it  is well communicated by the metro. A large-scale complex mall that is extremely convenient and full of things to enjoy.
It is easily accessible not only by car but also by subway and bus.

It is directly connected to a department store and also features a cinema and a wide variety of restaurants, making it a place where you can spend the entire day.

The first floor frequently transforms into a large event space, hosting movie promotions, new product showcases, and various themed markets.

It also houses a large E-Mart and a major bookstore, so you can enjoy both shopping and cultural activities in one place.

All areas, including restrooms and other facilities, are kept very clean, making this mall especially comfortable to use.

Just about a pleasant size of the mall and only has one kids attraction (zoo). It attaches to Shinsegae buildings and when u take that path (ground floor) it will lead u to Yeongdeungpo-gu market and to the subway  station which is a great walk to explore.

A beautiful place to shop, browse, eat, or just sit and relax especially if the weather is cold out.  I really love the Christmas decorations and the vibes.  We had an amazing time here and will visit again before we leave Seoul.

On the upper floors, you’ll find a dining area and a movie theater, making it a great all-in-one destination for shopping, eating, and entertainment.

reviews.text:
First time at this spa! I initially thought it was part of the Signiel Hotel, but they are actually just partners. I think their service here is way more special than the hotel to be honest.

From beginning to end, it was absolutely amazing. I highly recommend them—the special tea and snack at the end were such a lovely touch.

My massage therapist Anna was very sweet and very thorough.

The staff here was amazing.

A Luxurious, Worthwhile Escape — Exceeded My Expectations

I had a truly wonderful experience at Signiel Spa Retreat. My massage therapist was exceptionally professional, polite, and knowledgeable, making the entire treatment both relaxing and rejuvenating.

I had originally planned to spend my spa day at the Sulwhasoo Spa, but due to scheduling issues, I booked Signiel Spa Retreat at the last minute — and I’m so glad I did. From the moment I arrived, the atmosphere was serene and elegant. I arrived a bit early and had time to sit, unwind, and take in the breathtaking views before my appointment.

While the experience is on the expensive side, it was absolutely worth every moment and every won. The service, ambiance, and overall attention to detail made it feel truly special.

I honestly don’t understand why it’s rated 4.4 stars — my experience was flawless. If you plan to visit, give yourself plenty of time to arrive early and soak in the entire experience. Don’t rush; enjoy the calm and luxury you’re paying for.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for a peaceful, high-end retreat in Seoul.

I booked a 90 minute Les Nouvels Aroma massage here and highly recommend it for improving circulation and body slimming. It's mostly a Swedish style massage with elements of Asian massage. The level of service, from welcome tea to luxury accents during massage to post-massage treat, are all five starworthy. My only recommendation would be that the appointment duration is longer to savor all the delightful parts of the experience!

Absolutely loved the entire experience from start to finish. Clett was amazing. The deep relaxation with body scrub treatment was heavenly. Clett explained everything and used outstanding techniques. The staff were polished, warm, welcoming. The spa was beautiful. I just can’t say enough! Highly recommend!

I had an amazing time at Signiel Spa today. I had a massage with a stunning view of Seoul and the best location in Lotte Tower. A huge thank you to the management for their understanding and to the massage therapist for the amazing massage❤️

google_addr: 27 Cheongpa-ro 47da-gil, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: This is a great museum with a lot of important truths about the history of Korea. However with no available wi-fi and the majority of the information only available in Korean it's very difficult to visit as an interested foreigner to learn more about the hardships of Korean people in the past.
Small museum not much to see as it's mostly in Korean. Right by a university so lots of dining and cafe options. Highly recommend wako taco 🌮 which is a few min away

This museum is very special to Korean and a symbol of our democratic Korea. It is based on a late scholar named Lim, Jongguk's Japanese colonial studies. He found in 1960s that most of very powerful and respectful people including his own father and President Park, Chung hee were traitors worked for Japan in colonial times. And he found they hided their shameful lifes, furthermore they totally fabricated their careers and achievements to patriats'. So he alone investigated and recorded the traitors' histories eventhough his poverty and their threats. But he died in 1989 without any good results. After his death, his friends tried to tell people his achievements. Finally it opened this August owing to many people's donations and volunteering. There are some patriats' tombs and Bakbeom Kim Gu memorial center near. It is a private museum, so no free admission. But I highly recommend you visit if you want to know why Korea doesn't get along with Japan and normal korean people hate some rich families.
A museum that is dedicated to Japanese colonial period of Korea. The main exhibition is on the second floor. The exhibition is not extensive but very informative. There is no enterance fee.

The Japanese occupation of Korea was a traumatic part of their history , somewhat unknown to Westerners. Recommend that you watch the series PACHINKO to get some understanding. Little english to be had but not hard to pick up the gist from the displays and photographs.

reviews.text: Fun exhibition when we visited

일민미술관,
동아일보 사옥
Office Building of Dong-A llbo
서울특별시 유형문화유산
서울 종로구 화동의 옛 중앙학교 교사를 빌려 1920년 4월 1일 창간한 동아일보사가 1926년
12월 전용사옥으로 지은 건물이다. 국내에서 가장 오래된 언론사 건물로서 1992년까지
이곳에서 신문을 발행하였다. 준공 당시에는 지하 1층, 지상 3층으로 철근콘크리트와
벽돌구조이며 외벽에는 석재와 타일을 붙였고 인조석도 부분적으로 사용하였다.
현관 위에서 옥탑까지 수직으로 이어져 있는 내민창이 특징인데 이는 1920년대에 세계적으로
유행하던 모더니즘 디자인으로 음아가는 당시의 디자인 경향의 단계를 보여주고 있다.
1963년 4월 이 건물에서 동아방송이 개국하기도 하였으며 몇 차례 증개축을 거쳐 1968년 지상
6층으로 확장되었다. 충정로로 사옥을 음긴 후 1996년부터 일민미술관으로 사용하고 있다.
2001년 큰 규모의 보수 및 증축공사를 하여 내부 모습은 많이 달라졌으나 외관과 내부공간의
일부는 원형대로 보존되어 있어 1920년대 건축양식과 건축재료의 유구를 살펴볼 수 있으며
광화문 네거리의 근대시기 모습을 전해주는 유일한 건물이다.

입장권이 있는 박물관이에요~ 하지만 입장권 가격에 신문 만들기 체험도 있기 때문에 저는 괜찮았습니다.

신문의역사와 신문이 어떻게 만들어졌는지.. 신문을 만들었던 기계도 볼수 있어서 너무 좋았어요~

title: 신아기념관(서울 구 신아일보 별관)

reviews.text: After passing Jeongdong Theater along Deoksugung Palace's stone wall road in Jung-gu, Seoul, you'll find a vine-covered red brick building marked as the 'Former Shin-A Ilbo Annex Building.' Built in the 1930s with reinforced concrete, it was originally a private headquarters for an American sewing machine company. The building had one underground and two above-ground floors, with stairs leading to the first floor. Shin-A Ilbo acquired it in 1969, adding two more floors in 1975. Following media consolidation by the military government in the 1980s, it became the Shin-Ah Memorial Hall.

2008년 8월 27일 국가등록문화재로 지정되었다. 1930년대에 지하1층, 지상2층으로 건축된 철근콘크리트 건물이다. 외벽은 중국 상하이에서 가져온 붉은 벽돌로 쌓았다. 1975년에 지상4층으로 증축되었다.

구한말에는 세무총사(현재의 관세청에 해당) 사옥으로 쓰였고, 독일인 외교고문 묄렌도르프의 사무실도 이곳에 있었다. 그 뒤 미국기업 싱어미싱회사(Singer Sewing Machine Company)의 한국지부 사무실과 그 상사원들의 숙소 등으로 사용되다가 1963년 신아일보사에 매각되었다. 이후부터 1980년 10월 언론기관통폐합으로 《신아일보》가 《경향신문》에 흡수·통합되기 전까지 신아일보사 별관으로 사용되었다.

구한말의 파란만장한 역사와 함께 1980년 신군부 언론기관통폐합 조치로 언론수난사 현장을 대변하는 등 근현대 역사·문화적 가치가 높은 건물이다. 또한 당시 민간건물에는 거의 볼 수 없었던 철근 콘크리트조 건물로, 슬라브(Slab) 구조 및 원형철근 사용 등 일강점기의 건축수법이 잘 남아 있어 근대건축의 기술사적연구에 좋은 자료이다.
[두산백과]

신아기념관 이곳은 건물만으로도 충분히 볼만한 가치가 있으며, 1층에는 카페에서 가벼운 음료와 식사를 즐길수 있다.

2층에는 모순갤러리라는 공예전문 갤러리가 이곳의 분위기를 밝혀주고 있다.

신아일보사 별관.

신아일보(新亞日報)는 1965년 창간된 대한민국의 종합일간지였다. 1980년 언론 통폐합으로 인하여 80년 11월 25일자 지령 4806호를 끝으로 경향신문으로 흡수합병에 의해 통폐합(폐업)당하였다. 현재의 신아일보는 2001년에 창간한 신한일보가 2003년 6월 8일에 제호를 바꿔 재창간한 것이다.｜

시청역근처에 있는 구 신아일보사 별관.덕수궁길을 걷다보면 정동극장을 지나 구 신아일보사 별관이 나온다.서양식 벽돌이 멋스럽고 유럽에 온 것같다.1층 정문입구에 작게 신아일보사와 창업주에 대해 간단하게 사진과 글이 있고 지하 1층 식당으로 들어가면 아주 작은 공간에 신아일보사 역사와 신아일보사 신조와 창업주에 대한 글과프로필과  사진이 있다.창업주 장기봉님은 기자로 일을하였고 코리아타임즈 부사장을 역임하였고 한국일보 편집국장 서울신문사 사장을 역임하였다.또한 대통령공보관을 하였고 유엔총회 대표를 하였다고한다.신문사 기념관에서 글을 읽으며 한참을 감탄했다.그이유는 신문사가 사회적 정치적인부분에서 중립을 지키고 독립적이고 자유롭게 신문에 글을 썼기때문에 그시대에 정치적인 독립속에서 자유롭게 글을 쓴다는게 매우 어렸웠을 것으로 짐작된다.하지만 그럼에도 신문사 창업주의 의지로 독자적으로 글을 쓰고 16년을 운영을 해왔다니...놀라울따름이다...신문사의 창업주의 깊은 철학과 나라를 위하는 마음이 고스라니 느껴졌다.요즘 한국인들이 구 신아신문사 창업주의 정신을 조금이라도 배웠으면 하는 생각이 들었다

title: 싱크 넥스트 25(Sync Next 25)
google_name: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
google_addr: 175 Sejong-daero, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: My trip started on a high at Sejong Theatre, where I watched the musical Phantom. The performance was absolutely stunning—the set, the music, the voices. For a couple of hours, I was so absorbed I didn’t even check my phone (which, let’s be honest, says a lot for a Gen Z like me). It felt like stepping into a different world, and I left with goosebumps.

My time exploring Sejong Plaza was spent enjoying the beautiful statue of Sejong the Great. There's many animations on the buildings, hidden alley restaurants that are ALL 10/10, and subway/public transportation hub.

The Sejong Center for the Performing Arts is an iconic performance venue located in Gwanghwamun, Seoul. For Korean artists, performing here is considered the ultimate honor, and it wouldn't be an exaggeration to call it the Carnegie Hall of Korea. While the facilities are somewhat dated and inconvenient, they are receiving positive feedback. It is conveniently located right next to Gwanghwamun Square, and it is also great for a walk after the performance. Making its own original performances like Ilmu(One Dance) is also a promising idea.

Exhibition
Masterpieces from the San Diego Museum of Art: "From the Renaissance to Impressionism"

Hey, let me share a quick thought with you.

If you ever find yourself near Gwanghwamun, take a moment to walk by the Sejong Center. And if you already have a ticket in hand, even better. You are about to step into one of Korea’s most meaningful performance halls.

Sejong Center has long been considered a symbol of Korean performing arts. When it opened in 1978, its pipe organ was the largest in Asia. Back in Europe, pipe organs were a way for cities to show their pride and prosperity, and Sejong Center carried that same spirit here in Seoul.

Sure, some people might say it is not the most modern venue anymore. And they would not be completely wrong. But this place holds memories. It has watched generations grow up, quietly standing its ground while the city changed around it. That kind of history matters.

Personally, I have spent some memorable nights here. I watched THE GREATEST: Thrill with Jeong Dong-ha and Sohyang in September 2023, Universal Ballet’s The Nutcracker in December 2023, and Chung Myung-Whun conducting Beethoven’s Ninth with the KBS Symphony at the end of 2025. Since it is a multipurpose hall, you might not always get the same powerful acoustics as a dedicated concert hall, especially for classical music. Still, the experience feels special every time.

Getting there is easy. Just hop on Seoul Subway Line 5 and get off at Gwanghwamun Station. One small thing to note, though. There is no traditional cloakroom. Instead, you will find unmanned lockers on the second floor. They work, but the touch screen can be a little tricky. Maybe it is just me getting older.

The box office is on the first floor, and there are kiosks if you already bought your ticket. You will also spot vending machines for water on each floor, which always comes in handy.

One last tip. The Grand Theater usually opens about two hours before the performance for security reasons, and audiences are allowed into the hall about thirty minutes before the show starts.

Take your time, soak it in, and enjoy the moment.

Insadong is the perfect district in Seoul to immerse yourself in traditional Korean culture and escape the city’s high-tech bustle. The main street is lined with beautifully preserved hanok style buildings, art galleries showcasing calligraphy and fine arts, and classic tea houses serving traditional brews. It’s a wonderful place to shop for meaningful, handmade souvenirs like traditional papers (hanji), ceramics, and antique items.

The highlight for shoppers is Ssamziegil, an architecturally unique, spiral-shaped mall designed like a traditional Korean courtyard. You’ll find four floors packed with small, independent boutiques offering novelty items, whimsical modern crafts, and unique souvenirs that are distinctly Korean—far beyond the typical tourist fare. From quirky accessories to handmade jewelry and art, Ssamziegil is the best place to find that one-of-a-kind gift.

It’s a vibrant shopping and entertainment destination in downtown Seoul that offers a variety of options for visitors. Spanning 11 impressive floors, the mall is thoughtfully divided into sections: Fashion, Living, and Culture. It features the I Park Department Store, Digital Shopping Center, and Event Park, with standout attractions such as a CGV cinema, e-Sports Stadium, miniature golf, and a large bookstore. With over 100 restaurants, a diverse food court, and charming cafes, the dining options are plentiful. Shoppers can explore an array of electronics, fashion, and home goods, while cultural events, fashion shows, and festivals add to the lively atmosphere. Additional features like a video game arcade, an outdoor garden, and a culture center makes it a good destination for shopping, dining, and entertainment in the city!

reviews.text:
Visiting the Art Sonje Center in Seoul in Aug 2021 was a profoundly moving experience. The curated space and the photographic artwork were both thought-provoking and evocative. Themes of extremities, natural phenomena, and supernatural beliefs of the locals intertwined seamlessly, each element resonating on different levels. The use of white, thin cotton threads and mummified black lava created a stark contrast, while circles, composition, and texture added layers of meaning that felt both tangible and abstract.

The artwork spoke of redemption, debris, and the fragile linkage—or lineage—between past and present. Half-soaked in salty water, the imagery seemed to evoke the soul of the dead, with brass bowls symbolizing reconciliation rather than perfection. The emotions conveyed were desperate yet hopeful, a delicate balance that kept me reflecting long after I left the gallery.

There were so many elements to contemplate, each knocking on the door of the mind, inviting deeper introspection. The experience was like a conversation with the artwork—ongoing, never quite complete, yet profoundly fulfilling.

reviews.text: A really wonderful and unique experience for art lovers and those with a curious mind! It’s a really gentle and calming experience that I think everyone can enjoy. And it’s a cute neighbourhood to explore too!

진담 프로그램으로 예약하고 방문했습니다! 20대 후반으로 고민이 많고 많이 지친 시기에 좀 쉬고자 방문했는데… 너무너무 만족스러웠습니다. 해가 들어오는 따뜻한 공간에서 평소 생각해보지 못한 것들을 들여다보았는데 너무너무 힐링이었습니다. 옆에서 프로그램 진행도 해주시고, 어떻게 접근해야 할지 가이드도 주셨고, 또 혼자 몰입할 수 있게 자리를 슬며시 비켜주시기도 했습니다. 그 섬세한 배려에 또 한 번 따뜻함을 느꼈습니다! 다음에 또 다른 프로그랜 하러 방문하겠습니다!
조용히 나 자신의 내면과 대화하며 힐링이 되는 시간이었어요. 햇살 가득한 실내와 친절하고 편안한 사장님의 얘기들이 기분을 차분하게 해주면서 오랜만에 그림을 그려볼 수 있었네요.
차를 한 잔 하면서 평온하게 멍 때리면서 내면의 예술적 창작 본능을 자극해 보는 좋은 경험이었습니다.  자세한 안내 설명과 함께 직접 준비해 주신 차의 향이 은은하게 입안에서 오래도록 느껴 졌습니다. 누구나 바쁜 생활에서 잠시 나와서 이렇게 머리를 비우는 예술적 체험을 해보는 것도 아름다운 삶이라는 생각이 듭니다.
일상에서 잠시 벗어나 나를 천천히 들여다보고 싶은 분들께 추천하고 싶습니다. 손끝으로 나를 표현하는 경험은 생각보다 깊고 오래 남아 부모님 모시고 함께 와도 특별한 경험이 되고 정말 좋을 것 같습니다😊

reviews.text:
떡볶이와 튀김이 맛있는 분식집 입니다.
생활의 달인에도 나오고 해서 방문해 보았습니다.
국물과 같이 먹어야 맛있는 국물 떡볶이 입니다.
쌀떡이고, 어묵국물은 제공되지 않습니다.
깔끔하게 맵고, 달달함이 잘 어울리는 떡볶이 입니다.
튀김은 주문과 동시에 만드시는것 같아 바삭하니 맛있습니다.
장소가 협소하여 대기가 있을 수 도 있습니다.

생활의 달인에 떡볶이 달인으로 출연하신 떡볶이집. 비트로 떡볶이 소스를 만들어서 떡볶이 색깔이 갈색 베이스가 아니라 약간 와인색? 진보라색? 그런 느낌이 남. 고추장의 텁텁한 맛이나 억지스런 조미료 맛이 느껴지지 않음.

튀김은 오징어튀김과 가지튀김을 먹었는데 튀김 자체가 느끼하지 않고 깔끔하고 원재료의 맛과 향이 잘 살아 있음. 아주 바삭함. 간장 안찍어 먹는걸 추천. 사진에 나온 것 보다 색깔이 더욱 투명한 노란색임. 기름을 자주 가시는 듯. 특히 가지튀김이 아주 좋았음.

어묵은 쏘쏘함. 모두 다해서 11,500원 나옴. 가격도 저렴함. 또 갈거임.

25.01.18 토
장점?
1. 분식을 좋아하는 사람으로 재방문의사 있음!
2. 튀김 주문하면 바로 튀겨주는 시스템.
3. 떡볶이는 자극적인것에 길들여졌는지 밋밋하지 한거 같지만 제 기준에는 좋았음!
4. 순대도 맛있습니당!
5. 12,000원으로 이정도면 진짜 혜자인듯!
단점?
1. 휴지는 두루마리휴지

For lunch, we had tteokbokki, Modum Sundae, fish cake, and Modum Fried Chicken. As an old Korean atmosphere, it was a precious time to enjoy our meal together, although it may be a bit small. The seasoning of tteokbokki was spicy and delicious. Soondae was chewy. If you think of old memories of Korea, I recommend it.

reviews.text:
Nice neighborhood park with space to chill or to stroll. An entry/exit point to a mountain path is available near the temple plaza.

Surrounded by beautiful trees, including persimmons.

A lovely park with two dog parks (one for small dogs and the other for big dogs), a children's forest playground, 강감찬 cafe and an entrance to 서울둘레길 which leads to Gwanak mountain. It also has a magnificent shrine of general 강감찬. Its opening hour could be inconvenient if you work. The shrine has a wheelchair/pushchair access at the back but unfortunately it only leads to the first level of the shine (not the main part).

The park is amazing! There are mini farms in the the park, small pond, temples, plazas, science center nearby. The park is good for the family to visit. Kids can play in the plaza with their bikes, skateboard, scooter, etc. Older people hike the mountain that is behind the temples. There is even a place for a dog to walk or hang around. No doubt why there are many people visiting the park. The scenery is great, peaceful, and exciting. The park seems to be surrounded by the mountain so you’ll see more trees, and it’s beautiful in Autumn because of the color of the leaves. No fees to pay. The park is free to visit, and the historical site next to it. I’m not sure about the science center since it is closed when we visited the place. There is also an English village across the park. A lot of things to do around Nakseongdae park. I highly recommend family and everyone who’d like to enjoy the nature and have a simple activity outdoor.

I enjoyed a sunday morning at nakseongdea park and climbed gwanak mountain right next to it...
Recommended for everyone and the hike is suitable both for kids and adults...

Anyoung Insadong is a vibrant and eclectic shopping destination that offers a little bit of everything, making it a must-visit spot in the heart of Insadong. This multi-level complex is home to an array of small boutique shops and a lively flea market on the ground floor, where you can find unique crafts, souvenirs, and one-of-a-kind items that reflect the local culture.

The upper levels feature a variety of restaurants, catering to diverse tastes, from traditional Korean cuisine to international flavors. There’s no shortage of options for food lovers, and the mall even connects to a hotel, making it a convenient choice for travelers staying in the area.

One of the standout features is the Colorpool museum located on the top floor, which adds an artistic and cultural touch to the shopping experience. For those seeking a more relaxed vibe, there are also several charming cafes scattered throughout the mall, perfect for enjoying a coffee break while soaking in the vibrant atmosphere.

Anyoung Shopping Mall is a complex that primarily targets a young clientele. The upper floors house shops specializing in K-pop-related goodies (merchandise). You will find items like t-shirts, figurines, and posters. The lower floors are occupied by restaurants and cafés, while the ground floor features a resting and entertainment areas. 😊

reviews.text:
I recently had surgery at Answer Plastic Surgery, and I am extremely satisfied with the entire experience. From the very first online consultation to the in-person meeting, the surgery itself, and the post-op care, everything was absolutely top-notch.
I felt completely in good hands throughout the process and didn’t experience any pain at all. The nurses and doctor were incredibly attentive, providing exceptional care every step of the way. My recovery was quick and smooth, with no issues whatsoever.
The team at Answer Plastic Surgery is not only professional but also very friendly, making me feel comfortable and well taken care of throughout the entire journey. I would wholeheartedly recommend this clinic to anyone looking for high-quality care. If I ever need anything else in the future, I’ll definitely be coming back.
I'm truly grateful for everything and wish the entire team continued success. Thank you so much for making this experience such a positive one!

I had my revision rhinoplasty with Dr. Choi through Seoul Medical Guide, and I couldn’t be happier with the entire experience. My original nose had very little bridge, and after my previous surgery where the silicone was removed, it became upturned — something that had bothered me for years. These were my main concerns going into the consultation, and Dr. Choi immediately put me at ease.

He patiently explained the process and showed me examples of similar successful results. Dr. Choi reassured me that he could achieve the look I wanted — a higher bridge with a more refined, natural shape. He explained that he would use a silicone implant to create the bridge and donated rib cartilage to define the shape and tip. His professionalism and confidence gave me complete trust in his skills.

The clinic staff were incredibly caring and attentive, always making sure I was comfortable throughout each step. During my recovery, they checked in regularly and provided treatments to support the healing process, which made everything feel much smoother and less stressful.

After years of hesitation and dissatisfaction, I finally have the nose I’ve always wanted. I absolutely love my results — from the elegant high bridge to the cute, defined tip. I’m so thankful to Dr. Choi and the Seoul Medical Guide team for helping me regain my confidence and making this experience so positive and fulfilling.

Appreciate Dr. Choi Min for putting the time and effort into my care. I asked tons of questions during the consultation to make sure I was comfortable enough before progressing to surgery based on what I wanted. He answered most of my questions and made the process as smooth as possible. The surgery itself was surprisingly quick. I didn’t expect all to be done within a couple of hours. Do admit the post op process recovery was rougher than I thought, thought its expected, especially with the bruising. The red light therapy and IV antibiotics helped with the recovery process at each follow up. I also appreciate how attentive the front staff were in welcoming me to the clinic. I am still awaiting my final results, but am overall satisfied with the current outcomes.

So happy I came to this clinic. I traveled from the US here on a strong recommendation and they really put my mind at ease here. The doctor was very knowledgeable and friendly (he speaks English), beautiful boutique style clinical setting, and also had a translator provided with Seoul Medical Guide. I’m very happy with all of their services, attention to detail, and the final results. Everyone was very thorough and made me comfortable, something I had a bit of anxiety about initially. Definitely recommend to anyone looking to come here for medical/esthetic procedures.

I do not recommend this clinic. There are many clinics in Seoul that are much better. Their aftercare is appalling, don’t expect them to respond to any of your messages post surgery as they stop caring as soon as they get their payment and you’re out of the clinic.

If you want a clinic that doesn’t care about its patients post surgery and is unresponsive then this is the place for you.

'향교'는 조선시대에 지방에 설립된 국립 교육기관으로, 유교 경전 교육과 문묘에 대한 제사를 지내는 기능을 담당했고, 사립 교육기관인 '서원'과는 좀 다르다. 지방에서 주로 봐 온 향교가 서울내에 있다고 해서 좀 신기했다. 규모는 작은편이나 깨끗하게 관리되고 있는 느낌을 받는다. 옛 성인 등의 위패를 모시고 있는 대성전은 닫혀 있어서 내부를 볼수 없었지만, 명륜당을 비롯해서 동재와 서재는 구경할 수 있다. 방문했을 때 명륜당에서 아이들이 가르침을 받고 있는 모습을 봤는데, 현재도 교육기관으로써의 역할을 하고 있는것 같아서 흐믓했다. 지자체에서 지역주민들과 학생들을 대상으로 여러가지 교육 프로그램을 운영하고 있는 것으로 보인다. 주차공간은 거의 없기 때문에 대중교통을 이용하는편이 좋다.

The Hangang River stands as a vibrant and essential landmark in Seoul, dividing the city into northern and southern halves while offering a dynamic mix of recreation, culture, and scenic beauty. Its banks are lined with meticulously maintained parks, bustling food stalls, and a diverse range of recreational facilities, making it a favorite destination for both locals and visitors.
Recent enhancements, such as the new Hangang River Bus service, have further increased the river’s accessibility. This innovative option provides not only convenient transportation but also unique sightseeing opportunities, featuring panoramic views and onboard amenities. The river serves as a hub for outdoor activities throughout the year—biking, kayaking, water sports, fishing, and seasonal festivals ensure there’s always something to enjoy, regardless of when you visit.
Overall, the Hangang River remains a top destination for relaxation, adventure, and experiencing the heart of Seoul’s community spirit. Its blend of natural beauty, modern conveniences, and cultural events makes it a must-visit for anyone exploring the city.

Came here for lunch at the Le Café (reservation made via CatchTable). The set menu feels thoughtfully curated & every dish was beautifully presented. The atmosphere is elegant yet comfortable

After the meal, headed downstairs to browse the ready-to-wear collections. The store was surprisingly quiet for a Sunday afternoon. Bought a jumper with the help of advisor Jisoo Lim, who was attentive & helpful throughout.

Also noticed that many boutiques along this shopping district are housed in standalone buildings rather than inside a typical shopping mall, which gives the area a more refined & upscale feel.

Overall, a very pleasant & enjoyable visit — both for the café experience & the shopping.

Le Café Louis Vuitton is simply outstanding. The moment you walk in, the interior decoration takes your breath away, elegant, artistic, and perfectly curated, just as you’d expect from Louis Vuitton.

The service is hands-down the best in Seoul: attentive, warm, and flawless from start to finish. The food? Absolutely yummy, with finger-licking-good desserts that are on another level. I’m still thinking about them!

Highly recommended dishes: their club sandwiches, lobster rolls, and so many more delicious options.

I genuinely can’t wait to come back. If you’re looking for a place that blends luxury, comfort, and unforgettable flavors, this is the one.

Le cafe Louis Vuitton is so amazing fashion designer lv dessert good service

Seoul Louis Vuitton Cafe:☕️👜date @louisvuitton  To celebrate the romantic spirit of Pepero Day, we embarked on a special journey to the heart of Apgujeon, where the magnificent Louis Vuitton flagship store majestically stands.

The cafe welcomes guests into two elegant halls, one of which is particularly captivating: its stunning glass ceiling floods the space with light and air, creating an immense sense of boundless openness. This time, our mission was to delve into the world of Louis Vuitton's celebrated desserts and, of course, to savor a perfectly brewed, aromatic coffee ☕️.

To our delightful surprise, we discovered that they serve not only sweets but also a full dinner! Guests could choose individual dishes or immerse themselves in a world of gastronomic delights by ordering an exquisite set menu. My heart was set on the famous peach cake, but it was so popular it had already sold out! However, the vanilla cake exceeded all expectations – it was simply divine. The coffee, elegantly adorned with the brand's logo, provided the perfect concluding touch.

To immerse yourself in this luxury, advance booking via Naver is essential. The reservation fee for two people is 100,000 won, but rest assured, this amount is automatically refunded to your card upon arrival at the cafe.

The service here truly lives up to Louis Vuitton's impeccable standards: a concierge gracefully opens your car door, valet parking is provided, you are personally escorted to your table, and payment is conveniently handled right there, without needing to approach a counter.

After we had enjoyed our desserts, we went downstairs to see the Louis Vuitton collection and try the new premium fragrances. Thanks to the consultant, I chose the perfect perfume – the mysterious "FANTASMAGORY" from Louis Vuitton.

reviews.text:
I had an excellent experience at Etonne, and I’m really glad I chose this clinic.

From the consultation to post-op care, everything felt thoughtful and professional.  What I appreciated most was that Dr. Cho Jeongmok was very conservative and honest; he didn’t try to upsell unnecessary procedures and clearly explained what would and wouldn’t benefit my face.

The eyelid surgery itself was smooth, and my recovery has been much easier than I anticipated.  Even early on, the results look natural and still very much like me, just brighter and more defined which was exactly what I wanted.

The staff was kind, patient, and reassuring throughout the process, especially on surgery day and during follow-up.  I never felt rushed or pressured, and all my questions were answered clearly.

If you’re looking for a clinic that prioritizes natural results, honesty, and long-term aesthetics, I would absolutely recommend Etonne and Dr. Cho Jeongmok!

My Background
I’m in my mid-20s and from Singapore, and this was my very first plastic surgery experience. I did procedures for my eyes (incisional double eyelid + ptosis correction) and my face (AccuLift). Naturally, I was nervous going into it, but the entire experience turned out to be far smoother and more reassuring than I could have imagined.

About My Surgeon, Dr. Cho Jeong Mok
Dr. Cho performed the entire procedure himself. (I know this because I briefly woke up during the process and heard his voice.) I feel genuinely grateful to have been in such skilled hands. He is highly professional, fluent in English, and truly prioritises what’s best for his patients. He really listens for example, he respected my choice to avoid threads and fillers and he explains everything clearly and concisely without overwhelming me. I felt safe and confident with him from start to finish.

Staff and Translators
As a foreigner, I honestly don’t know how I would have managed in the operating theatre without Milk and Yenni, my translators. They made sure every single word was translated to me while I was lying on the operating table, which made a huge difference. The rest of the team  the anaesthesia staff, managers, and nurses were incredibly gentle, careful and professional especially when injecting/removing my stitches. They made me feel completely at ease throughout the entire process.

Consultation Process
Everything from pre-consultation to post-care was incredibly smooth. The clinic responds promptly, which reassured me at every step. Even the online consultation before my trip gave me a clear idea of the procedure and a ballpark estimate of the cost. Honestly, it didn’t take me long to decide on this clinic,  I had followed an Asian American beauty influencer who recommended Etonne, and I could tell her review wasn’t filtered or sponsored.

Costing and Transparency
Etonne’s pricing is transparent. After my in-person consultation, I was given a fair and clear quote, which made me even more confident in my decision.

Clinic Location and Cleanliness
The clinic is in a prime location in the heart of Gangnam, directly above the subway station, making it very convenient. The space is clean, hygienic, and has a prestigious atmosphere, which gave me confidence even before stepping into the procedure room.

Recovery and Results
My recovery has been fast, and the results are good. I’ve received compliments from friends, family, and even strangers. Now at week two, I still have some mild bruising, which is completely normal. The aftercare kit  including a cooling pack, saline solution, and Q-tips was very helpful, and the vitamin drip after surgery helped me regain energy and clarity quickly.

Final Thoughts
Experience it for yourself. I wrote this review in full confidence and in depth because the entire process genuinely went smoothly. I feel very fortunate that my first plastic surgery experience was with Etonne. The combination of Dr. Cho’s expertise, the professionalism of the team, and the seamless overall process made everything a success. I highly recommend this clinic to anyone looking for skilled, reassuring, and truly professional care.

This was my first time trying surgery in Korea, and I had such a great experience at Etonne clinic! The atmosphere was so calming and relaxed. As soon as I walked in the staff spoke to me in perfect English. I told the doctor what I wanted and one thing I liked was he didn’t try to upsell me. I originally wanted to do incisional eyelids surgery, but he suggested a less invasive approach and walked me through long term scenarios and think beyond the present moment.I had such a great experience speaking with the doctor that I decided to do chin filler, radio therapy, and Botox all at the same time as well.  I also wanted to do more chin filler but he provided his own opinion and in the end we agreed on more minimal chin filler. I highly recommend my doctor, Dr. Cho Jeongmok. The results for my eyelids and chin/jawline looks amazing thanks to him.

The clinic was clean and modern, and the staff were very kind and professional. During my consultation, Dr. Kim Jaegon spoke perfect English and took a conservative approach, recommending a non-incisional upper bleph and a slight alar reduction instead of the more extensive procedures I initially requested. His honesty and lack of pushy sales made me feel immediately comfortable and trusting.

My surgery went smooth, and post-op care was great. Although it’s been less than two weeks and my results are still settling in, I’m very happy so far. I’m especially grateful for Dr. Kim’s judgment in knowing exactly what was enough to achieve a natural yet enhanced result. I highly recommend Etonne and have already referred all my friends.

They were able to share before and after photos of other Caucasian patients (with their permission) during the consultation which was so helpful and encouraging. The experience at the clinic was very professional and caring. I highly recommend Etonne and Dr Kim.

reviews.text: I didn’t know this place existed until I came to the nearby park. I decided to take a walk through it, which took me a little over an hour. I stopped to take some quick photos along the way before heading back. I think this place will be really beautiful in the spring.

Saetgang Ecological Park, located in Yeouido, Seoul, is a place where you can take a quiet walk and feel nature away from your busy daily life. It is easily accessible by public transportation as it is within walking distance from Exit 2 of Singil Station. This park was established in 1997 as the first ecological park in Korea, and was built with the goal of preserving the natural ecosystem. One of the biggest features of Saetgang Ecological Park is its various natural ecological facilities. There is a 1.2 km (0.75 miles) long waterway, where you can enjoy the harmony of water flow and ecosystem. Aquatic plants grow around the waterway, and you can observe aquatic plants and small creatures living there. A 6 km (3.73 miles) walking trail circles the entire park, and as you walk along the path, you will experience various ecological environments.

Yeouido Saetgang Ecological Park is centered around Saetgang Stream, a tributary of the Han River, and features a wide variety of flora and fauna, making it a haven for nature enthusiasts. It is particularly impressive for its wetlands, which are home to migratory birds, amphibians, and rare plant species. The well-maintained trails and wooden boardwalks meander through lush greenery, providing visitors with a peaceful environment to unwind, jog, or cycle. The elevated observation decks scattered throughout the park allow for panoramic views of the wetlands and the Seoul skyline, creating an ideal spot for photography and birdwatching.

Yeouido Saetgang Ecological Park is both an exciting and relaxing place to visit. It is exciting because it has a beautiful bridge connecting two busy roads and some meters above the forested park. At the same time, it is relaxing because of the green forest and nature… It is also great for hiking.

We thoroughly enjoyed walking in this green space on the edge of the busy financial district.
Nice wide paths, lots of coverage from the sun, and plenty of benches to sit and relax.
