Yeouido Park covers approximately 230,000 square meters (2,475,700 Square feet).
The park is divided into a traditional Korean forest, a lawn, a cultural yard (Munhwa Madang), and an ecological forest.
The cultural yard and the bike paths throughout the park are remnants of the Yeouido Plaza era.
Due to its location in Yeouido, it serves as a park and resting place for both office workers and visitors. Surrounding the park are several buildings, including the Yeouido Financial District.

Yeouido Park stands as a pinnacle of creativity and aesthetics, seamlessly blending nature with thoughtful design.

Walking around its serene pathways offers an unmatched sense of calm and relaxation. The lush green spaces and tranquil water bodies create a peaceful escape from the everyday rush.

Divided into diverse sections, the park captivates visitors with its unique features, such as the picturesque grassy pond, the enchanting traditional Korean forest, and the eco-rich ecological forest.

Each area invites exploration, making it a perfect sanctuary for those seeking both beauty and tranquility.

Truly, an awesome and unforgettable experience.

reviews.text: Yeouido Hangang Park is a wonderful place to relax and enjoy beautiful riverside scenery. The wide open spaces, well-maintained paths, and fresh breeze make it a perfect spot for walking, cycling, or simply sitting down and enjoying the view. The atmosphere is calm yet lively, especially during sunset when the sky becomes really beautiful. It’s a great place to hang out with friends or family while taking a peaceful break from the busy city.

Wide open space, a large park beside the Han river that has its own bicycle lanes for slow and fast riders. Great for runners and walk-marathoners alike. The views are fine between the Seongsan and Hangang Railroad bridges. You can see in the distance the Namsan tower behind the cityscape. Tip: go here during the early morning and exercise; go when there are decors, or events especially with light shows.

Yeouido sits by the Han River and is one of three public parks that makes up Hangang Park. This park is accessible by the Seoul Metro and serves as the place where you can ride on a river boat for a cruise. During winter, a snow sled area gets set up from mid December to February

I like that it's a strip of Riverside. Overlooking the other part of Seoul. Cooling breeze with chairs for public to sit and enjoy. .. I saw many people picnic there as well. There are some floating shops there... CU Ramyeun library.... Can eat superb noodles Riverside!

I visited Yeouido Hangang Park at night, and surprisingly it didn’t feel as “Instagrammable” as I had expected. The area was quite quiet during my visit, possibly because of the cold weather, so the atmosphere felt a bit empty.

Still, the riverside view at night has its own charm, but overall it may be better to visit during warmer seasons or earlier in the day when the park is livelier.

여의샛강도서관은 2014년 3월 18일에 개관한 영등포 구립 도서관입니다. 개관 당시 여의디지털도서관이라는 이름에서 현 이름으로 변경되었습니다. 여의도 중심에에 있는데다 구립도서관 치고는 굉장히 협소한 도서관입니다. 시설의 규모는 1층 음료를 파는 북카페와 2층 개방형열람실 뿐입니다.

도서관의 목적 자체가 개인 학습을 위한 공간보다는 가족단위로 즐기러 오는 분위기가 더 느껴졌습니다. 잠시 찾아와서 쉬다 가는 용도로서 이용되기에는 제법 쓸만해보이기도 합니다.

매주 월요일은 휴무일입니다.

1층에 에세이나 여행 등 800번대 책이 있고
위에 000~700번대 책이 분류되어있다.

1층은 카페가 절반, 자유롭게 앉을 수 있는 공간이 절반 정도로 채워져있고

2층은 어린이 놀이터 같은 공간과 쭉 둘러있는 서가가 같이 갖추어져있다.

규모가 그리 크진 않고 도서 양도 그리 많진 않으나 영등포 소재의 도서관 대차 신청해서 받기엔 최고의 장소.

직장 바로 옆에 이런 공간이 있다는 것 자체도 큰 매력이고 점심 먹고 잠시 쉬기에는 정말 행복한 공간이 아닐 수 없다. 가볍게 책 좀 읽고 쉬다가 빌려가기도 하고 잠시 눈도 좀 붙일 수 있는 평화로운 공간.

오래오래 내가 여기 일하는 동안 곁에 있었으면 하는 사랑스러운 도서관.

여의도에 위치한 작은 공립도서관. 지하철 여의도역에서 도보로 10분정도 거리에 있다. FKI타워의 부속건물로 2014년에 오픈했다고 한다. 2개의 층으로 운영되는데, 1층은 작은 공간에 자유열람석이 30여개 있고 카페도 운영되고 있다. 2층은 상대적으로 넓은편이나 특별한 시설은 없고 자유열람석과 PC를 이용할 수 있는 자리, 그리고 어린이용 공간이 각각 작게 마련되어 있다. 1인당 최대 5장까지 무료로 인쇄할 수 있어 급할때 사용하면 좋은 서비스로 보인다. 주차는 FKI타워 주차장을 이용하면 된다. 지역 곳곳에 주민들이 무료로 이용할 수 있는 이런 시설이 많이 생기고 잘 운영되고 있는 현상은 매우 바람직해 보인다.

reviews.text:
(August 2025)
Hopped by Hippo Brunchhaus (Yeonnam-dong) 6 months ago and I’m still thinking about it 🥺🫶🏻

Ordered the [1] Seasonal Fruit French Toast. It was fig season and as a fig lover, I was SOLD!  Toast was super fluffy, nicely soaked in honey, and honestly felt like I'm prancing on fluffy clouds.

The [2] Hippomouse Plate was a hearty breakfast with the toast, brioche bacon, sausage, and cream sugar combo. Everything fits in place purfectly!

Definitely had to get my hands on their [3] Hippo Vienna too! The drink was creamy, smooth, slightly nutty from the soy milk, not too bitter from the espresso.

As a sweet tooth gurlie, this was literally my dream breakfast!  Everything felt indulgent, cozy, and worth it.

Would come back when fruit season changes. Can't wait to see what magic they can bring to our plate!

For the last brunch stop of our trip, we ended up at this cheerful little spot in Yeonnam-dong. It’s a bit of a walk from Hongdae Station, so I’d recommend taking the Gyeongui–Jungang Line to Gajwa Station instead—it’ll save you some steps!

The space is bright and playful, with plenty of natural light. They serve a variety of dishes like American-style breakfasts, hearty soups, French toast, and pasta, so there’s something for everyone. Portions are generous too, so don’t worry about leaving hungry.

I really liked the pudding for dessert—if you’re into bouncy, light textures, definitely give it a try!🍮🍮🍮

Came at 9am. Wasn't busy. We sat down stairs dining room.
4 of us had the brunch menu.
X1 grilled bacon
X2 fresh fruit
X1 cream egg toast
X2 vanilla latte and x1 Americano

The grilled bacon & egg toast came 1st. In good time. Coffees next. Then the fruit & toast.

All of it was tasty and very large servings.

This place was super cozy, a bit hard to find for foreigners tho but you can easily uber your way here.

Vienna coffee was 10/10 definitely recommend for everyone to try it out. had the philly steak burger which was also super good and my wife had some burrata salade (which was meh to our opinion).

Overall I’d say it’s still worth to visit!

Portions are quite small and a little expensive but for brunch/lunch it's perfect and leaves you with enough room for dessert. I got the most expensive item on the menu the black Angus steak and it was very VERY chewy and difficult to cut so I gave up from the start tbh. If you struggle with chewy food I'd avoid. title: 연세굿데이치과의원 양재점

reviews.text: The service here is great, I’m a South African and I do not speak any Korean but I was assisted and understood everything so it’s safe to say the clinic is foreigner friendly. They speak English and explain the procedure as they go. I will definitely be visiting again. I also think the prices are reasonable too.

This was the worst experience for me. I came to the clinic with a clear purpose-to remove a wisdom tooth. I had an X-ray with me. At the reception desk, they told me they could not give me the exact price for the extraction, but that it would be around 30–40k won.

I went into the examination room. The doctor came in and told me absolutely basic things that I already knew, but he refused to remove the tooth because he said he doesn’t do that procedure. He also refused to tell me the cost. Instead, without my consent, he started preparing for a completely different procedure - a dental cleaning - which I did not need at that moment. I repeated several times that I only needed the tooth removed because it was bothering me, and the doctor simply left.

Then another woman came in, looked at my teeth as well, and told me things I already knew. She also did not tell me the price of the extraction. It turned out that in the near future I couldn’t get my tooth removed at this clinic at all because they didn’t have the necessary specialist.

I went back to the reception and asked about the price again. They still couldn’t give me an exact number, but this time they said it could be from 200k to 400k won - even though the price listed on their own website was around 30k won.

I ended up paying more than 30k won for an hour completely wasted, for nothing. It felt like I wasn’t talking to doctors but to salespeople who were aggressively pushing unnecessary services while ignoring my real needs.

I have put off going to the dentist in Korea for 3 years, but I knew it was time… I’m so glad this is where I came! I just came for a check-up and cleaning since I haven’t been for over a decade. I was so worried about the language barrier, about the treatment, the cost, everything. But booking an appointment via WhatsApp was so easy. They had a translator there on the day who guided me through the process. They didn’t try to sell me anything extra and kept everything quick and professional. I received an x-ray and cleaning service. Especially with the national health insurance, everything was very affordable. I’m so glad I went and would definitely go again! They were quite busy so I can tell that they’re popular with the locals, too.

Just had a dental cleaning with xray an I'm really happy with the service! There was a very kind translator during the whole treatment. The whole process was very professional and the cleaning was done thoroughly, with a check by the doctor in the end. Would recommend and go again. 😊

The treatment and care are all high-quality, and the staff are friendly. Some of the dentists and receptionists can speak English well, so it is foreigner-friendly. They even have paperwork in English! It made it easy to register there, and it was also helpful to have English instructions for home care after the procedure. It’s a great dental clinic!

reviews.text: I had a great experience in this clinic. They have an English translator who is extremely nice and friendly. She even waited for us even our scheduled appointment is really late. We scheduled late because we want to avoid the crowd since I am pregnant. They took care of me really well as we informed them that I'm 9 months pregnant. They even consider to give me a private room for waiting to avoid any possibilities of Covid19. The staff and nurses are nice and attentive. They answer all our (my husband and I) questions in a detailed manner. The doctor who did my tooth extraction was really skilled. He could tell where the cavities are in my teeth by looking at the x-ray before checking my teeth. He did the tooth extraction fast like 5 minutes and I didn't feel hurt as they make sure that I only receive a little anesthesia. The doctor and the rests are all gentle to me. Overall, amazing and professional staff and doctor. I only paid 8k won (with NHI) for the service I got. They are being nice for charging us like the price of consultation. Very reasonable. I plan to go back here for other future treatments after I recover from giving birth.

If there was an option to provide more than five stars, I would.  This is the best dental clinic that I ever visited, and I have been to many dental offices before.  Everyone there is highly professional and knows their job well, from the front desk staff on up.  The dentists are highly skilled and explain every issue and option, then they provide recommendations using context.  Also, the clinic goes out of its way to make you feel comfortable.  My wife, who was nine months pregnant, broker her tooth during another steep rise in Covid cases, and the staff did everything to accommodate us, including offering a private room for us to wait in.  The waiting room was very big and we were see immediately, so we did not take the offer.  However, it was nice to know the option existed.  Moreover, when we called, the English translator said that I should not worry about visiting in the evening, because her shift did not end until 6:30 pm.  Then, when I asked how we could communicate with the dentist clearly if my wife required a procedure that went passed 6:30 pm, the translator said, and I quote, "Don't worry.  I will stay for however long it takes for the procedure to be completed."  And she did just that.  If you want a skilled and profession dental clinic, especially if you are a foreign, this would be the place.

Yeongdeungpo District is a dynamic and diverse area in southwestern Seoul, South Korea. Known as a commercial and business hub, it is home to a mix of residential, retail, and industrial spaces. Yeongdeungpo is a key part of Seoul’s economic landscape, with major office buildings, shopping centers, and the Yeongdeungpo Times Square, one of the largest shopping malls in the city. This mall offers everything from fashion and electronics to a variety of restaurants, entertainment options, and a large cinema.

Despite its modern, bustling atmosphere, Yeongdeungpo also has areas of greenery, such as Yeongdeungpo Park, where locals come to relax and enjoy outdoor activities. The district is also home to a number of traditional markets, like Mokdong Market, where visitors can experience authentic Korean food and street vendors.

Yeongdeungpo’s central location provides excellent transportation connections, with multiple subway lines and bus routes passing through, making it easy to access from other parts of Seoul. The area has a diverse population, with both young professionals and families calling it home, and it offers a lively combination of modern urban living and traditional Korean culture.

Market size is bigger than I've expected. If tourists from other countries ask me about marketplace, I am gonna recommend hear. Cause they can feel more local atmosphere than Gwangjang Market(in addition, price is cheaper).

When I visit South Korea, I always make it a point to explore traditional markets. Perhaps it's the nostalgia of the bustling rural markets during my childhood or the distinct aroma of a vibrant market, but there's something special about these places that I always look forward to. However, my recent visit to Yeongdeungpo Market left me with a sense of disappointment.

The market, known for its declining business, felt truly disheartening. It's a stark contrast to the popular and lively traditional markets you often find in South Korea, where both locals and foreigners gather to enjoy the variety of food and other attractions. In contrast, Yeongdeungpo Market was so quiet that it seemed like there were more staff members than customers. The overall atmosphere felt rather sluggish, which was unexpected.

Perhaps the less-than-ideal image of a traditional market in other places, with its charm and untidiness, was perceived quite differently here. The dark and somewhat dreary atmosphere made it appear untidy to the point of surprise. This visit was a reminder of how traditional markets can differ greatly in their vibrancy and appeal. I'd rate my experience at Yeongdeungpo Market with 2 stars.

title: 예술의전당
google_addr: 2406 Nambusunhwan-ro, Seocho District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I remember that afternoon so clearly—I was riding the metro through Seoul, feeling the gentle sway of the train as we moved from one neighborhood to the next. It was one of those unplanned moments of a vacation that turned into something special. There, amid the ads for local teas and tech gadgets, was a poster for the Renoir-Cézanne exhibit at the Seoul Arts Center. I'd always loved Impressionism from afar, flipping through books on rainy days back home, but seeing these names in person, in a city so full of its own vibrant energy, felt like an invitation I couldn't ignore.
I made my way there on a quiet weekday, hoping for a peaceful visit. What I found instead was a room full of people, all drawn to the same quiet thrill. It surprised me how many others had the same idea, even on a Tuesday. A kind staff member at the entrance noticed my hesitation and explained they were managing the flow to keep things comfortable. She gave me a slip with a time slot, just twenty minutes away. That wait didn't feel like a delay at all; it gave me time to sit nearby, watch families and friends share excited whispers, and enjoy a simple cup of coffee from the café. By the time my turn came, I was eager, my mind already wandering to what lay ahead.
Walking in, I was struck by how alive the paintings felt. Renoir's soft, warm scenes of people in gardens and city streets pulled me right into their world—the way the light seemed to dance on the canvas made me pause and just breathe it in. I'd read about Cézanne's mountains and still lifes before, but standing there, tracing the steady lines of his brush, it was as if he was showing me how to look at a hillside or a simple fruit in a new way. For someone seeing these works for the first time, it was quite an experience, like sharing a quiet conversation with old friends I'd only known through stories.
And then, near the end, the rooms opened into Picasso's pieces—a shift from gentle impressions to sharp, thoughtful forms that caught me off guard in the best way. His bold colors and shapes felt like a bridge to something more urgent and alive, rounding out the afternoon with an unexpected depth. I stayed longer than I meant to, letting the soft light from the gallery windows fall across the floors as I moved slowly from one wall to the next. Too bad photography wasn't allowed, but I'm so thankful I made the trip.

I didn't get to go inside the Arts Center, I only went round it and went to the restaurant there and it was awesome. I enjoyed the beef Bulgogi and loads of top-ins and with rice and Mackrel with some tiny Titus fishes

I visited Seoul Arts Centre in October 2025, one of the highlight of my 3rd trip to Seoul. I enjoyed walking around the huge compound. Paul Cezanne and Pierre Auguste Renoir exhibition was very well done!

The Sensory Tale helped me to have a better understanding of autistic, sensory, and people who has gone through trauma a little better. I throughly enjoyed this exhibition too.

I will definitely come here on every trip to Seoul from now on!

The fantastic concert hall boasts impressive audio effects. And the grassy lawn, adorned with a splendid musical fountain, exudes elegance and sophistication. The harmonious combination of nature's green carpet and the mesmerizing water feature creates an enchanting ambiance that elevates the entire experience. As the water dances to the rhythm of the music, it adds a touch of magic to the surroundings, making it an ideal spot for relaxation and enjoyment. This luxurious addition to the landscape truly enhances the overall aesthetic, making it a must-visit destination for those seeking a blend of nature and artistry.

Quite frankly, the concert hall in this arts center may be, acoustically one of the two best I’ve experienced in my lifetime. I found myself thinking of the hall as a musical instrument in its own right. We were sitting in the upper balcony, or loge, and we’re treated to a glorious experience, listening to performances of all three Rachmaninov piano concertos, all in one evening. Truly an extraordinary experience.

title: 예스24라이브홀
google_addr: 20 Gucheonmyeon-ro, Gwangjin District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Amazing place and great organization.
It's a very pretty and clean space. It's also not that big l, I would say it's pretty much smaller than some other places I've been for concerts, but that's exactly what makes it so special, that you are not fighting for a spot or fighting for the a view, due to the tickets are already numbered (even if you're in the standing zone, they are organized to admit people according to the numbers in their tickets).
The sound is good, too. The staff was respectful and organized all the time.
Inside, you can store your stuff in the lockers for 500won (you better bring 2 coins of 500won).  You can take the key for as long as your concert lasts, and at the end, you grab your belongings and return the key to the locker. Beware that you can lock the locker once. Once it's closed, it's closed, and if you put the key again and open it, you will need to put the coins again to use that locker.
There are many clean restrooms inside the place and a mini coffee shop outside (the coffee shop has no restrooms).
I truly recommend this place if you have the opportunity to come for a concert or any other event.

Great concert venue! There are rentable lockers outside where you can store all of your belongings safely. There’s also a cafe where you can eat before the concert. It is also easy to go to the venue. You just have to walk a bit after getting off the train
Great concert venue. They even have a lot of locker to store our belongings. Helpful for festival/standing audience. The seating on 2nd floor have good visibility too to the stage.

This was my very first time at this venue. My daughter and I went to the Kim Hyun Joong concert for his My Sun Tour.
There is a cafe right at the venue and restaurants nearby. I definitely recommend that you eat prior to attending any concert because everything was closed when we were leaving.
The building looks quite large from the outside, but once you're in, you quickly realize it is not as large as you thought.
The bathrooms to the left were closed off for staff, so we had to use the bathrooms to the right. I didn't even have to wait for the restrooms because most went to get their seats quickly.
When I finally went into the seating area I was highly disappointed. One, we had to wear masks still, but I think that was the artist's choice, which I can understand since some flew in a few nights prior, but that was a surprise to me and I was so excited to finally go to a maskless indoor concert 😢. Second, and this was the main issue -the seating! Now mind you, I am not that large, but the aisles were so small and the seats right up next to each other that I was so grateful to have my daughter with me for a little more space.
Also, this is still chilly season, so most still had their jackets on inside, including myself.
I could barely get down the aisle with all those people. Thankfully, I was able to switch to corner seats a row back because I knew I would need the restroom before the show was over and didn't want to interrupt others.
I was hoping the seats were going to be risers or at least be more space. Very unfortunate, but the actual concert was good.
The sound system of the concert was very good quality. The management was very organized and the people working there are friendly and helpful. It was an amazing experience.

title: 옛 용산신학교와 원효로 예수성심성당
google_name: Wonhyo-ro Catholic Church of the Sacred Heart
google_addr: 49 Wonhyo-ro 19-gil, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Very good

지금은 성심 여고 교정 안에 속하게 된 용산 성심 신학교(옛 용산 신학교 성심 성당)와 성심 수녀회 관구 사무실과 성심 기념관으로 쓰고 있는 옛 용한 신학교 건물은 성소의 못자리였던 당시의 자취를 아직도 간직하고 있다.

서울시 용산구 원효로 4가에 위치한 옛 용산 신학교 성당은 1902년에 축성된 건물이다. 여기에는 한국 천주교회의 첫 방인 사제였던 성 김대건 안드레아 신부의 유해가 축성 당시부터 1958년까지 모셔져 있었고 조선 교구 초대 교구장이었던 소 브뤼기에르 주교와 제8대 교구장이었던 뮈텔 주교의 유해가 거쳐 갔던 곳이다.

우리나라 최초의 신학교는 1855년 충청도 배론에 세워진 신학당에서 그 기원을 찾는다. 그 이전의 한국인 성직자 양성을 위한 노력은 이미 1830년대부터 시작되어 정하상에게 신학 교육을 시킨 바 있고 1836년에는 김대건, 최양업, 최방제를 마카오에서 신학교육을 받게 했다.

배론 신학교는 1866년 병인박해로 폐교됐지만 신앙의 자유가 확보됨에 따라 1882년 21명을 페낭 신학교에 유학생으로 파견하기도 했다. 1885년에는 경기도 여주군 강천면 범골에 예수 성심 신학교가 문을 열고, 1887년에는 바로 이곳 서울 용산으로 이전한다. 1892년에는 신학교 교사를 신축했고, 성당은 그 10년 후인 1902년에 신학교 부속 성당으로 건립되어 축성되었다. 용산 신학교 성당은 1982년 교사와 함께 사적 제255호로 지정되어 보존되고 있다.

그 후 1914년 성 유스티노 신학교, 1927년에는 함경남도 덕원 신학교 등 여러 군데의 신학교가 생겨났고 서울, 대구, 광주, 부산, 수원, 대전에 이어 1996년에는 인천 가톨릭 대학이 개교하기에 이르렀다.

옛 용산 예수성심 신학교 모습. 현재는 성심 기념관으로 수녀회 사무실 등으로 이용하고 있다.옛 용산 신학교 성당에 그 유해가 모셔져 있었던 조선 교구 초대 교구장 소 브뤼기에르 주교는 파리 외방 전교회 소속으로 1831년 조선 교구가 북경에서 독립하면서 초대 교구장으로 임명됐다. 하지만 그는 갖은 고난과 질병을 이겨 내고 조선 땅으로 입국을 시도하다가 결국은 조선 땅을 눈앞에 두고 조선을 향해 떠난 지 4년 만에 43세의 나이로 숨을 거둔다.

비록 그는 조선에 입국하지는 못했지만 그가 개척해 둔 입국 경로를 따라 곧 모방 신부와 샤스탕 신부가 조선에 들어옴으로써 한국 교회는 완전하게 조직을 갖춘 명실상부한 교회가 된 것이다.

파리 외방 전교회 소속의 조선 교구 제8대 교구장 뮈텔 대주교는 1877년 한국에 입국해 1933년 서울에서 선종할 때까지 중간의 몇 년을 제외하고는 평생을 이국땅인 한국에서 사목 활동을 했다.

박해 시대에 활동한 적이 있는 뮈텔 주교는 한불 조약 이후 지하 교회에서 해방된 교회의 모습을 좀 더 확고히 하기 위해 예수 성심 신학교, 종현 성당, 약현 성당을 짓는 한편 각 지방에서의 본당 창설에 많은 지원을 했다.

옛 용산 예수성심 신학교 성당 외부 모습.하지만 무엇보다도 그의 가장 큰 업적은 순교자들의 행적을 중심으로 한 순교자 현양과 한국 천주교회사의 정립 그리고 순교복자의 시복 등으로 꼽을 수 있다. 유명한 뮈텔 일기는 자신이 조선 교구장으로 임명된 1890년 8월 4일부터 임종하기 직전인 1932년 12월 31일까지 써 둔 일기로 총 6천여 면의 분량에 주교 개인 사정과 재임 동안의 교회 사정을 기록한 것인데 우리 한국 교회로서는 아주 귀중한 자료이다.

그 외에도 그는 "뮈텔 문서", "기해 일기" 등을 저술하고 황사영 백서의 원본이 발견되자 이를 프랑스어로 번역해 학계에 배포하고 그 원본을 1925년 한국 순교자 79위 시복식 때 교황 비오 11세에게 봉정했다. 현재 황사영 백서는 바티칸 박물관 내 선교민속 박물관에 소장, 전시되어 있다.

옛 용산 신학교 성당은 많은 순교자들의 유해가 안치되었던 곳이다. 우리나라 최초의 사제인 성 김대건 신부를 비롯해 조선교구 초대교구장 브뤼기에르 주교, 2대 교구장 성 앵베르 주교, 3대 페레올 주교, 4대 성 베르뇌 주교, 5대 성 다블뤼 주교, 6대 리델 주교, 7대 블랑 주교, 8대 교구장이자 이 성당 봉헌식을 집전한 뮈텔 주교에 이르기까지 8명의 역대 조선 교구장 주교들의 유해가 모두 이 성당에 안치되었었고, 기해박해 순교자인 성 모방, 성 샤스탕 신부를 비롯해 배론 신학당을 세우고 병인박해 때 순교한 오메트르 신부, 성 위앵, 성 브르트니에르, 성 도리, 성 볼리외 신부 등의 유해도 이 성당을 거쳤다. 이곳에 안치되었던 순교자들의 유해는 그 후 혜화동 신학교 성당을 비롯해 명동 주교좌성당, 절두산 순교성지 등지로 옮겨 모셨고, 역대 교구장들의 유해는 용산 성직자 묘지로 옮겨 안장했다. 2010년 노후화된 성당 외벽과 주변에 대한 보수공사를 시행하고, 2011년에는 성당 내부에 대한 보수공사를 진행중이다. [출처 : 주평국, 하늘에서 땅 끝까지 - 향내나는 그분들의 발자국을 따라서, 가톨릭출판사, 1996, 내용 일부 수정 및 추가(최종수정 2020년 2월 19일)]

원효로 예수성심성당은 새남터와 당고개 순교 성지가 보이는 부지를 1887년 매입하여 1902년 가톨릭신학교의 전신인 예수성심신학교의 부속 성당으로 축성하였습니다.
가톨릭대학교가 혜화동으로 이전한 후에는 성심여중고의 부속성당으로 이용하고 있습니다.
현재 성심기념관으로 티용 중인 성당 옆 건물은 신학교로 사용하던 건물이며 1911년에 지어졌습니다.
고딕풍의 아름다운 성당과 신학교 건물은 명동성당 건물과 같이 파리외방선교회 코스트신부님이 설계하였으며 사적으로 지정되어 있습니다.
성당이 여학교 안에 위치하고 있어서 평일에는 출입이 어려울 수 있습니다.
성심여중고 안에 위치해 있습니다. 그래서 평일에 가려면 정문 경비실을 통해 들어가야 하는데, 신분증이 없으면 못들어 갈 수도 있습니다. 성당 자체는 무척 신비로웠고 이뻤습니다.
작지만 멋지고 경건한 곳. 저녁 노을이 내리는 즈음 아무도 없는 성당 내부에서 느끼는 스테인드글라스의 색채가 황홀했습니다.

reviews.text:
A very good place for walking, relieving stress, and reflecting. The park is not large, but it is located on a hill, so you can get some cardio exercise while enjoying the smell and view of the forest. The very convenient paths laid out around the perimeter of the park and numerous benches make the park an excellent place for walking. And the rest areas with wooden tables and chairs allow you to sit down for a snack or a chat. It is very important that all the wooden paths are equipped with illuminated railings, so you can walk even in the dark. At first, I didn't understand why the paths in the park had such gentle slopes and inclines until I saw a sign indicating people with limited mobility. Yes, even people in wheelchairs can move around the park.
The park has some very unusual areas, as if for overcoming obstacles, where small pebbles alternate with wooden planks and then with large stones. There is also a toilet in the park, which is very clean and comfortable.

Nice barefoot path, they also had balance beams, workout equipment, kids playing dodgeball, lots of small birds singing, and I think I saw a couple of racoon-dogs running in the woods. Nice view from the top.
Not sure if it's a destination for travelers, but I would love to live next to a park like this.
Ogeum Park / 오금 공원 is a wonderful park to take kids or take a hike no matter what age. The downside to the park is there is no stroller access. Leave the stroller in the car or at home.
Such a beautiful place, you can come here for exercise or take a walk. It's a big place and fresh air.
Good to be relax.. even in the city..

오류공원이 생기면서 오랜 시간 단절됐던 오류1, 2동이 자연스레 연결된 것은 물론 새로운 문화공간도 탄생했다. 오류동이 위치한 구로구 서쪽 지역은 구의 동쪽에 비해 문화예술시설이 부족해 아쉬움이 있었다. 오류역문화공원 야외무대에서는 그간의 아쉬움을 씻기라도 하듯 다양한 공연과 크고 작은 행사가 줄지어 열리고 있다. 특히 매월 1회 펼쳐지는 ‘철길 위 옥상몽(夢)’은 이색콘서트·전통연희·서커스·인형극 등의 공연을 무료로 관람할 수 있어 눈길을 끈다. 자세한 공연 일정은 구로문화재단 누리집에서 확인할 수 있다.
오류역문화공원 놀이터 옆에는 오류문화센터가 자리한다. 지난해 3월 개관한 오류문화센터는 총면적 5276㎡ 규모에 지하 1층, 지상 5층으로 지어진 복합문화시설이다. 1층 구립 어린이집, 2층 오류아트홀, 3층 오류골 사랑방과 경로당, 4층 꿈나무장난감나라와 구로사회적경제통합지원센터, 5층 구로문화원이 들어서 남녀노소 모두가 즐겨 찾을 수 있는 면모를 두루 갖췄다.
365석 규모의 전문공연장인 ‘오류아트홀’은 클래식, 무용, 뮤지컬 등 수준 높은 공연으로 관객의 다양한 문화적 욕구를 충족시켜 준다. 지난해에만 모두 61번의 공연이 열렸고 관람객 1만여 명이 방문할 정도로 개관과 동시에 지역 대표 공연장으로 자리를 잡았다. 오류아트홀 공식 블로그를 방문하면 공연 스케줄과 공연에 대한 자세한 설명, 이용방법 등을 볼 수있다
전철역 옥상과 행복주택 아파트를 유기적으로 연결하려고 애를 쓴 흔적은 보인다.

I received cosmetic procedures at Opera Plastic Surgery, including eyelid, nose, and chin surgeries. Unfortunately, my personal experience did not meet expectations, and I encountered complications that have had a lasting impact on my physical appearance and emotional well-being.

I am sharing my experience not to defame, but to encourage others to conduct thorough research, ask critical questions, and seek second opinions before undergoing any medical or cosmetic procedures — especially abroad.

This review reflects my personal journey, and I hope it helps others make informed decisions about their healthcare.

The Olympics were held in Seoul in 1988. Of course, a lot has changed in the city since then. But the beautiful Olympic Park remains, with all its sports infrastructure, which still serves the Korean people. For me personally, the Olympic Park has become a wonderful place for walks and relaxation. You can simply stroll leisurely along the alleys or go for a run. There are plenty of benches for resting, toilets, and vending machines on the grounds, so relax among the shady trees and recharge your batteries.🙏
There is a very unusual service in the park. If you have walked a lot and your feet are tired, you can use a special foot bath with cool water to relieve fatigue, which is very cool.👌
The coffee shop in front of the park is quite expensive. Vibe in the morning is quite good. On weekdays, the subway is very crowded.

Olympic Park (올림픽공원) is a must-visit spot in Seoul if you're looking to enjoy nature, art, and a bit of history all in one place. The park is massive, with wide walking paths, scenic lakes, and open green spaces that make it perfect for a relaxing stroll or picnic.

All around the park, you’ll find large-scale sculptures and public art that add a unique charm to the landscape. There’s also historical significance here, with remnants from the 1988 Seoul Olympics adding character and depth to the visit.

Whether you’re into photography, jogging, or just need a peaceful break from the city buzz, Olympic Park offers a refreshing escape with something for everyone.

This is where the IU fan club Uaena meetup  named ‘Bye Summer’ took place on September 13th and 14th, 2025. As always, it was a time filled with warm communication and love between the artist and her fan club. As of 2025, the KSPO Dome is the largest indoor arena in Korea. While it's not a dedicated concert arena, so the acoustics and visibility aren't perfect, it's still one of the best concert halls in Seoul. I hope an even better concert-focused arena is built soon.

KSPO DOME (Olympic Gymnastics Arena) in Seoul is a top-tier venue that consistently delivers memorable experiences—especially for music lovers. As one of the city’s premier arenas, it offers excellent acoustics and sightlines, making concerts feel immersive and electrifying.

The venue itself is well-maintained and easy to navigate. Seating is comfortable, and there are plenty of concession stands offering everything from snacks to drinks. Crowd management and security are efficient, so entering and exiting events remains smooth even during high-attendance shows.

Located in a vibrant area with plenty of transport links, it’s convenient to reach by subway or bus. Whether you're going for a major concert, a sporting event, or a cultural performance, KSPO DOME delivers with style, quality, and excitement. A standout destination for live events in Seoul!

1846년 9월16일 새남터에서 순교하신 김대건신부님이 이곳에 잠시 묻히셨다가 미리내로 옮기셨다. 이후, 1866년 병인박해 때 새남터에서 순교하신 6분의 신부님들이 33년간 묻혀계셨으며, 서소문 밖 네거리에서 순교하신 성 남종삼 요한, 성 최형 베드로 그리고 홍봉주 토마스 등이  43년간 암매장되었던 곳이다.
왜고개는 조선시대 500여 년간 기와와 벽돌을 공급하던 와서가 있던 곳으로, 서울 명동대성당과 중림동 약현성당을 지을 때 사용했던 벽돌도 이곳에서 공급해 주었다고 전해진다.
왜고개 순교성지는 많은 성인들이 순져간  곳입니다 애청곡중에 미아리 눈물고개 라는 노래가있듯이 이곳이 미아리 고개에 있는 성지여서 눈물이 많이 흘렸던 곳이기도 합니다
국군군종교구가 있는 곳입니다. 불교 기독교 천주교 모두 경당을 들려볼 수 있군요.20181202 현재 외부 방문객을 위해 보수중에 있습니다.

title: 용마루 숲길 축제
google_addr: 13 Hyochangwon-ro 40-gil, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Its a market used by the locals. Then on the other side, there were plently of restaurants and drinking joints. The prices of the items sold at the local markets were considerably cheaper comparing to the Gwangjang market.

Yongmun Market in Yongsan is a traditional neighborhood market just a few minutes’ walk from Hyochang Park Station (Line 6 / Gyeongui–Jungang). It’s not a flashy tourist spot – it’s where local residents actually shop for meat, seafood, vegetables and side dishes, and recently the market has been renovated so the alleys are brighter and easier to walk through.

If you’re tired of tourist traps and want a more down-to-earth place to eat, Yongmun Market is a great option. Prices are generally reasonable, portions are generous, and most shops are clearly focused on regulars, not one-time tourists.

Some food spots worth checking out in and around the market:

Changseongok (창성옥) – A classic haejangguk (hangover soup) institution with decades of history. The broth is deep and rich, filled with beef bone flavor, ugeoji (greens) and soft blood curd. Many locals order a fried egg on the side and mix it in. It’s hearty, old-school Korean comfort food and perfect on a cold or rainy day.

Yongmun Haejangguk (용문해장국) – Another legendary place, often mentioned as one of the “big 3” haejangguk spots in Yongmun area. In the morning, they basically serve only haejangguk, with a very simple, focused menu, then switch to beef-bone dishes and stews in the evening. The soup is strong, the kimchi and radish pickles are excellent, and the overall feel is very local.

Janggun Bossam (장군보쌈) – A famous bossam (boiled pork with kimchi) restaurant near the market, known for its soft pork slices, fresh napa kimchi and, in season, oyster bossam. It’s been featured on Korean TV and is always busy with locals coming for dinner, group meals and drinks.

Vision Mandu (비전만두) – A small stall at the entrance side of the market selling old-school snacks like hot dogs, croquettes and chapsal donuts at very friendly prices. Everything is fried to order, hot and crispy, and the taste feels like classic Korean street food from years ago. The owner is known for being kind and chatty with customers.

On top of these, you’ll find many small banchan shops, fruit stalls with surprisingly cheap prices, butcher shops and seafood stands. It’s the kind of place where you can eat a proper meal, grab some snacks to go, and also feel how a real Seoul neighborhood market works – without constantly worrying about being overcharged.

If you want a more local, relaxed and honest traditional market in Seoul, Yongmun Market is a very good alternative to the more touristy places. Come hungry, walk slowly through the alleys, and just follow the lines of local people – that’s usually where the best food is.

title: 용마산
google_addr: Achasan, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I’ve hiked over 25 mountains in the greater Seoul area, reaching every summit, so I can confidently say that Achasan (아차산) is one of my favorite rocky mountains. What sets it apart is the stunning viewpoints along the trail—not just at the top like many other hikes. The climb is relatively short too—about 45 to 50 minutes to the summit, even with a few leisurely stops to take in the views or sip some coffee.

That’s exactly why I keep coming back on weekends.

From this rocky ridge, you get panoramic views of Seoul in all directions. On a clear day, you can see far into the north, south, and east. But honestly, no photo or video can truly capture the beauty of this mountain and the breathtaking scenery it offers.

There are several trail entrances, but I personally love starting from the 어울림정원 (Eoullim Garden) entrance. The trail from there climbs steeply—almost a 45-degree rocky path—leading up to 팔각정 (Palgakjeong Pavilion). Along the way, there are multiple scenic spots, so make sure to pause, look back, and take in the views around you—not just what’s ahead.

well paved and clearly marked hiking trail that is gentle and suitable for people of all ages.great views on the top with most of seoul and surroundings. maple trees are especially lovely in fall.walk up from walker hill.
If you hike for about 30 minutes at the entrance of Achasan, you can enjoy a wonderful view of Seoul. Make sure to enjoy the sunset and the night view here.

Beautiful Mountain range between Seoul and Guri-si. You can visit many temples and fortress in this mountain. View of Hangang River and the bridges. You will need about 3 to 3.5 hrs to complete the mountains of Achasan and the mountain on the north (forgot the name of it)

Compared to many popular mountains in Seoul like Bukhansan or Dobongsan, Achasan can be viewed as a piece of cake in terms of the level of difficulty and time required. There are a few access points and I accessed it via (...). I made it to the Goguryeojeong pavilion in 10 minutes and reached the Achasan peak in just shy of an hour. The hike comprises of a combination of wooden stairs, rocks and dirt trails. It's fairly easy without challenges of steep steps. There are a few picturesque lookouts along the way so be sure to stop and snap a few photos. The peak, however, is rather disappointing because it's just a stone plaque that tells the height of the mountain without any breathtaking views of the type that you usually get on mountain peaks. As the signage marking the peak is diminutive and easy to miss, many people stop there to take a photo of the signage as proof of hiking to the peak  From Achasan you can access Yongma-san, another mountain located less than 2 kilometers away. The interesting part of the hike was the presence of Goguryeo dynasty-era forts, especially how they remained in tact from the Gorguryeo dynasty until the 1990s when historical excavation works took place. An interesting part of Achasan's history. If you hike beyond the peak towards Yongmasan, you will come across the third and fourth forts shortly. The forts are closed to public viewing so don't expect to see any historical relics on display, but rather just signage explaining the history of the fort and the items excavated. Overall, a good hiking trail for beginners. Parking is a huge problem here though. I ended up parking in the market area, which is about a 10 minute walk away but you can use the chance to discover the endless number of Korean eateries that line the street that leads to the access points to the mountain.

title: 용마폭포공원

Yongma Waterfall Park (용마폭포공원) at 250-12 Yongmasan-ro, Jungnang-gu, Seoul, is a serene escape from the city hustle—a hidden gem perfect for nature lovers and anyone seeking peace of mind. As you stroll along the tree-lined paths, you’re greeted by the soothing sounds of cascading water and fresh, cool breezes that instantly refresh the soul.

The highlight, of course, is the waterfall itself—modest in size but beautifully integrated into the natural setting. It’s a peaceful spot to sit, reflect, or simply enjoy a moment of stillness. The park features well-maintained trails, shaded areas, and benches that invite relaxation—ideal for picnics, meditation, or leisurely reading.

Whether you're walking solo, spending time with loved ones, or just craving a break in nature, Yongma Waterfall Park offers that perfect blend of tranquility and natural beauty. Highly recommended if you're in the area and want to escape the urban grind—even just for a little while.

Yongma Waterfall Park is a beautiful and refreshing spot, featuring scenic waterfalls, lush greenery, and peaceful walking trails. The natural setting makes it perfect for relaxing, taking photos, or enjoying a quiet escape from the city’s hustle and bustle.

A true green oasis in Seoul – perfect for Familien

The best tip: bring a picnic blanket and some drinks and enjoy a wonderful day in this relaxing and family-friendly environment.

We recently visited I’Park Mall in Yongsan, Seoul, and it was such a fun experience! The mall is full of exciting shops and attractions that both teenagers and elementary school kids can enjoy. It’s a vibrant shopping and entertainment destination in downtown Seoul that offers a variety of options for visitors. Spanning 11 impressive floors, the mall is thoughtfully divided into sections: Fashion, Living, and Culture. It features the I Park Department Store, Digital Shopping Center, and Event Park, with standout attractions such as a CGV cinema, e-Sports Stadium, miniature golf, and a large bookstore. With over 100 restaurants, a diverse food court, and charming cafes, the dining options are plentiful. Shoppers can explore an array of electronics, fashion, and home goods, while cultural events, fashion shows, and festivals add to the lively atmosphere. Additional features like a video game arcade, an outdoor garden, and a culture center makes it a good destination for shopping, dining, and entertainment in the city!

I'Park Mall is a huge shopping mall at Yongsan Train Station, with many clothing shops and anime-related stuff (pop mart, Studio Ghibli, Marvel, toys, Nintendo Switch, etc.) and an arcade and lots of gacha. title: 우리 임산물 숲푸드 대축제
google_name: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
google_addr: 175 Sejong-daero, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: My trip started on a high at Sejong Theatre, where I watched the musical Phantom. The performance was absolutely stunning—the set, the music, the voices. For a couple of hours, I was so absorbed I didn’t even check my phone (which, let’s be honest, says a lot for a Gen Z like me). It felt like stepping into a different world, and I left with goosebumps.

My time exploring Sejong Plaza was spent enjoying the beautiful statue of Sejong the Great. There's many animations on the buildings, hidden alley restaurants that are ALL 10/10, and subway/public transportation hub.

The Sejong Center for the Performing Arts is an iconic performance venue located in Gwanghwamun, Seoul. For Korean artists, performing here is considered the ultimate honor, and it wouldn't be an exaggeration to call it the Carnegie Hall of Korea. While the facilities are somewhat dated and inconvenient, they are receiving positive feedback. It is conveniently located right next to Gwanghwamun Square, and it is also great for a walk after the performance. Making its own original performances like Ilmu(One Dance) is also a promising idea.

Exhibition
Masterpieces from the San Diego Museum of Art: "From the Renaissance to Impressionism"

Hey, let me share a quick thought with you.

If you ever find yourself near Gwanghwamun, take a moment to walk by the Sejong Center. And if you already have a ticket in hand, even better. You are about to step into one of Korea’s most meaningful performance halls.

Sejong Center has long been considered a symbol of Korean performing arts. When it opened in 1978, its pipe organ was the largest in Asia. Back in Europe, pipe organs were a way for cities to show their pride and prosperity, and Sejong Center carried that same spirit here in Seoul.

Sure, some people might say it is not the most modern venue anymore. And they would not be completely wrong. But this place holds memories. It has watched generations grow up, quietly standing its ground while the city changed around it. That kind of history matters.

Personally, I have spent some memorable nights here. I watched THE GREATEST: Thrill with Jeong Dong-ha and Sohyang in September 2023, Universal Ballet’s The Nutcracker in December 2023, and Chung Myung-Whun conducting Beethoven’s Ninth with the KBS Symphony at the end of 2025. Since it is a multipurpose hall, you might not always get the same powerful acoustics as a dedicated concert hall, especially for classical music. Still, the experience feels special every time.

Getting there is easy. Just hop on Seoul Subway Line 5 and get off at Gwanghwamun Station. One small thing to note, though. There is no traditional cloakroom. Instead, you will find unmanned lockers on the second floor. They work, but the touch screen can be a little tricky. Maybe it is just me getting older.

The box office is on the first floor, and there are kiosks if you already bought your ticket. You will also spot vending machines for water on each floor, which always comes in handy.

One last tip. The Grand Theater usually opens about two hours before the performance for security reasons, and audiences are allowed into the hall about thirty minutes before the show starts.

Take your time, soak it in, and enjoy the moment.

Good starting place to learn something about Korea stone sculptures, or at least know culturally what the stone sculptures are used for.  After a brief tour, now I knew a bit about Muninseok, Beoksu and Dongja sculptures.  Out of the museum building, there were more sculptures in the garden.  A lot to see.
The museum has also worked with Google Map to enable anyone to 'street view' the exhibits in their garden as they wish to expose the museum to more people locally and overseas.
It is also interesting to learn how the museum was started.  It was started by a successful businessman (also the Chairman of the museum) who is nationalistic and determined to keep Korean stone sculptures which some are national assets from being taken out of the country.  He also managed to buy back some from overseas collectors and bring them back home.  This museum is newly relocated from the old one.  He has chosen Seoul, perhaps more metropolitan - having potentially larger audience, both local and tourists, to expose the cultural stories behind all these stone sculptures.

title: 우표박물관
google_addr: 70 Sogong-ro, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Passed by the Post Tower while exploring Jung-gu during the Lunar New Year holidays. We wanted to visit the Museum inside, but unfortunately it was closed. The location is convenient if you’re sightseeing around the area, but do check the opening days if visiting during public holidays.

The Stamp Museum was a fun and unique place to visit. We loved the stamps you can collect as you walk around the museum. There are plenty of postcards and other small items you can take as souvenirs which made the visit even more enjoyable. There are videos and other interactive pieces that share interesting history and there are archives you can pull out from drawers to look at stamps from different time periods. The fact that the museum is free to enter is amazing.

For the negatives there is not much English translation inside the museum as most of the information is only in Korean. It can also be a bit hard to find within the building. I do not think there were toilets on site although they might be in another part of the building. It also feels like the museum is aimed more toward children than adults.

Overall it is a charming and educational stop especially if you enjoy collecting or looking at stamps.

Visited the museum to buy stamps but ended up being told nothing was available or rather all sold out.
The museum is very child friendly and I shall get my kids along for my next South Korea trip.
I asked around and wasn't directed to any counter but straight to a shop located outside the building, where I did manage to get many stamps especially BTS stamps.

The Korean Postage Stamp Museum is located in the basement of the Seoul Central Post Office building. Being on my second visit, the museum has changed since my first visit in mid 2019. It has become more interactive and child-friendly. Entry is free and there are free lockers to store your possessions until the 5pm closing time.

However, the museum counter no longer sells commemorative back issues of Korean stamps as it used to. This is a great pity as one of the joys of visiting the museum previously was to purchase stamps (especially important for stamp collectors) at face value - who would say no to a presentation folder of the 2018 North-South Summit as a nice keepsake!

To purchase commemorative stamps, head to Counter 10 of the Central Post Office, which is connected through a linkway to the museum, and ask for "special stamps". Stamp selections are mostly miniature sheets and far more limited in variety - but can still be bought at face value
Interesting museum of stamps and post right in the middle of Myeongdong. Many stamps and figurines from not just Korea but around the world. It's free as well.

An Unforgettable Escape: My Heartfelt Review of Walkerhill Hotels & Resorts, Seoul (5/5)
Stepping into Walkerhill Hotels & Resorts in Seoul was like entering a dream. From the moment I arrived, I felt an immediate sense of peace and luxury that truly melted away all the stresses of travel. This wasn't just a hotel stay; it was an experience that touched my heart and left me feeling utterly refreshed.

What truly sets Walkerhill apart, for me, is its breathtaking location. Perched atop a hill, surrounded by the lush Acha Mountain and overlooking the majestic Han River, the views are simply unparalleled. Waking up to the sunrise painting the sky over the river, or seeing the city lights twinkle below at night, was a daily moment of awe. It felt like a secluded oasis, yet I knew the vibrant energy of Seoul was still easily accessible thanks to their convenient shuttle service.

Beyond the stunning scenery, it was the genuine warmth and attentiveness of the staff that truly made my stay exceptional. Every single interaction, from check-in to dining, was met with genuine smiles and a desire to make me feel welcome. They anticipated my needs before I even voiced them, and their kindness felt truly sincere. It's rare to encounter such consistent, heartfelt hospitality, and it made a huge difference to my overall feeling of well-being.

My room was a sanctuary of comfort and elegance. Spacious, impeccably clean, and thoughtfully designed, it offered everything I could wish for and more. The bed was incredibly comfortable – I slept like a baby! And the view from my window, whether of the mountain or the river, was a constant reminder of the beauty surrounding me.

I also thoroughly enjoyed the various facilities. The pools, both indoor and outdoor, were fantastic for a relaxing swim, and the surrounding green spaces were perfect for a leisurely stroll. There's a wonderful sense of tranquility throughout the entire complex.

Leaving Walkerhill Hotels & Resorts, I felt a genuine pang of sadness. It was more than just a place to sleep; it was a place where I felt truly cared for, where I could unwind completely, and where I created beautiful memories. If you're looking for an escape that combines stunning natural beauty, impeccable service, and a truly luxurious experience in Seoul, look no further. Walkerhill has captured my heart, and I already dream of my return.

reviews.text:
We had a lovely experience renting cycling bikes in Seoul South Korea. The website was very easy to understand, and communication from the team was excellent. All the instructions for picking up the bikes were clear and straightforward.

The bikes were in good condition and fully equipped with everything we needed, which made the ride very comfortable. We cycled along the Han River for about 60 km and it was a beautiful route. We stopped for noodles at a CU convenience store and enjoyed a stunning sunset by the river.

There were plenty of clean bathrooms along the route, which was very convenient. Overall, a smooth, enjoyable, and well-organised experience. Highly recommended!

If you’re hesitating to book, I’m here to tell you don’t and book it. Bike tours are one of the best ways to see Seoul and this is THE company to book.

Joined the morning bike tour with Vincent and cannot recommend enough! Even in -10 degrees, it was thoroughly enjoyable. Stops were fantastic, the route made me feel like I’m a local in rhythm and Vincent’s knowledge on Seoul was something else. I was in Seoul for business and trying to compact many things in two free days was crazy - this tour did my itinerary justice and checked off most of the places I wanted to visit.

It also built my confidence cycling in Seoul (so much better than in Amsterdam) and I cycled by the Han river myself that same day in the evening.

Thank you Vincent and We Ride Korea for a lovely morning!

We loved this eBike Tour!! Taejin, our tour guide, was marvelous.  I feel like I learned so much and got so much out of it.  Taejin kept the tour moving swiftly and we stopped at quite a few places.  At each stop, he provides a great overview of what you are looking at and then becomes available for any questions you might have.  The tour includes food sampling in a non-touristy market, and a stop at a dessert & coffee place.  The cool thing about this tour is that Taejin leads you through a large number of back alleys that he seems to know like the back of his hand.  He deftly handles interesting twists and turns and did a great job of motivating all of us to follow suit.  Another nice plus is that Taejin snapped numerous photos of all of us along the way.  Soon after the tour was over, he sent them out to the group in a convenient Google Photo Album (no extra charge).  He has a nice quality camera so the photos are all very high quality.  We definitely recommend this tour.  It is a great way to learn about Seoul and have a lot of fun along the way.

We booked an afternoon e-bike tour for two, and Hagar was our guide. The tour was informative and moved at a good pace. Hagar had a great personality — easy to talk to and knowledgeable — and shared a lot about the history and culture of Seoul.

We rode through different neighborhoods, each with its own character, and learned about the city’s past from its early history to modern times. The e-bikes made it easy to get around without feeling rushed or tired.

It was a good way to see more of the city and understand it beyond the usual tourist areas. I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a different way to explore Seoul.

The bike bus is an excellent option to tour around Seoul, especially on your first visit. The guides take you to some off beaten track places and share some great fun stories along the way. The atmosphere was fabulous and chill throughout the tour. 🤩🤩

2008년 5월 16일 개관하였다. 명칭은 건립자인 유창종(柳昌宗)이 자신의 성과 아내인 금기숙(琴基淑)의 성을 따서 지었다. 법조인이자 한국기와학회의 명예회장이기도 한 유창종은 검사로 재직하던 시절부터 옛 기와에 매료되어 기와를 수집하였고, 2001년에는 25년 동안 수집해온 1875점을 국립중앙박물관에 기증하였다.

유금와당박물관에는 유창종이 2001년 이후 한국과 중국, 일본, 태국, 베트남 등지에서 수집한 각국의 기와들과 일본의 이우치 이사오[井內功]의 아들로부터 기증받은 1300여 점 등 총 2700여 점이 전시된다. 이우치 이사오는 1987년 국립중앙박물관에 한국의 기와 1082점을 반환한 인물로, 국립중앙박물관 2층에는 유창종실과 이우치실이 나란히 있다.

google_name: Site of Poet Yun Dong-ju's Boarding House
google_addr: 57 Ogin-gil, Nusang-dong, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Good place to remind this poet

비운의 천재 시인 윤동주가 머물렀던 하숙집 터.
시인은 1938년 연희전문학교(현 연세대학교)에 입학하면서 학교 기숙사, 북아현동, 서소문 일대에서 하숙을 했는데 1941년 5월부터 9월까지 ‘종로구 누상동 9번지’에서 살았다고 전해진다.

이곳은 평소 시인이 존경하던 소설가 김송의 집으로 불과 다섯 달 정도의 짧은 기간 머물렀지만, 이 하숙집에서 ‘별 헤는 밤’과 ‘자화상’을 포함해 주옥같은 열 편의 시를 써냈기에 오늘날 의미가 있는 공간으로 되새겨지며 방문객의 발길이 끊이질 않는다.

실제 윤동주 시인이 머물던 당시에는 기와로 된 한옥이었으나 지금은 옛 모습은 사라지고 다세대주택 담벼락에 ‘윤동주 하숙집’이라는 안내판만 붙어 있다. 하숙집에서 180미터 정도 들어가면 인왕산 입구인 수성동 계곡이 나온다.
훗날 시인의 벗이자 당시 룸메이트였던 정병욱 서울대 교수는 “아침 식사 전에 누상동 뒷산 인왕산 중턱까지 산책을 하고, 산골짜기 아무 데서나 세수를 하고 방으로 돌아와 청소를 끝내고 조반을 마친 후 학교에 갔다.”라고 이 시절을 회고하기도 했다.
한국인이 사랑하는 국민 시인 윤동주의 속살을 잠시나마 엿보는 듯한 기분과 무엇이 어린 시인에게 영감을 주었을까 하는 호기심이 사람들의 발길을 붙잡는 이색 명소다.(한국관광공사. 대한민국구석구석)

Eunpyeong Historical Hanok Museum is an absolute gem for anyone interested in Korean culture, architecture, and history. Located right next to the beautiful Eunpyeong Hanok Village, it’s the perfect place to start your visit if you want to understand the deeper meaning behind traditional hanok design and the lifestyle it represents.

The museum is not very large, but it’s incredibly well curated. The permanent exhibition shows the evolution of hanok architecture — from structure and materials to cultural symbolism — and explains how traditional homes were adapted to Korea’s seasons and way of life. Even without speaking Korean, it’s easy to follow thanks to clear visuals, models, and English explanations.

The building itself is impressive — a modern interpretation of hanok architecture with wide wooden beams, open spaces, and beautiful natural light. There’s a calm, respectful atmosphere that makes you want to slow down and really take it all in.

Staff are friendly and helpful, and entry is either free or very affordable. It’s rarely crowded, so you can enjoy the exhibits peacefully. Don’t miss the rooftop terrace — it offers a lovely view of the surrounding village and Bukhansan Mountain.

This museum is a must-visit if you’re already in Eunpyeong Hanok Village. It helps you see the traditional houses around you with completely new eyes. Highly recommended for anyone who loves culture, architecture, or just quiet, meaningful places in Seoul.

title: 은평한옥마을
google_addr: 193-14 Jingwan-dong, Eunpyeong District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
An underatted place in Seoul. Not too many tourists here. Free entry. It might not be too traditional since there's many occupants cars parked on the street/garage. But it stills offer a breathtaking view. Also, don't miss out Jingwansa Temple which is only 5-10 minute walk from the village. You'll be amazed on how beautiful the  area surrounding Temple is (hopefully).

The only  drawback is that there's probably no restaurants here (I could be wrong). All I saw were cafés and a  minimarket.

The experience is surreal, it's so beautiful and breathtaking. Traditional Hanok style houses in the midst of mountain scape... with the snow powdering the trees and landscape, everything is Instagram worthy.
The best part is that you can experience the rich heritage making it prefect for tourist who's looking for both cultural and nature.
Try the Korean tea house is one of the best thing I had - calming tea and the awesome view.
*To get here is best by train and bus.
From Gupabal Station on Line 3, use Exit 1, then jump on Green Bus 7723. This bus stop is behind where you exit, so make sure to U-turn once you get out of Gupabal Station to find it. Ride 9 stops (11 minutes), and get off at the Hana High School, Samcheonsa, Jingwansa bus stop.

Visited Eunpyeong Hanok Village and I enjoyed how quiet and peaceful it was. The traditional hanok houses are beautiful and the mountain view makes it even nicer. Though not a big place like Bukchon Hanok Village but great experience for a short walk and taking photos.

The direction by the bus from Yeonhui-dong Daewoo Apartment Bus Stop (near to a place where I lived nearby Hongdae) to go to Eunpyeong Hanok Village, takes around 30 to 40 minutes and after getting off, it’s just a short walk to the entrance.

Very scenic area but be aware that it’s basically a housing estate with houses that are traditionally Korean but made to modern standards and amenities. There is a temple about 10-15 minutes walk away and plenty of walking trails.

It was super pretty, a beautiful Hanok village so close to the mountains. All the houses are pretty new and well maintained so definitely a great place for photos. It is super quiet compared to the Bukchon village in Seoul. However one can easily tell that it’s more like a wealthy residential neighborhood, so it actually felt kinda weird coming all the way from Seoul just to walk around the streets here and see these fancy Hanoks from the outside where the rich people lives haha.

title: 의열사(용산)

reviews.text: 효창공원에 있는 애국선열들의 영정을 모신 사당. 정부 주도로 효창공원 정비공사가 시작된 후, 1990년 11월에 의열사와 창열문이 세워졌고, 1991년 7월에 선열들의 영정을 이곳에 모셨다고 한다. 의열사에는 대한민국 임시정부 요인 네 분 (백범 김구선생, 석오 이동녕선생, 청사 조성환선생, 동암 차리석선생)과 삼의사 (이봉창의사, 매헌 윤봉길의사, 구파 백정기의사) 세 분, 그리고 안중근의사의 영정과 위패가 모셔져 있다. 효창공원 안에 현재까지 유해를 찾지 못한 안중근의사를 제외하고 총 일곱 분의 묘역도 조성되어 있다. 조국의 독립을 위해 투쟁하고 목숨을 바친 애국선열들의 유해와 영정을 모신 효창공원과 의열사는 모든 시민과 국민들이 한번쯤은 방문해서 그 분들의 희생에 감사하는 시간을 가지면 좋겠다는 생각이 간절하게 든다.
효창공원 방문 시 잠깐 들려 독립운동 선인들에 대해 추모해본다.

reviews.text: One of the most famous and must-do experiences when visiting Seoul, Korea, is taking a trip along the Han River. The cruise 🚢 experience was great, it was perfectly on time. I wish it would have been for a lil longer, it was only for 30 minutes and the time flew by so fast witnessing the beauty of the Han River 🥰🥰🥰

I know, you've probably did some Dinner Cruises (just like me) and often the food was mediocre. Let me tell you: The sunset dinner cruise here is excellent. Fantastic food, wondeful crew, enough space, great ambience, i was totally impressed. An absolute No-Brainer - do it when in Seoul!

such a surreal experience!! i enjoyed every second of the e-land sunset cruise! seagulls may follow because of dried fish, which you can purchase downstairs in the cu on the cruise and feed it to them. (i’m not sure how much it was because i didn’t even know you could feed them at first 🥲 i was wondering why there was a slight fishy smell) i loved the live music and just the overall vibe. the cruise also tells you facts about the bridges/buildings/areas you pass through which i thought was pretty interesting! it’s about 30 mins long but totally worth it!! you also get a nice view of seoul tower.

title: 이문원한의원
google_name: 이문원한의원 (Lee Moon Won Korean Medicine Clinic & Medical Head Spa & Natural Holistic Hair Restoration)
google_addr: 33 Seolleung-ro 132-gil, Gangnam District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I got a Scalp and Hair Regenerarion program along with a medical consultation with Dr. Lee Moon Won. The spa treatment was incredibly relaxing and unlike anything I have experienced before. As someone who prefers head massages over any other body part, this was the best treatment I could have ever hoped for. Not only was my scalp treated and massaged, but also my neck and shoulder area, along with an incredible shampooing, which was the perfect wrap for the entire experience.

My consultation with Dr. Lee was brief but significant. We analyzed the photos taken of my scalp and was given a great analysis, advice, and treatment plan to follow. I found the consultation most helpful and informative. I am very happy to have been able to come here. Thank you very much Dr. Lee Moon Won, I hope to be back to your clinic soon!

My visit to Lee Moon Won Hair Clinic has been one of my best experiences in Seoul. The clinic itself is very cozy and welcoming. I chose the regeneration program along with a consultation with Dr. Lee Moon. He greeted me warmly, even calling me by name with a smile, and kindly explained the results of my scalp analysis — a smiling doctor is not very common in Seoul, and it immediately put me at ease!

I was recommended hair care and medical products to help with regrowth, and I purchased only the essentials. It’s great to know I can still order them online with shipping to Europe.

A big thank you to the English consultant for her kindness and warm welcome, to my therapist for a truly relaxing treatment, and to the hairdresser who blow-dried my hair so gently (never pulling!) and styled it beautifully.

Right after the treatment — and even days later — my scalp felt less sensitive, my hair is still shiny, silky, and light. It was truly a five-star experience that I definitely want to repeat next time I return to Seoul.

I strongly recommend this clinic to anyone struggling with hair issues.

I came back to Lee Moon Won Korean Medicine Clinic for the Slow-Aging Program again — and once more, it exceeded my expectations.

Since I already had such a great experience last year, I decided to repeat the program, and I’m honestly very happy I did. The quality and professionalism are consistently outstanding. The consultation was again very detailed and personalized, and I could really feel how much attention they give to individual progress rather than just offering a standard treatment.

The Slow-Aging Program itself was just as relaxing and thorough as I remembered. You can immediately feel that everything is done with care, precision, and deep expertise. It’s not just a “spa experience” — it truly feels like a structured medical wellness program designed for long-term results.

What makes this visit even more special is that I decided to begin a long-term treatment plan for the next 16 months. After seeing and feeling the results, I genuinely believe in their approach and methodology. The team carefully explained the strategy, the expected progress, and how we will monitor improvements over time. That level of transparency and commitment gave me a lot of confidence.

The staff are incredibly warm, professional, and attentive — especially Nour, who supported me throughout the entire process.

If you’re serious about long-term scalp health, hair improvement, and overall slow-aging care, I can absolutely recommend this clinic. I’m looking forward to seeing my progress over the next months.

I had an amazing experience at Lee Moon Won Hair Clinic in Gangnam! The staff were incredibly knowledgeable and kind, taking the time to carefully explain everything and address all my hair concerns in detail. I felt completely comfortable and well taken care of throughout my visit. The scalp treatment was truly the best I’ve ever experienced—my scalp felt refreshed, healthy, and revitalized afterward. The clinic is clean, professional, and offers a very relaxing atmosphere. I highly recommend Lee Moon Won to anyone looking for expert care and real results!

We had such a great experience! The treatment was so relaxing and all the staff were so friendly and helpful. Would highly recommend adding on the consultation with Dr. Lee Moon Won - it was fascinating to see my scalp up close and to see and understand my scalp issues. Also, it is such a pretty location!

Itaewon Market: A Global Bazaar in the Heart of Seoul
Itaewon Market, a vibrant stretch in Seoul's cosmopolitan district, is a microcosm of the world's cultures. It's a feast for the senses, where the aromas of exotic spices mingle with the sounds of diverse languages.
The market's narrow alleys are lined with shops overflowing with treasures from around the globe. Here, you can find Turkish carpets, Moroccan leather goods, Indian textiles, and African handicrafts. The antique stores are a haven for collectors, offering vintage cameras, vinyl records, and other nostalgic items.
Food lovers will find themselves in paradise. The market boasts a plethora of international restaurants and street food vendors. Sample savory Turkish kebabs, spicy Thai curries, authentic Italian pasta, or crispy Korean fried chicken. Don't forget to try the local specialty, Itaewon tacos, a fusion of Mexican and Korean flavors.
Beyond shopping and dining, Itaewon Market offers a glimpse into the neighborhood's rich history and multicultural identity. The area is home to a mosque, a historic church, and a variety of cultural institutions.
Whether you're a seasoned traveler or a curious local, Itaewon Market is a must-visit destination. It's a place to explore, discover, and immerse yourself in the world's diverse cultures without leaving Seoul.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Seoul, the Ilmin Museum of Art offers a small but richly rewarding experience for visitors interested in contemporary Korean art. Although the museum occupies a modest space, its well-curated exhibitions provide a thoughtful exploration of various artistic expressions.

Upon entering, I was immediately struck by the museum's commitment to showcasing innovative Korean artists. Each exhibit, meticulously arranged and presented, invites viewers to engage deeply with the themes. The museum excels in creating an intimate atmosphere where each piece of art can be appreciated in its own right.

A standout feature of the museum is the cinema room located on the top floor. This unique space offers a series of thought-provoking films that delve into the struggles of modern Korea. The films, ranging from documentary to experimental, challenge viewers to reflect on socio-political issues that shape contemporary Korean society. It's a poignant reminder of the power of art to influence and reflect cultural and historical narratives.

The museum also benefits from its dynamic location. Situated near Gwanghwamun Square, it provides easy access for anyone looking to immerse themselves in Korea's rich historical and cultural tapestry after visiting the museum.

Overall, the Ilmin Museum of Art is a compelling destination for those who seek to understand the pulse of modern Korean art and its reflections on society. While the space may be smaller than some of its counterparts, its exhibitions are thoughtfully selected and profoundly impactful, offering fresh perspectives on significant issues. I left with a deeper appreciation for the role of art in societal discourse and would recommend a visit to anyone with an interest in contemporary art and cultural reflection.

reviews.text:
ILCHI ART HALL is tucked away on the second basement floor of the King Kong building. Outside, you cannot miss the awkward King Kong statue hanging off the building. The box office is just near the main entrance.

To be honest, I had a hard time finding the entrance myself. It is surprisingly small, so I even took a picture to help others recognize it more easily.

The hall has about 220 seats, which makes it a fairly intimate venue. I think it works well for small events. I personally enjoyed Utagokoro Rie’s concert there on February 22, 2025.

About the seating, each section is marked by letters A, B, C, D, E and so on. Each lettered section actually has two rows, divided by yellow steel bars. The catch is that both rows in the same letter share the same elevation. This means you should always try to book the front row of that pair for a clear view.

For example, seats D-07 and D-27 are at the same height. If you sit at D-07, you will enjoy the performance without obstruction. But if you end up in D-27, you will be staring at the back of someone’s head the whole time. In that case, even E-07 is a much better choice. Trust me on this.

title: 잇미샤

reviews.text:
We recently visited I’Park Mall in Yongsan, Seoul, and it was such a fun experience! The mall is full of exciting shops and attractions that both teenagers and elementary school kids can enjoy. We loved exploring the Pokémon Card shop, the Gundam Base, and stores with all kinds of unique figures and collectibles.
Beyond that, the mall also has a wide range of fashion brands like Lee, Colombia, Nike, Uniqlo, and Adidas, making it easy to shop for clothes while the kids enjoy their favorite hobbies.
The facilities are modern and convenient, with plenty of places to relax and eat as well.
Overall, I’Park Mall is a perfect spot for families looking for a mix of shopping, entertainment, and fun!
The mall has 8 floors filled with good stores and was decorated beautifully for Christmas. An awesome spot in the city to visit for the holidays

It’s a vibrant shopping and entertainment destination in downtown Seoul that offers a variety of options for visitors. Spanning 11 impressive floors, the mall is thoughtfully divided into sections: Fashion, Living, and Culture. It features the I Park Department Store, Digital Shopping Center, and Event Park, with standout attractions such as a CGV cinema, e-Sports Stadium, miniature golf, and a large bookstore. With over 100 restaurants, a diverse food court, and charming cafes, the dining options are plentiful. Shoppers can explore an array of electronics, fashion, and home goods, while cultural events, fashion shows, and festivals add to the lively atmosphere. Additional features like a video game arcade, an outdoor garden, and a culture center makes it a good destination for shopping, dining, and entertainment in the city!

I'Park Mall is a huge shopping mall at Yongsan Train Station, with many clothing shops and anime-related stuff (pop mart, Studio Ghibli, Marvel, toys, Nintendo Switch, etc.) and an arcade and lots of gacha. This I'Park Mall surprised me as it had many more things than I had expected, because I always thought Yongsan Train Station was "just another KTX Station." But no, I will recommend any tourists to spend half a day here if you're nearby. There are many things to do here!

This eight-story consumer temple offers everything your heart desires. There's a cinema on the sixth and seventh floors with an iMaxx, food courts, countless shops, and of course, numerous restaurants. It's connected to Yongsan Station, where the blue subway line 1 and many Korean trains depart. Most restaurants close around 10 p.m. If you go to the cinema late, leaving can be like navigating a labyrinth. Many areas are already dark and locked, and many escalators are out of order. It's best to follow the locals.

This place is a local favorite and even though there are a lot of jokbal places nearby, you need to try this place because this place will change your life.

We arrived quite early and there was no queue at all, as they had just opened. By the time we left, the restaurant was packed. We noticed it was filled with locals, and no foreigners at all.

The smallest portion was 30k won, which we found to be quite a lot for 2, as we ordered another bowl of cold noodles as well. Pork was really tender and lived up to the hype! Would come back again just for the jokbal 😋

The owner was very kind, maybe because I came alone and am a tourist. She is an old lady but she can speak practical English. She showed me where to get the cutlery, all you can eat side dishes and water.

The pig foot I ordered is KRW30,000, really cheap! But the portion is too much for one person, haha! The meat is tender and the sauce is savoury. I will definitively come again!

The courage, solidarity and strength of the halmoni’s in the face of their tremendous suffering is deeply palpable in each exhibit and learning this history of these survivors especially in the face of continued global erasure and denial feels like a small act one can take to end violence against women. I am so grateful this museum exists, may these women and their descendants, may we all, may the world know peace.

This museum and the personal stories that were told brought me to tears. This museum is incredibly powerful.

Even as a Dutch person from Indonesian parents, I'm aware of the term 'comfort women'. But I've never heard personal stories. I can't imagine what these women has been going through, because there's no word to describe something as cruel as that.

We came from Japan yesterday where we have visited several WWII related sites. Living in a Dutch city that was severely damaged by bombing during WWII, I wanted to learn more about the Japanese part of this story. Of course, as expected, Japan doesn't acknowledge their role and their crimes during WWII. We travelled to more countries and we've learned about their war crimes. Like the death mars in Borneo for example. And the terrible camps in Thailand. But none of those areas taught us about this part that involved women.

We have a profound respect for the surviving ladies who are making a difference by demonstrating every Wednesday in front of the Japanese embassy. It's a disgrace Japan still doesn't acknowledge the facts and choose to ignore it.

Visiting this museum makes you more aware of these war crimes and how women and girls have suffered and are still suffering worldwide. It has to stop. These brave Korean women are still fighting for recognition. But visiting this museum, you show support and that's the least you can do.

Other than that, this museum is small. But the exhibitions are impressive and they hit you hard. We've spend 2 hours in the museum. The audio tour is included in the fee. The audio has an English option and it really gives you an experience filled with emotions, rather than just telling facts. The entrance is subtle and can be easily missed, by the way.

We highly recommend visiting this museum.

I can't describe how intense this museum is. All the memories and experiences are so moving and important. If you get the chance, come here and listen to this part of history that we should remember, always.

This museum was very educational and impactful. While at times it was a bit confronting its message was beautiful and necessary.

It was easy to find using Naver although keep in mind there are several staircases inside the museum and I’m unsure if there are ways around them. However it did have an audio guide available in multiple languages including English which was surprising and good quality.

This is a great place to learn more about the violence Korean women faced under the Japanese soldiers and women around the world continue to face as well as to pay your respects and donate if you can. I even saw a woman bring her daughter and son which I thought was a good idea to increase awareness and understanding among the younger generations.

Definitely worth checking out if you have time!!

A wonderful museum experience. The museum is in a quiet location and seems unassuming from the outside, but the amount of information, media and exhibiting objects they displayed was very impressive. I learned so much not only about history but also human suffering, resilience and hope.

I went when the Kim Bok Dong special exhibition was on, and it was such a special experience that made me tear up several times. The museum did an excellent job depicting her as a wonderful, exceptionally strong woman who despite her own suffering reached out to victims in need.

I also really appreciated the English audio guide devices the museum kindly provided, as I did not speak Korean at all but was still able to learn so much from the museum. This is an unforgettable experience, would definitely recommend it to others.

reviews.text:
OH – The Fourth Stand-in for the Dictator
Jeongdong Theater, Seoul

When comedy falls silent
The Jeongdong Theater’s OH – The Fourth Stand-in for the Dictator feels less like a traditional musical and more like a staged narrative with music. On a modest rectangular stage, a skilled live band with cello, piano, and winds provides the strongest moments of the evening. Vocals, however, prove uneven: a deep, resonant baritone appears only once, while much of the remaining singing feels thin and high-pitched.

Visually, the production makes inventive use of descending set pieces and a playful puppet sequence, though such ideas appear too rarely. The story of a supermarket worker turned reporter under a dictator is told consistently, but the leads lack charisma. Comedic touches go largely unacknowledged by the audience, leaving the tone subdued.

At more than two hours, the show maintains interest thanks to its music and stagecraft. As a musical, though, OH never fully convinces.
