title: 조계사(서울)
google_addr: 55 Ujeongguk-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
~throw back to Mid of November 2025~

This temple is truly beautiful.
There are flowers everywhere and many different statues of deities, making it a great place for photos.

Being here feels very calming and peaceful.
The atmosphere is quiet and soothing, and it really helps clear the mind.
It’s definitely a nice place to visit!!

We took a quick subway ride to see this beautiful temple. No admission fees or anything, all out in the open. The temple was decorated with flowers with beautiful colors and decor. The main shrine was crowded as a lot of locals go to offer prayers. A lovely sight to see while you are you exploring the city.

Jogyesa Temple is a beautiful and peaceful spot right in the middle of the city.

The vibrant lanterns, ancient trees, and traditional temple buildings create a calming atmosphere despite the busy surroundings.

It’s a great place to pause, reflect and experience a bit of Korean Buddhist culture.

The voice of the temple's abbot chanting sutras, amidst the resonant drumbeats, penetrates deep into the heart.
This marvelous combination of sound waves in the listener's soul. During the festival, the temple is beautifully decorated, and I saw Dragon claw Chrysanthemums here, which I hadn't seen in years. The flowers were so huge and stunning! Every morning, the temple holds its rituals, and the sound of chanting carries far into the distance.

Jogyesa Temple (조계사) is a peaceful and uplifting escape right in the heart of Seoul. The moment you step inside, the noise of the city fades and you’re surrounded by calm, colorful lanterns, and beautifully detailed temple architecture. The main hall is stunning—filled with vibrant artwork, golden Buddha statues, and a serene atmosphere that makes you want to pause and reflect.

The temple grounds are impeccably maintained, and the centuries-old trees add a special sense of history and spiritual grounding. Whether you visit during a regular day or during a festival, the experience is always inspiring.

The monks and volunteers are welcoming and respectful, and the signs around the temple make it easy for visitors to understand the traditions and significance of the space. It’s a perfect place for anyone looking to experience Korean Buddhism, take peaceful photos, or simply enjoy a quiet moment in the middle of the city.

A must-visit cultural and spiritual landmark—beautiful, calming, and truly memorable.

title: 종로 무계원

reviews.text:
서울시 종로구 부암동 인왕산 자락에 위치한 옛 안평대군 거처에 마련한 한국전통 문화공간입니다. 본체와 별체를 포함한 4개동에서 체험, 전시,공연,대관 등 다양한 문화예술프로그램이 운영되는 곳입니다. 특히 눈여겨 볼만한 것은 조선시대 안견이 그린 "몽유도원도"입니다. 몽유도원도는 세종대왕의 3째 아들인 안평대군이 꿈속에서 본 무릉도원을 화가인 안견에게 이야기한 것을 안견이 3일만에 완성한 대작입니다.
This traditional Korean cultural space, located at the foot of Inwangsan Mountain in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul, is housed in the former residence of Prince Anpyeong. A variety of cultural and artistic programs, including hands-on experiences, exhibitions, performances, and rentals, are offered across four buildings, including the main building and annexes. A particular highlight is the Joseon Dynasty-era painting "Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land." This masterpiece, completed in just three days, reflects a dream Prince Anpyeong, the third son of King Sejong, had dreamed of, and told the artist about it.
안평대군의 이상향이 안견의 몽유도원도로 탄생한 장소.  종로에 있던 오진암을 그대로 옮겨와 아름다운 한옥의 모습을 재현했다고 한다.  주차장도 편리하고 고즈넉한 한옥에서 여유있게 둘러보기 좋은 곳.

종로구 부암동에 위치한 전통문화공간 입니다. 원래는 익선동에 있던 한옥 건물인데, 조선말 서화가 이병직의 집이기도 했고, 7.4남북공동성명을 도출해낸 장소였다고 합니다. 이곳은 음식점인 오진암으로 운영되다가 이 건물자재를 이용하여 현재의 위치에 한옥문화공간으로 지었다고 합니다. 현재 위치는 안견이 몽유도원도를 그리게한 장소로 유명하며 조그만 방한켠에서 몽유도원도의 복사본을 전시하여 자세하게 설명을 하는 코너가 있읍니다. 전시가 아니더라도 한옥의 아름다움을 느낄수 있는 특별한 공간인거 같습니다.
오진암이라는 조선시대 요정집(고오급 술집)을 개조하여 문화재로 만든 곳으로, 현재는 원래 목적과 상관없는 한옥전시, 전통문화 전시, 에티켓교육 등을 하는 곳으로 거듭나 사용되고 있습니다. 한옥문화 체험으로 방문하시면 좋을 것 같습니다. 입장료 따로 없고 주차장 있습니다.

서울 한양도성길에서 인왕산 기차바위로 내려와서 부암동 주민센터로 방향을 틀면 만나게 되는 무계원.
근처에 현진건 소설가의 집터도 만나게 된다.
아주 멋진 트레킹길이다.
무계원에 관한 내용은 다른 리뷰 참고하기를~

title: 종로K축제
google_addr: 172 Sejong-daero, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
Visiting Gwanghwamun Square in mid-December is an absolute treat! The entire area is beautifully decorated with festive lights and ornaments, creating a warm and cheerful atmosphere despite the winter chill.

The lighting displays are stunning—perfect for evening strolls and photos. It’s a great spot to soak in the holiday spirit, enjoy the vibrant city energy, and take in the iconic views of Gwanghwamun Gate surrounded by sparkling decorations.

If you’re in Seoul during December, this is definitely a must-visit for the festive vibes and Instagram-worthy shots!

Gwanghamun Square is a very popular tourist destination in Seoul. It's a large public area where name activities are held. There are 2 statues here as well. There's the statue of King Sejong and the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. There are plenty of cafes and restaurants nearby.

Although on first sight Gwanghwamun Square might not look spectacular and any different to other city and town squares, I liked visiting it and walking around.

I started walking from one end of the square and took my time exploring the historical figures and monuments along the way. At the opposite end, the square leads to the grand Gyeongbukgung Palace.

I found the square to be quite large and appreciated the amount of space there. It was popular for tourists as well as locals having lunch and passing through yet I didn't think the area was crowded and congested. The square was very clean and well looked after.

Came across Admiral Yi, looking fierce as ever, almost like he was scolding the broken sign in front of him. The whole square has this mix of history and modern city energy that makes it really unique.  Even with a few things needing repair, the area still feels alive and inspiring.

Many people think this is just a square but behind the General's statue there is an entrance to a huge underground museum. It is so sad many people skip this place before entering the palace.

That reminds me the word: There is an unseen thing behind every visible one.

So if you go down the stairs or elevator you will at least witness the replica of this famous turtle ship here. Plus you can wear one of the traditional clothes here, get inside the replika ship and take photos.

Please visit this place before you visit the palace and you can also chill at the square there are many shadowy areas and street music is on.

Went in to today looking for some gold jewlery. I was warmly met in the store at booth 5 by Jung Ji Hye.  She was very attentive and took her time to assist me. She gave me a great deal and needless to say, I left the store with several gold items. I will for sure will be coming back again on my next trip to Seoul.
This is the only place to buy gold in Seoul. This is where all those small jewelry shops get their stuff and then mark it up.
Go here for jewelry instead of more expensive areas like ChungDahm. The prices was literally about 75% of what they tried to charge in other parts of Korea. Check out the shops here.
Must go if you want to find a place to buy jewelry.

title: 종묘 [유네스코 세계유산]
google_addr: South Korea, Seoul, Jongno District, Jong-ro, 157 종묘관리소

reviews.text: Jongmyo Shrine is a quiet and spiritual sanctuary right in the middle of busy Seoul. I love how well they have preserved the traditions here. I highly recommend taking the free guided tour, which is available in both Korean and English. it takes a little over an hour and provides great context. While the buildings themselves aren't flashy or tall, the immense scale of the space and the simple architecture are truly amazing. A must visit for a peaceful break and a deep dive into Korean history!

Jongmyo Shrine is the oldest Confucian shrine in Seoul.
And the most authentic of all.
It is located in the downtown (as far as I understood when I was there).

Originally, the shrine was built in the 14th century and it keeps its current form since the 16th century.

When you enter it, there is a path that you are not allowed to walk on - this is a path for spirits... As you enter the territory of the park, you pass by several buildings, all of which are built in accordance with traditional pungsu principles (simplifying it, balancing the key elements, as well as balancing the human life with the elements).

It is one of the key sites that you should visit if you are in Seoul.
It is very peaceful there and I always had a chance to ponder on eternal matters. A perfect place for that...

Jongmyo Shrine is an important historical landmark. It is the ancestry resting place for the tablets of the Joseon Kings and other important figures. The place is smaller than the other 3 palaces, Gyeongbukgung, Changdeokgung and Changyeonggung. Located just outside of Jongno 3 Sam-ga station and close by to Seosulla-gil with its trendy cafes and restaurants. Close on every Wednesday.

Recommend visiting here if you are into visiting historical landmarks or of significance. Joseon Dynasty’s shrine for royal family, it is well maintained, preserved, and shows the height of Confucianism in Korea.

The main attraction/building of the shrine (Jeongjeon) finished its 5 year repair and maintenance work, so it is now fully open and there are no scaffolds barring entry. Good time to visit now.

Tip: If your schedule allows while visiting, I recommend visiting here on the last Wednesday of the month, as entry fee is waived and you can walk around the site freely and tour around at your pace (on regular days, you have to pay to enter and be on a scheduled tour that a guide leads you through).

An excellent place in Seoul to see the ancient heritage of Korea - so we'll preserved.

The shrine is situated on sprawling grounds with thousands of trees with well laid out trails leading the visitors from one building to the next.

In popular belief - the middle stone "median" is not meant for humans to walk on since it is believed that spirits of ancient royalty walk there.

This heritage site deserves a good couple of hours. A very peaceful experience.

Entry is 1000 Won - from the ticket booth located to the outside right of the main gate.

reviews.text: Jongmyo Shrine is a quiet and spiritual sanctuary right in the middle of busy Seoul. I love how well they have preserved the traditions here. I highly recommend taking the free guided tour, which is available in both Korean and English. it takes a little over an hour and provides great context. While the buildings themselves aren't flashy or tall, the immense scale of the space and the simple architecture are truly amazing. A must visit for a peaceful break and a deep dive into Korean history!

Jongmyo Shrine is the oldest Confucian shrine in Seoul.
And the most authentic of all.
It is located in the downtown (as far as I understood when I was there).

Originally, the shrine was built in the 14th century and it keeps its current form since the 16th century.

When you enter it, there is a path that you are not allowed to walk on - this is a path for spirits... As you enter the territory of the park, you pass by several buildings, all of which are built in accordance with traditional pungsu principles (simplifying it, balancing the key elements, as well as balancing the human life with the elements).

It is one of the key sites that you should visit if you are in Seoul.
It is very peaceful there and I always had a chance to ponder on eternal matters. A perfect place for that...

Jongmyo Shrine is an important historical landmark. It is the ancestry resting place for the tablets of the Joseon Kings and other important figures. The place is smaller than the other 3 palaces, Gyeongbukgung, Changdeokgung and Changyeonggung. Located just outside of Jongno 3 Sam-ga station and close by to Seosulla-gil with its trendy cafes and restaurants. Close on every Wednesday.

Recommend visiting here if you are into visiting historical landmarks or of significance. Joseon Dynasty’s shrine for royal family, it is well maintained, preserved, and shows the height of Confucianism in Korea.

The main attraction/building of the shrine (Jeongjeon) finished its 5 year repair and maintenance work, so it is now fully open and there are no scaffolds barring entry. Good time to visit now.

Tip: If your schedule allows while visiting, I recommend visiting here on the last Wednesday of the month, as entry fee is waived and you can walk around the site freely and tour around at your pace (on regular days, you have to pay to enter and be on a scheduled tour that a guide leads you through).

As you stroll along the tree-lined paths, you’re greeted by the soothing sounds of cascading water and fresh, cool breezes that instantly refresh the soul.

The highlight, of course, is the waterfall itself—modest in size but beautifully integrated into the natural setting. It’s a peaceful spot to sit, reflect, or simply enjoy a moment of stillness. The park features well-maintained trails, shaded areas, and benches that invite relaxation—ideal for picnics, meditation, or leisurely reading.

Whether you're walking solo, spending time with loved ones, or just craving a break in nature, Yongma Waterfall Park offers that perfect blend of tranquility and natural beauty. Highly recommended if you're in the area and want to escape the urban grind—even just for a little while.

Palace with western architecture design ans built during the time of emperor Gojong as the royal library.  There are exhibits about the important turn in Korean history.

This beautiful, unique building was the royal library of the Deoksugung Palace at the late XIX century. Jungmyeongjeong or "Hall of everlasting brightness" was constructed by
Afanasy Seredin-Sabatin, a Ukraine born architect, steersman-pilot and reporter, who was the first European (Ukrainian and Russian) architect to work in the Korean Empire from 1890 to 1904.

Also very interesting to read a story about the discovery of a Taeguekgi in one of temples, thinking about the brave people in those challenging times. May peace shine upon and guard the world.

There’s a local cafe where you can try some Korean desserts and beverages, grandmas working there are super cute and friendly.

Combining this temple with the hanok area together, it’ll be brilliant fall foliage day.

Went to Eunpyeong to check out a cafe and did a little trekking to Bukhansan National Park. Many local seen trekking up in groups nearing to noon when it is not so cold but not crowded. Quaint and clean area, very impressed on how they maintained it. Even the washroom near the temple is so clean, you need to change to slippers before you enter. If you are exploring Eunpyeong checking out the hanoks & cafe, do drop by the park & temple. Is about 30-60 mins from Seoul City Hall area depending on your transport options. I wanted to write a review because I wish I had something like this to go off of while I was totally overstimulated and paralyzed from the sheer amount of options available lol. I looked at all the before and afters and picked this one cos a lot of the pictures weren’t heavily filtered so you can see the results immediately post and also how it settles in a few weeks later. People also stated how the actual doctor does the consultation himself even tho it’s just for filler - a lot of factory clinics in Korea will have assistants do the consultation so this was different and one of the selling points.

Had a consultation with the doctor on the 6th floor (which is where you will check in as well) The doctor was so kind but also straight to the point; I told him what I wanted and he was able to give me more realistic expectations about the results - and he said he will try to meet my requests as much as anatomically possible. Moved to the 5th floor for the treatment. Sat in a comfy couch in semi private waiting area while waiting for the numbing cream to take effect. Went to the treatment room and completed the treatments with doctor - he took a lot of care and time molding/ looking at the before pics. I got 1cc in lips and 2cc in my left cheek to fix my asymmetry. Pain was a normal level from what you’d expect at these treatments, lessening as you go by. Also they give you a shot of antibiotics/a prescription to fill at a pharmacy.

Overall a great experience, staff was nice too and I’d recommend the doctor because he was very very kind and doesn’t rush you. Staff was also very patient with my questions.

Also don’t be like me and forget to bring your passport to the clinic - i think they can still do a tax refund with a picture but save yourself the trouble and bring it with you. Note also I’m Korean American and fluent in Korean - I can’t speak to the ease of English communication with the staff but nothing that can’t be done with a translator/app.

I went to Chamin Plastic Surgery after doing much research and decided to do ulterapy and rejuran as well as botox around my lips and chin. Everything went pretty quickly and nicely. can’t wait to see my results!
The service is really good and the doctor did a good job on me with lips filler, ulthera and 10therma. I highly recommend this clinic!

She is a doctor in Korea who can apply Russian techniques lipfiller , she is really good at her job, she listened to me and understood what I wanted. I am a foreigner living here and it was important for her to understand me because I am a foreigner and I liked her kindness and technique. title: 창경궁
google_addr: 185 Changgyeonggung-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
~ throw back to mid of November 2025 ~

This palace is so beautiful!
Although the area isn’t very big, every corner is incredibly unique and perfect for photos.

It would be good you can spend about 2 hours walk through the whole place.
It definitely worth a visit!

This place is absolutely breathtaking. The scenery stretches out in a mesmerizing panorama, filled with vibrant colors and textures. Lush greenery surrounds the area, and the air feels crisp and refreshing. Sunlight filters gently through the leaves, casting dappled shadows that dance along the ground. Every corner seems alive with natural beauty, from the soft whisper of the breeze to the distant sound of birdsong. It is a place where time feels as if it slows down, inviting you to pause, breathe deeply, and take in every detail of its serene charm.

This palace is connected to the neighboring palace, but you need to buy a ticket to enter each one.
You can either purchase a combined ticket for both places or buy separate tickets at each gate.

I visited early on a Saturday morning after it snowed, and the scenery was stunning. It was a bit cold walking around outside, but I really enjoyed the experience.

Saw this place close to the hotel.   Very large area so lots of walking.   Interesting to read the history, the kings and queens.  Can't imagine the servants going up and down the large stone steps.   Also recognized many areas that have been shown in historical k dramas.   Just loved the architectural designs.   It's winter now so very cold to walk through but minimal crowds.  Able to take pictures without people in the middle of them.  Loved not having to deal with large crowds.

Changgyeonggung Palace is a very pleasant and calming place to visit.

When I went, it was surprisingly quiet, which made the experience even more enjoyable.
The peaceful atmosphere allowed me to take my time walking around and really appreciate the surroundings.

One of the highlights was the garden at the back of the palace which it added to the sense of tranquility and felt like a perfect escape from the busy city.

Overall, it’s a lovely spot to relax, enjoy some greenery and experience a more serene side of Seoul.

title: 창덕궁 낙선재

reviews.text:
The Joseon Dynasty did not truly come to an end in 1910. It only became history in 1989, with the passing of Princess Deokhye. From the moment thirteen-year-old Princess Deokhye was sent to Japan in 1925 and endured years of suffering, to remaining confined there even after Japan’s defeat, and finally being allowed to return to Korea only when she was nearly fifty and already mentally broken — her life was marked by sorrow at every turn. She then spent the rest of her days quietly living in the land where she was born, until her death. Even simply reading these historical records is enough to leave one choked with emotion.

Although history has passed and today we advocate peace — and cannot hate or forgive on behalf of others — the people who were swept up by the tides of history, those who endured immense suffering and relentless torment, never truly received a sincere apology. And this is true not only for Korea, which was invaded, but for countless people across many nations who endured similar pain.
This section of the palace grounds ends up being more well-kept and more interesting to see than the rest of it. The buildings are quite nice and their layout is rather beautiful and intricate.

It contains the sad story of Korea Royal family.
The last Queen and Princess passed away here till 1986.
So while I walked this place I feel I hear their stories.
It used to be king’s library , Queen ‘s quarter , concubine’s quarter as well.

This complex of buildings was used as residences by the kings and their families. It is one of the more recent additions to the palace, but still, plenty of history here. The multi-tiered nature of this area of the palace makes for some pretty nice views. Definitely worth stopping to see if you visit the Changdeokgung Palace

仁政門是 昌德宮 中極具代表性的正門之一，也是通往主殿「仁政殿」前的重要關卡。走到這裡，已經正式進入昌德宮的核心政治空間。

仁政門前方視野開闊，整體配置莊重而不浮誇，展現朝鮮王朝強調節制與秩序的宮殿美學。這裡過去是文武百官進入仁政殿覲見國王前的必經之地，因此在空間尺度與中軸對稱上都相當講究。

站在仁政門前，可以清楚感受到昌德宮由外而內逐步遞進的設計邏輯，也能理解為什麼昌德宮被認為是最貼合自然地形、同時兼顧實用與禮制的宮殿之一。這一區域不僅適合拍照，也很適合靜靜觀察宮殿整體的布局與氣氛。

The Secret Garden at Changdeokgung Palace, once used for royal entertainment and ceremonies, is a significant heritage site showcasing traditional landscaping.

The garden was kept as natural as possible, the landscaping, pavilions and buildings reflects traditional Korean architecture, demonstrating a masterful harmony between structures and nature.

In my opinion, the most beautiful time to see the garden is during the fall when the autumn foliage is at its peak and the leaves have just started to fall.

I visited this garden on 5 November 2025 and autumn foliage was nearing its peak, it was so beautiful.

A magical night at Changdeokgung Palace’s Secret Garden (Huwon)! Originally the private retreat of Joseon kings, Huwon was designed as a hidden sanctuary where nature and philosophy shaped royal life. I joined the guided night tour at the palace, each of us carrying lanterns to light the way through moonlit paths and historic pavilions. The atmosphere was immersive, with traditional performances unfolding in a quiet courtyard toward the end. A rare chance to experience Korean heritage after dark.

This is the rear garden of the royal palace Changdeokgung. The garden is so nicely designed. The design respects the natural hill. The garden was built with slopes. Check carefully when you buy the tickets.

reviews.text:
Champion 1250 at IPark Mall Yongsan is a great indoor play space for kids, conveniently located at the train terminal/shopping/grocery complex, making it easy for the whole family to spend the day without leaving the building. The kids cafe is on the top floor and is spacious enough to accommodate many children.

They do a good job maintaining cleanliness, although it can be a challenge when it's crowded. The staff is attentive and ensures kids don’t wander out on their own, which is a huge plus for parents.

However, the prices are on the expensive side, especially for drinks and baked goods inside the cafe. For a better experience and to avoid crowds, I recommend visiting on weekdays or Sundays. A great option if your kids need to burn off some energy indoors!
Great indoor playground for kids. It is appropriate for kids aged 5-10, in my opinion. My kids had a blast here and left all sweaty from running around so much.

Champion 1250 is a large indoor playground ideal for elementary school children, located near the Han River and connected to several shopping malls and a subway station.

While it offers plenty of activities, the restrooms are insufficient for the venue’s capacity.

There are a few free seats near the restroom, but seating remains limited even if you purchase an entrance ticket as an adult.

I dropped my 9 year old off here for 2 hours for ₩22,000. You need to have socks with grip which you can buy there for ₩3,000. My kid had a fun time and would go back, there was rock climbing, mirror maze and a zip line that he enjoyed. And I enjoyed my 2 hours of shopping! It's on the 6th floor of i'park mall.

Great place for toddler and pre-schoolers. Lots of places to climb, crawl through and the beloved trampoline. There is also a small zip and a high ropes for slightly older kids. Parents are catered to by a great cafe- well located to catch a glimpse of your zooming toddler. One could argue that it’s more expansive relative to other areas - paid 25k Krw for me and one kid but it offers more space and more play area so worth a slight premium. As a foreigner so far the lowest I paid anywhere was 16k as a bench. Also bring google translate- all the stuff is very nice but English can be a challenge. I was here during the week so can’t comment on weekend crowds but you will get those anywhere!

마음 쉼 힐링캠프 일환으로 방문했습니다. 천도교의 독립운동을 위한 희생과 기여에 대해 배울 수 있어서 유익했고 좋았습니다.  | 여행유튜버 지구별시골쥐 @joonimism

동학운동의 역사를 배울 수 있는 곳.

인사동 옆, 운현궁 맞은 편에 위치하여 연계탐방하면 좋은 곳.
1921년도에 완성한 성당.. 손병희님 주도로 탄생하게 됨.. 명동성당, 조선총독부와 같이 서울 3대 건축물.

1921년도 근대에 지어진 서양식의 건물로 붉은벽돌과 화강암이 조화를 이루는 아름다운 건물이다. 3.1 독립운동의 주역인 손병희가 주도하여 지은 건물로 서울시 유형문화재로 지정된 문화재이다. 천도교는 우리나라에서 발생한 종교로 근대 최제우 최시형 손병희로 연결되어 현재에 이른다.
It is a Western-style building built in modern times in 1921. It is a beautiful building with red bricks and granite in harmony. It was built by Sohn Byeong-hee, a leading figure in the 3.1 Independence Movement, and is designated as a tangible cultural property of Seoul. Cheondogyo is a religion that originated in Korea and has been connected to Choi Je-woo, Choi Si-hyeong, and Son Byeong-hee in modern times.

title: 충무공 이순신 동상

reviews.text:
An impressive 17-metre-tall statue standing proudly along Gwanghwamun Square. The monument feels powerful & dignified, fitting for the Korea’s legendary naval hero.

At the front of the pedestal are two stone drums & a replica of the famous turtle-shaped battleship (Geobukseon). The Myeongnyang Splash Fountain was turned off during our visit — likely due to the winter season — but the statue remains striking even without the water features.

A significant landmark that’s hard to miss when exploring central Seoul.

This is a statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin at Gwanghwamun Square. It's opposite the statue of King Sejong the great. The front of the statue has multiple fountains but it's not always on so tourists can get near the statue at certain hours.

Yi Su -Sin was a Korean admiral and military general known for his victories against the Japanese navy during the Imjin War in the Joseon period. He fought in at least 23 naval battles, achieving victory in all. In many of these engagements, he commanded forces that were outnumbered and poorly supplied.

One of South Korea's most famous generals!

Very good - this is a statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin and is located opposite the statue of King Sejong the great. The front of the statue has multiple fountains - which are on / off at various hours of the day.

World's greatest admiral, according to both the greatest English and Japanese admirals of all time. There are historical plaques around the statue that you can read up on, plus there are QR codes you can scan to get thorough history lessons. Underneath the admiral statue is a model of tortoise ship that he utilized in defense during his time. There are plenty of water fountains you can jump into, especially those hot and humid summer, and act like a kid 😊 Highly recommend a visit. 😎👍

After I picked out the items I needed, I was about to pay at the cashier, and the clerk asked me if I had a foreign nationality and I said yes.
The clerk said that if I have my passport now, the VAT (tax) can be deducted immediately, so I could purchase the product with the VAT refunded immediately by presenting my passport.
If any of the people reading my review have a foreign nationality other than the Korean nationality, please take your passport and get a VAT refund right away when you shop the Kakao Friends store in Korea.
Anyway, thanks to the friendly clerk!

Kakao Friends Store Info.

Kakao Friends is a popular South Korean character brand that has gained worldwide recognition in recent years. The brand features various adorable characters that have captured the hearts of people of all ages. If you're a fan of these lovable characters, you should definitely visit the Kakao Friends store.

The Kakao Friends store is a themed store that offers a wide range of merchandise featuring the brand's beloved characters, including Ryan, Apeach, Muzi, Con, and Frodo. From plushies and stationery to clothing and household items, there's something for everyone at the store.

The store is designed with the brand's signature colors of yellow and white, and is decorated with various character-themed installations that are perfect for taking Instagram-worthy photos. The store also features interactive installations where visitors can take part in various activities related to the characters.

Apart from merchandise, the store also offers a variety of food and drinks at its café, such as character-themed lattes and desserts. There's also a separate section in the store where visitors can purchase Kakao Friends-themed snacks and confectionery.

The Kakao Friends store has multiple locations across South Korea, including Seoul, Busan, and Jeju Island. Each location offers a unique experience, so be sure to check out the store's website for more information on each location.

Overall, if you're a fan of Kakao Friends or just love cute characters, the Kakao Friends store is a must-visit destination for a fun-filled and adorable shopping experience.

reviews.text:
We recently visited I’Park Mall in Yongsan, Seoul, and it was such a fun experience! The mall is full of exciting shops and attractions that both teenagers and elementary school kids can enjoy. We loved exploring the Pokémon Card shop, the Gundam Base, and stores with all kinds of unique figures and collectibles.
Beyond that, the mall also has a wide range of fashion brands like Lee, Colombia, Nike, Uniqlo, and Adidas, making it easy to shop for clothes while the kids enjoy their favorite hobbies.
The facilities are modern and convenient, with plenty of places to relax and eat as well.

The mall has 8 floors filled with good stores and was decorated beautifully for Christmas. An awesome spot in the city to visit for the holidays

It’s a vibrant shopping and entertainment destination in downtown Seoul that offers a variety of options for visitors. Spanning 11 impressive floors, the mall is thoughtfully divided into sections: Fashion, Living, and Culture. It features the I Park Department Store, Digital Shopping Center, and Event Park, with standout attractions such as a CGV cinema, e-Sports Stadium, miniature golf, and a large bookstore. With over 100 restaurants, a diverse food court, and charming cafes, the dining options are plentiful. Shoppers can explore an array of electronics, fashion, and home goods, while cultural events, fashion shows, and festivals add to the lively atmosphere. Additional features like a video game arcade, an outdoor garden, and a culture center makes it a good destination for shopping, dining, and entertainment in the city!

I'Park Mall is a huge shopping mall at Yongsan Train Station, with many clothing shops and anime-related stuff (pop mart, Studio Ghibli, Marvel, toys, Nintendo Switch, etc.) and an arcade and lots of gacha. This I'Park Mall surprised me as it had many more things than I had expected, because I always thought Yongsan Train Station was "just another KTX Station." But no, I will recommend any tourists to spend half a day here if you're nearby. There are many things to do here!

This eight-story consumer temple offers everything your heart desires. There's a cinema on the sixth and seventh floors with an iMaxx, food courts, countless shops, and of course, numerous restaurants. It's connected to Yongsan Station, where the blue subway line 1 and many Korean trains depart. Most restaurants close around 10 p.m. If you go to the cinema late, leaving can be like navigating a labyrinth. Many areas are already dark and locked, and many escalators are out of order. It's best to follow the locals.

It’s not just about looking at products, it’s about discovering yourself through technology.
What makes this exhibition stand out is the use of MinART technology, a combination of AR and AI that creates a futuristic and highly personalized experience 🤍

Skin & Scalp Analysis
In this area, visitors can check their skin and scalp conditions in detail.
The analysis is powered by AI, making the results more accurate and tailored to each individual.
It feels like a professional consultation, but faster, smarter, and more modern.

Personality Color Test
One of the most exciting parts of the exhibition.
Using AR technology, visitors can discover their personality color, not just based on appearance, but also on vibe, mood, and overall impression.
It’s surprisingly insightful and makes you reflect on how you present yourself.

Decoration & Atmosphere
The decoration is honestly stunning.
Every zone is thoughtfully designed with a clean, modern, and immersive concept.
Walking through the exhibition feels like stepping into a beauty-tech art space rather than a regular expo.

Overall Impression
BtheB successfully blends beauty, art, and technology into one seamless experience.
With the support of MinART, the exhibition feels innovative, interactive, and deeply personal, making it not just visually pleasing, but also meaningful.

reviews.text: Pretty good aquarium experience, with a clear path to follow. Kids enjoyed the mermaid show even though it was in Korean. The other exhibits and tanks were also very enjoyable and informative. However, it's not cheap though,and can get crowded, like it's was when we visited on a Saturday afternoon.

SEA LIFE at COEX is such a fun and fascinating place to visit, especially for kids! There are so many kinds of colorful fish and marine animals to see, all beautifully displayed in well-designed tanks.

The aquarium is clean, well-organized, and easy to explore. It’s conveniently located inside COEX Mall, so getting there by public transport is very easy.
Kids and even Adults absolutely loved every moment. A great place for families to enjoy and learn together!

South Korea's premier marine theme parks, located within the Starfield COEX Mall in the Gangnam District. It is home to over 20,000 marine animals representing 650 species, spread across 14 themed zones under the theme "Fantastic Journey of Water."

Opening (2000): Originally opened as the COEX Aquarium, it was the first marine theme park in Korea to introduce professional concepts like "aquarist" and structured marine storytelling.

Acquisition (2022): The facility was acquired by Merlin Entertainments, a global leader in location-based entertainment, as part of their strategy to establish flagship attractions in major gateway cities.

Rebranding (2025): On July 26, 2025, it officially rebranded as SEA LIFE COEX, Seoul Aquarium. This transition included a major "glow-up" with updated branding, improved animal habitats, and new interactive exhibits.

Ocean Kingdom: Features South Korea's largest shark habitat, housing 17 different species including the sand tiger shark.

Deep Blue Sea Tunnel: An immersive walkway where visitors can observe sharks and rays swimming directly overhead.

Seal Beach Cove: A newly expanded area for harbor seals that is five times larger than the previous habitat to better reflect their natural land-based behaviors.

Unique Experiences: Offers Seoul's first glass-bottom boat ride over shark enclosures and a "Sea at Night" zone that uses media art to enhance the jellyfish exhibits.

reviews.text: As far as malls go, this one serves its purpose well. There are plenty of selections and it's not very crowded and it  is well communicated by the metro. A large-scale complex mall that is extremely convenient and full of things to enjoy.
It is easily accessible not only by car but also by subway and bus.

It is directly connected to a department store and also features a cinema and a wide variety of restaurants, making it a place where you can spend the entire day.

The first floor frequently transforms into a large event space, hosting movie promotions, new product showcases, and various themed markets.

It also houses a large E-Mart and a major bookstore, so you can enjoy both shopping and cultural activities in one place.

All areas, including restrooms and other facilities, are kept very clean, making this mall especially comfortable to use.

옛 공간을 새로운 느낌으로 활용하고 있는 곳.
건물은 무척 낡았으나 기존의 낡음을 버리지 않고 새로운 시도의 확장은 무척 환영할만 하다.

새로운 도전이 있는곳
공공건물의 재생 교과서

탈영역 우정국은 우체국으로 사용중이던 건물을 전시공간으로 리모델링한 상업적 성격과는 거리가 있는 전시 공간 입니다.
외부는 아직도 일반적인 우체국 건물특성을 유지하고 있지만, 내부는 화이트 공간에 가깝게 재생된 상태지만, 우체국 지역분점으로 사용되던 상태의 내부 시설과 흔적들이 아직 그대로 유지되고 있습니다.
특히 내부에 남아있는 대형 금고와 30센치 두께의 금고문이 이 공간만의 개성이라 생각 됩니다.
2층은 세미나실 성격으로 개조돼 있고, 단체 모임들을 처리할 수 있을 시설들이 있습니다.
1층 외부에는 예전 우체국에서 파쇄기 대용으로 사용됐던 공무서 파기용 화로와 작은 굴뚝이 있어서, 90년대 이전 사용됐던 우체국이었겠구나~ 하는 시대감을 느끼게 되더군요.
공간은 크지 않지만 지역내 개성을 유지하면서도 문화공간으로써 지역특성을 반영하고 있는 멋진 곳입니다.

이곳은 시립이나 공립이 아닌 개인 사비로 유지되는 공간이더군요. (대부분의 대안공간들이 그래왔듯이)
골목 안쪽에 위치하고 있고, 주차공간은 없습니다. 가족단위 나들이 위치로는 보편적인 성격을 갖고 있는 공간은 아닙니다. 상설 전시가 아닌 매달 전시가 바뀌니 웹검색으로 전시 검색을 해서 참고할 필요가 있습니다.

자전거 라이딩 중에 잠시 전시관람하기 좋은 장소 입니다. 바로 옆 아파트 단지를 지나면 한강으로 진입할 수 있어 지나다니며 들르기 편한곳입니다.

reviews.text: In the lively Gangnam district, you'll find a group of royal tombs that are recognized by UNESCO, showcasing Korea's fascinating history. reviews.text: Jongmyo Shrine is a quiet and spiritual sanctuary right in the middle of busy Seoul. I love how well they have preserved the traditions here. I highly recommend taking the free guided tour, which is available in both Korean and English. it takes a little over an hour and provides great context. While the buildings themselves aren't flashy or tall, the immense scale of the space and the simple architecture are truly amazing. A must visit for a peaceful break and a deep dive into Korean history!

Jongmyo Shrine is the oldest Confucian shrine in Seoul.
And the most authentic of all.
It is located in the downtown (as far as I understood when I was there).

Originally, the shrine was built in the 14th century and it keeps its current form since the 16th century.

When you enter it, there is a path that you are not allowed to walk on - this is a path for spirits... As you enter the territory of the park, you pass by several buildings, all of which are built in accordance with traditional pungsu principles (simplifying it, balancing the key elements, as well as balancing the human life with the elements).

It is one of the key sites that you should visit if you are in Seoul.
It is very peaceful there and I always had a chance to ponder on eternal matters. A perfect place for that...

Jongmyo Shrine is an important historical landmark. It is the ancestry resting place for the tablets of the Joseon Kings and other important figures. The place is smaller than the other 3 palaces, Gyeongbukgung, Changdeokgung and Changyeonggung. Located just outside of Jongno 3 Sam-ga station and close by to Seosulla-gil with its trendy cafes and restaurants. Close on every Wednesday.

Recommend visiting here if you are into visiting historical landmarks or of significance. Joseon Dynasty’s shrine for royal family, it is well maintained, preserved, and shows the height of Confucianism in Korea.

The main attraction/building of the shrine (Jeongjeon) finished its 5 year repair and maintenance work, so it is now fully open and there are no scaffolds barring entry. Good time to visit now.

Tip: If your schedule allows while visiting, I recommend visiting here on the last Wednesday of the month, as entry fee is waived and you can walk around the site freely and tour around at your pace (on regular days, you have to pay to enter and be on a scheduled tour that a guide leads you through).

An excellent place in Seoul to see the ancient heritage of Korea - so we'll preserved.

The shrine is situated on sprawling grounds with thousands of trees with well laid out trails leading the visitors from one building to the next.

In popular belief - the middle stone "median" is not meant for humans to walk on since it is believed that spirits of ancient royalty walk there.

This heritage site deserves a good couple of hours. A very peaceful experience.

Entry is 1000 Won - from the ticket booth located to the outside right of the main gate.

Hey friend, if you remember Techno Mart at Gangbyeon, you probably remember how big it used to feel. For a long time, this place was one of Seoul’s go-to shopping spots. Busy, loud, full of energy.

These days, though, things feel different. Walk through the floors and you will notice plenty of empty shops. It is hard not to feel that shift.

Honestly, the reason is not that hard to figure out. Online shopping changed the game. Now we buy things with a few taps on our phones instead of wandering through big malls. Convenience won, and places like this felt it first.

Still, it is not the end of the story. As long as there is a CGV theater on the 10th floor and ENTER6 on the first, people will keep coming back for movies, food, and a reason to step outside.

Techno Mart may not be what it once was, but it is still standing. And sometimes, that is how places find a new role. Enjoy.

Floors 3 through 8 seem to feature the tech-related products that this place is known for. I am not used to seeing technology malls such as this, so it was a unique experience for me. On the 9th floor you will find a good selection of restaurants and a movie theater. I feel one of the hidden gems is the rooftop terrace on the 9th floor. If you like photography and good sunset spots, I recommend this location. The terrace faces south west, so you can get some amazing sunset views of Lotte World Tower and the Jamsil neighborhood.

reviews.text:
Mario Outlet in Gasan-dong, Seoul, is Asia's largest downtown fashion outlet, featuring over 600 brands across three connected buildings with discounts often ranging from 40-50%. Located near Gasan Digital Complex Station (Line 7), it offers extensive shopping for apparel, luxury goods, and, specifically, Korean fashion brands.
Key Details
Location: 23 Digital-ro 9-gil, Geumcheon-gu, Seoul.
Hours: Monday-Thursday 10:30-21:00, Friday-Sunday 10:30-21:30.
Structure: Three halls (Mario Fashion Town) specializing in fashion, outdoor gear, and accessories.
Brands: Over 600 local and international brands, featuring a "No Brand Shop" and Daiso.
Amenities: Food courts (mainly in Hall 3), tax refund services, and lockers on the first floor.
Transportation: A short walk from Exit 4 of Gasan Digital Complex Station (Subway Lines 1 & 7).
Shopping Tips
Best Time: Friday to Sunday for the best selection, though it can be crowded.
Activities: Plan to spend at least 3 hours exploring the three buildings.
Deals: Look for additional discounts on top of marked prices, especially for winter clothing in October or summer clothes in April.
Nearby: Lotte Factory Outlet and W-Mall are located nearby for more options.

reviews.text: I stopped by this new place on the first floor after visiting my usual café upstairs, and it was so good that I came back two days in a row! They have a wide variety of unique makgeolli, so when I went in the evening I also ordered drinks, and the makgeolli pairing is highly recommended. The lobster pasta, marked as a signature dish, came with a fresh and generously sized lobster tail on top—it paired beautifully with the K-chamnamul oil pasta. The gochujang tomato hangover stew was hearty, spicy, and so satisfying, making it a perfect choice as an anju. I also enjoyed the seaweed chip salad made with the famous Geochang gim, which was refreshing and light. And the makgeolli slush? Absolutely delicious! You can really tell they use quality ingredients because everything felt easy on the stomach afterward, and the staff were all very kind. Definitely planning to return!

title: 페즈 (FEZH)

reviews.text: It is a great cultural space for others to relax and heal through open, relaxing spaces. The building is unique, with lots of influence taken from nature. A potential improvement could be utilizing more nature colors within the building itself; however, having an open resting place within the city is a great strategy to enhance the community.

I had the pleasure of visiting FEZH and was very impressed by the innovation and the marketing concept presented by CEO Lim Clint. His values and mission are clearly reflected through the architecture and community spaces. It was extremely inspiring and I am so grateful for this opportunity. I’m looking forward to see FEZH evolve.

I had the opportunity to tour Fezh and even have a small sound bath. It is an impressive space and I appreciated learning about the intention behind each and every detail. It’s nice that it is accessible to anyone and it would be a great place to have coffee with a colleague or spend time at the Blue Cat bar.

Fezh was an awesome space that I got to visit on my trip to South Korea. The yoga studio and outdoor spaces were some of my favorites and I recommend this place for any events. Our guide was great and very informative as well. Amazing experience!

Fezh was an awesome space that I got to visit on my trip to South Korea! I really enjoyed how purposeful everything about it was. From the wave-like architecture of the front of the building, to the dirt that was included in the plaque at the entrance, Fezh was entirely curated to fit the needs of the community while also going back to the natural roots that the space was built on. 10/10 experience overall and I’d consider this as an event space if I lived closer!

reviews.text:

This place is pretty awesome. It's a multi-level figures collection museum, which is a haven for geeks and nerds. And the staff was friendly too. There was this young lady at the front desk who spoke perfect English too! Thank you to her for her guidance on how to navigate the museum!
Full of amazing gundam model kits, robots, dragon ball statues, one piece figure statues, Hollywood movies super heroes, transformers statues, really really phenomenal!!! 5 stars recommended!!

I had an amazing time at Figure Museum W in Seoul! The collection is incredible, featuring superheroes, Japanese anime icons, and rare, high-end statues. The displays are beautifully curated, making it feel like a mix between an art gallery and a collector’s paradise.

The atmosphere is cozy, the staff is friendly, and there’s something for every fan—Marvel, DC, Gundam, and classic Japanese anime. If you love figures and pop culture, this hidden gem is definitely worth a visit!

My initial impression after the visit was that the owner must have ran out of run at his home for these figures and this is his fancy figures warehouse 😂
Honestly for 15000 won the collections were mediocre for my expectations. There were many limited and numbered figures but overall you can see the taste and preferences. There were many times when I questioned why certain photos, posters, or collection were on display there as they have no meaningful value to visitors.  By the way you can finder better deal on entrance fee through 3rd party sites than at the door. Kids and adults are same price and the place is pretty tight.  The display windows are not windex cleaned which is a big minus.

Piknic is a complex cultural space, a building with 5 floors including the t basement and rooftop, and a cafe, wine bar, restaurant, gift shop, and exhibition hall.
There is a large tree on the way down to the parking lot, a greenhouse and flower beds in front of the building, and a pretty garden on the rooftop.
If you take the elevator from the rooftop to the basement level, you will reach the gift shop. There are permanent brands, pop-ups, and the products in the gift shop change depending on the exhibition.

I’ve been to many museums and art galleries and this one was one of the most unique and educational one by far. The exhibit about starting business and how to communicate with people was amazing. I loved a reminder that failure is the best teacher. There is also a cafe and garden. Everyone was super friendly and helpful.

It has a good atmosphere. I didn't know that there is  a good cafe like piknic in hoehyun-dong near namdaemun station. We enjoyed a coffee here after having lunch in namdaemun market. It was cozy. There weren't lots of people on weekeday. You can wandering along namsan after a coffee here.

I think it's a bit pricey..but I guess it depends on what's inside..!
One of the things that I liked about here was that it doesn't allow photography inside the exhibition. Rooftop's view is really great.

reviews.text: This is more than a flagship store — it’s a full experience. The multi-floor space combines gallery installations, a stylish café, and the complete range of Gentle Monster eyewear. There is a waiting area with seats. Waiting time was ~20 min. Staff was quick to adjust the frame. On the spot tax refund, so remember to bring your passport if you are a tourist.

title: 하이커 그라운드
google_addr: 40 Cheonggyecheon-ro, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
HiKR Ground is a really fun and modern spot to explore Korean culture, especially if you’re into K-pop, K-dramas, and Korean media.

The space is very interactive, with digital installations, photo zones, and hands-on experiences. It’s easy to spend time taking photos and trying out the activities, even if you’re not a hardcore K-pop fan. Everything is well designed and visually impressive.

It’s also free to enter, which makes it a great stop if you’re in the area or looking for something fun to do indoors. The location is convenient and easy to find.

Overall, a great place for tourists and anyone curious about modern Korean culture. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Seoul.

HiKR Ground is a fantastic experience. It is interactive and completely hands-on, with activities ranging from K-Pop performances/ Karoke,  becoming a DJ, to taking photos and seeing them memorialized on a magazine cover. Kids can explore experiences tied to space, the subway system, and even Korean laundry culture. It is an incredible interactive opportunity for children, and best of all, it is completely free. With 4 to 5 floors of engaging activities, kids will stay busy for hours. We had an absolute blast and highly recommend it.

5 levels of stuff to explore, great for escaping lousy weather. Kids enjoyed the more interactive and visual exhibits. I would have loved for more time to appreciate the artsy and thought provoking exhibits. Free of charge, not crowded on a Thursday noon.

Amazing place not just for kids but adults can fulfill their inner child here too. Free entrance to so many fun things! Even free photo studio area? (something like that) + the whole places looks like straight out of kpop music video. Definitely worth it visiting this place.

Free entrance for you to experience South Korean cultures. There are few floor to explore. Top floor being showcasing the beauty scene of South Korea in photos, then other lower floors have many Kpop experience which teens and kids enjoy. Many photo or video opportunities inside.

title: 한강 다리밑 영화제
google_addr: 330 Yeouidong-ro, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Yeouido Hangang Park is a wonderful place to relax and enjoy beautiful riverside scenery. The wide open spaces, well-maintained paths, and fresh breeze make it a perfect spot for walking, cycling, or simply sitting down and enjoying the view. The atmosphere is calm yet lively, especially during sunset when the sky becomes really beautiful. It’s a great place to hang out with friends or family while taking a peaceful break from the busy city.

Wide open space, a large park beside the Han river that has its own bicycle lanes for slow and fast riders. Great for runners and walk-marathoners alike. The views are fine between the Seongsan and Hangang Railroad bridges. You can see in the distance the Namsan tower behind the cityscape. Tip: go here during the early morning and exercise; go when there are decors, or events especially with light shows.

Yeouido sits by the Han River and is one of three public parks that makes up Hangang Park. This park is accessible by the Seoul Metro and serves as the place where you can ride on a river boat for a cruise. During winter, a snow sled area gets set up from mid December to February

I like that it's a strip of Riverside. Overlooking the other part of Seoul. Cooling breeze with chairs for public to sit and enjoy. .. I saw many people picnic there as well. There are some floating shops there... CU Ramyeun library.... Can eat superb noodles Riverside!

I visited Yeouido Hangang Park at night, and surprisingly it didn’t feel as “Instagrammable” as I had expected. The area was quite quiet during my visit, possibly because of the cold weather, so the atmosphere felt a bit empty.

Still, the riverside view at night has its own charm, but overall it may be better to visit during warmer seasons or earlier in the day when the park is livelier.

title: 한강레져스포츠

reviews.text: One of the most famous and must-do experiences when visiting Seoul, Korea, is taking a trip along the Han River. You can enjoy the stunning views all along the river, and I especially recommend going at night when the scenery is even more breathtaking. The cruise offers live music, which was excellent, and the atmosphere on board is truly amazing.

The cruise 🚢 experience was great, it was perfectly on time. I wish it would have been for a lil longer, it was only for 30 minutes and the time flew by so fast witnessing the beauty of the Han River 🥰🥰🥰
The cruise was clean, well maintained and very time bound!

I booked the moonlight cruise. Price is very reasonable.  Intresting insight was provided about bridges, landmarks and buildings.  Thereafter, a talented young lady entertained the guests with some festive melodies.

I know, you've probably did some Dinner Cruises (just like me) and often the food was mediocre. Let me tell you: The sunset dinner cruise here is excellent. Fantastic food, wondeful crew, enough space, great ambience, i was totally impressed. An absolute No-Brainer - do it when in Seoul!

such a surreal experience!! i enjoyed every second of the e-land sunset cruise! seagulls may follow because of dried fish, which you can purchase downstairs in the cu on the cruise and feed it to them. (i’m not sure how much it was because i didn’t even know you could feed them at first 🥲 i was wondering why there was a slight fishy smell) i loved the live music and just the overall vibe. the cruise also tells you facts about the bridges/buildings/areas you pass through which i thought was pretty interesting! it’s about 30 mins long but totally worth it!! you also get a nice view of seoul tower.

title: 한강시민공원 잠원수영장(실외)
google_addr: 145-57 Jamwon-ro, Seocho District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text:
I wasn’t always a fan of Han River swimming pools—in fact, I had avoided them for a while. The ones I visited in previous years didn’t leave a great impression: the water wasn’t very clean, and some even had an unpleasant odor. But my recent visit to the newly opened pool right next to the Starbucks at Seoul Wave Center completely changed my mind.

I initially went to the area to visit the Starbucks branch, which offers stunning riverside views, and was pleasantly surprised to discover the new pool just next door. Unlike my past experiences, this one was clean, well-maintained, and smelled fresh. The poolside offers a beautiful, unobstructed view of 강북, and the atmosphere felt much more elevated than I expected.

I rented a sunbed for just 10,000 won, which was worth it for the comfort and view. The entrance fee is only 5,000 won, making it an affordable way to cool off and relax by the river. In fact, I’d confidently say the view from here is even better than the one at the more expensive Walkerhill Hotel pool.

The only downside is the limited food options. Since outside food isn’t allowed unless you packed it from home, you’re mostly stuck with typical Korean street snacks like 라면, 떡볶이, 오뎅, and corn dogs—which aren’t really my thing. Also, drinks are only allowed in tumblers, so I’d recommend stopping by the Starbucks beforehand to grab your favorite beverage to enjoy poolside.

Overall, it’s a great summer escape with a surprising level of comfort and a view that’s hard to beat for the price.
Best outdoor pool in Hangang river by far. It has 3 separate pools, one only for adults. totally recommended to go visit in summer. They open 9am until 12pm. then 1pm to 6pm. then 7pm till 10pm

If you’re looking for a budget friendly pool day by the river, this is a good option. There is plenty of space and an option to rent one of the lounge chairs that line one of the three pools. The main pool has a swimming lane but most people are just causally taking a dip. (YOU MUST WEAR A SWIM CAP) but they also allow ball caps… I even saw a handful of people with head scarfs… just cover your head. Theres a few options for snack food including a pizza truck. (Not sure if it’s a permanent situation) The crowd is mostly locals ranging from 20’s to 30’s but there were a handful of kids running around. Overall, it’s a solid option if you want to switch it up from attending one of the hotel pools in Seoul.

Not bad and especially in the hot weather a nice refreshment. In Korea you have to wear a bathing cap to go into the water and the pool is not deeper than 130m. There is food to buy which is ok. Generally no green and lots of concrete.
This area will be a tube sliding park in winter season. Feel quiet so you can slide more than you would rather than in another sliding park.

A fantastic experience which guests could 'time-travel back' to Joseon dynasty.  Though the name of this beautiful museum is Korea Furniture Museum (Kofum), it covers a bigger scope beyond just a collection of Joseon furniture.  The premise houses ten restored hanuks (which were built without nails and by wood joinery techniques) with these furniture inside, providing a context of how people (aristocrats) of Joseon used to live and how the furniture were used.

The English guided tour lasted about an hour, though short but pretty intensive.

Though some may think the entrance fee is high, it's worth it, well curated and lots of information like the design of various types of cabinets, tables, book-cases, etc. After which could get close to the furniture and observe the craftsmanship.

An interesting section was the lady's quarter where it displayed and described how a Joseon Queen was dressed with her 6-layer costume before putting on the heavy head-gear. As the Lady mostly stayed indoor,  her room would get the best view and with a large window looking out.  The guide would invite the guests to sit on the floor and experience the scenery (as what the Lady in past did).

Please note no photography is allowed inside the museum.  Around the compound, the guide did not insist.

Overall, a nice museum to truly experience Korean tradition, aesthetic and culture, just wish the tour could be slower.

The Korea National Folk Museum is a beautifully curated place that gives you a real window into how Korean life evolved through the centuries. One of the first pieces that stood out was a stunning driftwood animal sculpture — simple, artistic, and a perfect introduction to the museum’s blend of creativity and history.

Inside, the exhibits walk you through traditional tools, farming equipment, fishing gear, and everyday household items in a way that’s easy to follow and visually engaging. The old handwritten manuscripts and medical texts were fascinating to see up close, showing just how carefully knowledge and culture were recorded and preserved.

The outdoor area adds even more charm. The pagoda is absolutely striking, and the small wooden home replica gives you a quiet moment to imagine how families lived generations ago.

Overall, this museum offers a calm, meaningful experience that deepens your understanding of Korean culture. It’s informative, relaxing, and definitely worth adding to your Seoul itinerary.

reviews.text: Seoul Central Mosque, located in Itaewon, is the largest and most well-known mosque in South Korea. The mosque serves as a central place of worship and community for Muslims in Seoul. Surrounded by halal restaurants and international shops, it also reflects the multicultural atmosphere of Itaewon.

The Seoul Central Mosque (Korean: 서울중앙성원; Arabic: مسجد سول المركزي) is a mosque opened in 1976 in Itaewon, Seoul, South Korea. It is located in Hannam-dong, Yongsan District. It holds lectures in English, Arabic, and Korean. Friday prayers regularly attract between four hundred and five hundred worshipers in the afternoon, though regular attendance has sometimes been known to climb as high as eight hundred people.

Seoul Central Mosque is a peaceful and inspiring landmark in the heart of the city. Blending beautiful Islamic architecture with the vibrant spirit of Seoul, it offers a calm refuge for prayer, reflection, and cultural connection. The welcoming atmosphere, diverse community, and spiritual serenity make it a must-visit place for anyone seeking tranquility and unity beyond borders.

Per staff: Jumuah offered 1pm on Fridays, only one timing, it is done in Arabic, English, and Korean.
Weekly programming for new Muslims/people interested in Islam
Barakah cafe located on the premises
If you’re walking to get here, it’s an uphill climb.

Ramadan: nightly Iftars (come early to get a meal coupon, as they are limited), nightly Taraweeh (8 rakah I believe), per staff, Eid Salah currently offered at the masjid itself but it gets very crowded as thousands attend.

reviews.text:
Drab. Just too much of the paint odor, and, sanitary  spray smell lingering throughout the exhibition.

We didn't get to care more about Baekje history although we spent some  hours to browse through the lame story boards. Waste of structure and public fund.

The English captions are missing from the beginning, and, if there are, it was patchy. There are English captions in some on 2nd level, but they were not reviewed by the native speakers and many displays still miss the English captions for foreign visitors.

I think they do not have the in-house curators but outsourced the story boards to some graphic editor who had done a very amatuerish job.

For example, the huge wall of the historic events were wrongly posted the old-to-new historic events in Korean peninsula  and other world regions, from right to left, when the public procession is from left to right.

They did not bother to change it.

And posting oldest event at the bottom and newest at the top on each era This was confusing and not intuitive. It is as if there was no one who reviewed each board before hanging them.

Situated in a bygone sculpture park from military era of 1980s, the surrounding setting is outdated and neglected by the Gangdong district office.
The whole area, indeed, is inaccessible from neighboring apartment complexes due to "baricated" road and sidewalk/ raised landscape elements, and  subway stops were located remotely, discouraging the visitors to come (for nothing).

We really tried to acknowledge the museum setup, but had to take a on-call taxi to leave the area, giving up to walk to the subway. We felt forced to walk in this area.

Very inhumane.

The Museum itself is  a many of the patchy curation work done by cheap graphic contractors with no screening.

The building was poorly designed and, imo, copied from de Young Museum SF concept and many others using the mass floating over the slope design concept, in domestic Korean architecture trend almost 20 years ago.

The Space inside was totally wasted and their programs do not match the building space flow, either.

The program inside is mediocre at best. It is not well developed story or experience. Just cheap cheap cheap.

I would not recommend to visit this place, but we tried.
The building’s architecture is more impressive than the actual collection.  They do have some interesting videos but it feels limited for the beauty and scale of the building.

- Came on a weekday AM, a few different groups but not crowded
- Free admission!
- Multiple guided tours per day in Korean- you can ask the front desk OR the tour times are listed on the informational pamplet
- Highly recommend the guided tours, guides are very friendly and informative
- Parking for ~2 hours was ~4,000 won
- Currently had a special Hittite exhibit- can be viewed in
I learned the history of Seoul as the capital of Baekjae. In weekend, it was not too crowded for visiting with children.

Seoul Baekje Museum (Korean: 한성백제박물관) is a museum in South Korea. Based on the natural silhouette of the nearby Mongchontoseong, the appearance of Seoul Baekje Museum was shaped a ship of Baekje in honor of Baekje. Seoul Baekje Museum is a civic lifelong education center with an emphasis on the educational role. There are a variety of Baekje artifacts and vividly embodied materials on ancient history of the Korean peninsula.

reviews.text:
The museum and outside exhibit provide a deep insight into the history of the city walls. Great interactive exhibits inside, and an excavated section of the original wall outside - plus the certificate issuing office for those completing the walk around the walls.

I visited twice in one day - around 10am to begin my 22km hike clockwise, then returned around 4:15pm - tired, but happy to collect my certificate and badge. You need to take a selfie at 4 specific points around the walls, then upload to their website to verify your completion of the walk.
Stunning views, and great exercise, as you loop around Inwangsan, Bugaksan, Naksan and finally Namsan.

There are 4 badges to collect - one for each 3 month period of the year. Collect all 4 and you get a special gold badge - the museum guide was proudly wearing hers.

Highly recommended!

Despite being pretty small it's interactive.
Also offers you a playful way to find your favourite historical trail in Seoul.
The employee there was very helpful and patient.

One of few original Seoul fortress walls that have been excavated. Nice history lesson as you hike up Namsan N-Tower area! Very wide open space and a great photographic opportunities to take along with the N-Tower in the backdrop on your selfie. Highly recommend to view the history, it only takes 15 to 20 minutes.
It's quite small but well organized. Seoul's wall is well explained along with a brief history of Nam mountain. Beautiful multimedia art works well.

Whether you’re an art lover, architecture enthusiast, or simply someone looking for a quiet moment in the city, I highly recommend a visit to Hanji Gaheon.

reviews.text: Yeouido Hangang Park is a wonderful place to relax and enjoy beautiful riverside scenery. The wide open spaces, well-maintained paths, and fresh breeze make it a perfect spot for walking, cycling, or simply sitting down and enjoying the view. The atmosphere is calm yet lively, especially during sunset when the sky becomes really beautiful. It’s a great place to hang out with friends or family while taking a peaceful break from the busy city.

Wide open space, a large park beside the Han river that has its own bicycle lanes for slow and fast riders. Great for runners and walk-marathoners alike. The views are fine between the Seongsan and Hangang Railroad bridges. You can see in the distance the Namsan tower behind the cityscape. Tip: go here during the early morning and exercise; go when there are decors, or events especially with light shows.

Yeouido sits by the Han River and is one of three public parks that makes up Hangang Park. This park is accessible by the Seoul Metro and serves as the place where you can ride on a river boat for a cruise. During winter, a snow sled area gets set up from mid December to February

I like that it's a strip of Riverside. Overlooking the other part of Seoul. Cooling breeze with chairs for public to sit and enjoy. .. I saw many people picnic there as well. There are some floating shops there... CU Ramyeun library.... Can eat superb noodles Riverside!

I visited Yeouido Hangang Park at night, and surprisingly it didn’t feel as “Instagrammable” as I had expected. The area was quite quiet during my visit, possibly because of the cold weather, so the atmosphere felt a bit empty.

Still, the riverside view at night has its own charm, but overall it may be better to visit during warmer seasons or earlier in the day when the park is livelier.

title: 헌인릉 생태경관보전지역(오리나무림)
google_name: Heolleung (Tomb of King Taejong and Queen Wongyeong)
google_addr: 산13-1 Naegok-dong, Seocho District, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: 조선 3대 태종 이방원과 원경왕후가 묻혀진 장소입니다.

헌릉은 조선3대 태종과 원비 원경왕후 민씨의 쌍릉이다. 건립당시부터 오른편을 비워두어 쌍릉으로 계획되었으며 난간석으로 두 능을 하나로 연결하였다. 조선 건국이래 첫 쌍릉으로 능상위에 배치되는 문, 무인의 수가 다른 능보다 두배 더 배치되었다. 1856년 순조의 인릉이 건립되면서 헌인릉으로 불렸다.
1420년 7월 원경왕후가 승하하자 광주군 대모산 남쪽에 터를 잡았다. 9월17일 국장하여 능호를 헌릉이라 불렀다. 1422년 태종이 승하하자 9월 6일에 재궁이 석실에 안치되어 쌍릉으로 안치되었다.

reviews.text: The most popular dish here is, of course, a spicy beef shank stew(매운 사태찜). I decided to go for their signature menu as usual, which costs 20,000 won. The food comes in generous portions, the beef was well cooked, and it tasted good. The spicy sauce wasn’t too overwhelming. It went along perfectly with soju, so ended up drinking two bottles of Hallasan with lemon and tonic. After that, I ordered another cuisine: fried beef (한우 튀김), which costs 18,000 won. I really needed to cut down on the fried stuff, but I couldn’t hold it any longer. The meat was perfect, with all the crispy parts on the outside, and tender and juicy on the inside. The restaurant was already full of young people at 6 PM, in just one hour after the restaurant opened up at 5 p.m. This place is not the most ideal destination for couples, but when it comes to hanging out and chatting with friends, I believe this place is a pretty nice choice. I would probably come back the next time I crave for a spicy beef stew.

reviews.text: Hongdae Street is an incredibly fun and energetic area that truly represents the 'young' side of Seoul. I loved seeing all the talented street performers doing magic, live music, and impressive dance routines right on the sidewalk. There are so many unique shops and restaurants to explore that you could spend an entire day here and not see it all. It’s the perfect place to soak in the creative energy of the city!

We visited this street during the festive Christmas season and it was extremely busy and very packed, so it’s definitely something to be mindful of if you’re not a fan of crowds. That said, there is so much to see and do, and the lively atmosphere really adds to the experience.

Everything was open, and the street was bright and colourful with lights everywhere, making it feel vibrant and exciting. There were performers along the street, which added to the energy, and plenty of food markets and stalls offering a wide variety of options.

Despite the busyness, it’s a great place to visit and soak in the atmosphere, especially if you enjoy busy streets with lots happening around you.

This street is amazingly rich in culture, full of life, and very much alive. It is a must visit if you are doing a city tour of Seoul. We arrived at 7pm and left at 9pm. We thought 1.5 hours was enough but while we are there we needed to extend it to 2 hours. Still, it wasn't enough. You can easily spend 4 hours here and you won't notice the time. There's so much to see, listen, and taste for you to enjoy.

홍지문은 탕춘대성의 성문으로 조선 숙종 41년(1715)에 서울도성과 북한산성을 보완하기 위해 세웠다. 지금 있는 건물은 1921년 홍수로 오간대수문과 같이 허물어진 것을 1977년에 복원한 것이다.
기능적으로도 1413년 폐쇄된 숙정문 대신 실질적인 북대문의 역할을 하였다고 볼 수 있다. 일종의 관문성(關門城) 성격을 지니게 되었다

reviews.text: Amazing Tour outside Seoul 😍  it was great to see the country side of Seoul and experience the tour, you see the crops, all green and sights. Didn't realize the bikes were physical but each tunnel was unique and. Highly recommended to explore the countryside of Seoul!

A must visit if you're in Seoul for an extended period. It's a bit outside of what you would consider the central part of town but definitely worth it. It's basically an old railway line dating from the Japanese occupation era, which is now transformed into a park. It's a nice place to get some exercise while also getting a dosage of history. The whole line is roughly six kilometers although I just visited one of the main disused stations section. This area also housed disused trains, which I found to be super cute. I would definitely want to return to visit the other sections as they wind through different neighborhoods in Seoul!

This place is suitable for families, couples, adults… I came here right before the rain on Sunday afternoon so the photos did not come out well but I enjoyed my time here. They also have train village nearby so I will definitely come back next time on a sunny day to enjoy the train village.

Long ago, the closed railway station was recycled very well. It has become a good park to come out for a walk and it is good to use as a photo zone.
It would be good to go on a memory trip here.
Outdoor museum especially for kids to learn about trains & railways

reviews.text:
효민공 이경직 묘역

조선 인조 때 호조판서를 지낸 이경직(1577~1640)과 그의 두 부인 보성오씨와 고성이씨의 삼위합장 묘가 있는 묘역이다. 묘역의 봉분은 쌍분으로 이경직과 오씨가 오른쪽 봉분에 합장되고 고성이씨가 왼쪽 봉분에 따로 매장돼 있다.
신도비을 비롯하여 묘표. 혼유석. 상석. 향로석. 망주석.문인석 등 석물이 있다
이경직 자는 상고 호는 석문. 1601년(선조 34) 사마시를 거쳐 1606년(선조 39) 문과급제 사관이 되고 홍문관정자, 1613년(광해군 5) 병조정랑.지제교.종사관.병조참판.도승지.강화부유수를 지내다.비문은 승평부원군 김류가 지었고, 문필가였던 이경직의 셋째 아들 이정영이 비문과 전액을 썼다.(인조.현종실록.국조인물고)

reviews.text: Good

서울의 숨은 문화 보석, 흰물결아트센터

안녕하세요, 문화 탐험가 여러분! 오늘은 서울 서초구에 위치한 아름다운 복합문화공간, 흰물결아트센터를 소개해드리려고 해요. 법조단지 한가운데 자리 잡은 이곳은 예술의 물결이 도시의 삭막함을 씻어내는 듯한 느낌을 줍니다.

흰물결아트센터의 탄생
흰물결아트센터는 한 변호사의 아름다운 꿈에서 시작되었습니다. 법조단지의 차가운 분위기에 문화의 씨앗을 심고, 사람들의 순수함과 선함이 물결처럼 퍼져나가기를 바라는 마음으로 탄생했죠. 2007년에 문을 연 이곳은 그 이후로 서초구의 문화 중심지로 자리 잡았습니다.

다양한 문화공간
흰물결아트센터는 단순한 공연장이 아닌 복합문화공간입니다. 이곳에는 세 개의 공연장과 갤러리, 출판사, 서점이 한데 모여 있어요.
= 흰물결화이트홀: 457석 규모의 메인 공연장
= 흰물결예술극장: 303석의 중형 공연장
= 흰물결아트홀: 193석의 소형 공연장
= 흰물결갤러리: 다양한 전시를 위한 공간
= 도서출판 흰물결: 문화 콘텐츠 제작의 중심
= 서점 북앤뮤직: 책과 음악이 어우러진 공간

최고의 음향 시설
흰물결아트센터의 자랑은 뛰어난 음향 시설입니다. 각 공연장은 소리의 울림과 잔향을 고려해 특별 제작된 반사판과 음향시스템을 갖추고 있어요. 덕분에 관람석 어디에서나 풍성한 소리를 즐길 수 있답니다.

다채로운 공연과 전시
이곳에서는 클래식 음악회부터 뮤지컬, 연극, 북콘서트, 팬미팅까지 다양한 장르의 공연이 열립니다. 갤러리에서는 회화, 조각, 설치미술, 사진 등 다양한 예술 작품을 만나볼 수 있어요.

편리한 접근성
흰물결아트센터의 또 다른 장점은 뛰어난 접근성입니다. 지하철 2호선 서초역에서 도보 1분 거리에 있어 대중교통으로 쉽게 방문할 수 있어요.

마무리
흰물결아트센터는 단순한 문화공간을 넘어 예술과 일상이 만나는 특별한 장소입니다. 바쁜 도시 생활 속에서 잠시 쉬어가며 문화의 향기를 느끼고 싶다면, 이곳을 방문해보는 건 어떨까요? 흰물결아트센터에서 여러분만의 특별한 문화 경험을 만들어보세요!

reviews.text:
A little over a month ago, I finally crossed the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul off my must-visit list. As a venue dedicated to showcasing both established masters and the vibrant contemporary scene, the MMCA is a truly world-class institution.
The most satisfying aspect of the visit was finally standing before works that feel legendary. Nam June Paik's Junk TV (잡동사니 벽) is an anarchic, mesmerizing wall of visual noise that beautifully captures the artist's genius and prescience regarding media overload. It remains a chaotic, vital masterpiece that anchors the modern collection.
Equally compelling, though in a profoundly quieter way, was Do Ho Suh's Floor. The simple act of walking across the glass surface, supported by hundreds of tiny, straining figures, transforms the space into an interactive, existential metaphor. It's a testament to Suh's ability to imbue architectural space with deep, personal meaning.
However, the highlight of the visit, and a thrilling discovery for me, was Jung Yeondoo's Cinemagician. Experiencing this piece for the first time was genuinely captivating. Jung has a powerful way of blending the real and the imagined, and Cinemagician offered a fresh perspective on narrative and memory. It was the perfect example of the MMCA's strength: honoring foundational artists while actively championing the next generation of visionary creators.
The collection is diverse, the curation is thoughtful, and the combination of monumental installations and unexpected delights makes it an absolutely essential stop for anyone interested in contemporary art.

We visited last year and were a bit disappointed in the exhibits. Our friend convinced us to attend this year as Kim Tschang-yeul was showing and we are so glad we did. What an incredible show and artist. Another National Icon and his art is highly sought after, so to be able to see so many of his original pieces in one spot was incredible. You can also see some of his work in the main lobby to the Lotte Hotel Seoul after the show finishes. The Gallery itself is extremely large and they've done a great job renovating the old building and creating a large gallery behind it. There is a large cafe in the lobby with limited food options  and lots of large spaces so it never feels too busy. It's free to walk around the main building but depending on the exhibits you will need to purchase tickets, which can be done easily at the museum in person or at a both. I think you can book online too. The price was really low for an exhibit this size and quality.

I loved this visit and the art work on display this time. The grounds and buildings of the museum are really quite interesting in themselves. Busy coffee shop on site as well as a matcha tea shop.
Don't miss the two art gallery shops and the bookstore. The surrounding neighborhood is also good to explore.
