Beautiful place to walk around and experience traditional Seoul. The hanok houses, narrow alleys, and city views make it feel like stepping back in time, especially early in the morning when it’s quiet.
It can get crowded later in the day, but if you go on a weekday or before noon, it’s very peaceful and great for photos. There are small cafes, galleries, and hidden viewpoints along the way, so it’s fun to explore slowly.
Just remember people actually live here, so be respectful and keep noise down. Overall, a must-visit spot if you want history, culture, and great views all in one walk.

Bukchon Hanok Village is easy to combine with Gyeongbokgung Palace in a day trip. The bus drops you right at Bukchon-ro, where maps help you plan your walk. The village sits on a hillside, so expect some gentle climbs, but the backstreets reveal clusters of traditional hanok homes, rooftop views, and even glimpses of Gyeongbokgung Palace. There are cozy cafes with terraces for a break. Best to allow at least 2 hours to explore and find photo spots. Keep in mind it’s a residential area with access limited to 10 am–5 pm, so be respectful when taking photos. We visited around noon in early January and found it pleasantly uncrowded, though we only managed to see a few hanok houses compared to online photos. Still, it’s worth a visit for the atmosphere and views.

Just remember to keep your voice down to avoid causing disturbance to the residents.

There’s a tourist time window to visit certain areas: 10am to 5pm. Make sure to come within this time range.

Free museum. Several floors, with exhibits on 5th and 3rd. Interactive kids on 4th. Interior room with a view, and on the 8th floor roof outdoor viewing of the palace and Blue House.  couple cafes and areas to sit and rest. The exhibitions were nice, with some English translations.

After Korea’s liberation in 1945, this building served as the headquarters for the Ministry of Education and later the Ministry of Culture and Information, becoming the administrative center for national education and cultural policy in the early Republic of Korea.
When those offices moved to Sejong City, the site was reborn in 2012 as the National Museum of Korean Contemporary History.
This makes the museum’s location itself historically meaningful — it’s a place where the modern nation’s governance and cultural identity first took shape.

Inside, the exhibitions are well organized by period, from liberation to the present, making it an excellent introduction to modern Korean history — even for first-time visitors or foreigners.
Its surroundings also add to its significance: right across from Sejong Center and the Government Complex, and just behind it lies Gyeongbokgung Palace and Mt. Bukak. Together they form the symbolic axis of Korea’s politics and history.

One place you absolutely shouldn’t miss is the rooftop observatory on the 8th floor.
From there, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the entire Gyeongbokgung Palace, beautifully framed by the surrounding mountains.
It offers a perfect vantage point to appreciate the geomantic (Pungsu-jiri) harmony of the palace’s location — encircled by mountains that were believed to protect the king and ensure the dynasty’s stability.
It’s not just a museum; it’s a window into Korea’s landscape of power and tradition.

Highly recommended — especially the rooftop view that reveals the deeper meaning of Gyeongbokgung’s setting.

reviews.text: This is the best hotel in the district by a mile. They were accommodating throughout our stay and went above and beyond to make our stay as smooth and trouble free as possible. Don't listen to the Gen X's complaining that it is outdated and not contemporary or modern. This hotel has everything you could possibly want and more. The staff are super polite and friendly. Our hotel room also had a bath which is a rarity these days in modern hotels that only offer a stand up shower. With my old creaky joints and bones the bath was a welcome addition after trekking over Seoul I needed a place to relax and refresh my tired and weary body. Take a trip down to the lobby and step outside to have a selection of different eateries and restaurants lined around the hotel and you will be spoilt for choice. If eating out isn't your thing and you consider yourself to be an introverted person then the convenience store is just a couple of steps next to the hotel so no problem. This hotel is well worth a look and booking and I recommend to all travellers that are visiting Seoul. Away from the tourists if you enjoy your peace and quiet too.

We booked this last minute for a 5 day stay. And it was the best hotel! Check in and out was nice and easy. The rooms and bathroom was so nice, and we just loved everything about this hotel. If your coming to korea I highly suggest staying here!!

I had a great stay here. We got a room upgrade with an adjustable bed that let us raise both the head and foot sections. The room was spacious and beautifully designed. The hotel is in a high-rise, and it was my first time staying above the 20th floor.

The lobby has a sleek, modern, and minimalist style.

It’s about a 10-minute walk to the main train line, with plenty of coffee shops and convenience stores nearby. There’s also a Olive Young right next to the hotel.

The hotel is generally clean and well-maintained, but our stay was far from pleasant. The biggest issue was the air conditioning—no matter how we adjusted the settings, the room temperature remained at 26°C both day and night. This made it uncomfortably warm for a good night’s sleep. When I asked for assistance, the only suggestion was to turn off the air conditioning entirely. While this did lower the temperature slightly, the lack of airflow made the room feel stuffy and suffocating, eventually causing headaches.

Additionally, the double-bed rooms come with only one blanket, which may not be ideal for some couples. When I requested an extra one, I was informed that hotel policy does not allow for additional blankets. Instead, they provided me with the address of a nearby mall where I could purchase one myself. This was the first time I’ve ever had to buy my own blanket while staying at a three start hotel.

Overall, while the hotel meets basic cleanliness standards, these issues made for a very uncomfortable experience.

Awesome experience! Very clean rooms, great and helpful staff- late check out time as well (12pm). Very great facilities. Definitely a little far from the main city centre and so commuting is slightly annoying given how big seoul is but definitely a lovely hotel.

reviews.text:
If you want a true 5-star experience, this is the place to stay. It’s perfectly located close to everything you need which makes the stay incredibly convenient. I’m currently staying here and honestly have nothing to complain about.
The room is amazing and spotlessly clean, and the staff are genuinely friendly and welcoming. From start to finish, this stay truly feels like a 5-star experience. Highly recommended.

This is probably the WORST hotel we have EVER stayed in. Reading the reviews, it sounds like it’s dated but charming. However, the reality is it is POORLY maintained and not worth the value for what you pay for. I usually do my research and trust Google review and saw that this was a 4 star hotel with 4 star reviews. Wow - were we misled!

Our bathroom has mold and they’re attempting to wipe it down with a rag as we speak. We had to leave the room for them to clean and there is no lounge area to sit in. The chairs are stained and the wall paper is slowly but surely chipping away. Sink is incredibly low. No water bottle, lotion, q-tip is provided. You can barely even see from the window, since they don’t even clean it. It really is a bare bone hotel.

Please stay far away from this hotel. I feel extremely disappointed that I booked this hotel and feel like I wasted my money.

The only pro is the location and the bigger size room, but it does not make up for how old the space is and it’s lack of maintenance. It highly highly needs to be renovated.

Great location, 2 x double bed room was spacious and comfy with bathtub, overall classy facilities. Breakfast was good quality with great barista coffee included. Slightly old fixtures (the shower head of our unit was leaking a bit and the bath tub plug didn't fully close so we had to keep refilling the tub). Slightly pricey to me, but on par with Seoul prices and the very central location. The only thing I would hesitate about is the carpark, it's very tight and very steep entrance, you may need a bit of a running start to get up without losing traction especially if it is wet, but once you are up just go slowly and it will be fine. If you are not a confident driver just pay for valet. The very affordable 10k won a day parking price (non-valet, but there is valet option too) makes up for it. Super polite and helpful staff who helped us find and book a great strawberry picking place just outside Seoul. Would stay again.

Location was the best!! We were able to walk everywhere and explore during our short stay. We didn’t have to use the transportation systems and were able to walk everywhere we wanted under 20 minutes.

Service was good. The rooms are a bit outdated. Room was always cleaned and made once we got back from our adventure.

Smells like clean scent when you walk in the hotel. Always busy when we were there.

Cons
Carpet was filthy with stains. It was not vacuumed daily as fluff remained there for days.  Surfaces were not dusted properly.
Furnishings are old & 1 chairs apolstery was coming apart. Room was unbearably hot & the temperature wouldn't go below 23 degrees. We ended up calling reception who gave us an electric fan & showed us we could vent the window but this resulted in street noise.
Only 1 side table.
Bed practically against the wall, had to move it over to fit the 1 chair in the room down the side & use as a bedside table.
Breakfast ridiculously expensive at $48 AUD per person. Purchased items from a convenience store next door.
Lifts always  took a long time to come to the floors.
Not shown to your room nor assisted with cases.

Pros

Fabulous toiletries, they smelt divine & were a very good quality.
Laundry facility available
Comfortable firm bed & pillows
Huge wardrobe

Dongdaemun Plaza looks really impressive from the outside, the architecture and lights make it feel fun, futuristic, and almost magical, especially at night. It's definitely a great spot for photos and just walking around to enjoy the atmosphere. If you love architecture and art, you will definitely enjoy Dongdaemun Design Plaza. Designed by renowned architect Zaha Hadid, DDP is an iconic landmark known for its futuristic curves and seamless, flowing form that blends architecture, design, and urban space.

I visited early in the day when there were only a few visitors, and the experience was amazing. The atmosphere felt calm and peaceful, allowing me to fully appreciate every corner of the space, both indoors and outdoors.

While DDP hosts many art and design exhibitions, the building itself is truly a work of art.
What an amazing place! The New Years event was incredible with light show then fireworks. Great music, unique art installations and the building was so futuristic.

Free museum. Several floors, with exhibits on 5th and 3rd. Interactive kids on 4th. Interior room with a view, and on the 8th floor roof outdoor viewing of the palace and Blue House.  couple cafes and areas to sit and rest. The exhibitions were nice, with some English translations.

After Korea’s liberation in 1945, this building served as the headquarters for the Ministry of Education and later the Ministry of Culture and Information, becoming the administrative center for national education and cultural policy in the early Republic of Korea.
When those offices moved to Sejong City, the site was reborn in 2012 as the National Museum of Korean Contemporary History.
This makes the museum’s location itself historically meaningful — it’s a place where the modern nation’s governance and cultural identity first took shape.

Inside, the exhibitions are well organized by period, from liberation to the present, making it an excellent introduction to modern Korean history — even for first-time visitors or foreigners.
Its surroundings also add to its significance: right across from Sejong Center and the Government Complex, and just behind it lies Gyeongbokgung Palace and Mt. Bukak. Together they form the symbolic axis of Korea’s politics and history.

One place you absolutely shouldn’t miss is the rooftop observatory on the 8th floor.
From there, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the entire Gyeongbokgung Palace, beautifully framed by the surrounding mountains.
It offers a perfect vantage point to appreciate the geomantic (Pungsu-jiri) harmony of the palace’s location — encircled by mountains that were believed to protect the king and ensure the dynasty’s stability.
It’s not just a museum; it’s a window into Korea’s landscape of power and tradition.

Highly recommended — especially the rooftop view that reveals the deeper meaning of Gyeongbokgung’s setting.

A well-known luxury department store located in the vibrant Sinchon area of Seoul, South Korea.

It offers a wide variety of high-end fashion, cosmetics, accessories, and household items from both international and Korean brands.

The store is popular for its premium shopping experience, with customer service and product quality being top priorities.

In addition to shopping, Hyundai Department Store Sinchon also has a range of dining options, including cafes and restaurants located within the building, offering both Korean and international cuisine.

There’s also a food court in the basement that provides quick and affordable meals. The store often holds seasonal sales, so checking ahead for any promotions could be beneficial.

The department store is easily accessible by public transportation, with Sinchon Station (Subway Line 2) located nearby. It’s also within walking distance of Ewha Womans University and Yonsei University, making it a popular destination for students and tourists alike.

There’s parking available for those driving, but it can get crowded on weekends and holidays, so public transport is often the better option.

The store’s operating hours usually range from 10:30 AM to around 8:00 PM, but it’s always good to confirm times beforehand.

reviews.text: One of the moderate, medium of difficulty level of trail for hiking near Seoul. I love this route by many reasons.
Nice walking across Han river.

나지막한 산길로만 구성된 서울둘레길 16코스
완만한 산길로만 구성돼 있어 대부분의 길에 나무 그늘이 있어 그늘길로 시원하게 다닐 수 있습니다.
구파발역 3번출구에서 시작해서 증산역 3번출구까지 8.6km, 보통 속도면 3시간 정도 잡으시면 됩니다.
둘레길답게 운동화로도 충분히 다닐 수 있는 길이고 서울둘레길 중에서도 산길로만 구성된 아주 좋은 코스입니다.
앵봉산에는 조망점은 하나도 없고 봉산에는 3곳의 조망점이 있습니다. 봉산 정상인 봉수대가 조망이 제일 좋은 데 데크에서 북한산과 은평구, 남산타원까지 시원하게 보입니다.
나머지 두곳의 조망점은 모두 이름이 봉산전망대인데 봉수대에서 남쪽으로 둘레길따라 30분 가면 첫번째, 다시 15분 가면 두번째가 나오고 모두 북한산부터 여의도까지 보입니다.

나즈막한 산이지만 산은 길게 누워 여러 코스로
우리 를 안내합니다.
가까운 향동은 산을 넘어 다닐만 합니다.
멀리 서오릉 까지는 힘들지만 편도 코스로 갔다
돌아 올때는 버스 를 타고 돌아오는 재미도
쏠쏠 합니다.
서오릉에 가면 맛있는 식당들이 줄비해서 소풍
삼아서 다녀 올만 합니다.
비록 잡목들이 다수지만 봉산은 깊은 숲과 오롯이
나만이 즐길수 있는 코스가 있어서 행복한 시간을
갖을수 있읍니다.
무엇보다 꾸준하게 관리해서 모두가 편하게 접근
할수 있도록  관할구의 노력이 돋보입니다.

중간 중간 급경사가 있기는 하지만, 험한 길은 아니여서 편하게 산책을 할 수 있는 둘레길임.
앵봉산 정상 부근, 봉산 봉수대 등의 전망포인트에서 딱 트인 광경을 볼  수 있음.

북한산 둘레길 8코스의 구름다리정원길은 중간 중간에 오르막길이 더러 있었지만 시원한 데크길을 걸으며 가을 하늘과 바람을 느끼며 걷는 것에 집중할수 있어서 좋았다. 가을이 왔음을 알리는 듯 하얀 속살을 드러낸 억새잎이 햇살을 받으며 반짝인다. 오를수록 북한산의 암벽 전경이 시원하게 드러나니 발걸음이 한결 가벼웠다.

title: [서울둘레길 20코스] 북한산 강북코스
google_addr: Insubong-ro 55-gil, Suyu-dong, Gangbuk-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.text: Nice scenery

원래 둘레길은 산 정상까지 목표로 가지 않는 길이다. 오솔길과 예쁜 길, 걷기 편한 길이다. 그러나 흰구름 둘레길(북한산 둘레길3구간, 서울둘레길 20코스) 전망대는 마치 산 정상에 올라 내려다 보는 뷰같다. 360도의 시원한 경치가 보인다. 용문산과 유명산까지 보인다. 반대편으로는 칼바위 정상과 만경대, 인수봉은 당연 보인다. 전망대 바로 밑은 자연 그늘 칸이 되어 돗자리 피고 자연바람을 느끼며 쉴만한 곳이다. 이 칸 역시 쉬면서 360도 뷰를 바라볼 수 있다. 아주 좋은 포인트에 이런 전망대를 만들어 주어 감사하다.

북한산성북19코스 가운데 있는전망대로
날씨좋을때는주변 산세와 경관을 시야에담을수있고 카메라에도 선명하게남기는 순간포착은 기회인것같다.
화계사에서정릉을거쳐서 평창동으로연결되는 둘레길은 자연의모습인 숲과 물의흐름을 담아. 바람에 땀을 묻을수있는순간도 자연의 순리인것같다.
계절의시간이바뀌면 이또한 새로운 자연미를 보여줄 팔색조의 구간이지않을까  생각합니다.
북한산 둘레길 1구간은 흰구름길이다. 그길의 하이라이트는 아무래도 흰구름 전망대. 전망대는 사진처럼 생겼고, 그 위에서 바라보는 풍경은 이렇다. 정말 시원한 모습이다. 그리고 뒤로는 북한산이 버티고 서 있다.
북한산을 가봤다고 말하려면 한번은 가봐야 하는 곳이라 생각이든다. 정말 아름다운 곳이었다. 남산 전망대, 북악산 팔각정을 능가하는 뷰가 이 곳이었다.

즐기고 있어요 ,

- 2022.4.8 안양천 양천 둘레길에 벚꽃이 만개.

- 양천 둘레길의 안양천 구간. 안양천 양측 모두 산책길이 있는데 서쪽의 산책길임. 동쪽과 달리 벚나무로 터널이 만들어져 있어서 여름에도 그늘에서 걸을 수 있음. 5월 초에 반짝 벚꽃 터널.

- 둘레길은 북쪽으로부터 신목동역 근처 양화교에서 양평교, 목동교, 오목교, 신정교를 지나 오금교까지 5.1km 이어짐. 중간중간 식수대와 운동기구들, 화장실 설치돼 있음. 화장실에 물비누와 손 건조기 등이 있고 관리도 비교적 잘 되고 있음.

- 그늘 장점 때문에 햇빛을 피해 자전거도 가끔 다니는데 둘레길은 보행자 전용이므로 자전거는 바로 아래 자전거도로를 이용해야.
